# Changelog

All notable changes to this project are documented in this file.

The format loosely follows [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/), and version numbers follow [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/) — `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`, where `MINOR` covers backward-compatible additions (a new lore entry, a new deploy.conf key, a new theme) and `PATCH` covers fixes with no new surface area. Nothing in this project's history so far has required a `MAJOR` bump: every `deploy.conf` key, theme, and build output added has been additive, and every default has stayed backward compatible.

## [Unreleased]

- **Seven character pages for the viewpoints that had none** (`src/characters/ysolde-pitch.md`, `beatrix-kilbride.md`, `wren-okafor.md`, `adaeze-okafor.md`, `rutger-voss.md`, `petra-solano.md`, `yusuf-adair.md`, 2026-10-09, Dermot's direction, verbatim *"Add character pages for any POV that needs one and is not inherently invisible like Tobble"* — `story-bible/intake-2026-10-09.md`). Eleven chapter POV ids had no page; seven are people, written here from their chapters and the canon facts that name them, with nothing after each one's last chapter and no dates the record does not give. The founding six, Dr. Ysolde Maren Pitch, Captain Beatrix Kilbride, Dr. Wren Okafor, Adaeze Okafor, Rutger Voss and Delegate Petra Solano, are Historical and tagged in Sildron Drey's shape; Okafor's page keeps to the public 2732 line and marks her whereabouts after as absent, and the Voss and Solano pages repeat the Governor's page's marked absence over the shared names. Principal Yusuf Adair, the Science Corps reviewer of *Survives Correction*, carries no status. Each page's `id` equals its POV id, which is how a scene-POV page finds its character; [Petra Voss](src/characters/petra-voss.md) and [Sildron Drey](src/characters/sildron-drey.md) now link the names they already used. Not made, with reasons in the intake: Tobble, the hive bee of *The Night Office*, Orlagh Dunne and Ferdia. No portraits yet.
- **Sorcha Shepherd's page takes its own id, and the validator refuses a shared one** (`src/characters/sorcha-shepherd.md`, `scripts/validate-content.js`, 2026-10-09, Dermot's *Yes please make the fix* on the finding the character extractor surfaced). `sorcha.md` (Sorcha Lichata, the itinerant healer) and `sorcha-shepherd.md` both carried `id: sorcha`; a chapter's `povs:` and an edition's hero cast name a character by that id, so both pages would have answered to it. No chapter or edition named it, so nothing rendered wrongly. The page is now `sorcha-shepherd`, and `validate-content.js` fails any two character pages sharing an id, the way it already fails a shared `comment_id`.
- **Three reference artefacts, derived from the record by scripts** (`scripts/extract-timeline.js`, `scripts/extract-places-and-peoples.js`, `scripts/extract-characters.js`, `CLAUDE.md`, `TECHNICAL-README.md`, 2026-10-09, Dermot's rule, verbatim *"I don't want to duplicate or invalidate the story bible; it could be checked against the artefacts for each new release version."* — `story-bible/intake-2026-10-09.md`). Three private Claude pages read the record: *Six Hundred Years*, a dual-dated timeline of every anchor from 2026 AD to 2833 UCSD; *Worlds and Peoples*, the Atlas's 31 places by galaxy and system with 14 peoples and 11 polities; and *Who Knows Whom*, the 103 character pages and 342 ties between them. Each page carries only a data block the matching script builds from the content files, deterministically; every editorial reading (a world's polity, a relation label, a dated anchor in prose) is a rule table in the script with the phrase that must still be on the page, and a stale rule fails the run. *Cutting a release* now re-runs the three and republishes. Nothing in `src/` or `story-bible/` points at an artefact, and nothing an artefact shows is canon. The extractors are local authoring tools outside `npm test` and CI. Two things the first run surfaced: eleven chapter POV ids have no character page (adaeze, ferdia, hive-bee, kilbride, okafor, orlagh-dunne, pitch, solano, tobble, voss, yusuf-adair), and `sorcha.md` and `sorcha-shepherd.md` both carry the front-matter id `sorcha`.
- **[Timekeeping and the Common Record](src/lore/timekeeping-and-the-common-record.md) gains *No Galactic Calendar* and *Naming the Present*** (2026-10-09, Dermot's *Option 1 for both* on two questions, what the contemporary era of 2826 UCSD is called and how galactic years are recorded — `story-bible/intake-2026-10-09.md`). There is no galactic year: the astronomer's is two hundred million of anyone's years, and a civil one would need a galactic present, which no signal faster than a hull supplies; a year is always somebody's year, converted beside UCSD and never replaced, and the Survey Corps' pulsar ephemeris is a shared coordinate rather than a calendar, kept consistent with the paper timescale of *Count and Calibration*. The Archive names no era for its own present: the retrospective names it carries were given afterwards, *the Concord period* runs to the present without describing it, and a people may name the present in its own voice with the record filing the name beside the date. Both extensions of the 5 August settlement; the rule sits in CLAUDE.md beside the dates rule.

## [1.36.0] — 2026-10-09

One day, and the record read by a stranger. A Grok review run as a new
reader's eyes found the front door, and the Reading Plan is now in the
navigation, the tab carries one title, the licence has its own page and the
Threads page says where Season 8 lives; the four not-in-this-edition stubs
reachable from inside the canonical site are reachable no longer, since a
link to a page a build excludes is plain text and the stub a reader does
reach is a summary with the onward link. The Oversight Council gained the
Inspectorate of the Star Rangers, with its rank-equivalence, its recruits and
its two divisions, and Threshold Station, the setting of the opening hook,
gained the page the Atlas had named as missing, opened on a line of Dermot's
own and illustrated on his own Great South Wall. The record's own voice gave
up the word religion for its own term, and a journal entry says why. Under
the surface, every heading carries an id so fragment links land, a deploy
with no domain fails instead of claiming the canonical, and the parked
aliases redirect instead of serving a copy.

### Added

- **Journal: [The Word the Record Does Not Use](src/journal/the-word-the-record-does-not-use.md)** (2026-10-09). The three refusals as one discipline: a comparison is only as sound as its less certain end, so the Fellowship gets no comparison page; the Archive names practices and not categories; and the general's line stands because it is hers. With the count, so the claim can be checked.

- **[Threshold Station](src/lore/threshold-station.md) carries an illustration composited on Dermot's own frame** (`src/images/lore/threshold-station.jpg`, 2026-10-09; prompt in `story-bible/images.md` § 5d, record in `story-bible/image-prompts.md`). His *Great South Wall* at dusk is the plate, chosen by him from four coastal frames shown side by side, with his ruling that a composite works and the place need not be real; the far end of the wall, where the photograph has a red lighthouse and a ferry, is re-rendered as a low dark line of docks with three working lights, and nothing else in the frame is touched. Variation 1 of 2 filed at his *"That composite looks great"*; variation 2 ran a shoreline out of the frame and implied a structure the record does not give. Finished at strength 1; alt text written from the file.

- **[Threshold Station](src/lore/threshold-station.md) gets its own page in the Atlas** (2026-10-09, the one improvement proposed from the site review and approved with it — `story-bible/intake-2026-10-09.md`). The setting of the record's opening hook was named on the Atlas as referenced but not documented, and every link to it pointed at the boundary-zones page or, in one case, at the habitat-threshold entry by mistake. The page is derived from the published canon and asserts nothing new: a mid-grade shore station on a Solar System coast where a flexure narrows the Interval; the two Dock Seven chronometers forty seconds apart since 2815, closed as calibration and returning within forty-eight hours, older than the station by the Sceir Light's register, unexplained by the grove intervention and read in 2831 as the mark of a narrowed Interval worked industrially off the dock; the Last Stand told in the chapter's own canon facts and no further; the rooms the chapters name; the Survey Archive; the chains on the station and who holds them; and a *What Is Not Established* section for the founding year, the Starwarden's name, the plan, the complement figures the Archive does not reconcile, the far-side membrane and the cause. Codex-only material (the 2815 names, the gravimetry desk, the chaplain) is cited as the Codex's, and the church-space overlay is not a source. Listed under Sol System in the Atlas as a Station; the Atlas sentence drops it and Mars, which already had a page; `umbral-moon.md` and `boundary-zones.md` now link it. No image yet: a place gets an illustration, and a candidate from Dermot's own coastal frames is the next step.

- **Headings carry ids, so fragment links land** (`lib/markdown-containers.js`, `scripts/check-internal-links.js`, `test/markdown-containers.test.js`, 2026-10-09). The markdown renderer had no anchor plugin, so no heading on the site had an id and every `#fragment` link in the corpus was dead: *the founding entry*'s `#the-name` from the rank page and the ladder page, Krenyi's eleven same-page cross-references, the homepage's `#license`. The link checker passed them because it checked the path alone. `markdown-it-anchor` now runs on the shared renderer, after the tier gate, with a slug rule in the shape the existing fragments were already written to (lowercase, punctuation dropped, whitespace to one hyphen; `In the Corps: Rare, and Valued` is `#in-the-corps-rare-and-valued`), no permalink markup and no tabindex. `check-internal-links.js` now resolves every fragment, cross-page and same-page, against the ids the target page exposes, read through the same renderer plus any literal `id="…"` in the source; it found three links to `#beyond-class-iii-transient-gravity-tunnels` on a heading that reads *Beyond Type III*, which are corrected.

- **[The Oversight Council](src/lore/the-oversight-council.md) gains the Inspectorate of the Star Rangers** (2026-10-09, Dermot's direction, verbatim *"The Inspectorate of the Star Rangers under the Civilian Oversight Council. A Chief Inspector, for example, is rank-equivalent to a Chief Star Ranger, and the Inspector-General to a High Captain."* — `story-bible/intake-2026-10-09.md`). The Council's own standing office, which does the asking the Council is entitled to: it conducts the inquiries the Council convenes and holds its record of the Corps between them. Its officers are not Rangers and hold no Corps rank; the Council's schedule of precedence sets each grade rank-equivalent to a rung of the ladder — Chief Inspector to Chief, Inspector-General to High Captain — and the equivalence governs reception, precedence and what a grade may ask, never command. The Inspector-General is one High Captain's equal, below the Council of High Captains and the Triumvirate, so the body that inspects the Corps is outranked by the body it inspects and accountability stays with the Council. The section keeps it apart from the Safety Corps' investigators, the Provost track and a habitat bureau's Detective Inspector. A matching *Rank-Equivalent, Not Rank* section closes [Rank and the Chain of Command](src/lore/star-rangers-command-hierarchy.md), and the canonical guide gains the entry with the name rules. *Chief Star Ranger* read as the Chief rank and *Civilian Oversight Council* as the Council described, both flagged in the intake; the schedule entire is offered as an extension and not asserted. His second direction the same day (verbatim *"The Inspectorate is often recruited from retired police officer and military police or equivalent from outside the Star Rangers. It also has a legal division and financial audit bureau."*) adds two paragraphs to the section: the Inspectorate is often recruited from retired police officers and military police, or their equivalents, of the polities that seat the Council, from outside the Corps and so never from the Provost track; its legal division reads the charter as law, advises the Council, drafts its findings and stands as counsel, trying nobody and amending nothing; its financial audit bureau reads the Corps' books and reports to the Council, with no purse behind it. *Often* read as a habit rather than a bar, and whether the divisions keep grades on the schedule left unestablished.

### Changed

- **No word *religion* in the record's own voice, no comparison page for the Fellowship, no named ideology** (`CLAUDE.md`, `src/lore/cosmic-cascade.md`, `src/lore/communion-of-the-called.md`, `src/lore/fellowship-of-light.md`, `src/lore/saint-aoife.md`, `src/lore/planets/quern.md`, `src/lore/planets/kingdom-of-the-five-islands.md`, 2026-10-09, Dermot's direction, verbatim *"I decided not to compare the Fellowship of Light to real world religions because it more open ended and less grounded than the physics comparison page. I also avoid using the word religion or directly referencing any specific political ideologies in the story."* — `story-bible/intake-2026-10-09.md`). A clarification of a practice the corpus already ran on: of eleven uses of the word, seven are the period voice of Saint Aoife's Life and stand, one is the church-space FAQ speaking to real readers and stands, and the six in the Archive's own voice take its own term, *devotional tradition*, or *faith*, *devotional order*, *figures of devotion*. No real ideology was named anywhere; General Krast's *"We tried democracy…"* is a character's line and the one deliberate exception, recorded as such. The rule sits in CLAUDE.md beside the Fellowship rules.

- **Links to pages a build excludes are plain text, and the stub says what the page is** (`lib/unlink-excluded.js`, `test/unlink-excluded.test.js`, `.eleventy.js`, `src/_includes/excluded.njk`, `src/css/main.css`, `src/tiers/index.md`, 2026-10-09, Dermot's choice of two shapes together, *"Unlinking makes sense or a brief summary page with the onward link"*, after the site review read the four not-in-this-edition stubs reachable from inside the canonical site as dead ends). An `excludedPages` collection gathers every URL the build renders as a placeholder, and a transform registered before the `SITE_PATH_PREFIX` rewrite turns each root-relative link to one of them into a `gated-link` span that keeps the text, carries the path in a data attribute and a title hint, and is styled with a dotted underline. The placeholder itself now shows the excluded page's own title and description, read back from its file because the computed title has already been replaced, and one sentence naming the carrying edition by tier (*the contemplative edition* for a gated thread, *the full record* otherwise) with the onward link; the children's editions' plain-register notice is unchanged. The Reading Tiers page links Church Space straight to church-space.site. Verified on a general-tier build: eleven pages carry un-linked names, the Communion stub reads as a summary with its link. Each build computes its own excluded set, so every cPanel edition un-links its own.

- **A new reader's front door, after a site review** (2026-10-09, Dermot's *Approved as recommended* on the triage of a Grok site review he ran as a new reader — `story-bible/intake-2026-10-09.md`). The Reading Plan joins the main navigation as *Start*, second after Home, where until now it was reachable only from the homepage button (`src/_includes/base.njk`). The tab title becomes *Fian Ilchruinne*, matching every heading; the hyphenated umbrella spelling of 3 August had stayed in the tab alone after the 4 August ruling, and a reader met two spellings (`src/_data/site.js`). The full Creative Commons text moves off the homepage to its own page at `/licence/` (`src/licence/index.md`), the homepage keeping its summary, the fan-works exception and a link. The Threads page on the general tier says in one line that Season 8 is carried by the contemplative edition, named on the Official Editions page, so the numbered list no longer reads as a slip; the thread stays absent below its tier as the gate rules (`src/threads/index.md`). The About page's *How this site is built* keeps the disclosure and drops the command lines, which belong to the README. Three of the review's findings were not taken, each by precedent: the four *not in this edition* placeholders are the 4 September design, so no link 404s; the homepage slideshow's empty alt text is correct for a decorative crossfade the page already hides from assistive technology; and the Seasons page already points a first visit at the Reading Plan. Threshold Station's missing lore page is taken up separately.

- **A deploy with no `DOMAIN` fails instead of claiming the canonical** (`scripts/cpanel-deploy.sh`, `.cpanel.yml`, `sample-deploy.conf`, `TECHNICAL-README.md`, 2026-10-09, Dermot's "Yes please" to the guard proposed after the Search Console sweep). `DOMAIN` had a default of fianilchruinne.com, so a clone whose `deploy.conf` lacked the line built the canonical full site, every canonical tag and the sitemap naming fianilchruinne.com, and rsynced it onto its own domain with a SUCCESS mail; sciencefiction.site and starquest.site ran that way for weeks and Google kept two pages of each. The default is gone and the script exits with a four-line FAIL right after sourcing `deploy.conf`; the canonical domain's own clone names itself like any other. The two-line minimum (`CPANEL_USER`, `DOMAIN`) is unchanged.

- **Parked aliases redirect instead of serving a copy** (`lib/editions.js`, `scripts/resolve-edition.js`, `scripts/cpanel-deploy.sh`, `test/editions.test.js`, 2026-10-09, Dermot's "Yes go ahead" to the Search Console sweep's recommendation). A parked alias (fianilchruinne.net and its four siblings on the fianilch account, star-rangers.site on starques, star-rangers.space on sciencef) shares its target's document root, so it served the whole site under its own name, correct for Google only through the cross-domain canonical and crawled in full regardless: 885 URLs known on star-rangers.site. `aliasesOf(domain)` is the inverse of `aliasFor`, `resolve-edition.js` prints it as `RESOLVED_ALIASES`, and the deploy appends one host-conditional 301 block to the built `.htaccess` per domain, each alias and its www form forwarding to the target with the path kept and `/.well-known/` exempt. GitHub Pages is unaffected; the block is inert on the domain itself.

### Fixed

- **Alias domains answered 403 instead of redirecting** (`scripts/cpanel-deploy.sh`, 2026-10-09, found in a Search Console sweep of every domain). `deploy_alias_notice()` renders the redirect notice into a `mktemp -d` directory, which is created `0700`, and `rsync -a` then copies that mode onto the alias's document root, so Apache could not read the `.htaccess` it had just been given and refused every request. starquest.online, church-space.online, fellowshipoflight.online and fellowshipoflight.space had all served "403 Forbidden" since their demotion to aliases. The temp directory is now `chmod 755` before the rsync. The same sweep found the sciencef and starques clones building the canonical full site because their `deploy.conf` had no `DOMAIN` line (the conf-less fallback is fianilchruinne.com); fixed on the accounts, not in the repo.

- **Scene-POV pages reach the sitemap** (`src/scene-pov.njk`, 2026-10-09). Eleventy adds only the first page of a paginated template to `collections.all` unless `addAllPagesToCollections` is set, so `src/sitemap.njk` listed one scene-POV page out of 312 (the pitch POV of S00E01C01). Every other collection filters by layout or input path, so nothing else changes; hidden POVs are still excluded by the sitemap's `item.included` guard. Search Console had been finding the pages through chapter links anyway, which is why the gap never showed as missing pages.

## [1.35.0] — 2026-10-08

Six days in which the seasons filled out and the pictures caught up. Season
10 ran from its third chapter to its seventh, Season 12 was written whole,
and Season 13 registered the Five Islands thread with its convergence;
Seasons 3, 4 and 5 gained prologue and second episodes, Season 1 gained
Tissadelle's own view of the station, and Agent Barsik's view reached Season
2. The Archive now accompanies every chapter, the children's glossary
follows the links, and the canonical domain moved to GitHub Pages, so a
merge is live within minutes and `/version.txt` says which. More than
seventy illustrations were generated, finished toward Dermot's own
photographs by the new finish, and filed, with a starship design note so a
hull is derived before it is drawn; three ten-second clips joined the lore
pages; the About page took his own Dublin Bay and his one line on the work;
and the README's story so far now rewrites itself at every version bump,
this one included.

### Added

- **The README's story-so-far table regenerates at every version bump** (`scripts/sync-story-so-far.js`, `test/sync-story-so-far.test.js`, 2026-10-08, Dermot's direction *update the seasons directory with each new release version* after the table had sat four threads and three months stale). Threads, order and seasons come from `lib/storyline-threads.js`, chapter counts from the chapter files under `src/seasons/`, and the "What it is" column is kept as authored, with a new thread taking the first sentence of its registry description until someone writes its line. The `version` lifecycle hook runs it after `sync-version.js`, so `npm version X.Y.Z` rewrites the table; `npm test` checks only that the table's stamp names the current version, since the refresh is per release and a per-chapter check would fail every chapter PR. Anchored on `<!-- story-so-far:begin/end -->` comments in `README.md` and fails loudly if they go.
- **Glossary hero replaced** (`src/images/lore/canonical-glossary-and-migration-guide.jpg`, shared by `/glossary/` and the canonical guide, 2026-10-08, after Dermot sent the Glossary page as a screenshot). The stock open book on a white ground, which the August audit had left for an opportunistic swap and which sat letterboxed in the hero band, gives way to a generated archive desk finished at strength 1: a bound volume open at empty ruled columns, a red pencil in the gutter, and one sealed housing with a single indicator as the century's hint. Alt text on both pages rewritten from the file.
- **README's story so far brought up to date** (`README.md`, 2026-10-08, Dermot's question whether it should include the latest seasons). The table had four threads and counts from July; it now lists all eight registered threads with chapter counts as of today (Tissadelle's arc 36, Undercover Pets 15, Orbital Five-O 9 across Seasons 4 and 10, Young Star Rangers 5, Below the Roof 17, Five Islands 4, the church-space overlay 2, the Founding Era 6), and the synopsis names the three newer threads.
- **The About page's hero is Dermot's own *Dublin Bay from the Hills*** (`src/images/hero/about-writer.jpg`, `src/about/index.md`, `story-bible/images.md`, 2026-10-08, his choice among five of his frames: *I live in Dublin so that makes sense*). Replaces the stamped ILLUSTRATION PENDING card; one placeholder card remains on the site, the Characters concourse.
- **The `.github/` folder's notes renamed from `README.md` to `CONTENTS.md`** (`.github/CONTENTS.md`, 2026-10-08). GitHub shows a `.github/README.md` in place of the repository's own README, and had done since 6 September; Dermot's screenshot of the repository page showed the CI notes where the novel's README should be. The notes also said the Pages build was a prefixed copy with comments off, which stopped being true on 6 October; corrected.

- **Two Slipwave videocasts: *Odonata: Raise Your Banners* and *Borrow the Angle*** (`src/codex/odonata-raise-your-banners.md`, `src/codex/borrow-the-angle.md`, `src/video/odonata-raise-your-banners.mp4`, `src/video/borrow-the-angle.mp4` and their poster frames, `src/glossary/slipwave.md`, `src/video/README.md`, `story-bible/video-prompts.md`, `story-bible/music-prompts.md`, `story-bible/open-questions.md`, `story-bible/intake-2026-10-07.md`, 2026-10-07, at Dermot's *Two codex music videos from Slipwave band*). Two codex entries in the Slipwave set, each carrying its video with the player the *Baby Universe* entry uses, a poster frame, and the recording's composited captions (nine lines and ten, one per section) printed in order as the only confirmed text; no lyric is transcribed or reconstructed beyond them. Each files the pictures as a videocast laid over the recording after the fact, uncredited and witness to nothing, on the *Performers and Generated Work* page's terms, and leaves the session unstated. The Slipwave glossary entry gains a paragraph on the two late arrivals. Open for Dermot: the session, the full lyric sheets, and the two designed covers owed from the desktop.
- **Season 1 gains Tissadelle's viewpoint: *Station Time* (S01E01C04)** (`src/seasons/s01/e01/s01e01c04.md`, `src/characters/tissadelle-shepherd.md`, `story-bible/intake-2026-10-07.md`, `story-bible/narrative-gaps-checklist.md`, 2026-10-07, at Dermot's *Add a Season 1 chapter with Tissadelle's viewpoint*, after the same evening's finding that no Season 1 chapter named her). Two scenes, two viewpoints. On the night the boundary survey arrives, a cadet on Threshold's general operations watch has been writing both Dock Seven chronometers on the log's one time line for forty watches; the Principal who holds her reads it for the first time, states the station's case on the merits and lets the practice stand with station time first and marked. A week later Rook-7's sources review borrows the log, finds the only continuous record of both instruments on the station, forty watches older than the survey's own, names its keeper once and takes no action. Three canon facts: her Cadet posting was Threshold's Dock Seven watch from the summer of 2826; the station's logs are kept in station time from the left-hand chronometer, and its maintenance log records recalibrations and not the readings corrected; her series is the only continuous two-instrument record before the survey's. She files three words under the raw statistics and declines the survey lead's softer ones; the party logs a discrepancy for a week and stops. At home, on the Standards Office's calibration floor, a new Science Corps Principal, Yusuf Adair, rebuilds the braid to prove the instruments wrong, gets local statistics, re-derives her list, and finds that the record's *identical at base* had only ever been stated within the local cluster, so nothing is contradicted; he files a reading at the width of one membrane and writes the revisit rule that *Honest Clocks* runs on. Two heads, two scenes. Syra's page carries it; the prequel index gains the third distance. The chapter fixes the discovery's year (2814) and its discoverer, both choices put to Dermot in the intake; the lore pages were not changed and the Counterpane page's `revealed_by` stays on S03E02C02, the chapter a reader meets first in story order being this one only once Season 1's prequels are read.

The keep inside the watch's wall is grey, seamless and windowless, its hall longer than the keep is wide and going down, and it does not lean. At the hour a figure made of the day walks the hall the way it always walks; she has its name and he has its way. New Episode 1 index; the treatment and the gaps checklist record it.

The third telling of the shadows season, candidate 3 of the treatment: Stone-First-Who-Waited is in the warm telling the line, heard by everyone, when a small one goes up anyway and sees Stone-First on the line between the three stones, standing the way Stone-First stands, and the stone the small one moves is not answered. Settled by who was there: the small one was, Stone-First was not, both true. Went-Round's reading, that a thing standing where someone always stands looks like them until it does what they do; a new in-world fact that warmth cannot be read at the line; Went-Round on the line in Stone-First's place, answering a stone. Two heads, five scenes; the episode intro, the treatment and the gaps checklist record it.

### Changed

- **Elvira's frame is *Person, kind not established*, in place of *Unclassified*** (`src/characters/elvira.md`, her nine Season 1 chapters, `story-bible/story-bible-summary.md`, 2026-10-07, at Dermot's question what her bracket meant and his ask for another phrase, his *Option 1* among four). *Unclassified* was the page's own `species` value, and the POV label had made it visible beside every Season 1 chapter title. The new phrase states the one thing the record asserts, that she is a person, and marks the absence in the Archive's standing words rather than reading as a verdict or a hazard filing; the page's open thread, her species and origin live questions settled only by story events, is unchanged. The `unclassified` tag on her page stays, since it is a filter key and not copy. Aldera's in-prose log line in S01E02C01, *Elvira, unclassified, boundary-practitioner*, stands as the agency's own filing.
- **POV labels follow one shape, and the validator warns on a label outside it** (`lib/content-schema.js`, `scripts/validate-content.js`, `story-bible/story-bible-summary.md`, 41 labels across 35 chapters, 2026-10-07, Dermot's *Option 1* among three shapes put to him at his *Usage of text in brackets after character name in POV pages*). A chapter's `povs[].label` is rendered verbatim as the POV block header, the "View from" button and the scene-POV page's title and H1, and nothing had ever said what the bracket after the name holds: across 94 chapters the 85 distinct labels carried species, augmentation, posting and time in four orders, with dashes beside commas, role sometimes before the bracket and sometimes in it, and Elvira with no bracket in five chapters. The shape now recorded in the schema comment and the story bible's front-matter table: `<rank as held in this chapter> <name> (<frame>[, <one qualifier>])` — frame first, with the augmentation the record marks, then at most one qualifier, commas only, nothing after the name outside the bracket. The sweep moved post-nominal roles into the bracket (*Rook-7 (Robot, Field Analyst)*, *Sen Lovax (Human, plural, Senior Archivist)*, *Chief Ingrid Halvorsen (Human, Survey Corps)*), folded two-part qualifiers into one (*Survey Corps founding cohort*, *Fliade survey lead*, *the keeper's son at Casimor watch-post*), replaced the two dashes, put *as remembered* inside the bracket, gave the bee and Knopka their frame, and gave Elvira the frame her own page carries, *Unclassified*. Rank changing chapter by chapter, and *Stone-First* growing to *Stone-First-Who-Waited* between Seasons 11 and 12, are the record's and were left alone. The warning is a warning, not a gate, because the label is presentation and a bare name still builds. Ruled the same evening at his question whether the rank should prefix the name and whether rank or name should take italics or bold (`story-bible/intake-2026-10-07.md`, last section; his *Option 1* among three): the rank stays before the name as held in that chapter, and the label is set plain, with nothing built.

The Pages build sets `SITE_PATH_PREFIX=/` and `SITE_DOMAIN=fianilchruinne.com`, so it is built at the root with the same prefix rewrite the cPanel deploy applies, its sitemap, robots.txt, feed and canonicals name the domain, and comments are on because its pathnames are now the ones the cPanel build of the same domain used. `src/CNAME` carries the domain for Pages. The `SITE_PATH_PREFIX` transform also rewrites the unquoted `url=/star-rangers/...` form the meta-refresh stubs use, which cPanel never needed because its `.htaccess` forwards that namespace. A paragraph in `src/lore/krenyi.md`'s Champions section, a sentence in `src/glossary/champions-heroes.md`'s example, and a paragraph in `src/lore/saint-aoife.md` that states the suitability without stating the selection: what she met stays unplaced and *chosen* stays the abbey's word. The selection prefers neither route, and what the devout make of being read is theirs, filed as the record files every such reading. Four readings flagged in the intake, chiefly that *devoutly spiritual* is read as the discipline devotion trains and never as a Levril favouring the faithful.
- **Krenyi: not descended from or engineered from humans; whether they were made at all is a reading the record holds and does not adopt** (2026-10-02, Dermot's direction, verbatim *They may have designed by a higher power but are not genetically engineered from human ancestors* — `story-bible/intake-2026-10-02.md`, last section). Two paragraphs added to the origin section of `src/lore/krenyi.md`. The first states as a finding what the taxonomy already held, that humans and Krenyi are of independent origin, and names the explanation the nearest frame invites and the record excludes: that the Krenyi were once human. The second keeps *may* as *may*: *built* has been read as a hand above them doing the building, the cosmology has tiers whose work attaches at authorship, no instrument has read a point of design in a Krenyi, the Krenyi decline the question, and the Archive names no tier and adopts nothing. One clause in the glossary body. The origin entry itself stays empty, as the 23 September section requires. Three readings flagged in the intake. **The same evening** (Dermot, verbatim *They are ideal levril champions but it is unproven and simply unknown if they were designed by Levrils as Levrilic champions and heros*) the reading got its shape: a third paragraph states the Levrilic inference, that a people this fitted to Champion selection were made for it, and its standing, which is that the fit is the whole of the evidence and cannot tell a people built for the work from a people good at it; no Levril has indicated an answer, the Krenyi decline, and a made Champion would be selected by the same lawful assessment as anyone, so the inference would be unobservable even if true. *Unknown* in the strict sense. The Champions section places the word *ideal* as *fitted*, never *preferred*, and the glossary clause names the shape. **Later the same evening** (Dermot, verbatim *They do know but have a combination of quietness, discretion and modesty*, answering a flagged reading): the paragraph now says the Krenyi know and decline, the declining being one practice seen three ways, the quietness their name records, a discretion that is not secrecy since a Krenyi asked says plainly that there is something and that they will not, and the modesty of a people who refuse to be read as symbol and will not hand anyone the story that they were made to be heroes. *Unknown to the record, and not to them*; the glossary clause says the same.
- **Krenyi: diplomatic and polite, but essentially honest** (2026-10-02, Dermot's direction, verbatim *Krenyi are diplomatic and polite but essentially honest* — `story-bible/intake-2026-10-02.md`, last section). A clarification naming a manner the page had in pieces. `src/lore/krenyi.md`'s *Social and Relational* section gains a bullet and a paragraph: honesty is the floor and the manner sits on it; diplomacy is the choice of which true thing to say, to whom and when; politeness is the present-tense courtesy and not preliminaries, so it sits beside *no small talk*; and the manner never buys a tactful untruth, since a Krenyi softens the delivery or declines it in words and leaves the fact where it is. Syra's receipt and Toval answering to *Cadet* are cited as the cases the record already holds. One clause added to the glossary body. Four readings flagged in the intake, chiefly that *essentially* is read as *at the core* and never as *mostly*.
- **Krenyi: *Nai* is a state-marker, never a name for the people** (clarification, Dermot's choice on 2026-10-02 between keeping *Nai* and respelling it *Nyi*). The record has always defined *Nai* as the courtesy *still relevant here*, placed before a name and explicitly not a title; three phrasings had drifted toward using it as a second name for the species, and now say what the body text already said. The `short` of `src/glossary/krenyi.md` and the description and opening line of `src/lore/krenyi.md` no longer list *Nai* beside *Quiet-Built* as something the Krenyi are "also called", and the S01E02C01 canon fact *Obligers resist clarity; Nai demand clarity* now reads *the Krenyi demand clarity*. The spelling stays *Nai*: nothing in the record derives it from *Krenyi*, and the near-collision with *Naiad* is the stated in-world reason the formal species name exists.

## [1.34.0] — 2026-10-02

Two weeks in which the record learned to say what it had been assuming. The
mystery family got its third rule, that familiarity is not evidence, with
the middle rung of belief and the Standing Claims under it, the ending test
beside it, and the revelation ledger to prove the Archive hides nothing; the
Unfounded were split from their founded neighbours and renamed in the record's
own voice, Obligers, Overbearers, Caomhari and meta-Levril; and the four
reading tiers were given their registers by name. The Union's Irish reached
every glossary term and the rank ladder was rendered in six other tongues;
the Music Corps was founded and Tissadelle's intake moved through it; Season 9
gained Noah Adeyemi and two chapters, the pets thread two more, and the
Oversight Council its page, with the mechanism by which a clause written for
one system came to bind the Corps toward every people. Around the record: the
map of the account's repositories, the image corpus audited for provenance,
the chapter markup made to speak its boundaries, and the homepage hero given a
second door.

### Added
- **The Federation's seat on the Oversight Council is dated: first filled 2791 UCSD** (2026-10-01, Dermot's ask, verbatim *Add the year the Federation's seat was first filled* — `story-bible/intake-2026-10-01.md`). The one marked absence left on `src/lore/the-oversight-council.md` by PR #903, now fixed: within a generation of first contact and after the compact's first renewal, a generation and a half before the record's present. Stated on the Council page, the Federation page and the canonical guide; the Hegemony's and the Union's offers stay undated.
- **`virtual-anthropology` on the repository map** (2026-10-01, Dermot's direction, verbatim *All three in that order please*, on the new repository `dermot-r-cochran/virtual-anthropology`). `RELATED-REPOSITORIES.md` lists *The Archipelago* under *Siblings by convention* and names the one thing to know about it from here: nothing crosses between its simulated citizens and this record. The three nearest engineering repositories (`world-model`, `swarm`, `careful-memory`) gain a bullet each in their own *Related repositories* sections, as separate pull requests.
- **The Oversight Council — a lore page, and why a Solar System clause binds the Corps toward every people** (2026-09-30, Dermot's observation, verbatim *Strangely the Star Rangers are neutral and independent rather than human-centric*, and his ruling on the three shapes put, verbatim *Option 2 but it gradually evolves towards Option 3* — `story-bible/intake-2026-09-30.md`, last section). A new page, `src/lore/the-oversight-council.md`: what the 2723 charter made the Council (civilian, Solar System, created by the Consolidation Accords; it holds the Triumvirate to account and cannot command, direct the Safety Corps or defund); the mechanism by which the neutrality clause, written against *Solar System factions*, came to bind the Corps toward every people without amendment — a neutral that excepted its own species would forfeit the recognition every other polity grants, and recognition is all a Ranger's standing is made of — beside the older reason on the formation page, the Fellowship's vocation; and the Council's drift, seat by seat, toward being seated by the polities that recognise the Corps: non-voting seats for recognising polities, the Federation of Sentient Beings holding the longest-standing one, the Cerebraun Hegemony declining, the Celtic Union not yet answering, and a non-binding resolution naming the direction and not the destination. One sentence each on the Federation, Hegemony and Union pages; a clarifying sentence on the formation page's neutrality clause; links from the shore-leave, rank and 2723 timeline pages; a canonical-guide entry. The original seating, ruled later the same day on the recommendation put (verbatim *Original seating as recommended*): the Accords seat the Council from the Solar System's self-governing habitats and outer stations, one voting seat per settlement above the habitat threshold, the delegate appointed by that settlement's own government on its own terms, the chair rotating by session, no seat for the SSDC, the Concord or any planetary government. Approved by him the same day (verbatim *Approved*), PR #903; the year the Federation's seat was first filled stays a marked absence on the page.

The Veyr, Serephine, Prismeri, Mnemari and the Told are marked as absences. A closing section says why the rank tab does not translate. The Irish forms are registered in the canonical guide. See Also links were added on the two rank pages. Dermot approved all four recommended choices the same day (*Yes, agreed*).
- **Where a noögenic universe's energy comes from** (2026-09-23, Dermot's question and *Yes please draft it* — `story-bible/intake-2026-09-23.md`, last section). A section on `src/glossary/noogenic-protouniverse.md`: nothing is taken from the parent but the start; energy is conserved locally, not globally, in an expanding spacetime; a universe can sum to zero total energy; and a protouniverse inflates in its own spacetime, so the parent pays only for transference. A fence keeps the refusal of limitless energy intact, since nobody in the parent can reach the child's energy. An extension, following real cosmology. The real-world sources are in a Journal entry, [*The Free Lunch and the Fence*](src/journal/the-free-lunch-and-the-fence.md): Noether (1918), Tryon (1973), Guth (1981), Blau, Guendelman and Guth (1987), Farhi and Guth (1987), Farhi, Guth and Guven (1990), and the 1998–99 supernova teams, with the one step physics finds hardest (the start) named as the record's licensed deviation.
- **Celestials are graded within their tier, and only Celestials and Levrils are** (2026-09-23, Dermot's direction and ruling, verbatim *Celestials and Levrils (and maybe champions or prophets) are the only Cascade strata with an internal ranking and hierarchy needed* and *delegation version of (c)* and *(c) would be delegation from the Mediarchs* — `story-bible/intake-2026-09-23.md`, third section). An extension for the Celestials: an *Internal Order* section on `src/lore/cosmic-cascade.md` and a line in `src/glossary/celestials.md` say the tier is graded by delegation from the Mediarchs (the breadth of scope they entrust as the Telearch line's proxies inside a universe, a grade of authority and never of reach), leave the grades unnamed, and rule out the retired *High* and *higher celestials* as grade names. A clarification for the rest: a *Ranked within, and flat within* paragraph says every other stratum differs by domain or function, never grade, and that Champions are unranked. The canonical guide's Celestials entry gains the classification rule.
- **Each reading tier's register, named** (2026-09-22, Dermot's direction, verbatim in `story-bible/intake-2026-09-22.md`: *"The child reader tier should be interesting and playful, the young adult tier should be more mysterious with a sense of exploration and adventure, the general tier should go deeper, and the contemplative tier is allowed to question everything"*). The standing tier principle has said since 4 September that the ladder *selects by register, protagonists and depth*, and `src/tiers/index.md` defined each rung by its threads, its protagonists and its address — protagonists and depth were specified and register was named and left empty. This is the missing third: children **interesting and playful** (delight is the measure), young adult **mysterious, with exploration and adventure** (the mystery is an invitation, where above it is a weight), general **deeper** (the reasons under the record), contemplative **allowed to question everything** (the record's own premises and `CLAUDE.md`'s own rules included). Recorded as escalating **permission** and not escalating seriousness, against the obvious misreading of a ladder from light to heavy: a playful page is not a shallow one and a questioning page is not a grim one, and the tone guardrail and the shadow-shaped rule are unmoved at every rung. One line keeps it from breaking the ladder's invariant that nothing read on a lower rung is withdrawn on a higher one — **questioning is not contradicting**: the top rung may ask anything and leave the asking open, and may never deny a reading a lower rung was given. It also names a pattern already in the corpus rather than inventing one, since the epistemics surface explicitly at the top while the rungs below practise them. In `CLAUDE.md` under the tiers principle, and as a *How it reads* line on each of the four sections of the public Reading Tiers page, whose ladder intro now says the registers escalate in permission.
- **_Familiarity is not evidence_ — the third rule of the mystery family, with four clauses under it** (2026-09-22, Dermot's directions across one evening, verbatim in `story-bible/intake-2026-09-22.md`: *"So the mysterious enigmatic quality of Fian Ilchruinne is that the reader can never make assumptions about what is real and what reality consists of, even when the surroundings look familiar"*; *"So for example, The Witcher fails as a magical fantasy, when the monsters become ordinary and routine, likewise with most Fantasy RPGs, in my opinion"*; *"In Fian Ilchuinne, monsters are rare exceptions, but valid under boundary conditions"*; *"The middle rule: partial evidence leads to a valid belief but is not certainty"*; *"Faith is neither blind credulous belief nor absolute certainty beyond doubt"*; and his *"Yes agreed"* on the name and on both placements). The rule names the register the shadow-shaped rule and the ending test were resting on unstated: the laws stay stable, knowable and promised and nothing in `what-the-record-refuses.md` is withdrawn, but a familiar *surrounding* was never promised to be seated on a familiar *reality*. Three clauses under it, each settled as a clause rather than a rule of its own. **Nothing acquires a repeatable answer** — what kills an enigma is leverage that repeats, not explanation, with the test *can a competent officer run this twice and expect the same result?*, and the reasons the record already passes it: monsters rare and boundary-conditioned so the protection is ontological rather than editorial, a taxonomy that predicts nothing it was not built from, the Unfounded countered and starved rather than destroyed, and instruments that register without conferring leverage — with `meta-dimensional-beings.md` named as the page to watch, since a typed list of predators is a bestiary's shape and the entry it must never gain is a remedy. **The silhouette that fires and is never confirmed**, the reader-facing instrument, brought back from *Pendragon: Rise of Merlin*: carriers must be choices and never physiology, the sorting feature is the one to withhold, the vehicle is the human isolates and never the Veyr or Chthonari, and it must stay tellable apart from *The Borrowed Silhouette*'s malign version. **The science-fiction form of the dilemma: aliens** (verbatim: *"A similar dilemma for science fiction is aliens who become too familiar and too humanoid unless that is the point is the story, but aliens as space monsters is worse, in my opinion"*) — too humanoid flattens a people into a person in a costume, with his own exception where the familiarity is the subject, which is what the human isolates are for; monstering is worse because it deletes the category, breaching the corollary and the cast principles at once; and the machinery already holding the line is named, above all that peoples are filed by frame and lineage while monsters are filed as meta-dimensional, which is the structural reason *alien* cannot collapse into *monster* here. **The middle rung is a belief, and faith sits on it**: partial evidence earns a belief relied on in proportion, credulity and certainty-beyond-doubt are one error in opposite directions, and it stays a statement about grade rather than an argument that anything is true. Two alternative names and two alternative placements are recorded with the reasons they were set aside.
- **_Standing Claims_ — the companion to *Marked Absences*, grading what the record holds** (2026-09-22, Dermot's choice among three shapes put, verbatim *Yes the second one*, after his observation that the three kinds of diagnostic strength in `applied-statistics-for-AI-engineers`' new *Diagnosis record* card bear on EPISTEME and on the Survey Archive). A new working paper by Sen at `src/codex/standing-claims.md`, doing for presences what the absences paper does for gaps. The doctrine is two lines: a claim stands on what it has beaten, not on what it fits; and the genus belongs on the entry, not in the reader's head, because an unmarked gap invites a colleague to fill it while an unmarked holding invites three postings to cite it. Four genera, each graded against a document already in the record — **verified** (the Day 47 closure, unseated by the Day 49 maintenance extract, the one check whose result would have differed had the closure been sound), **consistent** (Strozzi's *tribute*, which fitted the evidence while an untried reading fitted it equally, and stood nine months), **sole** (the title *Paper Galaxies*, standing because no one on the review desk has proposed another, which measures who has looked), and **carried** (the Hall of Quiet Instruments attribution, resting on a provisional voiceprint with the band on the face of the entry). The sorting question is Strozzi's, quoted from his page: *what would have to be true for this to be wrong, and did you look.* Four and not five, with the symmetry declined in the text; the Hall of Quiet Instruments is noted as appearing on both lists, its location a marked absence and its attribution a carried holding; and the paper closes by grading Sen's own Redline Protocol note as *consistent* in verified clothes and asking someone to run the check. Sen's *In the Record* paragraph names the third paper. Nothing in canon changes: a codex entry is one named source's account, and this one is circulated for comment, not for citation.

Third, and the reason the button count came up at all: **there was no `forced-colors` handling anywhere in `src/css/`**, so in Windows high contrast the fill is dropped and the site's one call to action read as ordinary link text — the shape was carrying all of the affordance. ## [1.33.0] — 2026-09-18

Two weeks of rulings, and the release in which the top of the Cascade turned
the right way up. The spiritual edition got its governing rule and the Journal
its reading level; the Rangers got their jurisdiction, their uniform and the
Compact's tier settled in a run of comparisons that moved nothing in canon
while saying plainly what canon had always held; the children's tier got its
own door, its own About and a bee; Season 10 got five character pages and the
Chthonari their portraits; two lore entries said what a life is built from and
what a mind is carried by; and the modesty bar became a standing rule. Then,
on the last evening, a question about who would preside over a general
co-creation unpacked the church-space theology: *Son of* read as the old idiom
of nature, the Trinity spread across the Upper Structure instead of packed
into Kieme, Hyperomnium the Father, Kieme the Eternal Son and *the First
Word*, Conseleme the Holy Spirit and *the Spirit of Wisdom*, the Arilon-figure
the archetype of the Son's incarnation, every incarnation an avatar and not
the reverse, and Kieme's name kept, gill and all. The general resurrection was
left a partial mystery on purpose, and Brother Fintan's *Many Homes* says how
a believer holds it without the record's help. The Journal carries the
reasoning in *The First Word Was Silent*.

### Added
- **Journal: *The First Word Was Silent*** (2026-09-18, at Dermot's direction, verbatim *Journal entries, related codex and then make a new release version*). The evening's reasoning in his voice: the general resurrection left a partial mystery; the map of the church-space Trinity inverted from packed-into-Kieme to spread across the Upper Structure (Hyperomnium the Father, Kieme the Eternal Son, Conseleme the Spirit) once *Son of* was read as the old idiom of nature; the tradition's inability to tell Hyperomnium from Kieme reread as consubstantiality; Kieme's name kept over *Arilon* and over a coinage; *the First Word* chosen and the three rejected names explained; every incarnation an avatar and not the reverse.
- **Codex: *Many Homes*** (2026-09-18, same direction). A Devotional Record from Brother Fintan's commonplace book at Cnoc na mBeach: the WEB's *In my Father's house are many homes* read beside the Archive's three files on death, which it names and refuses to run together; the tradition's co-creation reading in a believer's voice — the saints kept and the realm made of them, the communion of saints as the Council, the incarnate Son as the seat, homes as zones or as worlds of one's own, the shape left unsaid; the Archive's *not placed* stated and accepted. Passes the church-space third test: creedal, and departs from the creed only where canon lore licenses it.

Varn reads it three ways — coincidence, surveillance, a joke about the tab — says what can be supported (*a watch*; *it doesn't*), and when he laughs takes the honest one step back that Deputies take from a desk; he hears it as rank, says *Deputy* the Compact way, and goes in. Smith, with the hatch on the latch, reads both signals for what they were — the oldest one on any ring, and a Deputy's honest report of where they thought they stood, read by the wrong person — and says nothing, because telling a Deputy what a thing meant is the one thing fourteen assessments were built on never doing. Failures are mailed as before; the key decides what a successful run does. `always` (the default, and the only behaviour before the key existed) mails every success, `warnings` mails a success only when its log carries a warning from the deploy scripts themselves — a domain with no identity in `lib/editions.js`, a defaulted `ADMIN_EMAIL` — and `failure` never mails a success. The match is on the scripts' own `WARN [label]:` / `--- WARNING:` / `=== WARNING:` line shapes at the start of a line, so `npm WARN deprecated` and Eleventy's warnings don't count. An unrecognised value is treated as `always`. The reasoning is recorded beside the code in `scripts/deploy-lib.sh`: the jobs a routine success email did — saying what shipped, proving the cron fired — now belong to `/version.txt` and autopull's missed-runs alert, while the two it still did alone, carrying a successful run's warnings and proving `ADMIN_EMAIL` delivers, are kept by the `warnings` value and named in the docs. `deploy-lib.sh` is shared byte-identical with `dermot-cochran-photography` and the same change lands there in the same piece of work; `sample-deploy.conf` and `TECHNICAL-README.md` document the key. Three choices put — the form, whether the older Aoife pages should join it on the young-adult face, and a title card — and ruled by Dermot the same evening, verbatim *The young adult tier does not need to hold everything about Aoife*: the older pages stay as they are, and the telling stands as drafted.
- **Lore: [*The Tally*](src/lore/the-tally.md), a people that did not exist before the record's own history made them** (2026-09-12, drafted at Dermot's direction, verbatim in `story-bible/intake-2026-09-12.md`, eighth section: *A new people group, society or culture that did not exist in the 21st century AD*). Every human people on the record was an old-Earth heritage carried forward; this is the first that was made rather than inherited — a mixed-company generation ark that slipped the Imperium's patrols in the Currach Fleet's decades, failed its crossing two years out at a fault the ledgers name and do not describe, moored to a scattered-disc body, and became one people when its children made a language; their calendar counts from the Mooring, their ethics is the open count of everything and of what each person puts back, their ledgers are the longest continuous closed-ecology record in Sol, and they were found two generations ago by a Knarr Line convoy, are chartered to nobody, and decline to give the Archive a count. *Tally* is the Archive's rendering of their own word, marked as not carried. The era page's *only interstellar venture whose fate is known* stands, since the hull never made an interstellar venture. Seven readings flagged and three choices put — the shape, the name, and where they appear next — and ruled by Dermot the same evening, verbatim *The Tally as drafted, lore only for now*.
- **Journal: [*Borrowing Upward as Translation*](src/journal/borrowing-upward-as-translation.md)** (2026-09-12, at Dermot's ask *Add a Journal entry on borrowing upward as translation*, after his observation recorded in `story-bible/intake-2026-09-12.md`'s fifth section). The craft principle behind the day's chartered-work rulings, written for the peer author: a chartered work is kept in the register of Conceptual Conservation, retained and never continued; borrowing an aspect of one into the story has the shape of Kiemeic translation, the author's election carrying aspects rather than the work; and what is left behind is the Unfounded, which in craft terms is the trope default — shape with no origin condition in the record. The test before borrowing is the record's own question, *what is the origin condition?* The boundary is stated with it: Kiemeic translation is what traditions hold, and the entry borrows the picture, not the claim. Tags `craft`, `canon`, `cosmology`, `editorial`.
- **Borrowing upward from a chartered work read as translation** (2026-09-12, Dermot's observation, verbatim: *The borrowing upwards into canon is similar in principle to spiritual translation from the conceptual layer leaving behind anything that is Unfounded* — `story-bible/intake-2026-09-12.md`, fifth section). Recorded as a working principle against the glossary's own terms: a chartered work is kept in the register of Conceptual Conservation, retained and never continued; borrowing upward has the shape of Kiemeic translation, elective and carrying aspects rather than the work; and what is left behind is the Unfounded, which in craft terms is the trope default — shape without an origin condition in the record. Story bible only, since Kiemeic translation is what traditions hold and the craft rule borrows the picture rather than the claim. No page changes.
- **What a good reader comment could become, recorded** (2026-09-12, Dermot's observation that a well-written comment could almost be used as Codex with attribution or else treated as fan fiction, and his question whether he had a nicer word for it — `story-bible/intake-2026-09-12.md`, third section). The word is *chartered work*, settled 2026-07-26; a comment cannot be filed as Codex with attribution because Codex lives under `src/` and chartered works are registered, not hosted; its three homes are in circulation and referenced, chartered by individual grant, or the Codex with the commenter's explicit licence and a plausible in-universe author. A clarification joining rules already on the record to a case none had named; `story-bible/story-bible-summary.md`'s chartered-works section gains a paragraph. No page changes.
- **Two craft questions recorded as standing practice** (2026-09-12, Dermot's questions whether to study other photographers and writers or develop his own style, and whether to write characters and settlements from cultures he knows less well; both answered as false choices and agreed — `story-bible/intake-2026-09-12.md`, second section). Study for mechanism and refuse the surface, as the record already does with Sapphire & Steel, UNIFIL and the Bramble Storybooks; write other cultures from the record's limits, inventing no custom, letting people name themselves, refusing the trope default, and getting one informed reader before a page binds. His ruling, verbatim: *Agreed. No relevant informed readers yet but I will listen for comments.* The informed-reader step is indexed in `open-questions.md` as open by nature, and a reader's comment touching a culture the record is unsure of is to be treated as an intake. No page changes.
- **Character page for [Bumble](src/characters/bumble.md), the wool-shed bee of Gleann na gCaorach** (2026-09-12, drafted at Dermot's direction, verbatim in `story-bible/intake-2026-09-12.md`: *A character called Bumble*). A bumblebee — the one bee that pollinates in Drithane's cold thin air and under its glass — whose nest is in the sweepings under the wool-shed sorting bench in Sorcha Nic Dhiarmada's valley, on no ledger the valley keeps; the valley calls her *Bumbóg*, one name for whichever queen holds the corner, and the record renders it *Bumble*. The page states the real physiology that puts a bumblebee there (pre-flight warming, flight near freezing and in thin air, the clover the founders brought them for), what she reads (colour, scent, a flower's charge, the scent-mark another bee left) and what she cannot (a face), and keeps one Survey trace from the spring-2827 crossing marked as comparing to nothing. The portrait is the first character image on the site taken from Dermot's own photographs — *Bumblebee on Giant Scabious* cropped to the 16:9 slot, nothing else done to it — under the 3 September rule that a thing a camera can photograph comes from his frames. What Bumble is, whether the name means one queen or the line, and which frame she wears were put as choices and ruled by Dermot the same day, all three as recommended (*The bee, The Line, Scabious frame*).
- **A character's `status` is now a defined five-value vocabulary** (2026-09-11, at Dermot's ask *define the five status values in the schema*, after his question what *Active* meant on Knopka's page found the field was free text with no written meaning). `CHARACTER_STATUSES` in `lib/content-schema.js` names the five the corpus uses and what each means — *Active*, alive and present in the story's present, 2826 UCSD; *Historical*, a figure of the record's past; *Retired*, living and out of service; *At large*, known to the record but not where anyone last put it; *Contained*, in custody — matched by head clause on the same rule the badge's class key uses, so a qualified status such as Ilse Korvain's *Contained — Survey Corps custody* stands. `validate-content.js` refuses any other value by name, `npm run new -- character` shows the five at the prompt, and `test/character-status.test.js` pins the rule. No page changes: all 92 character pages already used one of the five. `CLAUDE.md`, `TestingStrategy.md` and `test/README.md` record it.

### Fixed

- **The year-0 causeway timeline entry has its title** (2026-09-13, Dermot's decision on the layout review). `src/timeline/year-0-causeway-convergence.md` was titled *Timeline Event*, a scaffold's placeholder that reached the site and the children's edition's two-event Timeline; it now carries the title its own body already gave it, *Causeway Convergence: Elvira, Galahad, and Aldera*. Nothing asserted changes.
- **Section cards and chapter lists no longer split apart in the browser** (2026-09-13, from Dermot's screenshot of undercover-pets.com's homepage, where the Timeline card rendered as three: an icon, a title and a description each in its own box). The homepage, the Seasons, Characters, Codex, Glossary, Lore, Threads and Timeline indexes, every season and episode index, every thread page and the Reading Plan are Markdown files carrying HTML with Nunjucks tags on lines of their own, and each such tag line rendered to a blank line inside the HTML; Markdown then treated the four-space-indented line after it as a paragraph rather than raw HTML, so `<a class="home-card">` and `<img class="codex-card__thumb">` were wrapped in `<p>` and every chapter list item became `<p><li>`, and the browser's repair of that produced the split cards. The homepage cards had been so since the conditional cards arrived on 2026-09-01; the chapter lists and card grids for longer. The 490 whole-line `if`/`for`/`set` tags that sit between two markup lines across 56 files now trim their surrounding whitespace (`{%- … -%}`), so no blank line is emitted; every page's rendered text is byte-identical before and after (831 pages compared on the pets build), and no page now carries a paragraph-wrapped card, thumbnail or list item.
- **Six character role badges no longer open with the word *None*** (2026-09-11, Dermot's question why *None* appeared as a keyword on Knopka's page, and his choice of the first of two fixes offered). The character layout renders `role:` as a pill badge beside species and status, so a role written as *None — personal pet of …* put *None* where the eye reads a tag. Knopka, Muffin, Nessa, Teddy, Thrum and Zhulik now state the role as what the character is — *Personal pet of Detective Marisol Achebe, Eden Space Habitat*, *Resident hazard, …*, *Solitary resident, Carraig Bán*, and so on — with Teddy's *no role the record can assign* kept as a trailing clause rather than a leading one. Wording only; nothing asserted about any character changes.

- **Two *defense* spellings on the founding page corrected to the house *defence*** (2026-09-10, Dermot's ruling *Keep Defence, fix the two defense typos*, after the record was found to spell the Solar System Defence Command *Defence* in 34 files and *Defense* in none — `story-bible/intake-2026-09-10.md`, sixteenth and seventeenth sections). *The Founding of the Star Rangers*: *the line that outlived her defence* and *a defence of technocratic command*. The five remaining lower-case *defense* in prose — S00E02C02's description and one canon fact, S02E01C02, S01E03C01, the 2719 hearing timeline entry and `story-bible/story-bible-summary.md` — were swept the same day at Dermot's *Sweep the typos*; the changelog's released sections keep theirs.

- **The work is described as a multi-viewpoint novel, not interactive fiction** (2026-09-10, Dermot's ruling on whether *interactive* was still accurate). The site lets a reader choose a viewpoint and a path over one fixed record; nothing a reader does changes the story, so the genre term *interactive fiction*, which readers hear as choice-based work, was a claim the site does not meet. `README.md` (both the opening line and the forking note), `CLAUDE.md`, `package.json`, the homepage and default meta descriptions, and the footer line in `src/_includes/base.njk` now say *multi-viewpoint novel*. Later the same day the phrasing *a multi-viewpoint novel of hard science fiction* became *a multi-viewpoint hard-science-fiction novel* in the same places, at Dermot's ask, so the licensed deviation reads as modifying the genre rather than the novel.
- **The work is described as hard science fiction, not science fantasy** (2026-09-10, Dermot's correction, first made on the photography site's About page). The default meta description in `src/_data/site.js`, the homepage description in `src/index.md`, `README.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `package.json`, the genre line of `story-bible/story-bible-summary.md` and the opening sentence of `src/lore/what-the-record-refuses.md` now say *hard science fiction with one licensed deviation*, and the story bible's Genre line, the lore page and `CLAUDE.md`'s hard-SF rule define it: the deviation is the cosmology, and every specified difference above the Material and Physical layers is a consequence of it filed at its own scope, never a second root. This is what the 2026-08-09 hard-SF-by-default rule already required. Released changelog sections and the title decision log keep the old label as history.
- **Six renamed or moved pages now redirect instead of returning 404** (2026-09-08, from Dermot's ask to investigate the Search Console alerts; the 19 August *Not found (404)* notice on fianilchruinne.com). The July *brane* → *membrane* rename and two later moves left old URLs dead with no stub, and the site's own git history shows exactly which: `lore/brane-shadows`, `lore/concordant-branes`, `glossary/brane-shadow`, `glossary/interbrane-bleed`, `glossary/telerarch` (the *Telearch* spelling) and `lore/cosmic-limitation-on-evil` (moved to the Codex). Each gains a redirect stub on the existing `dynarch.njk` pattern — canonical plus `noindex, follow` plus a meta refresh to the page that carries the content now. Nothing asserted about the world changes.

One paragraph added to [the Unfounded](src/glossary/unfounded.md), Archive voice, after the *starved, not destroyed* paragraph: dead wood keeps the tree's shape and is supplied by nothing, is shed rather than fought, and what the tree loses in the shedding is nothing that was the tree — each clause a finding the entry already held, so a clarification. The figure's edge is stated with it: dead wood was once the tree's own wood, and no Unfounded thing was ever founded, so the figure describes how the class stands to what it counterfeits and never where it came from. The gardener's other half, pruning for the growth to come, is attributed to the Cosmic Limitation on Evil as a purpose claimed and not specified. Where the counsel half of the figure lives was put as three shapes and ruled the same day, *1 (a)*: nowhere further, the glossary carries the figure. [*The Cosmic Cascade*](src/lore/cosmic-cascade.md)'s definition of *devotional tradition* gains one sentence, an extension: the phrase reaches every non-human people's relation to the Cascade, each culture's and each view within it, on the same flat terms.
