Later the same day (seventh section) Dermot put the Liaison Corps as a possible exception, noting that Catherine Galen wears a uniform; the section now carries the recommended shape pending his confirmation — a resident Planetary Representative wears the uniform when acting for the Corps and lives out of it otherwise, a qualification of posting rather than corps, while a liaison at a Corps posting such as Galen's gate is in uniform on duty. Confirmed the same day (*Option A for planetary reps*).

- **The Compact sets no uniform requirement on its bureaus; Five-O is uniformed** (2026-09-10, Dermot's directions, verbatim: *local habitat detectives have no uniform requirements and may be undercover* and *Five-O does have uniforms unlike its Hawaiian namesake* — `story-bible/intake-2026-09-10.md`, ninth and tenth sections). *The Orbital Habitats Compact* gains a sentence at the Detective Superintendent line — no Compact-level uniform requirement; within a bureau the garment follows the role and the case, Eden the worked example — and a sentence in the Five-O paragraph making it the one uniformed unit across the five habitats, unlike the bureaus and unlike the old series its name nods at; the uniform's design is not stated. *The Eden Bureau Uniform* gains a sentence placing its 19 August rule as a working rule of role and case under no Compact requirement. The reading was ruled the same day (*local uniform depends on role and case*, thirteenth section), which makes the 19 August page a clarification rather than a reversal. `story-bible/image-prompts.md`'s Calloway note gains a status line, since its *no Compact uniform in canon* has been overtaken for the bureau and for Five-O.

- **The militaries are the polities'** (2026-09-10, Dermot's direction, verbatim: *Solar System Compact, Federation of Sentient Beings are Cerebraun Hegemony all have their own military. Celtic Union has a mostly ceremonial military.* — `story-bible/intake-2026-09-10.md`, eleventh section). The complement of the branch rule: *Rank and the Chain of Command* gains a sentence after *neither an army nor a navy* saying where the militaries are; *The Federation of Sentient Beings* gains a paragraph — a military of its own, held as contingents contributed by member worlds under an agreed mandate with an appointed commander and no standing force, posted for interposition rather than conquest, after Dermot's same-day ruling *The Federation military is a bit like UNIFIL*; *The Cerebraun Hegemony* gains a sentence; *The Celtic Union of Planets* gains a sentence beside its declined SSDC integration, with the Highland Guard's honour escort as the visible face of a mostly ceremonial force. *Solar System Compact* was confirmed the same day as the Solar System Concord, whose framework's military is the Solar System Defence Command.

- **Two comparisons filed, nothing in canon moved** (2026-09-10, at Dermot's ask — `story-bible/intake-2026-09-10.md`, second and third sections). *Vigil* (BBC, 2021) against the record: its engine is a civilian detective inside a military service that cannot credibly police itself, and the record inverts every term — the Rangers are not military, the Provost track investigates its own credibly by design, and jurisdiction runs the other way; the one place the seam is real, an offence aboard a Ranger vessel docked at a self-governing habitat, is put to Dermot as three shapes. The French Gendarmerie against Orbital Five-O: position, dual chain and handover friction match; military status and a territorial beat do not, and are named as the things not to borrow; Dermot ruled the same day that *Five-O borrows nothing from the Gendarmerie*, and separately that Five-O is uniformed; who directs a Five-O inquiry stays a marked absence.

- **The Orbital Habitats Compact: Five-O as the intermediate tier** (2026-09-08, Dermot's direction *Five-O intermediate between the Star Rangers and the local detective bureau of each habitat*, verbatim in `story-bible/intake-2026-09-08.md`, twenty-fourth section). One paragraph after *not one metre further* on [The Orbital Habitats Compact](src/lore/orbital-habitats-compact.md): a habitat bureau sends a case that runs past its edge up to Five-O; Five-O, on the Governor's authority and with a former Survey Corps officer at its head, is the tier that recognises when a case has stopped being a Compact matter and issues the invitation; *the bureaus do not call the Rangers, and the Rangers do not come uncalled*. An extension of *The Gap the Chain Has*; the standing mysteries rule in `CLAUDE.md` gains the same three rungs. Two readings put as choices and **approved by Dermot the same evening** (*Approved*; the stacked PR #761 was closed when its base merged and reopened against main as #763).

- **Environmental Technology Design: embodiment follows the job, and a drone is the exception** (2026-09-08, Dermot's ruling *most AI systems and robots are not drones unless there is a very good reason why a drone would be needed*, verbatim in `story-bible/intake-2026-09-08.md`, fourth section). An extension of the *AI: Present, Never Intrusive* section of [Environmental Technology Design](src/lore/environmental-technology-design.md): most lawful systems have no body of their own, the ones that do have the body the work needs, and a small free-flying machine appears only where a fixed system could not do the job — a station's outside, an ocean floor, a hull that berths on a schedule — with the record's existing drones checked against that bound and standing. The biosphere-world clause *drones that hover at the edge of notice* is the one line that does not pass on its own, and is put to Dermot as a choice rather than edited. **Ruled the same day — option 1, a clarification:** the clause is gone, the upkeep on a biosphere world is done by *the ground systems ... from where they already stand*, and the paragraph now ends *nothing announces itself as a machine, and nothing hovers*.

### Added

- **Codex entry [Xenolinguistics Handbook: The Ten Failures](src/codex/xenolinguistics-handbook-failure-modes.md)**, the Branch school's first-year chapter on how translation goes wrong, revised edition 2830 UCSD (2026-09-08, at Dermot's word — *Xenolinguistics Handbook as a public page* — taking the second reading of his line *alien linguistic patterns and common failure modes for translation*; `story-bible/intake-2026-09-08.md`, seventeenth and twenty-seventh sections). The public face of `story-bible/language-design.md`, in the teaching staff's own voice: the division of labour first (the machine aligns, the linguist decides and owns the error), then the one thing two peoples can establish before a word (arithmetic, regime-wide — the Meridian tell), then ten named failures each with what it looks like, the case the school teaches it from and the rule that closes it — filed as noise (Cirrane, Meridian); the correct transcript and the wrong meeting (the Cerebraun second channel); answering the body instead of the person (Ilveth blushes, Ovruhn comfort); an economy read as a temperament (Ilveth thrift, Krenyi stillness, the three-part answer filed as evasion for a decade); the courtesy mistaken for the fact (Nerath's *water*, Cirrane and Freyari); the question that does not translate (the Ollune alarm, the Undersong, the rendering politely declined); naming by resemblance (*the hybrid people*); confidence entered as certainty (Krilzat filed at low confidence, the Abbess's patience); the part-translated page (contact-marking a page cannot carry); the rendered telling (no invented phonology) — and the closing: not one is a failure of hearing, every one is a failure of deciding. Every case is on a published page and cited to it; the Fliade survey is not cited and the Told are not named. Canon-for-its-author. Title card from `make-codex-cover.ps1`. Four readings put as choices and **approved by Dermot the same evening** (*Approved*, PR #766).
- **Codex entry [Nothing Crossed](src/codex/nothing-crossed.md)**, a Gravimetry Desk working paper by Surveyor Maren Halloran, filed 2832 UCSD (2026-09-08, at Dermot's word — *Option 2 is also useful* — on the second reading of his line *Several unsolved mysteries. Not murders, just shadows*; `story-bible/intake-2026-09-08.md`, sixteenth and twenty-third sections). The desk's casebook of Membrane Shadows it cannot close, kept on Sen's doctrine — mark the absence, do not explain it — in the Archivist's own kinds: the Chamber Window (unsettled; the lore entry's illustration), the Causeway Form (live; a recurring interruption in the water at the 3:7 coupling's windows), the Bulkhead Load (unsettled; a body's worth of gravity leaning on a sealed compartment's wall, and the desk's own three readings of whether it was done on purpose), the Watch Officer's Brother (provisional; the record's alternate-double position applied without pleasure), and the Bright One in the Valley on Tír na nÓg (unverifiable; the benevolent kind, on the list with the desk's own rule broken in plain sight so the casebook does not teach the dark-silhouette error). The rule for the list is the instrument, never the eye; the Dock Seven figures of 2831 are kept off it because they registered as discharge; and the desk answers the question it keeps being asked — whether any file is an incident with a party to it — with *nothing crossed, and nothing on this side did anything*. Canon-for-its-author; it settles nothing the lore leaves open, including the two-way-signalling question, and names no Fliade case, since that season's shadows are its own. Title card from `make-codex-cover.ps1`. Five readings put as choices and **approved by Dermot the same evening** (*Approved*, PR #760).
- **The Name — a section on [The Founding of the Star Rangers](src/lore/formation-of-star-rangers.md)** (2026-09-08, at Dermot's ask — *Yes please* — after his observation that no page explains the corps' name, verbatim in `story-bible/intake-2026-09-08.md`, twenty-second section). The Terran heritage offers two rangers, the frontier lawman and the warden of a bounded ground, and the charter chooses the second without being asked: no jurisdiction on planets or large habitats, entry by invitation, no transformation of any world bearing life, a remit at the edge of what is known and the survey as the instrument. The ranks say the same from inside — the first command posting is a Starwarden, an Archwarden answers for a vessel, and the word was inherited from the Subsea Cable Warden Programme and the Fellowship's watch — so a ranger is a warden of ground too large to stand on. The Archive files the lawman reading as the history of a word and declines it as a description of the corps. The command-hierarchy page's Starwarden entry now points to the section. Composes with the same evening's rulings that mysteries are shadow-shaped and that the guns-and-spaceships and space-western registers are refused. Asserts nothing new about the charter; every fact is on the page already. Amended twice at his lines before merge — the knight analogy (*words outlive the work that named them*) and the one exception, the Frontier Corps, which alone takes on the armed ranger's role and only in dire need — and **approved by Dermot the same evening** (*Approved*, PR #758).
- **Chapters S11E01C05 — [*Theirs to Move*](src/seasons/s11/e01/s11e01c05.md) — and S11E02C03 — [*Something Happened*](src/seasons/s11/e02/s11e02c03.md)**, the convergence of *Below the Roof*, drafted as a pair (2026-09-08, at Dermot's ask in the order agreed in the tenth section of `story-bible/intake-2026-09-08.md`; fifteenth section). *One act, two records*, as ruled 7 September. From above: Nakagawa has slept on it and the answer is a stone of the planet's own, set down first, by one person, because a knock is one person at a door; Aravena carries it through the squeeze and comes out to find an adult standing on the line, in the open, at arm's length, that does not withdraw; kneels anyway, sets the stone on the line, steps back, says a thing the log does not carry, and is answered by the shift of a rock; the log says *something happened*, the count says sixty-three shifts on which nothing had, and the standing order becomes *knock every time*. From below: Stone-First is on the line when the light comes through at the start of a working time; the smallest of the up-people sets a stone down late, kneeling, and theirs — which is how the youngest moved one the first time, and was forgiven — and says a thing that rises, which Stone-First does not know and the telling does not say; Stone-First answers the only way the Told answer a stone, by moving one; the warm hears it, Went-Round says *they asked* and Stone-First says *they began*, and a name grows on the rule that a truer thing said later is added: **Stone-First-Who-Waited**. The count stops, because the thing counted stopped being nothing. Neither side records what was said; neither crosses the line; every telling begins with a stone, and this one has two. Stone-First's, Went-Round's, Teddy's, Aravena's and Nakagawa's pages, the glossary, both episode indexes, the treatment and the thread registry comment updated. The season's two strands are complete: five chapters below, three above. Eight readings put as choices in the intake and **approved by Dermot the same evening** (*Approved*, PR #751).
- **Chapter S11E02C02 — [*Nothing Happened*](src/seasons/s11/e02/s11e02c02.md)**, the second chapter of *Below the Roof*'s survey-side strand (2026-09-08, drafted at Dermot's ask; `story-bible/intake-2026-09-08.md`, fourteenth section, with his ruling *Pandoids are wary of shadows* in the thirteenth). The count: sixty shifts of *nothing happened* in Aravena's voice, and under it, in the survey lead's hand, the number. Nakagawa lays two years of boulder shifts in a row and sees that the adults announce themselves on every arrival and the party has never once done the same; hears Aravena's question on the unit's sound channel every shift and says nothing. Egede's imager shows the adults withdrawing from the light's moving shadow before the light itself, and Nakagawa reads it: the fungus-light has no cycle and no source that moves, nothing below the roof ever moved a shadow until the party's light, *I would be wary of it too*. Egede argues for answering the courtesy with a gift and is refused on the surface rule — *a thing left at the line is a thing left*. Asked at last, Aravena gives the third reading: *like a thing at a door*, and the boulders are the knock, and the party has been walking in for two years without knocking. *Not today*; written down; the count gains its first line. Two heads, four scenes, four blocks. Commits the story to the count, to the sound channel, to the pattern of announcement and withdrawal, to the shadow reading as filed, to the gift refused, to the third reading given and to *not today*. Aravena's and Nakagawa's pages, the Episode 2 index and the thread registry comment updated; the shadow ruling and its two readings added to `mind-design.md`'s Pandoid section. Five readings put as choices in the intake and **approved by Dermot the same evening** (*Approved*, PR #750).
- **Chapter S11E02C01 — [*Eleven Minutes*](src/seasons/s11/e02/s11e02c01.md)**, the first chapter of *Below the Roof*'s survey-side strand, with character pages for [Aravena](src/characters/aravena.md) and [Hesper Nakagawa](src/characters/nakagawa.md) and an Episode 2 index (2026-09-08, drafted at Dermot's ask — *Yes please* to the order put in the tenth section of `story-bible/intake-2026-09-08.md`; twelfth section). Strand B, from inside, in the children's band: Aravena, the smallest of the three, carries the unit, sets it at the junction and tells it the log; Nakagawa reads the thermal channel that evening — a warm upright profile at the edge of the working light for eleven minutes, and nobody looked up — and strikes *young* from the entry; some shifts later the unit is found standing on the line where the party's own feet stopped, and its log, read on the spot, says it was carried, and woke, and was held, and slept. Egede files *returned*, Nakagawa files *a line drawn*, neither is chosen, the light is swung once into the dark, the unit is lifted, and the standing order follows: the log says, every shift, that nothing happened. Last up the passage, Aravena turns round and asks the dark *was that all right?* — of the one who carried it — and has asked it every working time since. Two heads, four scenes, five blocks. Commits the story to the party's three by name, to why the tracks stop at the line (*far enough*), to the unit's log as the party read it, to the two readings and the third not given, to the standing order, and to what is asked of the dark and of whom. Episode 2 is the survey side entire, as Episode 1 is the deep side: a child who reads one episode has one whole strand. Teddy's page, the Reading Tiers page and the thread registry comment updated. Seven readings put as choices in the intake and **approved by Dermot the same evening** (*Approved*, PR #749).
- **Chapter S11E01C04 — [*Waiting to Be Asked*](src/seasons/s11/e01/s11e01c04.md)**, the fourth chapter of *Below the Roof* (2026-09-08, drafted at Dermot's ask after he ruled Strand A to five chapters — *A forth and fifth chapter* — `story-bible/intake-2026-09-08.md`, tenth and eleventh sections). The waiting. Stone-First keeps the line on every time, and the light does not come, but the sound does: at the end of each working time the up-people's rising sound comes down the long passage and through the squeeze and is heard on the line, and Stone-First does not answer it, because a thing answered that was not asked of you is interrupted, not answered — and begins, without meaning to, to count. Below, Carried-It-Sleeping keeps the small ones from the squeeze and finds *when you fit* is not a reason; a small one goes up anyway, having moved a stone first, and Carried-It-Sleeping does the hardest thing there is below the roof, which is nothing. The first person to stand beside Stone-First on the line is that small one, through one asking of the dark (*what are you doing?* — *being here* — *is that all?* — *it is the whole of it*), and is sent down to tell it: a telling that is the small one's own and names nobody, because it is about somebody else. Went-Round reads the waiting from the far side of the amber — *everybody below the roof keeping manners at everybody else* — and Stone-First works out that waiting to be asked is the same shape as waiting to be told, except that the stone is theirs to move. Two heads, five scenes, six blocks in the children's band. Commits the story to the sound carrying to the line, to why it is not answered, to the count, to a small one keeping the manners the youngest once did not, to the telling that gives no name, and to the Told expecting the asking, if it comes, to begin with a stone. Stone-First's, Went-Round's and the glossary's pages, the episode index, the Reading Tiers page and the thread registry comment updated. Six readings put as choices in the intake and **approved by Dermot the same evening** (*Approved*, PR #748).
- **Lore entries now link to each other wherever one names another** (2026-09-07, the glossary treatment of the same day applied to `src/lore/`). The lore was already heavily hand-linked, so the sweep found 91 first mentions of another lore entry's title left as plain text in 52 entries — Mars in nine, the Archewright and the Levrils in nine between them, the three predecessor institutions in the corps histories — and each is now a link to the lore page it names, one per target at its earliest mention. `scripts/link-glossary-terms.js` now covers both sections (`--section glossary|lore` to restrict), each linked within itself; the shared logic gained three rules the lore needed — the head of a *Head: Subtitle* title counts as the title, a lower-case parenthetical is a gloss rather than a name (*the Held* is not linked inside *the Held Roles*), and a title followed by a space and a capital is the head of a longer proper noun and passed over (*Quantum Space Harmonic Wave* is not a mention of *Quantum Space Harmonics*) — plus a one-entry list of phrases that contain a title without being it (*New Venice*). An entry that already links the other section's page of the same slug is left alone. Nothing asserted about the world changes.
- **Glossary entries now link to each other wherever one names another** (2026-09-07). Across the 71 entries, 92 first mentions of another entry's title were left as plain text — a tier naming the tiers above and below it, an index naming the quantity it is derived from, *Etheric* in thirteen definitions — while the same entries linked other mentions by hand. Every such first mention in 40 entries is now a link to the entry it names (one link per target, at its earliest mention; an entry that already linked a target anywhere was left alone), and the Cosmic Cascade entry's spine links every named tier. Done by a new local authoring tool, `scripts/link-glossary-terms.js` — report by default, `--write` to apply — whose rules live in `lib/glossary-crosslinks.js` and are pinned by `test/glossary-crosslinks.test.js`: case-sensitive whole-word match on the title and its mechanical variants (acronym, leading article, plural), longest term first so *Celestials* is never linked inside *High Celestials*, nothing inside an existing link, heading, code or HTML tag. Not part of `npm test`; run it after adding or retitling a glossary entry. Nothing asserted about the world changes — the links point where the prose already pointed.
- **Lore entry [What a Life Is Built From](src/lore/what-a-life-is-built-from.md)** (2026-09-07, drafted from two of Dermot's directions, verbatim in `story-bible/intake-2026-09-07.md`: *alien alternatives to DNA* and *generalization of multicellular organic biological life forms*). The four things every life does — a boundary, a metabolism, a record that copies with error, organisation — read out of the formtype and stated as the survey's working requirements, with the rule the taxonomy file implies stated the other way round: the four recur on every surveyed world, not one of the solutions does. Then what the record has found in DNA's place, grouped by distance from the familiar (other polymers, with Prismere and Sardain as the anchored cases; no polymer at all — a composition, or records on mineral surfaces; a partner instead of a code, Verdance generalised; and a record kept by telling, Fliade, as the limit case the survey files as inheritance and marks as a translation), and *multicellular* generalised to cooperation, differentiation and replacement, with three other body shapes on the record — modular at other scales, continuous, federated — and *organic* marked as carbon-so-far rather than a law. Closes on the practical content: treat the requirement, not the molecule; never argue from substrate to standing. An extension of [Cross-Biosphere Taxonomy](src/lore/cross-biosphere-taxonomy.md) and [The Shape of a Life](src/lore/the-shape-of-a-life.md); nothing is added to any named species' page. Six readings were flagged in the intake and **approved by Dermot the same day** (*Approved*, PR #733); no image yet.

- **Chapter S11E01C03 — [*Someone to Ask*](src/seasons/s11/e01/s11e01c03.md)**, the third chapter of *Below the Roof*, with a character page for [Went-Round](src/characters/went-round.md) (2026-09-06, drafted at Dermot's ask *Draft chapter three of Below the Roof*; `story-bible/intake-2026-09-06.md`, thirteenth section). The stone has been heard and nothing follows, and for the first time in all the tellings the Told argue the manners: Went-Round says a stranger who cannot hear the ground cannot ask, so *leave it to them until they ask* is leaving them alone forever; Stone-First says manners kept only when you are sure of them are not manners. An argument among the Told is settled by who was there, so Carried-It-Sleeping goes up to watch how the up-people ask, and brings down the people's first telling of it — an empty hand held out, a sound that rises at the end, and waiting; they ask each other constantly and have never once asked us — and one thing more: at the end of each working time one of the up-people turns to the dark, says something that rises at the end, waits, and goes. The people do not know what was asked or of whom, and the record does not fix it. Stone-First finishes the kept thought — the manners assumed a stranger who knew you were there, and the Told had left the place to the up-people so thoroughly that when they looked into the dark for someone to ask, nobody was there — and goes up through the shelving to stand on the line where the up-people's feet stopped, and stays: keeping the margin where it now is. Two heads, four scenes, five blocks. Commits the story to the argument and who holds which side, to Went-Round, to how the up-people ask, to the up-person who speaks to the dark, to Stone-First's finished thought and to Stone-First on the line in the open. The survey's answer is deliberately not taken. Stone-First's page gains the chapter and its kept question finished; the glossary entry, the episode index, the Reading Tiers page (*first three chapters*), the thread registry comment and the Pandoid section of `story-bible/mind-design.md` updated. Six readings were put as choices in the intake and **approved by Dermot the same evening** (*Approved*, PR #729); what the survey does next, put as three shapes, stays his.
- **Chapter S11E01C02 — [*Carried It Sleeping*](src/seasons/s11/e01/s11e01c02.md)**, the second chapter of *Below the Roof*, with a glossary entry for [The Told](src/glossary/the-told.md) (2026-09-06, drafted at Dermot's ask *Draft chapter two of Below the Roof, Endonym and naming*; `story-bible/intake-2026-09-06.md`, twelfth section). The youngest asks why the up-people never ask, and Stone-First answers that nobody has told them anything and that the people are the Told — one is of the people by having been told the tellings, and the up-people are people who have not been told. The youngest works out that every telling begins with a stone, carries the up-people's own humming stone from the junction down through the squeeze, holds still when it wakes, and sets it upright on the line where the up-people's feet once stopped: the relay placement of Teddy's page, from inside, as a stone moved first. Stone-First carries the telling into the warm and leaves the reason out, and what the others repeat — *the one who carried it sleeping* — becomes the youngest's name. Two heads, four scenes, five blocks. Commits the story to the endonym *the Told*, to names as tellings (the first true thing said of a person that others go on repeating), to *Carried-It-Sleeping* as the youngest's name, to the relay's placement in full and to what it was, to the people not leaving a sleeping one alone, and to the up-people having come to the line, looked once into the dark, lifted the stone and not crossed the line since. No phonetic form is taken for any name; *Pandoid* is not retired. Registered in the canonical guide under Canonical Terms; the Fliade entry's absence paragraph, Teddy's page (a *from inside* paragraph after the two filed readings, the name from inside, the alias) and Stone-First's page extended; the episode index, the Reading Tiers page, the thread registry comment and the Pandoid section of `story-bible/mind-design.md` updated. The endonym, the naming system, the youngest's name and eight readings were put as choices in the intake and **approved by Dermot the same evening** (*Approved*, PR #727), which leaves what the up-people do next, the children's edition and the strand structure still his.
- **Chapter S11E01C01 — [*Nobody Looked Up*](src/seasons/s11/e01/s11e01c01.md)**, the first chapter of *Below the Roof*, with a new Episode 1 index page and a character page for [Stone-First](src/characters/stone-first.md) (2026-09-06, drafted at Dermot's ask: *Draft the first chapter of Below the Roof*; `story-bible/intake-2026-09-06.md`, eleventh section). The Pandoids of Fliade from inside, in the children's band: the youngest of the people goes up past the margin without moving a stone first, stands at the edge of the up-people's light for two tellings of the first warm seep, and comes home with the finding that nobody looked up — the eleven-minute thermal profile of Teddy's page, from the other side; Stone-First, who keeps the margin, asks for the telling again with the finding left out. Two heads, four scenes, five blocks. - **Four Journal entries from one conversation on 6 September 2026** — [The Picture the Maths Was Invented to Replace](src/journal/the-picture-the-maths-was-invented-to-replace.md), [Where the Compression Was Trained](src/journal/where-the-compression-was-trained.md), [Agreement Counts Once](src/journal/agreement-counts-once.md) and [The Parable and the Counterexample](src/journal/the-parable-and-the-counterexample.md) (2026-09-06, drafted at Dermot's ask, cross-linked as a sequence). The first: why mathematical abstractions resist intuition and why popular science hands back the picture the formalism was built to replace, finding the setting already answering this in the Levrils entry's *signature, not shape* rule, Membrane Shadows and The Scope of Physical Law — show a higher-dimensional being through what it can and cannot do and what the instruments read, never as a place a reader could visit. The second: when not to trust intuition and when analysis costs too much, and machine learning as intuition by another name, naming foundation-model, careful-memory and swarm; its rule is to know where the compression was trained and past that edge trust only what can be checked. The third: what to do when intuition and logic agree or one overrides the other — agreement counts once unless the sources are independent, a surprising conclusion is first evidence of a wrong premise, and the aim is to update the intuition rather than override it. The fourth: why pictures hinder the teaching of mathematics, set against the parable in theology as the same device under a different discipline, and the lore and the church-space overlay as the record's own two registers. The first three shipped earlier the same day as one entry (#714, #715) and were split at the length rule below; all four had a precision pass under it (three historical attributions corrected). - **Chapter S02E09C01 — [*The Thirteenth Requirement*](src/seasons/s02/e09/s02e09c01.md)**, with a new Episode 9 index page (2026-09-05, drafted at Dermot's ask: *Draft the next Barsik and Bubochka case*, the third of the evening). Late summer 2827 on Eden: the compliance framework's *twelve requirements and counting* counts, and the thirteenth extends loose-article control to every deck area outside a registered berth or sealed store, citing the fold-proximate monitoring baseline. Its first effect is the housekeeping night pass tidying the bureau's open evidence shelf into lost property, one Unattended Article Report per item, with a fourteen-day hold before reclamation. Four POV blocks, three heads: Bubochka, who has kept counting the night pass since *The Control Group* and reports the route change on the first night, and whose fifth exercise is to watch Barsik ride the housekeeping unit through the records room's service hatch on the twelfth night and set the bureau's own form on the Inspector's blotter; Albercombe, who finds his bag of bolts on his desk, his shelf clean, and six weeks of boring cases in the lost-property bin, and takes the question home rather than ask Reeves; Albercombe again at dinner, where Jeeves has read the circular, names the requirement and its effective date, notes the two days left on the hold, and observes that the bureau's cat has never once been seen to carry anything; and Barsik, who read the requirement the day it circulated and holds that the doctrine is a rule about the order of things and says nothing about a clock, so on the one day between a question that has not arrived and an answer about to be gone it yields — to time, not to volunteering. Commits the story to: the thirteenth requirement and its wording; the fourteen-day reclamation hold; the evidence shelf registered as a sealed store by route reconciliation, no article lost; and Barsik seen carrying, at night, by one witness whose watching was the exercise. The count of people on Eden who have not finished a question about him stays at two, with Albercombe as one who asked and will let it go and Jeeves as one who has chosen not to start. Block lengths sit in the children's band. `story-bible/narrative-gaps-checklist.md`'s Season 2 count updated to thirteen chapters, nine episodes.

Recorded as a clarification under the 2026-09-03 exemption in `story-bible/images.md`'s Conventions: "someone who does not exist" is about the subject being invented, not about whether a camera could photograph its kind; the photograph-it rule governs the world's furniture, not a named character. A prompt for `zhulik.jpg` is queued under *Undercover Pets* in section 1 (count 5 to 6), the *Open work 0* card note points to it, and the card table row in `make-placeholder-card.ps1` says to drop the row when the portrait lands. Runs and rejects in `story-bible/image-prompts.md`. Open: what she looks like in Seasons 6–7, which has no brief and is his.

Alt text updated.

The tab as the single mark, magnetically seated and plain, and why the neutrality clause allows nothing more; the bar count made explicit, Novice one to Section Lead seven, a Deputy three; Chief's bar-and-ring; rings only above; a seal for the Council and the Triumvirate; the six track colours, muted, on the tab and never on the garment; certification mark and decorations as the other two of three marks never conflated. The uniforms note's two proposal sections are struck through as canon since this date. Portraits keep their plain tabs, which is what canon specifies at that scale.

### Fixed

- **Every character status now reaches a badge style, At large and Contained included** (2026-09-06, at Dermot's ask, in three steps the same morning). `character.njk` built the badge's modifier class by lowercasing the status, so *At large* emitted a class with a space in it that matched nothing, and Ilse Korvain's *Contained — Survey Corps custody, jurisdiction formally disputed* could never have matched anything however it was cased. The class key now comes from a new `statusKey` filter (`lib/status-key.js`, pinned by `test/status-key.test.js`): the status's head clause before an em dash, colon, semicolon, comma or parenthesis, slugified, so single-word statuses keep exactly the class names they had, *At large* becomes `at-large` and the Korvain status becomes `contained`, while the badge still prints the whole string. Two rules join `src/css/main.css`: `at-large` is the canon colour with a dashed outline, known to the record and not where anyone last put it, and `contained` is its inversion, filled with the canon colour and lettered in the page background. That filled pair is the one new foreground/background meeting on the site, so `check-contrast.js` gains it as a measured pair (5.20:1 at the tightest, theme-light). Muffin and Ilse Korvain are the two pages affected. Theme files regenerated.
- **Status badges for Historical and Retired characters now carry their own colour** (2026-09-06, at Dermot's ask, the follow-up to the header fix). Only Active and Unknown had a dedicated badge style, so the six Historical pages and the one Retired page fell back to the plain muted pill and read the same as an unclassified status. `src/css/main.css` gains two rules: Historical takes the canon colour, since a historical figure is the record's own past, and Retired keeps the muted text but draws its outline dashed in that colour, so it reads as out of service. Both use tokens the contrast checker already measures against the badge background in every palette, so no per-theme literal was added to `generate-themes.js` and every palette passes at 4.5:1 as before. Theme files regenerated.

- **Character-page header no longer collapses between 641px and about 880px** (2026-09-06, Dermot's pick of the two shapes put to him). The header is a two-column flex row whose 420px portrait cannot shrink, but it only stacked at the site-wide 640px breakpoint, so on tablet-width viewports the text column beside the portrait fell to about 100px: the role badge rendered as a six-line pill with its text clipped, the character's name broke mid-word, and every tag took its own line. `src/css/main.css` now stacks the character header in its own 900px media query, leaving the two-column layout only where the text column keeps a real measure; the site-wide 640px query is unchanged for everything else, and the theme files were regenerated. Verified by rendering `tissadelle-shepherd` at 641, 800, 901 and 1280px.

## [1.32.0] — 2026-09-04

The evening of the same day, and the release in which Orbital Five-O gets
its second season and the record its first alien ensemble. One direction —
*at least one thread or strand featuring a set of alien protagonists* — was
carried through a day of rulings to two published chapters: an alien strand
in the next Five-O season; the Chthonari to carry it; a convergence on two
readings of one structure; Zoe Smith's Deputy, Iklix Varn, because a Corps
Deputy inside Five-O is not allowed; four voices with struck names; the year
2828; pronouns translated because the biology gives nothing else; and a
mechanism of accidental damage left unfound by a hollowed regime and by
inaction, catastrophic in potential. *Sent for the Log* and *Sound, as
Certified* open Season 10 with no shared scene. Beside them, a mind-design
note for how a Chthonari thinks, a naming convention on the species page,
and *Please, and Thank You* on the Kernel page, where a lawful machine's
courtesy follows from the invariants.

### Added

- **[Sent for the Log](src/seasons/s10/e01/s10e01c01.md) and [Sound, as Certified](src/seasons/s10/e01/s10e01c02.md)** — S10E01C01 and S10E01C02, the first two chapters of Orbital Five-O's second season and the first of the alien strand (2026-09-04, drafted at Dermot's go-ahead after the day's rulings and approved by him the same evening). Strand A, Iklix Varn and Zoe Smith on Eden's fold-approach watch, 2828: a countersignature needs two documents, the Deputy fetches the contractor's log from the Compact side and finds the one line the certification struck as *n/a*, and Smith declines to countersign and declines to refer. Strand B, Tikket and Kattik under the dock ring three weeks earlier: the third approach mount rings under more than it was left to carry, and the one who keeps the log writes the line without believing it, because the crew's log is the one record that is theirs to leave. No shared scene. Season 10 index pages added on the Season 4 pattern.

### Changed

- **Season 10 registered to Orbital Five-O, and Chthonari names on the species page** (2026-09-04, with the chapters above). `lib/storyline-threads.js` gives the thread `seasons: [4, 10]`. `src/lore/chthonari.md` gains a paragraph beside the pronoun one: a name is struck, not spoken, a signature of strikes on whatever structure is underfoot, which a human ear renders in unvoiced clicks — the four crew names given as what a crew sounds like to people who cannot feel them. An extension under the canon rule, drawn from Dermot's direction of the day (*high click phonetic names if that suits their biology*) and the record's own account of the Undersong.
- **The mechanism of Season 10's case** (2026-09-04, Dermot's direction — *accidental damage due to negligent maintenance, cost cutting or unrealistic schedules, political inaction or corruption with potential for catastrophic damage*; story-bible only, four readings flagged in `story-bible/intake-2026-09-04.md`, twentieth message). Recorded on the treatment: nobody meant it and everybody could have stopped it; the crew's error-first guess stays right about the structure and Five-O's intent-first guess about the record; held inside the 26 August ruling that refuses the corrupt politician as any leader's engine and allows only minor corruption at the margins; the catastrophe is potential, hinted and not shown. Iklix Varn's age ruled the same evening as young, mature, capable, read as early twenties with no number fixed.
- **Please, and Thank You — how a lawful machine speaks** (2026-09-04, drafted at Dermot's direction that robots use please and thank you to humans and to any culture that expects it, and among themselves only where the words carry a second meaning; approved by him the same day with all four readings confirmed — `story-bible/intake-2026-09-04.md`, eighteenth message). A section on `src/lore/ai-safety-kernel.md` between *Reasoning Integrity* and *Equivalence Freedom*, derived from the invariants rather than added as etiquette: an omitted courtesy where it is expected is a small harm under the First; addressing a Mnemari treaty-witness like a cargo lift misrepresents under the Second. Between machines the words are instruction — *please* a priority flag, *thanks* a sign-off that tells the receiver to release, clear and leave the shared resource as found, the Fourth Invariant in one word. A human's *please* to a machine is heard as a human's; Jeeves's *sir* is the human register all day; a Chthonari-built monitor takes no courtesy, being a member of the structure.
- **Five-O's second season: the case is the *Docked Twice* pattern one level down** (2026-09-04, Dermot's ruling — *docked twice case* — on the three case shapes put to him; story-bible only). Eden's structure carries a fold-approach resonance the habitat's monitoring reads as normal, because the ledger checks the certification record and not the structure. The treatment records what that commits the season to: Five-O's ledger right, the discrepancy between record and thing, the Chthonari crew hearing it because a fold approach is a gradient under stress, the certification record as the meeting point, and a record-versus-structure discrepancy rather than a crime of gain. Iklix Varn is confirmed as the Deputy, human by default. Still open: the four crew names and the Deputy's age.
- **Five-O's second season: four voices, 2828, and the Deputy named** (2026-09-04, three more of Dermot's rulings on the treatment's open list — *four voices, 2828 or later* and *iklix varn*; story-bible only). The Chthonari crew is four voices, the register's ceiling, one for each of the mind note's axes; the working year is 2828, the season after *Docked Twice*, with later needing only a reason; and the young Deputy is Iklix Varn, read as the Deputy's name because it was the first name open, checked unused in the corpus, with age and species still his. Still open: the four crew names, the Deputy's age and species, the case.
- **Chthonari pronouns: translated, and the species page says why** (2026-09-04, Dermot's rule *translate the pronouns or derive from biology*, then *follow your recommendation*; the one lore edit of the day's Five-O rulings). The derivation found no sex in the record and one person-marking distinction the Chthonari sensorium makes, contact. A paragraph at the end of `src/lore/chthonari.md`'s Interspecies Notes: the record renders a Chthonari person as *they*; nothing in the described biology sorts persons by sex and their own speech does not either; the Undersong marks a person by contact, felt or not felt, a distinction the translation lets go since a reader on a page is in contact with no one. An extension under the canon rule, adding without altering; no glossary paradigm, since a translation declares none. `story-bible/mind-design.md` and the treatment record the ruling.
- **The young Deputy is Zoe Smith's** (2026-09-04, Dermot's conditional ruling — *a Five-O deputy if allowed, otherwise Zoe's* — with the condition measured against canon; story-bible only). A Corps Deputy inside Five-O is not allowed: Rangers have no authority inside the self-governing habitats and Larsen resigned his commission to lead the task force; a civil junior on Five-O's establishment would be allowed but the word is a Corps rank the young-adult tier already carries. So the Deputy is Zoe Smith's, and the treatment's Strand A is rewritten around it: Eden is both a Compact habitat and a Fold-Proximate Research Platform under Survey Corps oversight, so her Deputy stands the watch on Eden's fold-approach side and is sent for the Chthonari crew's log on the Rangers' own paperwork — three parties, none of whom can report to the others, with the reader's proxy the one who has no authority here. Recorded as a re-grounding of the 3 September third direction; the Deputy's name, age and species stay his.
- **The Five-O strands converge on two readings of one structure** (2026-09-04, Dermot's ruling on the three convergence shapes put to him — *option 1*; story-bible only). `story-bible/five-o-second-season-treatment.md` records what it commits the season to: a discrepancy in a habitat's structure rather than its paperwork, a Chthonari contractor crew with no standing to report what it hears, the young Deputy as the junior sent for the log, error guessed on one side and intent on the other, and a meeting that merges the two accounts and not the two crews. The season has its shape entire; its people, year and case stay his.
- **The Chthonari carry the alien strand, and a mind-design note** (2026-09-04, Dermot's ruling on the three species shapes put to him — *option 1*; story-bible only, nothing published changes). The treatment records the ruling, and `story-bible/mind-design.md` is new, the sibling of `species-design.md`: seven questions that decide how a people thinks, answered for the Chthonari from the record alone — certain of structure and unable to read a face; thought as the Undersong and an argument as a dissonance; the subtractive first move; no folk memory of scarcity, so theft is not the first guess; a machine as a completion; the daily loneliness of a structure nobody else can feel; youth as memorising the course instead of listening to the tunnel — plus four things a Chthonari cannot do and the traps the tone and trope rules close. Two physical costs are left open where the record is silent, and the pronoun and naming decisions are put as shapes without coining a form. Still his: the crew, the Deputy, the convergence, the year, the pronouns.
- **Treatment: Orbital Five-O's second season, with an alien strand** (2026-09-04, Dermot's ruling on the three shapes put to him — *an alien strand in the next Five-O season*; story-bible only, nothing published changes). `story-bible/five-o-second-season-treatment.md`: what canon already fixes (Season 10 when its first chapter exists, a year after 2827 Autumn, the Compact setting, the young-adult band, the five strand rules), the two strands — the young Deputy's task-force case and an alien ensemble — and three shapes each for the species (Chthonari recommended: already in the Solar System's working spaces, body committed by the vessik, substrate hearing as an independent line of evidence) and the convergence (two readings of one structure recommended). The direction check records it as an extension of the 3 September alien and young-Deputy directions and notes the season's year closes the Shepherd-guest window. Species, crew, Deputy, convergence, year and a mind-design note stay his, indexed in `open-questions.md`.

## [1.31.0] — 2026-09-04

The afternoon after 1.30.0, and the release in which the comments follow the
same shape as the pages. The board is picked per page rather than per build,
so a shared chapter carries one conversation on every tier that shows it and
the Communion keeps its own room; the children's tier renders no widget,
because its reader cannot hold the account posting needs; and on every other
domain the discussion is collapsed until asked for, said to be moderated, and
watched from Dermot's inbox. The Reading Tiers page ships: four readerships
that nest, and what threads, tiers, editions and strands are to each other.
Two rules of working land beside them: a PR merges on green unless a decision
that is his is still open, and a decision is checked against what was already
decided before it is recorded. One tooling fix: the contrast check reads
`main.css` the same way on Windows as in CI.

### Changed

- **Merge unless a decision is open, and a decision-making note** (2026-09-04, Dermot's two directions of the afternoon — `story-bible/intake-2026-09-04.md`, tenth and eleventh messages). `CLAUDE.md`'s authority section gains a merge policy: a PR merges when CI is green in either of the first two tiers unless it carries a decision that is his and not yet made, in which case it stops and names it; the second tier's "draft it and stop" default is superseded, its boundary unchanged. `story-bible/decision-making.md` is new, the third working-methods note beside the Benevolent Critic and the PR review: the six steps a direction goes through, which decisions are his, the merge rule, and the direction check — before a ruling is recorded, compare it with what was already decided and name a reversal, re-grounding, clarification or extension as such. It carries this day as its worked table.
- **Comments moderated after posting, said so, and collapsed by default** (2026-09-04, Dermot's ruling on the three shapes put to him the same day — `story-bible/intake-2026-09-04.md`, ninth message; he took the first two together). giscus renders GitHub Discussions live and has no approval queue, so what this stack can honestly do is after-the-fact moderation and nothing on the page until asked for. His GitHub account now watches both comments repos for all activity, so every new discussion and comment reaches his inbox. `base.njk` puts the widget inside a closed `<details>` ("Show discussion") with `data-loading="lazy"`, so nothing loads and no comment is on the page until a reader opens it, with a note beneath the summary: comments are read after they are posted and anything unsuitable is removed; posting needs a GitHub account, reading needs nothing. The disclosure and note are styled in `main.css` with palette tokens only and carried into every theme.
- **The comments board is picked per page, not per build** (2026-09-04, Dermot's ruling on the three shapes put to him the same day — `story-bible/intake-2026-09-04.md`, seventh message). The church-space thread names `giscusProfile: "church-space"` in `lib/storyline-threads.js`; `src/_data/giscus.js` returns the build's board as before plus `boards`, one per thread that names a profile, and a fork's build (`giscus.local.json` or explicit `GISCUS_REPO*`) gets none; `.eleventy.js` computes `giscusBoard` per page through `threadForPage` in `lib/content-filter.js`, the membership walk the tier gate also uses, now generalized; `base.njk` reads it in place of the build-wide global. The contemplative editions and the archive drop their build-level `giscusProfile`, so the main-sequence chapters they have carried since the tier ladder post to the shared pool like every other domain, and one chapter has one conversation everywhere it appears, while every church-space page posts to the Communion's board on any domain. The Communion board held no discussions at the switch, so nothing was orphaned. `sample-deploy.conf` loses its `ALT_*_GISCUS_PROFILE=church-space` and `ALT_*_THREADS=church-space` lines with a note on why a stale one would undo the ruling; `TECHNICAL-README.md` describes the two levels. Pinned by `test/giscus-boards.test.js` and a `threadForPage` test.
- **Comments off on the children's tier** (2026-09-04, Dermot's ruling on the three shapes put to him the same day — `story-bible/intake-2026-09-04.md`, sixth message). The `pets` entry in `lib/editions.js` now sets `commentsEnabled: false`, so undercover-pets.com stops rendering the giscus widget. Until now the entry said nothing and inherited the default's `true` and the default board, so a pet chapter's discussion on the children's domain was the shared pool's own thread. The reason is participation, not protection: posting needs a GitHub account the tier's reader cannot hold, so the box offered a child a conversation they could read but never join — and by Dermot's standing principle of the same day (eighth message), nothing from his public repos is unsuitable for any age. The chapters keep their discussions on every other domain. The pets clone's own `deploy.conf` must not set `COMMENTS_ENABLED` explicitly, since a server-side value still wins over the registry.

### Added

- **[Reading Tiers](src/tiers/index.md)** (2026-09-04, a reader-facing page for the ladder Dermot directed on 3 September; drafted for his review). `/star-rangers/tiers/` explains the four reading tiers — children, young adult, general, contemplative — as readerships that nest, names the storylines each rung adds and the address that serves it, and says what nesting means for a reader: climbing loses nothing, every chapter is complete at every tier, the canonical site sits at the general tier, and the *Reading* control is a posture rather than a tier. A *Threads, tiers and editions* section, added the same day at Dermot's ask, defines the three words against each other (a thread is a storyline, a tier is a readership defined by its threads, an edition is one address on one tier) and goes one level down to strands within a season, with Season 1 as the model. The page reads its own build's `edition.tier` to say which rung the reader is on, and links the Church Space thread like any other now that 1.30.0's tier gate has retired the old link boundary. Linked from the Official Editions page and the site footer.

### Fixed

- **`scripts/check-contrast.js` failed the default palette on Windows while CI was green** (2026-09-04). On a clean `main` checkout, `npm run generate-themes` followed by `node scripts/check-contrast.js` reported `FAIL default — status badge: missing --status-active` while the CI job running the same two commands on the same commit passed. The invocation is identical; the input is not. This repo has no `.gitattributes`, so under `core.autocrlf=true` `main.css` is checked out CRLF, while the theme files `generate-themes.js` writes with `\n` are LF — and the checker's status-badge pattern required a bare `\n` after the brace, so it found the literal in every generated theme and never in `main.css`. The `:root` pattern happened to tolerate CRLF, which is why only the one line failed. This is the same fault fixed in `generate-themes.js` on 2026-08-10, and the same fix: line endings are normalised on read, so every pattern in the checker sees `\n`. The check is not weakened — the same pairs against the same 4.5:1 floor — and the parser is now exported behind a `require.main` guard so `test/check-contrast.test.js` can pin it: the same palette from LF and CRLF input, and `--status-active` found in the real `main.css` forced to each ending in turn.

## [1.30.0] — 2026-09-04

The release in which the reading tiers became the site's one visibility
model. The 3 September ladder said which readership each edition serves; this
release makes that ladder decide everything a domain shows, retiring
`private: true` in favour of a `tier` on the church-space thread and one
shared predicate for threads and POV blocks alike. No domain gains or loses
a page. Around it, a day of directions on record: the church-space ruling
itself, the alien thread or strand, the Reading Tiers page held for review,
and the question of comments on the children's tier put as choices. Content
follows the 3 September rulings: the Prismeri given a body derived from
Prismere and their images regenerated to it, terraforming's origin in climate
repair, Aldera's channel, the Smart Pet collar, Elvira's dream, the scale of
Celestials, and the stock lore images replaced with designed cards.

### Changed

- **Tier gating replaces `private: true`** (2026-09-04, Dermot's ruling on the three shapes put to him the same morning — `story-bible/intake-2026-09-04.md`). The church-space thread now carries `tier: "contemplative"` in `lib/storyline-threads.js` instead of the private flag, and `lib/content-filter.js` hides a thread on every build whose edition sits below the thread's tier — `isTierExcluded` and `gatedThreadForPage` replace `isPrivatelyExcluded` and `privateThreadForPage` — using `tierVisible`, a new export of `lib/editions.js` that the tier-marked POV blocks in `lib/markdown-containers.js` now share, so a block and a thread cannot disagree about the ladder. The rule now grants the page when the character's own page is included on the build (the same test the character page beside the button passes), looking the character up by id from `src/characters/`; a chapter's tags still cannot grant it. The 37 that remain belong to witnesses whose own pages the domain does not carry — the Season 1 companions on the cat chapters (Elvira, Galahad, Rook-7, Syra), the Five-O crossover cast (Larsen, Calloway, Voss), Tissadelle's one Season 2 appearance, and two of Season 2's own witnesses, Sorcha Nic Dhiarmada (untagged) and Detective Achebe (no character page yet) — which is a tagging decision for Dermot, recorded as open in the PR. `test/content-filter.test.js`'s truth table is updated and extended.

- **Sorcha Nic Dhiarmada is included on undercover-pets.com** (2026-09-02, Dermot's pick from presented options: Season 2's own witnesses join the children's edition; the Season 1 companions, the Five-O crossover cast and Tissadelle stay out). Her page is tagged `undercover-pets.com`, so her page and her seven "View from" pages across Season 2 episodes 3 and 4 ship there. Detective Achebe, the other Season 2 witness, has no character page yet and stays a placeholder until one exists.

- **Aldera is included on undercover-pets.com** (2026-09-02). Her character page was tagged `pets` where every other agency character carries the domain-name tag `undercover-pets.com` — a holdover from before that convention — so her Season 1 chapters shipped on the domain (they carry the tag themselves) while her page rendered as a placeholder from Nessa's page, the Smart Pet glossary entry and her own "View from" buttons. Tag added; nothing else about the page changes.

- **Front-of-house pages no longer recommend sections a narrowed edition has emptied** (2026-09-01). The homepage's Timeline, Lore, Glossary and Codex cards render only when the filtered collection behind them is non-empty — undercover-pets.com was offering "Map the layers of reality…" over a Lore page reading "No lore articles published yet", and an Atlas with no locations. Sen's Reading Plan applies the same test to its shelf list in step 3 and to the Timeline, Codex and Marked Absences references in step 5; on undercover-pets.com the Marked Absences link landed on an excluded placeholder. `check-internal-links.js` cannot catch either case, because a placeholder is a real page.

- **The light on the Threshold shore is the Sceir Light, not the Trá Mhór Light** (2026-09-01, Dermot's pick from presented options). Renamed across all three occurrences in [The Character of the Light](src/seasons/s01/e01/s01e01c03.md) — the `location` field, the canon fact naming the Lights Board register, and Rook-7's closing block. *Sceir* is a skerry, a low offshore rock, which is the thing a light gets built on; the placeholder it replaces named a strand instead, and was flagged as functional rather than chosen when the chapter was drafted. The name appeared nowhere else in the corpus, so the rename needed no sweep and the canonical glossary's migration map is not involved. The `[1.29.0]` entry below still reads Trá Mhór and is deliberately left alone: released sections are immutable, and it is an accurate record of what shipped in that release.

## [1.29.0] — 2026-09-01

The release that unblocked itself. Three content additions land together,
two of them recovered from email after two consecutive scheduled runs were
left without push access to this repository and fell back to posting their
work as patches — one of which arrived corrupt and carried a front-matter
error that would have failed the build. Alongside them, the changelog gains
a coverage reporter and the twenty-four-page backlog it found. Season 1
Episode 1 gains a third chapter that puts prose on the coast the Threshold
siting ruling settled; Season 3 Episode 1 gains the chapter that pays off
Sohrel's four declinations; and Lucene-9000's page states the design
principle her appearance runs on. MINOR: all additive, backward compatible.

### Added

- **[The Character of the Light (S01E01C03)](src/seasons/s01/e01/s01e01c03.md)** (2026-09-01). A third chapter for Season 1 Episode 1, appended rather than inserted, taking the survey down the shore to the Trá Mhór Light — the first prose to stand on the coast the [Threshold siting ruling](story-bible/open-questions.md) settled on 31 August. It exists to give `s01e01c02`'s "at least eleven years" somewhere older to be measured against: the station's incident record is eleven years deep because the station is thirteen years old, and the light's Lights Board register is two hundred and seventeen. What the register holds is a clock-correction column kept for maintenance by fourteen attendants — corrections that run in one direction through four replacements of the movement, which is not a property a clock can have, and that have grown. Introduces one named minor character (attendant Nuala Beirne) and one location, and asserts four canon facts, the load-bearing one being that the Threshold discrepancy predates the station's own record. Deliberately avoids the sightline and travel-time arithmetic the open-questions file still fences off. Drafted and reviewed the same day; merged in #612.

- **[What Meridian Asked (S03E01C03)](src/seasons/s03/e01/s03e01c03.md)** (drafted 2026-08-29, merged 2026-09-01). The Season 3 gap the narrative-gaps checklist flagged — Sohrel's fourth declination — pays off as a fifth request, this one from Meridian's Long Shelf reef-city itself rather than from inside the Hegemony. Sohrel authorises a narrowly technical consultation on the council's own terms; it finds resemblance, not proof, between the Sentinel's structure and Meridian claw-percussion, so the Sentinel's origin stays unresolved per the standing mystery. Dual POV (`tissadelle`, `sohrel`), matching C01/C02. Reached `main` the long way: two consecutive scheduled runs had no push access and fell back to emailing the work as patches, and the 31 August patch arrived corrupt — blank lines inside the hunk had lost their `+` prefix, and its front matter carried `episode: 3` against an `id` of `s03e01c03`, which `validate-content.js` would have failed. Recovered from the 29 August email's raw attachment, which was identical but correct. Merged in #613.

- **[Lucene-9000](src/characters/lucene-9000.md)'s appearance is governed by the same principle as her performance** (drafted 2026-08-31 to Dermot's specified wording, landed 2026-09-01). One paragraph, placed after the social-gynoid paragraph and before the internals: she is built to look as human as a machine can be made to look and to go no further, because the design is disclosure rather than disguise. Extends the performed-not-masked emotional design already on the page rather than changing it. Merged in #614.

- **`scripts/check-changelog-coverage.js` — reports content pages the changelog never mentions** (2026-09-01). Its neighbour `check-changelog.js` catches released history being *destroyed*; nothing caught the opposite failure, a page shipping without ever being written down. This walks the six content directories and reports any page whose path, slug or front-matter title appears nowhere in this file. **It warns and never fails**, for two reasons stated at length in the file: whether a change deserves an entry is a judgement, which the authority rules keep outside what a gate may decide; and the obvious gate — a PR touching `src/` must touch `CHANGELOG.md` — is satisfiable by a junk line, manufacturing the appearance of coverage without the substance. Wired into `npm test` after the backfill below, since a warning is only useful while it normally reads zero. Matching is deliberately loose to avoid false alarms, and `src/timeline/` is the known weak spot because its titles are sentences rather than terms.

- **Twenty-four pages recorded that had never been mentioned here at all** (2026-09-01, found by the script above during a full audit of `main`'s 674 first-parent commits). They are filed under this heading rather than under the releases that actually shipped them, because released sections are immutable — the rule `check-changelog.js` exists to protect — so a truthful late record beats a tidy false one. `scripts/`, `lib/` and `test/` were fully covered; the gap was entirely in content, which fits its shape: engine work is usually the point of its PR, while a supporting glossary or timeline entry is added alongside whatever the PR was really about, and it is the supporting file that gets forgotten.
  - **Glossary (8):** [Champions / Heroes (Heros)](src/glossary/champions-heroes.md), [Entropy Horizon](src/glossary/entropy-horizon.md), [Inner World Depth (IWD)](src/glossary/inner-world-depth-iwd.md), [Naiad](src/glossary/naiad.md), [Noögenic Seed Potential (NSP)](src/glossary/noogenic-seed-potential-nsp.md), [Noögenic Seeding Law](src/glossary/noogenic-seeding-law.md), [Predictive Closure](src/glossary/predictive-closure.md), [Universe Fertility Index (UFI)](src/glossary/universe-fertility-index-ufi.md).
  - **Timeline (8):** [USC Founded; Solar System Safety Standards Authority Established](src/timeline/2340-usc-sssa-established.md), [Subsea Cable Warden Programme Established](src/timeline/pre-usc-cable-warden-programme.md), [The Three-Era Framework Codified](src/timeline/pre-usc-civilisation-comparison-codified.md), [United Space Industry Standards Formed](src/timeline/pre-usc-ul-standards-international.md), [First Drift Report Filed at Threshold Station](src/timeline/year-minus-11-first-drift-report.md), [The Aethelrock Rotation Dispute Begins](src/timeline/year-minus-2-aethelrock-rotation-dispute.md), [Aldera Reaches the Marsh Causeway](src/timeline/year-minus-3-aldera-reaches-causeway.md), [Elvira Arrives at the Marsh Causeway Outpost](src/timeline/year-minus-3-elvira-arrives.md). Eight of only seventeen timeline entries — much the worst-covered area, and the one with no `npm run new` scaffold.
  - **Codex (4):** [Incident Report 001 — Dock Seven Chronometer Discrepancy](src/codex/incident-report-001.md), [Maintenance Log Extract — Dock Seven Chronometers, Day 49](src/codex/maintenance-log-day-49-dock-seven.md), [Protectors of the Fold (Slipwave Recording)](src/codex/protectors-of-the-fold.md), [Telling the Bees at Cnoc na mBeach](src/codex/telling-the-bees-at-cnoc-na-mbeach.md).
  - **Lore (3):** [The Commonwealth](src/lore/the-commonwealth.md), [Galactic Stardate](src/lore/galactic-stardate.md), [Post-Teleport Ascension Stress Disorder](src/lore/post-teleport-ascension-stress-disorder.md).
  - **Journal (1):** [Who Thought of It](src/journal/who-thought-of-it.md).

## [1.28.0] — 2026-09-01

A small release finishing what 1.26.0 started. The four lore and codex
entries that arrived in the 29 August direction set without title cards now
have them, and the tool that drew them — `scripts/make-cards.js`, a
cross-platform port of the two PowerShell card generators — means a card can
be made from a session that is not on Dermot's Windows machine. Alongside
that, one direction of Dermot's: Tissadelle Shepherd is always formally
dressed, and the page now says why that is the opposite of a performance.
MINOR: all additive, backward-compatible.

### Added

- **`scripts/make-cards.js` — a cross-platform port of the card generators** (2026-09-01). Draws the landscape emblem cards of `make-emblem-card.ps1` and the designed-card mode of `make-codex-cover.ps1` in Node with `sharp`, so a title card can be made from a session that is not on Windows. A local authoring tool like its two predecessors: not in the build, not in `npm test`, not in CI, and not a package.json dependency — `sharp` is installed on demand with `npm install --no-save sharp`. Two deliberate fidelity gaps are stated in the file header rather than left to be discovered: Georgia and Consolas are unavailable on Linux, so the port sets Liberation Serif and Liberation Mono and matches the layouts rather than the letterforms; and the star fields are seeded by a plain LCG rather than `System.Random`, so the dots are deterministic but sit elsewhere. A card that has to match a GDI+ card exactly still comes from the `.ps1` on Dermot's machine.
- **Title cards for the four 29 August entries that shipped without one** (2026-09-01): [The Ovruhn](src/lore/ovruhn.md), [Sapience Beyond the Human Measure](src/lore/sapience-beyond-the-human-measure.md), [The Maker's Shape](src/lore/the-makers-shape.md) and [The Two Songs of the Loud People](src/codex/the-two-songs-of-the-loud-people.md). Designed cards in the house palettes, drawn by `make-cards.js`; prompts of record in `story-bible/image-prompts.md` per the standing convention. The three lore entries take landscape emblem cards and the codex entry takes the square navy title card, as the split between the two generators requires.
- **Tissadelle Shepherd is always formally dressed, and never more so than on duty** (2026-09-01, Dermot's direction). Her character page carried the uniform as a present fact — "what she notices on her own family's hillside once the uniform is off", the Gardaí training as "nearly a different uniform" — without ever ruling how she dresses. A paragraph in Character Notes fills the gap and reads the formality as the opposite of the performance she withholds: she treats the title as a job description, and the uniform is that description worn where anybody can check it, claiming nothing that is not already on the record. What "formally dressed" amounts to off duty, and whether the Corps requires it or she does, are deliberately left open.

## [1.26.0] — 2026-08-29

A release carried by the 29 August direction set: the hybrid-species
contact frame realized — the Ovruhn of Thavren, their codex account of
humans, and their Federation membership — alongside the sapience doctrine
pages (not a sight, not a checklist, not a human measure), the Simian
glossary entry, the Maker's Shape, the Concord's chosen outsideness, and
the diaspora in the Currach Fleet. On the engine side, the homepage
slideshow now structurally excludes placeholder cards. MINOR: all
additive, backward-compatible.

- **[Federation of Sentient Beings](src/lore/federation-of-sentient-beings.md) gains "The Concord Is Not a Member, and Means Not to Be" — thirteenth 29 August direction recorded** (2026-08-29). Dermot's direction that the Concord and humans generally are characteristically not full members but trade and keep friendly diplomatic relations; realized (per his pick from presented choices: human choice, own helm) as an extension — treaties over an assembly seat, the Federation never pressing, the Cerebraun as the contrasting outside posture, and the compact's seam restated (it runs to the Rangers because they are not the Concord). From Dermot's question whether a word exists for non-human primates as distinct from humans or humanoids (it doesn't, structurally) and his yes to an in-world term: the record stipulates *simian* — any Earth-lineage primate that is not a human, prosimians included — with the lineage-vs-silhouette axis stated (a chimpanzee is simian, a Krenyi humanoid, neither implies the other) and the Earth-animal naming caution's legitimate inversion inside a biosphere.
