## [1.25.0] — 2026-08-28

A release carried by the 27 August direction set: the Tissadelle/Tobble
terminus — register, authored closing line, both scene drafts approved —
alongside the command detail rule, the Institute's purpose, and the
inner-world rulings. Around it: the Common Manifold reconciled with the
surveyed-universes canon, the Ilveth join the species roster, and the
engine gains unit tests for its last untested `lib/` modules plus
`TestingStrategy.md`. MINOR: all additive, backward-compatible.

### Added

- **The command detail rule's two founding reasons recorded** (2026-08-27, follow-up to the seventh direction; approved by Dermot the same day). Dermot's direction that the rule is a reaction against General Krast's MSC leadership style, existing to avoid micromanagement and to prevent the Star Rangers becoming a military dictatorship; realized into the "Where an Order Has to Stop" section's MSC paragraph (founding-era rationale, Krast named, the certification tier as the joint an unbroken will would need). Verbatim capture and canon check in `story-bible/intake-2026-08-27.md`, indexed in `story-bible/open-questions.md`.
- **[Rank and the Chain of Command](src/lore/star-rangers-command-hierarchy.md) gains a "Where an Order Has to Stop" section — seventh 27 August direction recorded** (2026-08-27, same intake; approved by Dermot the same day). Dermot's direction that Line Captains, Starwardens and Archwardens are not allowed to give overly detailed technical instructions to Chiefs, Section Leads or Principals; realized as standing Corps doctrine extending the Guild Leadership section's what/how line inside the chain of command — *overly* as the load-bearing word, the certification-seam reasoning, the deliberate floor at Principal, and the Dock Seven evacuation order as the lawful example. Verbatim capture, canon survey and five flagged readings (chief among them: "Chief Officers" as the Chief rank tier; whether the flag ranks are bound too) in `story-bible/intake-2026-08-27.md`, indexed in `story-bible/open-questions.md`. All five readings confirmed by Dermot the same day, with the fourth ruled wider — Star Captains and High Captains bound in the same way, normally delegating via the post-holding tier — and the section extended accordingly. A same-day follow-up supplied the doctrine's named inappropriate example (a Starwarden telling a Principal how to manage a cadet), settling that "technical" means the craft of the rank's own work, not instrumentation alone.
- **[Two in the One Currach](src/codex/two-in-the-one-currach.md) — codex devotional record** (2026-08-27, approved by Dermot the same day). Brother Daire's meditation from the river abbey on the circulating Baby Universe ballad, set in the published Deep Winter 2832 window: the song sings one woman through the seam, the abbey keeps vigil for two — the woman and the cat, a crew in one currach — in Aoife's own shown-not-healed discipline; the appended reconciliation-desk filing note restates the record's position (the seed stalled, completion neither observed nor foreclosed) and marks the plural-founder question as an absence the record has not been asked to fill. No title card yet.
- **Unit tests for the three previously-untested `lib/` modules** (2026-08-27): `test/markdown-containers.test.js` (the scene/POV fence-length rule and rendered attributes), `test/storyline-threads.test.js` (`threadForSeason`, the unsorted fallback, and the registry invariants the privacy machinery assumes) and `test/image-size.test.js` (the header parser's null-rather-than-guess contract). Engine only, no content touched; inventory in `TestingStrategy.md`.

- **[The Institute](src/lore/the-institute.md) gains a "What it is for" section — sixth 27 August direction recorded** (2026-08-27, same intake). Dermot's direction that the Institute is an independent nonpolitical academic body designed to provide intelligent constructive criticism, especially but not exclusively directed at the Star Rangers; realized as a design/purpose section (independence via the subscription model, non-political in the 2723 charter's constitutional sense, academic in form, *constructive* as the load-bearing word) plus a matching `description:`. Extension plus clarification under the canon-stability rule; verbatim capture, canon survey and four flagged readings (chief among them: "designed to" as standing remit, not founding intent — the Institute predates the Corps by centuries) in `story-bible/intake-2026-08-27.md`, indexed in `story-bible/open-questions.md`. All four readings confirmed and the section approved by Dermot the same day.
- **The terminus scene's external coda drafted** (2026-08-27, at Dermot's direction, same file). Scene 2, Wender POV: the terminus from outside — the final phrasing as Shepherd's last order to close the file, executed by Wender with cause of closure *founding*; the levril's watch complete; a cadence under the phrasing kept out of the record. By-proposal commitments flagged in `story-bible/open-questions.md`; approved by Dermot the same day, completing the draft — both scenes now stand approved.
- **The terminus scene drafted** (2026-08-27, at Dermot's direction). `story-bible/scene-draft-terminus-farewell.md` — the five 27 August directions realized as prose: the farewell in the ruled register, the authored closing line placed as her last words, Tissadelle and Tobble POVs, the other members' farewells marked rather than transcribed, the lost named once without the record carrying the names. Unpublished per the scene-draft precedent; interval and slot deliberately unfixed; four open items answered by proposal and flagged in `story-bible/open-questions.md`. Approved by Dermot the same day; remains story-bible material until a chapter slot is chosen.
- **The closing line — fifth 27 August direction recorded** (2026-08-27, same intake). Tissadelle's last words to Tobble, authored verbatim by Dermot and filed as prose-of-record for the unwritten terminus scene (not quoted in the changelog per the story-bible spoiler policy; the line, its reading, and its placement are in `story-bible/intake-2026-08-27.md` and the arc note's terminus section). Fixes the terminus against the protouniverse's founding and realizes the fourth direction's register in one sentence. No canon touched — the line binds its scene when written.
- **The terminus register — fourth 27 August direction recorded** (2026-08-27, same intake). Tissadelle Shepherd experiences almost no grief in her final moments — only fond farewell to Tobble and the other surviving headmates. Rules the register of the arc's unwritten terminus (the published chapters end on "a woman still becoming"), promotes the system's other members from the character page's "more people than the form has boxes for" implication to on-page participants, and completes the grief's distribution (author, Tobble's book, survivors, reader — none of it hers). Verbatim capture, canon survey and three flagged readings ("final moments" as the unwritten terminus; "surviving" as implying members lost; "almost no grief" as register, not retroactive costlessness — all three confirmed by Dermot the same day) in `story-bible/intake-2026-08-27.md`; arc note gains the terminus register; residue updated in `story-bible/open-questions.md`; distilled line proposed into `story-bible/life-lessons.md`. No canon touched — the terminus binds when written.
- **The redacted book, not the tulpa — third 27 August direction recorded** (2026-08-27, same intake). Tobble considered cultivating a new tulpa to represent the lost fantasy world, judged it "a museum or ghost of the original", and instead made a redacted book — an internal codex, some scenes glossed over for modesty. Verbatim capture, canon survey (the tulpa refusal as personhood ethics; the redaction as Marked Absences practised inside a mind; the book as the downgrade admitted) and two flagged readings (the modesty's sense; the refusal as Tobble's judgement, not doctrine — both confirmed by Dermot the same day) in `story-bible/intake-2026-08-27.md`; arc note gains the book as S7 prop; residue updated in `story-bible/open-questions.md`; distilled line proposed into `story-bible/life-lessons.md`. No canon touched — the book reaches canon when S7 writes it.
- **Tissadelle's RPG-structured inner world and Tobble's disciplined subsystem — direction recorded** (2026-08-27). Dermot's direction that Tissadelle's inner world is structured like a high fantasy RPG while Tobble's deeper internal subsystem is much more disciplined and scientific; verbatim capture, canon survey (the division of labour already on the page at Dock Seven, unnamed) and four flagged readings in `story-bible/intake-2026-08-27.md`, indexed in `story-bible/open-questions.md`. All four readings confirmed by Dermot the same day. Second direction, same day, ruled the craft question the realization had left open: a pure fantasy world-system would not survive the transition — the RPG-structured layer's fate at Dock Seven is **lost or downgraded, not held**, with the mechanism (the preserver's archival idiom filters what is preserved; enacted things cross only as their own record) and the grief register worked through in the intake and the arc note; distilled line proposed into `story-bible/life-lessons.md`. No canon touched by the ruling — the published pastoral interior already shows the downgrade.
- **[Tissadelle Shepherd](src/characters/tissadelle-shepherd.md) gains "The inner world" section** (2026-08-27, after the readings were confirmed). The shared interior structured — not merely dressed — as a high-fantasy role-playing game (named places with rules, party-held roles, quests, earned advancement), stated on the system's own account; the architecture as the inside view of "different members front in different roles"; Tobble's deeper subsystem far more ordered and scientific — depth as structure, never standing. Spoiler-guarded (no IWD/noögenics/Dock Seven on the page); the arc-side half in `story-bible/tissadelle-arc-s6-7.md`, and one craft question (the RPG layer's fate at Dock Seven) deliberately open in `story-bible/open-questions.md`. Extension under the canon-stability rule; approved by Dermot the same day.
- **The burnt-out leader, not the corrupt politician — direction recorded** (2026-08-26). Dermot's direction rejecting the corrupt-politician trope while claiming the burnt-out leader; verbatim capture, canon survey and flagged readings in `story-bible/intake-2026-08-26.md`, theme section in `story-bible/ideas.md`, distilled line in `story-bible/life-lessons.md`, readings indexed in `story-bible/open-questions.md`. Scope ruled same day: minor corruption in minor or supporting characters not ruled out — corruption never the engine of a leader or major figure. No canon touched.
- **The John Smith comparandum and the prayer/magic/Levril-perception direction — recorded** (2026-08-26, same intake). Smith identified as a third figure (the complicit leader, distinct from both poles) in `story-bible/ideas.md`; the prayer direction's canon survey finds three of four assertions already Archive-voice canon. The rendering reading confirmed by Dermot the same day; the proposed `canon_facts` rule (the experience is the fact, never the answered prayer) stays open in `story-bible/open-questions.md`. Complicit-leader scope also ruled same day: a major character could be a complicit leader who repents — in scope, the repentance part of the licence; recorded in `story-bible/ideas.md`. Fourth direction same day: the Church Space overlay may consider the possibility of answered prayer and spiritual voices — three non-Archive homes for an answered prayer (codex, POV experience, overlay), the Archive's refusal unmoved. Both remaining readings confirmed the same day (the reader-test transfers to the overlay; the `canon_facts` rule stands — no entry may assert a prayer was answered, the experience is the fact), and the rule is now a content authoring convention in CLAUDE.md. Everything from the 26 August intake is ruled; the Levrils Who Notices draft remains the one artifact awaiting approval.
- **[Levrils](src/lore/levrils.md) gain a Who Notices section** (2026-08-26, approved by Dermot the same day, after he confirmed the rendering reading). Below enforcement salience, noticing a Levril is rendering work by the witness: reports cluster among the contemplative, devout, and deeply attentive as a fact about practice, never a faculty, with the answered-prayer interpretation pattern explained as a selection effect the record files without adopting; matching Common Misinterpretations bullet. Extension under the canon-stability rule; direction verbatim in `story-bible/intake-2026-08-26.md`.
- **[Neither Author Nor Warden](src/codex/neither-author-nor-warden.md) — codex working paper** (2026-08-25). Kade's companion to the Limitation filing, answering the recurring petition on the design tiers and suffering: the biological-life template neither prevents pain (a template enforces nothing, fastens to no point of design in an authorless system, and holds no outcomes to pre-filter) nor establishes it (shape is specified, implementation is not — nociception filed with DNA as local contingency), with the record's one moral law placed above the design tiers, not at them. No title card yet.
- **[The Courtesy That Was Withdrawn](src/codex/the-courtesy-that-was-withdrawn.md) — codex official document** (2026-08-25). The Tír na nÓg Keeper of the Rolls' minuted standing reply declining the recurring petition for courtesy recognition of ancestral titles, on the burned-once precedent the founders carried with the constitution: the old republic's heralds tried courtesy recognition, certified a pedigree written backwards, and stopped for good. Supplies the history behind the Celtic Union's titles policy; archivist's note cross-references Marked Absences. No title card yet.

- **[The Celtic Union](src/lore/celtic-union-of-planets.md) gains a Titles and honours section** (2026-08-25). The charter confers no titles and its law neither abolishes nor endorses the old ones — nothing conferred, recognised, or taken away — a policy inherited from the old Irish republic's constitution. Completes a three-road taxonomy with the Four Islands (reform by decision) and New London (vacancy by incapacity), and supplies the standing model for how an Expansion-era territorial honour persists unextinguished.
- **`TestingStrategy.md`** (2026-08-24). The test layers, what each gate catches, where each runs (npm test vs CI) and why, the extension rules, and the open items — mechanics only; the authority boundary stays in `CLAUDE.md`.

- **The link and related-term checkers joined `npm test`; contrast and shared-script drift became CI gates** (2026-08-24). `check-internal-links.js` and `check-related-terms.js` now run on every test run; CI additionally runs `generate-themes` + `check-contrast.js` + a git-diff check that no `theme-*.css` was hand-edited, and a shared-scripts job diffing the four shared deploy scripts against `dermot-cochran-photography`'s `main` (which found `cpanel-autopull.sh` already drifted — the 15 August gap-alert default had never landed there; synced in that repo the same day).

- **Unit tests for the content filter and page classifier** (2026-08-24). `npm test` now opens with `node --test test`: `test/content-filter.test.js` pins `lib/content-filter.js`'s narrowing and private-thread opt-in truth tables (including that church-space stays hidden on unfiltered and narrowed builds alike), and `test/classify-content.test.js` pins `classifyContentPath`/`isContentIncluded` with regression tests for the layout-vs-inputPath hazard and the journal fallthrough. Those three functions moved verbatim from `.eleventy.js` into `lib/classify-content.js` to be testable; no behaviour change. Built-in `node:test`, no new dependencies.

- **[The Shape of a Life](src/lore/the-shape-of-a-life.md) — doctrine entry** (2026-08-23, approved by Dermot the same day). Dermot's direction: aliens may have gender; no terrestrial DNA; development need not pass through sexual reproduction or natural selection; the birth-to-death arc is not universal; some civilisations do not hold individual personhood in the Concord's sense. Generalises standing instances (Mnemari, Prismeri, Krenyi, Verdani, plural minds); direction verbatim and readings flagged in `story-bible/intake-2026-08-23.md`. No title card yet.
- **[Plural Minds](src/glossary/plural-minds.md) gains a Responsibility Before the Law section** (2026-08-23, approved by Dermot the same day). Dermot's ruling: joint and collective responsibility for every action of the shared body regardless of who was fronting or co-fronting; sole exception a court finding of dysfunction on a psychiatric diagnosis, with all it carries. Direction verbatim and readings flagged in `story-bible/intake-2026-08-23.md`; a scene draft applying it (Suvra Kel and Sen Lovax POVs) in `story-bible/scene-draft-one-warmth-in-the-room.md`, unpublished per the scene-draft precedent.
- **[Suvra Kel](src/characters/suvra-kel.md) — first named Ilveth character** (2026-08-23). Search-and-rescue specialist, among the first Ilveth in Corps service; the *lanterns that cannot be put out* line attributed to her, with a cross-link added from the Ilveth lore entry. Rendered *she* in the record's translation register. Approved by Dermot 2026-08-23; open ends updated in `story-bible/open-questions.md`. No portrait yet.
- **[The Ilveth (Warm-Eyed)](src/lore/ilveth.md) — new species entry** (2026-08-23). A cold-bodied people of a new world, Sardain, who see warmth as light: thermal night vision grounded in the self-glow constraint (cheap for the cold, impossible for the warm), dry mirror-pit eyes, heat-costed signalling, geothermal industry. Extends the energy-bottleneck set to four answers. Approved by Dermot 2026-08-23; remaining open ends recorded in `story-bible/open-questions.md`. No title card yet.
- **[The Working-Out of Justice](src/journal/the-working-out-of-justice.md) — journal entry** (2026-08-23). Two detective traditions — the brilliant individual as special pleading, the inevitable working-out as the Limitation in genre form — with the finding that the Unfounded countermeasures are the investigative method item for item; kill the lie, leave the person standing. Season 4 application recorded in `story-bible/ideas.md`.
- **[Special Pleading](src/journal/special-pleading.md) — journal entry** (2026-08-23). The cosmology read back as a confession: prayer and magic rejected as special pleading, faith in ultimate goodness kept — good founded, evil not; providence structural, never local; the chooser question left open on both sides of the page.

### Changed

- **The Common Manifold's definition formula corrected to "cross-membrane coherence"** (2026-08-28, Dermot's direction, following the reconciliation above). "Cross-Concordant coherence" misstated the scale — the manifold's work is inter-membrane, and two zones share no Interval — at the four sites carrying the formula: [the manifold lore entry](src/lore/post-eleven-dimensional-manifold.md), [Concordant Membranes](src/lore/concordant-membranes.md), [the glossary entry](src/glossary/common-manifold.md) and the canonical glossary's definition. Migration-map row added, scoped to the formula alone: Telearch/Levril "cross-Concordant" keeps its zone sense, and the registered band name *trans-concordant constraint field* stays, like *post-11*. Two front-matter stragglers of the reconciliation's approved migrations swept in the same pass ("every universe in the Cascade" in the manifold entry's description; "primary universe" in Concordant Membranes' description).
- **Common Manifold cosmology reconciled with the 2026-08-10 surveyed-universes canon** (2026-08-28, drafted for review — draft-and-stop). Three groups of edits, each labelled per the canon-stability rule. (1) *Genuine dilemma resolved* — fold-transit scope: [The Scope of Physical Law](src/lore/the-scope-of-physical-law.md), [FTL Mechanics](src/lore/ftl-mechanics.md), [Higher-Dimensional Folding](src/glossary/higher-dimensional-folding.md), [Concordant Membranes](src/lore/concordant-membranes.md) and the canonical glossary's Flexure/Interval notes no longer state that fold transit runs only inside one universe or that cross-universe contact is never travel — claims Deadwater's certified route and the Counterpane survey (both 2026-08-10) contradicted. Resolved by distinguishing reach across a *standing* Interval (the band rule, unchanged) from fold *adjacency* (separation compressed and released, nothing traverses a gap); the practical instrument floor moves from archecluster to formcluster, with the archecluster floor restated as history the Counterpane survey ended. (2) *Clarification* — "every universe in the Grand Ensemble is seated in it" scoped to the record's reach in [the glossary entry](src/glossary/common-manifold.md), the canonical glossary's definition and [The Grand Ensemble Multiverse](src/lore/ensemble-multiverse.md), matching the manifold lore entry's own Formwright-tier position (2026-08-01). Two migration-map rows added. (3) *Clarification* — "primary universe" corrected to the settled coherence criterion in the [Common Manifold](src/glossary/common-manifold.md) and [Interval](src/glossary/interval.md) glossary entries, applying the existing 2026-07-29 migration row.
- **[The Cosmic Cascade](src/lore/cosmic-cascade.md)'s no-moral-cosmology invariant clarified** (2026-08-25, Dermot's direction: the limitation does not imply the Cascade is immoral or amoral). The bullet now states its own scope — morality as mechanism ruled out, moral character not adjudicated: no tier administers virtue or sin, the design tiers are agents whose abstention is a choice, the record's asymmetry (founded things by design, the Unfounded by nothing, the one moral law bounding evil alone) stands, and operational silence is the cost of an open future, not indifference. A clarification under the canon-stability rule: says better what the corpus already held.
- **[Sir Galahad Thorne](src/characters/galahad-thorne.md)'s territorial honour given a kind** (2026-08-25). One clause on the character page: an old Earth-descended grant of the Expansion's leaving — kind only, territory and date still unnamed. Heads off the reader inference that the "Sir" is a Kingdom of the Four Islands knighthood, which the contact timeline and the Old Houses' hereditary peerage cannot support.

### Fixed

- **The Commissioned Standing lore entry retitled "Commissioned Standing: What the Gate Grants"** (2026-08-25), clearing the duplicate-title warning against the glossary entry per the FTL Mechanics pattern (glossary keeps the bare term, lore gets the subtitle). Title only; no `related:` list named it and inline links are URL-based, so no sweep needed.

## [1.23.0] — 2026-08-22

A release with a survey at its centre. The planetary-physics set — a dozen
entries, from weather and tides to soils and night skies, with *Coasts, and
Other Edges* as its capstone — walks the same physics across every kind of
ground the habitable worlds have, and six of those pages now carry Dermot's
own photographs, re-filed from the portfolio. Beside it, the constitutional
thread arrived whole: the Enrolled Text, the Amendment Atlas, and Ilsabet
Corren, who wrote it.

The other half of the release is the editions growing into readers: a reader
profile and style guide per edition, a hero cast per edition, presentation
modes a reader can override for themselves, and a domain strategy that names
which site carries which signal — each arriving with the check (contrast,
hero casts, the URL a layout actually emits) that keeps it from failing
silently. The portrait backlog closed too: `PORTRAIT PENDING` is gone from
the cast.

### Added

- **[Tides Without Shores](src/lore/tides-without-shores.md) gets its image — Dermot's own photograph** (2026-08-22). `lore/shoreless-sea.jpg`: the portfolio's *Sunset at Sea* as a radical left crop losing the ship's deck entirely — open water to a pink horizon with two distant vessels hull-down, kept because on a shoreless ocean the only witnesses are afloat. *Where the Water Was* judged unusable for the soils page on a second look (litter across the best texture); reason and upgrade path recorded in `story-bible/images.md`.
- **Four planetary-physics entries get images — Dermot's own photographs, re-filed from his portfolio** (2026-08-22). [Stone, Fire, and Ice](src/lore/stone-fire-and-ice.md) takes `volcanic-strata.jpg` (cropped to the strata alone, removing a guardrail and fence — scale deliberately unreadable); [Coasts, and Other Edges](src/lore/coasts-and-other-edges.md) takes `cloud-sea.jpg` (a cloud sea with ridges standing out of it — the entry's "shoreline between atmospheres"); [The Ledger and the Truce](src/lore/the-ledger-and-the-truce.md) takes `grassland-storm-tree.jpg` (one tree in dry grassland under a storm sky — the truce with its enforcer arriving); [The Forest Is Waiting](src/lore/the-forest-is-waiting.md) takes `drowned-forest.jpg` (the century-bet lost). Selection survey and provenance in `story-bible/images.md`.
- **[Rivers Old, Lakes Young](src/lore/rivers-old-lakes-young.md) gets its image — Dermot's own photograph** (2026-08-22). `lore/young-lake-margin.jpg`: a flooded lakeshore in February light, bare trees standing in the shallows, gorse in flower on the drowned bank — a young lake's margin as the entry defines one. Cropped and resized from his D3100 original; provenance recorded in `story-bible/images.md`.
- **The About page's fan-works section notes its first fan work** (2026-08-22). A "Noted" paragraph applies the licence's standing *referenced, not endorsed* formula to [tissadelleshepherd/star-rangers](https://github.com/tissadelleshepherd/star-rangers), a fan fork whose one addition is an uncaptioned AI-generated image evidently intended as an off-duty Tissadelle Shepherd. A reference only — it confers no status, and the identification is recorded as the maker's, not the record's.
- **[What the Stones Say](src/codex/what-the-stones-say.md) — the first Quernish document in the record** (2026-08-21). A codex entry in a settler's own voice: the address line-keeper Odal Ferren gives a watcher standing a first rain-watch, taken down under the lore entry's transcription arrangement. Valid-for-its-author throughout; it keeps the Hush absence marked from inside (what is held is said at carryings, never to the record) and is the in-world source of the "the stones say where the rain is, not where it is going" reply the lore entry quotes. Cross-linked from Quern's Balance or Collapse section and See also.
- **[Quern](src/lore/planets/quern.md) — a tidally locked world in a new Kiln System, settled along its storm belt** (Dermot's direction, 2026-08-21, two pitches). One face a standing rock-vapour storm over a substellar melt, the other a volatile cold trap ending in nitrogen snowfields, and between them the Millrace — a permanent terminator shear belt of horizontal rain with the lightning inside it. A small independent human settlement lives at the belt's night-ward edge: wind-scooped architecture, baseload power from the inter-hemisphere temperature gradient, air electrolysed from the rain, and a calendar (the Breathing, kept by eye against turning-stones) set by the belt's quasi-periodic ~3-year walk — a QBO-analogue, not orbital mechanics. Settler cosmology divides the world into the Burn, the Howl and the Hush, filed at Archive distance; the surveyors' names (the Glazing, the Meal) are kept alongside. Grounded in real lava-world and atmospheric-collapse physics under the standing hard-SF default; whether the atmosphere is in equilibrium or slow collapse is deliberately left unadjudicated in-world on the two-readings pattern, with the settlement's turning-stone records as the longest baseline on the question. Self-registers in `/atlas/`. No image yet.
- **[Habitable, for Whom](src/lore/habitable-for-whom.md) — humanly habitable worlds versus the wider habitable category** (Dermot's direction, 2026-08-22). Tenth of the planetary-physics set, and the taxonomy the other entries were quietly leaning on. **Habitability is a relation, not a property**: unqualified, the record allows *habitable* one meaning — bears its own biosphere — while the class people actually mean, **the full human envelope occurring naturally**, holds Earth and Tír na nÓg and nothing else, with Drithane at the envelope's edge (acclimatisation, agriculture under glass) and Kernowek Reach's merely-survivable native air farther out. Each species carries an **envelope** (gravity, atmosphere, temperature, chemistry, light), and the envelope is a different fact from the frame — the near-humanoid Pandoids' home would kill an unprotected human, so *humanoid-habitable* is the loose phrase the survey gently declines: the accurate index is the species, never the shape. The symmetry is canon's own: no alien people is natively compatible with Earthlike parameters, so **nobody's envelope is the universe's default** and *hostile* is as unfinished a sentence as *habitable* — Meridian is somebody's mild world. Consequences drawn: meetings happen in rooms somebody built; human settlement is mostly envelope manufacture; and Tír na nÓg's standing gets its doctrinal name — the one ground where *habitable for humans* finishes without an asterisk.
- **[The Star Rangers Survey Corps](src/lore/star-rangers-survey-corps.md) — the Corps and its branches** (Dermot's direction, 2026-08-22). The record's most-quoted institution gets its page, organised around the branches he named — the **Archive** (custodian of the record, named for an institution older and larger than the Corps), **Planetology** (ground: rates wearing the costume of places), **Meteorology** (the fluid envelopes, atmospheres and oceans as one subject), **Ecology** (who lives there; *habitable for*, never bare *habitable*) — plus the Academy page's existing Xenolinguistics branch, under the Academy's own open-list rule. The soil file deliberately carries two branches' stamps; the collect/explain seam with the Science Corps is restated per-branch. Science Corps page's inline Survey Corps link re-pointed here from the codex protocol.
- **[Ilsabet Corren](src/characters/ilsabet-corren.md) — a character page for the Amendment Atlas's author** (Dermot's direction, 2026-08-22). The Institute's Fellow in Comparative Records: institutions' registers read as instrument logs. One new commitment beyond her paper — her method's origin in exercising Schedule C's verification clause as an elector and finding the discrepancy was her own arithmetic; the count was right, the exercise measured her. World of origin, family and age left as marked absences. Her signature and Sen's in the Atlas codex entry now link to their character pages. Closes the second of the 22 August draft's open questions; the Atlas-drawing hook stays open.
- **[The External Codex](src/journal/the-external-codex.md) — journal entry on the constitutional material's real-world provenance** (Dermot's direction, 2026-08-22). References his 2013 PhD thesis, *Formal Specification and Analysis of Danish and Irish Ballot Counting Algorithms* (IT University of Copenhagen), as the formal-methods source behind Schedule C, the Verification Doctrine and the Enrolled Text — cited in the Journal's out-of-character layer only, never in-universe, under the *referenced, not filed* rule.
- **Glossary mirrors [Enrolled Text](src/glossary/enrolled-text.md) and [Difference Form](src/glossary/difference-form.md)** (Dermot's direction, 2026-08-22). Short forms of the two load-bearing terms from the Enrolled Text lore entry, on the `commissioned-standing` mirror pattern — `short` and `plain` summaries, mutual `related:` links, filed under the glossary's `Records` category — asserting nothing beyond the merged doctrine. Titles drop the leading article so the lore and glossary pages stay distinctly reachable by exact title. Closes the last of the three open questions the 22 August draft recorded.
- **[The Thin Inheritance](src/lore/the-thin-inheritance.md) and [The Honest Dark](src/lore/the-honest-dark.md) — soils and night skies** (Dermot's direction, 2026-08-22), completing the planetary-physics set at eleven, **plus the moon and glacier placements the set had left open**. Soils: the one substance needing stone, water, life and time together — *soil is the mountain on its way to the sea, paused; a field is a queue* — with Winterbourne's parish strips as a polity drawn on a soil profile, Difenland's terraces as detention engineering, the Abbeylands as soil-as-heirloom, Trígrian's deep ash as violence feeding what life makes, Fliade's *mineral-sharp* surface as the negative case, and soil as the fourth natural archive with an asterisk: the one its keepers eat. Night skies: dark by default on every settled world because the technology does not shine (What the Record Refuses, applied upward) — Drithane's timetabled drithle, Prismere's instrument-sky, Trígrian's negotiated night, and New Cotswolds' sky holding the Milky Way as an object: *the only settlement whose night sky contains everyone else, and the oldest stale file anyone looks at*. **Placements**: Tír na nÓg's canonical tidal flats get their raiser — a single large moon the founders declined to rename, **An Ghealach** — Drithane's image-canonical low bright moon, polar ice and walking snowline are stated in prose, and Aethelrock's glens are ice-cut, its glaciers long finished: *an old world even in this*.
- **[The Enrolled Text](src/lore/the-enrolled-text.md) — how settled space keeps its constitutional law** (Dermot's direction, 2026-08-22). The Concord compact as a founding enrolment (Tycho, 2543 UCSD) that is never edited in place, plus every amendment since in **difference form** — strike/insert against a named state of the text, laid open for objection, certified to apply cleanly, enrolled beside its predecessors and never over them. The current text is a derivation any reader may re-perform, which is why the compact outlasted its enforcers: custody can be seized, re-derivability cannot. Defeated and withdrawn proposals stay on the register as the law's null results. Cross-linked from the Concord entry's See Also.
- **[The Amendment Atlas: A Proposal](src/codex/the-amendment-atlas.md)** (Dermot's direction, 2026-08-22). A visiting working paper by a new Institute fellow, Ilsabet Corren, proposing to read the compact's three centuries of enrolled amendments as survey data — four charts: the boundary of the person over time, the lag between a correction first argued and enrolled, the never-amended still core, and enrolment density by era — with plural registration as the worked figure and the method's limit as its caption (*the record's line, not the people's*). Sen's shelf comment is filed beside it: favourable, two conditions. Proposed in-universe, not built — a story hook, not a settled fact.
- **[Where the Weather Stops](src/lore/where-the-weather-stops.md) — caves and the underground on habitable worlds** (Dermot's direction, 2026-08-21). Ninth of the planetary-physics set. Opens on Fliade's own survey lesson made standing policy — the underground is the one country a survey cannot read from orbit, and a surface survey says so on its cover. **The slow room**: depth silences the set's doctrines one by one, and a deep cave's held temperature is the surface climate's mean — the third sibling of the natural archives (the glacier keeps the years frozen in order, the tree alive in order, the cave keeps only the answer). **Three chemistries make caves** — dissolution (Winterbourne's spring line as karst-in-progress), fire (lava tubes under Kernowek and Veyr-3), and neither (Aethelrock's granite verdict: nearly caveless) — so a cave inventory is readable from a geology map. **The quiet has tenants**, and the census makes the thesis: Fliade's chemistry-fed biosphere, the Anstolik walking to a schedule nobody set, the Pandoids keeping a spoken archive in the one environment constant enough to trust a memory to, the Martian pressure-hermitages, and the Cavern Constraint's quantum computers — *the underground's one export is constancy, and every tenant is a customer for it*. Closes the loop: a cave mouth is a coast, and the underground is the country almost no survey finishes.
- **[The Cost of the Crossing](src/lore/the-cost-of-the-crossing.md) — islands and archipelagos on habitable worlds** (Dermot's direction, 2026-08-21). Eighth of the planetary-physics set. **What makes an island is not the water but the crossing** — insularity measured in crossing-cost, not kilometres. **An archipelago is a mountain range that lost the argument** once the sea joined in: the Four Islands as a caldera rim's surviving summits, Thalassa's shoals as islands that failed by metres, Saltmere as the completed judgement — a world where every candidate island lost, which is the geological reading of why its civilisation brought its own ground. **Isolation is a laboratory**, with the Kingdom's lost colony as the worked case — not a survival despite isolation but what isolation is *for*, seen from the far side — and crossing-cost writing archipelago politics as enforced specialisation. **The record's driest islands never touch a sea**: Ynys Wydrin's domes (an island whose sea is the sky, in its own name), Kernowek's moored band of air, Fliade's warm caverns, and habitats as the pattern at its purest — New London as the island preservation effect with a station-keeping budget. Closes on the record's most important island being a planet: Tír na nÓg, the catalogue's one walkable world, named fittingly for an island out of myth.
- **[Coasts, and Other Edges](src/lore/coasts-and-other-edges.md) — coasts and coastlines on habitable worlds** (Dermot's direction, 2026-08-21). Seventh of the planetary-physics set and its capstone. Opens on survey doctrine: the Corps records no coastline length, because the figure depends on the ruler — every coastal measurement is stamped with its scale. The coast is the one landform whose rates run at human speed (the argument between land and sea, held daily, with the tide as the clock), and the address every settlement wants — an interface being two economies with one address, run to its limit by the Four Islands, a kingdom that is nearly nothing but coast. The definition-benders were all waiting in canon: Saltmere and Thalassa have **zero natural coastline** and are coastal civilisations anyway, their entire shore the engineered perimeter of their own hulls; the **Pelagene Littoral** rotate the concept ninety degrees, a boundary-layer people whose littoral runs horizontally through the water column; Kernowek's Cloud Line is a shoreline between atmospheres; Fliade's cavern mouths are its beaches. Closes the set on the record's own naming — *Threshold*, *Causeway*, *edge behavior*, *thin places* — the coast as the everyday rehearsal for the edges the record exists to watch, claimed as an observation about vocabulary, not metaphysics.
- **[The Forest Is Waiting](src/lore/the-forest-is-waiting.md) — forests and woodlands on habitable worlds** (Dermot's direction, 2026-08-21). Sixth of the planetary-physics set, completing the biome coverage. The tension that organises it: a forest is the **default** cover of watered land — Winterbourne's twice-recorded reversion is the proof nothing needs to plant it — and simultaneously a **bet** that the next century will resemble this one, which is why Trígrian's canonical *no forests* is a correct price rather than a poverty (grass bets a season; a tree bets a century). A canopy builds its own building and partly waters itself — Verdance's canopy belt as the full expression, with the Canopy Concord's cities built *into* the structure; Winnow Hanger's mist-combing wood as the working end, a wood as a water instrument. Trees keep the living half of the archive the glaciers keep frozen — same annual bookkeeping, alive while it records — with Vellamar's dynasty-old specimen trees as the witnesses. The strange woods are held apart: glasswood is genuinely a wood doing a second job; a dryadic grove is boundary apparatus wearing woodland's shape, and filing one as forestry mis-files a layer.
- **[The Ledger and the Truce](src/lore/the-ledger-and-the-truce.md) — deserts and grasslands on habitable worlds** (Dermot's direction, 2026-08-21). Fifth of the planetary-physics set. **A desert is a line in a water ledger, not a temperature** — the driest surface in the settled record (Fliade's) is among its coldest, since frozen water pays no bills — and every desert carries the signature of the doctrine that made it: rain shadow (mountains), continental distance (weather), permafrost (freshwater), Aspenar's mineral extreme. Deserts are precise rather than empty, with the Serephine Dunekin as the worked case — a civilisation run on the one resource a desert has in surplus, contrast — and the Monasteries of Mars as the desert-hermit instinct carried to a desert no Earth hermit ever had. **A grassland is a truce between desert and forest, and something has to enforce it**: fire on Trígrian, teeth on Winterbourne (the turf's reversion is on record twice), climate itself on Verdance's steppe, whose herding ecologies answer with the grassland's characteristic politics — movement over territory. Closes the set's arc: biomes, like mountains, are rates wearing the costume of places, and a map of either is dated the day it is drawn.
- **[Stone, Fire, and Ice](src/lore/stone-fire-and-ice.md) — mountains, volcanoes and glaciers on habitable worlds** (Dermot's direction, 2026-08-21). Fourth of the planetary-physics set, and terrain read as three verbs caught mid-sentence. **A mountain is a rate** — uplift against erosion, with Aethelrock's granite highlands as mountains in retirement, the exposed roots of ranges nobody will ever see. **A volcano is the interior still speaking** — the record's most varied hazard: Kernowek Reach settled *on* its volcano because altitude was the resource, the Four Islands live inside a volcano's afterlife, Fliade takes the heat as landlord, and the Veyr Basaltborn were handed metallurgy for nothing. **A glacier is the archive nobody kept** — annual layers sealing each year's air, a climate record begun before any charter and maintained without staff; glaciers had zero prior mentions in the corpus, so this is the set's one genuinely new subject, introduced doctrine-first with no ice asserted for any named world. Trígrian's canonical *no polar caps* becomes the eloquent exception: the world whose climate most needs remembering keeps no ice memory of it. Includes a preventive terminology note distinguishing geological faults from Etheric fault lines before that collision happens.
- **[Rivers Old, Lakes Young](src/lore/rivers-old-lakes-young.md) — freshwater on Tír na nÓg and the other habitable worlds** (Dermot's direction, 2026-08-21). Third of the planetary-physics set. The thesis pair: a **river** is the oldest unbuilt infrastructure a world has — the integral of climate over topography, a record you can walk along — and a **lake** is news, recent violence or active tending, so a landscape can be aged from orbit by counting them. Tír na nÓg reads as both ages stacked by altitude (patient lowland wetlands, upland falls in spate). Groundwater: the well as a settlement's handshake with water it cannot see, Winterbourne's spring line as the handshake offered in a line, Fliade as the limit case whose hydrology has no surface chapter at all, and Aoife's well-water blessing crossing as living observance. One air-readable diagnostic synthesised from existing canon: ordinary treelines trace the drainage, **dryadic groves trace the Etheric fault lines and ignore the valley** — on Tír na nÓg, whether trees follow the river is the difference between botany and boundary cartography. Warm wells handled in scope: a warm spring has a heat source, geothermal common, boundary physics lawful where a flexure runs close; the two famous wells' warmth is instrument-grade fact and the *meanings* stay filed in the Warm-Edge Correlation.
- **[Tides Without Shores](src/lore/tides-without-shores.md) — currents and tides on the water worlds** (Dermot's direction, 2026-08-21). Sequel to *Weather on Other Worlds*, same discipline below the waterline. Two derivations do the work: **a current needs a wall** — no landmass means no basins and no boundary currents, so every current on Saltmere is the circumpolar kind, Earth's one anomaly become the whole regime; and **a tide needs a shore to be seen** — on a shoreless ocean the tide is a planetary heave nobody has ever watched, felt only in mooring tension, so Saltmere's founders knew their star moved their ocean *only* through telemetry, reversing the oldest fact in human science. Draws on canon already in place: the survey's own "too deep to break the surface at any tide", Saltmere's tide-*like* platform cycle, Venice's foundation "that no longer cared what the water did" inherited by Thalassa, and the Four Islands as the with-shores counter-case — where the Tideward Sisterhood's "it has never once failed to come" is cited as the one subject on which the devotional and mechanical readings walk in step. No moons asserted for any world: which raisers a world answers to stays a line in its survey file.
- **[Weather on Other Worlds](src/lore/weather-on-other-worlds.md)** (Dermot's direction, 2026-08-21). The record's doctrine on alien and remote-world weather, synthesised from what per-planet canon already held rather than invented: same physics on different numbers, with the Four Islands' storm-lock, Saltmere's landfall-less storms, Trígrian's three-sun burning seasons, Drithane's dry clear skies and Winterbourne's spring line as the worked examples. Two consequences drawn out: **the sky is local** — no FTL communication means no interstellar weather service, forecasting is locally kept continuity, and the local record outranks the transit-lagged survey file (Prismere's sky-reading treated as instrumentation being the limit case); and across Mediarch realms the *parameter ranges* themselves are lawfully scoped, so another realm's weather is ordinary weather on untabulated numbers. Closes with the refusals: **no storm is sent** — the pathetic fallacy is a figure of speech in every jurisdiction and a mechanism in none, with the Warm-Edge Correlation cited as the attributed Codex reading — and managed weather (Kernowek Reach) is still weather.
- **[Commissioned Standing](src/lore/commissioned-standing.md) — a commissioned mind is not property** (Dermot's direction, 2026-08-21). Lore entry plus a [glossary mirror](src/glossary/commissioned-standing.md): a system commissioned *as a mind* acquires standing at the gate — not saleable, not scrappable, for age or obsolescence or a discontinued line. The standing rides on the commission rather than any later measurement, so a mind's inner life is never re-litigated at an owner's convenience; withdrawal from service exists for cause, through process, and is never a disposal instruction. This is the deeper reason classic units like [Xenon](src/characters/xenon.md) and [Lucene-9000](src/characters/lucene-9000.md) continue in service — the kernel page's economics-only explanation is revised to layer standing over economics rather than contradict it. The right is framed as most visible in the jobs that exist because of it: Xenon's repair-indefinitely-make-none licence, the classic-generation certifications, the Eden Warden's welfare authority. Does not attach to the uncommissioned, which `glossary/uncommissioned.md` now names as part of why the found-mind custody question is hard.
- **[The Kept Line](src/characters/the-kept-line.md) — a Dragon, the Levril subclass that had no worked example** (Dermot's direction, 2026-08-20). The corpus had a Higher Levril ([the Turquoise Dove](src/characters/turquoise-dove.md)) and nothing for the other half of the split. Filed by signature per the lore entry's own rule — named for an inverted anomaly, a containment edge that stops drifting when every model says it should. Arrives during an event where the Dove arrives after; never recorded speaking, mentoring or selecting a Champion. Whether it was at Dock Seven is left unanswered: the function and occasion match, no signature survives, and the entry says that establishes nothing. Uses *it* because no witness has supplied it a figure — the pronoun follows the evidence, not the entity.
- **sciencefiction.site carries the story's people** (2026-08-21, Dermot's ruling). A `characters: [...]` list of every `povs` id used by the seasons its two threads own that has a character page — the general-tier domain had been publishing every chapter and none of the people in them, because characters are matched by id or tag and never by season the way chapters are. **114 shown pages → 244; 0 character pages → 16.** Its hero cast is drawn from the same list and deliberately differs from the canonical domain's.
- **A hero cast per edition** (2026-08-21, Dermot's direction). `starquest` gains Larsen, Albercombe, Voss, Calloway and Jeeves; `fellowship` Asteria and Brother Fintan; `fellowship-archive` Asteria alone; `church-space` Brother Fintan alone; `default` swaps Elvira (no portrait) for Tissadelle, the arc's protagonist and previously absent from the cast fronting the canonical domain. `pets` is unchanged — it already had one. **Six of the seven editions now render a hero slideshow, against two before.**
- **`validate-content.js` checks every edition's hero cast against the corpus and that edition's own filter.** A `heroCharacterIds` entry that names no page, names one with no `image:`, or names a character the edition filters out now fails the build; an edition whose pool is empty warns instead, since that is a fact about the domain rather than a mistake in the list.

- **A reader-side reading-mode switcher** (2026-08-21, Dermot's direction). A "Reading" control in the site header lets a reader override the domain's presentation mode for themselves — the edition's own setting plus Standard, Large print, Compact and Spacious. Client-local and nothing else: one `localStorage` key, per-origin, never sent anywhere, and absent entirely with JS off. [`src/js/presentation.js`](src/js/presentation.js) builds and drives it; the restore is an inline `<head>` script in [`base.njk`](src/_includes/base.njk), since a deferred file would let the page paint in one mode and jump to another. `PRESENTATION_MODES` gains a reader-facing `label` beside its engine `summary` — a reader picks a type size, not an allegiance to another edition.
- **`validate-content.js` now checks the URL a layout emits for `image:`**, not only that the file exists somewhere under `src/images/`. The existing check matches on basename so a partial path can resolve; this one rebuilds `<category>/<value>` exactly as the five image-bearing layouts do.

- **Presentation modes — a third axis beside edition and theme** (2026-08-21). `PRESENTATION_MODES` in [`lib/editions.js`](lib/editions.js) registers four postures — `story`, `primer` (undercover-pets.com), `archive` (fellowshipoflight.site), `contemplative` (fellowshipoflight.org, church-space.site) — implemented as `:root` custom-property overrides in [`src/css/main.css`](src/css/main.css), keyed off a `data-presentation` attribute `base.njk` writes onto `<html>`. Identity, palette and posture are now three independent things. No `deploy.conf` key and no deploy plumbing: the mode rides into the build with `EDITION`. `validateEditions` fails on an unregistered mode and on a registered mode `main.css` never implements. Reasoning and a reader profile per edition: `story-bible/edition-reader-profiles.md`.
- **`story-bible/edition-reader-profiles.md`** (2026-08-21) — one profile per edition (who arrives, what they came for, what loses them) and the style guide that follows: the three axes, the house floor, the mode token table, per-edition page counts measured that day, and five open questions indexed in `open-questions.md`.
- **[`scripts/check-contrast.js`](scripts/check-contrast.js)** (2026-08-21) — checks every palette against WCAG 2.2 AA (4.5:1) on the pairs `main.css` actually composes, including hover states and `--color-surface-2`. Outside `npm test` because it reads the generated theme files. `solarized` is exempt, with the reason in the script.
- **A coverage check in `scripts/generate-themes.js`** (2026-08-21) — fails if `main.css`'s `:root` and `ROOT_KEY_ORDER` disagree. A property added to one and not the other was silently dropped from all eight generated themes: correct in local dev, wrong on every branded domain.

- **A candidate subdomain list** in `story-bible/domain-strategy-and-duplicate-content.md` (Dermot's direction, 2026-08-20), with measured indexable/codex/lore/character counts for eight faction filters plus two utility subdomains. Recorded because the codex-site idea otherwise reads as an argument for buying domains: a subdomain costs nothing, needs no registrar, and resolves cleanly against the registry (verified). Two limits stated with it — a codex subdomain serves a subset of its parent's pages so it canonicals there and will not rank, and a subdomain protects no name, so it complements the anti-squatting registrations rather than replacing them.
- **A domain registered as an alias now gets a one-page redirect deployment instead of a refused deploy** (Dermot's direction, 2026-08-20). `deploy_alias_notice()` in [`scripts/cpanel-deploy.sh`](scripts/cpanel-deploy.sh) renders three files from `scripts/alias-notice/`: an `.htaccess` 301ing the whole namespace to the target with path and query preserved (`/.well-known/` exempt for AutoSSL), an `index.html` carrying `rel=canonical` and a meta refresh for hosts without `mod_rewrite`, and a `robots.txt` that deliberately does **not** `Disallow` — a crawler has to fetch the URLs to see the redirect and consolidate them. Runs with `rsync --delete` so the previous full build is removed, and needs no Node, Eleventy or build step. Replaces the refusal added earlier the same day, which was safe but did nothing: a refused deploy leaves the stale full build serving, so the duplicate survived until someone opened cPanel. **The consolidation is now real from the first deploy** and the cPanel repoint is tidying rather than a prerequisite.
- **`ALIASES` in [`lib/editions.js`](lib/editions.js), and `cpanel-deploy.sh` refuses to build a registered alias.** The eleven alias hosts move from prose in a comment to a checked map; `validateEditions` rejects a host that is both an alias and a served domain, or an alias pointing at a domain no edition builds. The deploy fails on either path with an error naming both fixes. **Third-party forks and independent deployments are explicitly unaffected** — the check keys off a *named* alias, not off "unknown to this registry", so a fork on its own domain still deploys the full site with the two-key minimum `deploy.conf`, as `FORKING.md` promises. Replaces the identity check added hours earlier, which refused any unconfigured domain and would have broken exactly that path.
- **`cpanel-deploy.sh` refuses to deploy a domain nothing has given an identity.** If a domain is absent from `lib/editions.js` *and* `deploy.conf` sets no `THEME`, `SITE_NAME`, `CHARACTERS`, `TOPICS` or `THREADS`, the deploy now fails loudly instead of silently building the **full unfiltered site** — 566 indexable pages rather than a narrowed clone's 60–90, unbranded, self-canonicalling, with its own 443-URL sitemap. Deployed to a domain meant to be an alias that is a brand-new duplicate of the canonical site, reported as a success. Two ways in, both of which happened on 2026-08-20: removing a domain from the registry while its `ALT_DOMAINS` build is still configured server-side (the alias demotions below need a cPanel change the merge cannot perform), and an editing accident dropping an edition entry. Checked before `THEME` is defaulted, since afterwards a domain that chose the main palette is indistinguishable from one nobody configured.
- **`ranksAt` in [`lib/editions.js`](lib/editions.js): one domain per tier family carries the ranking signal.** A non-ranking domain emits a cross-domain `rel=canonical` at the same path instead of a self-canonical, and drops its sitemap entries and robots.txt `Sitemap:` line to match; `og:url` stays self-referential. `validateEditions` fails the build on a `ranksAt` no edition claims, and on a ranking domain whose filters are not a superset of a sibling's. Threaded registry → `resolve-edition.js` → `cpanel-deploy.sh` → `SITE_RANKS_AT` → `site.js` → `base.njk`. Prompted by Search Console duplicate-content reports — the fellowship and church-space editions were serving the identical 62 indexable pages from six domains. Background, measurements and the two remaining decisions: `story-bible/domain-strategy-and-duplicate-content.md`.
- **A build now has to pass a written test, and four domains failed it.** An independent build is justified only when it has its own page set (framing alone fails), its own reason to be searched for, and asserts nothing the central record does not. `fellowshipoflight.online`, `fellowshipoflight.space`, `church-space.online` and `starquest.online` are cPanel aliases now rather than builds — eleven hostnames, seven builds.
- **`fellowship-archive` — the first codex site, at `fellowshipoflight.site`.** The Fellowship's own comparative archive: `topics: ["fellowship-of-light", "arilon"]` and deliberately **no** thread, which is what makes it a codex site rather than a fourth reader of the same story. 59 indexable pages, 6 codex entries and 3 lore entries of its own, against 0 for the chapter-house framing it replaces. Canon-safe by construction — the Codex is already valid-for-its-author — with one hard limit: a codex site is a filtered view of the central codex, never a domain with entries of its own. `fellowship` widens to the same topics so it stays a superset of its sibling.
- **The contemplative tier is two families, split by institution.** Fellowship of Light (`fellowship`, `fellowship-archive`) ranks at `fellowshipoflight.org`; Communion of the Called (`church-space`) is a family of one. A **family is not a tier**: a tier is a readership, a family is a set of domains serving the same pages that must consolidate on one host.
- **`starquest.online` demoted from a build to a cPanel alias of `starquest.site`**, under the rule that settled the duplicate-content question: a registration defends the name, a build has to earn its keep. The orbital-five-o thread is one task force and Season 4 is one chapter, so there was no second face to give it. Returns the young-adult tier to a family of one.
- **[New Cotswolds](src/lore/new-cotswolds.md) — a human settlement in another galaxy** (Dermot's direction, 2026-08-20). Limestone village country in the **Wolds End** galaxy, founded from the [New London Space Habitat](src/lore/new-london-space-habitat.md). Grounded in two established constraints rather than invented reach: fold transit is *geography, not distance* (an admissible corridor makes a galaxy reachable where a near star without one is not), and there is **no FTL communication**, so the file is ninety-one years stale and the Archive declines to write it in the present tense. The mirror of Winterbourne — there the intent is unrecoverable, here it is a filed document.
- **[Greenward](src/lore/greenward-habitat.md) and [The Guest Ring](src/lore/the-guest-ring.md) — a reciprocal habitat instrument** (Dermot's direction, 2026-08-20). A human ring above Federation [Verdance](src/lore/planets/verdance.md), a Federation ring above Celtic Union [Drithane](src/lore/planets/drithane.md), one page-and-a-half instrument, and three ways it is less symmetrical than it reads — most usefully that the Rangers hold **no planetary jurisdiction** and so had no world to trade, making a two-party document with three parties on one side. The shared non-descent clause is one sentence covering two different facts: protocol at Verdance, chemistry at Drithane.
- **[Habitats and the Worlds Beneath Them](src/lore/habitats-and-the-worlds-beneath-them.md)** (Dermot's direction, 2026-08-20). States the general principle the two rings are instances of: a habitat manufactures its own environment, so **the species it supports is a fact about the habitat and not about the world it orbits**, orbit is chosen for access rather than compatibility, and a ring above a world is not a claim on it. Includes why the contrary assumption is near-universal — everyone learns habitats at Sol, where all six happen to be human above a human world, and a rule drawn from that sample does not survive first contact.
- **[Winterbourne](src/lore/planets/winterbourne.md) — a chalk-downland world of spring-line villages** (Dermot's direction, 2026-08-20). An agricultural independent in a new **Albion** system: an escarpment, a line of springs at its foot spaced two to three kilometres apart, and a village on every one of them — Ashenden, Nether Wickham, Over Wickham, Chilverstoke, Marlbrook, Bramblecote, Hazelcombe and the market town Downminster, plus Winnow Hanger off the line with a dew pond. The settlement pattern is derived from the hydrogeology rather than decorative, per the standing hard-SF default; whether it was *intended* is left unadjudicated on the three-reading pattern. Self-registers in `/atlas/`. No image yet.
- **The last six portraits, and `PORTRAIT PENDING` is gone from the cast** (2026-08-20) — [Bertram Ashcombe](src/characters/bertram-ashcombe.md), [Demelza Trevithick](src/characters/demelza-trevithick.md), [Imogen Petrakis](src/characters/imogen-petrakis.md), [Rhian Gwynne](src/characters/rhian-gwynne.md), [Sen Lovax](src/characters/sen.md) and [Zara Wayland](src/characters/zara-wayland.md). **Every character page on the site now carries a real image and written alt text.** The candidates had been generated on 18 August and were sitting unfiled; the work was mostly choosing between them against each page rather than making them. **The exception is Bertram Ashcombe, whose prompt was wrong and was fixed.** It asked for *"science-fiction detective setting with a period sensibility"* and stated no era, so the generator kept the period half and dropped the other: both candidates were a Victorian panelled office that could not be a station in 2826. `images.md`'s own rule — *state the era, or the setting defaults to contemporary Earth* — turns out to apply to a stated **sensibility** too, which a generator reads as a setting unless something anchors it. Regenerated with the year, the bulkheads and a window onto the planet; the tailoring and the good humour are his and were kept, so the joke still works — an old-fashioned man in a plainly modern room. Where a pair differed, the one showing the person *at* the work won over the one showing them beside it — Demelza with both hands on the machine she keeps, Rhian with a hand in the wiring — which is the same instinct that made the clan heads land: a portrait that argues from the page beats a portrait that poses in front of it.

- **`-Underlay` on `scripts/make-codex-cover.ps1`** (2026-08-20) — the card compositor. A photograph is centre-cropped to fill the square and scrimmed in the template's navy, **heaviest at the two bands the lettering occupies** (the category line and the title block) and lightest through the middle, then the existing text pass runs over it. **The point is spelling**: an image generator cannot letter a card — the supplied set produced *Healng*, *ooroting*, *aa' Star Rrarles* and *superical* — so the picture is generated wordless and the words are set by the font engine, correct by construction. `-Scrim` is a percentage (default 62) and an underlay turns the motif off unless `-Motif` is passed explicitly, since a motif drawn over a photograph fights it. Underlays should be generated **square**: the crop is centred, so a 16:9 source loses a third of its width and loses it from the edges. Parses clean and the crop and scrim arithmetic are verified against five aspect ratios; **not render-tested**, since the tool is Windows-only and CI has no GDI+.
- **Portraits for the five Aethelrock clan heads** (2026-08-20) — [Cormac Dubhghlas](src/characters/cormac-dubhghlas.md), [Fergus Aonghas](src/characters/fergus-aonghas.md), [Idris Bryneth](src/characters/idris-bryneth.md), [Niamh Ó Ceallaigh](src/characters/niamh-o-ceallaigh.md) and [Rhiannon Ceridwen](src/characters/rhiannon-ceridwen.md), replacing the five `PORTRAIT PENDING` cards with real images and written alt text. Each clan head stands on the ground that gives them their argument — Cormac in his own crop rows, Fergus at the cut of a mine working, Idris on open moor under an arriving squall, Niamh on the fjord quayside, Rhiannon beneath her relay mast — which is the right shape for a dispute that is *about* territory: hand a reader any one of the five and they infer half the page. Filed at the 1200×675 convention rather than the 1600×900 the placeholder cards happened to use.

- **`idris-bryneth`'s prompt corrected, and the portrait regenerated** (2026-08-20). The prompt asked for a herder *"of about sixty"* while the page says he took the headship in 2815 UCSD as **"the youngest clan head on Aethelrock at the time of his inheritance"** — mid-forties against the current 2826. The first run obeyed the prompt and produced a man of seventy who was also near-indistinguishable from Cormac Dubhghlas: same grey beard, same weathered face, same staff, which the generator had added unprompted to both. **Two of five clan heads reading as one man is a real cost when they sit at one table**, so the revision fixes the age and separates the silhouette deliberately — dark close-cropped hair against Cormac's grey beard, and no staff. `story-bible/images.md` carries the reasoning beside the prompt.
- **Saint Aoife's portrait brief, reframed from the *Aoife of Stars* card** (2026-08-20, Dermot's ruling: **keep the concealed face, take the rest**). The card showed her front-lit and facing the viewer, which collides with a constraint adopted 19 August and marked as outranking other briefs — her face stays turned, shadowed or away, because *the record genuinely does not know it, and the page's whole argument is that she never claimed to know what she had seen.* So the brief in `story-bible/images.md` moves from grey overcast daylight to **night**, gains the star field, the moorland horizon and the red hair, and keeps the well, the thorn and the turned face. **Two things from the card deliberately not taken**: the embroidered gown, because ornament argues with a standing built on refusal — the card's colour survives as the colour of the night instead — and any sense that the sky is *doing* something, since a sky that appears active tells the viewer what she saw, which is the one thing seven centuries of record declined to say. The portrait still does not exist: the card cannot be cropped into one (a 479 px art region and the title burned across her shoulders), so it needs generating at 1200×675.

- **Two supplied recordings identified** (2026-08-20, Dermot's direction): the 3:49 is **Slipwave**, the 1:44 is **a muster piece**. Both cards are now unblocked in `story-bible/prompt-sheet.md`, and both raise a canon question a card cannot answer. The Slipwave track makes a **fourth** recording by a band whose catalogue is already characterised — *a handful of habitat-circuit recordings, most of them incomplete or badly mic'd, two are not* — so it fits as one of the handful surfacing later and **cannot** be a polished studio cut from their own era. The muster piece needs its filing to match its sound: the audio is a dense full-band mix with drums, so it is a recording **of** a muster piece rather than one made **at** a muster — a distinction that matters because the anthem's spread is explained by the opposite property, being singable unaccompanied by a room of non-singers. Neither can become a codex entry until **the lyrics are supplied**: a lyric is canon-for-its-author and cannot be derived from a spectrogram.

- **Church Space has a theme of its own** (2026-08-20, Dermot's direction that *Rotational Hum* is site furniture): `src/audio/rotational-hum.m4a`, registered in `lib/editions.js` as **"Ambient drone"**. Those domains registered no `themeAudio` and fell through to the default's Celtic ambient — **an omission rather than a decision**, and this was the only edition that could take a new theme without displacing a track already live. Two precedents set with it and recorded beside the entry: **m4a rather than wav**, a third of the bytes for a decorative footer element; and **a theme may be a piece rather than a loop** — this one runs 4:02 and builds, which survives only because the player is click-to-play behind `preload="none"`, so nobody hears it who did not ask to. If the loop restart ever grates, the fix is a trimmed cut of the same recording rather than a different track.

- **The *Paper Galaxies* fragment is now audible on its own audit page** (2026-08-20). `src/audio/paper-galaxies.m4a` attached to [The Paper Galaxy Audit](src/codex/paper-galaxies-audit-dialogue.md), which already described the artifact it now carries — *a single held frame, a singer before a painted, swirling field of light… audio: one performance, repeating.* No prose added: the entry's framing paragraph already introduced it, so only the player is new. The degraded, lossy, low-resolution provenance is an asset here rather than a defect, which is why this is the one supplied recording that needed no remaking.

- **`story-bible/prompt-sheet.md`** (2026-08-20) — the paste queue. Eight cards to recreate (each generated wordless, titled afterwards), the two recordings the corpus is actually missing, and what is conditional. Derived and disposable by design; the three runbooks stay authoritative.

- **Music is for the live domains** (2026-08-20, Dermot's direction), recorded in `story-bible/music-prompts.md`. Licensing stops being a footnote: **Udio** becomes the recommendation for anything with published lyrics — inpainting protects a canon lyric line, and its rights position is the strongest among tools that can sing — while **MyTunes stays the sketchpad and stops being the delivery path**, since a consumer app's terms are the wrong ground for audio served from five domains.

- **Prompts split into app-sized fields, and tool guidance for both media** (2026-08-20). Every music brief is now six short lines — Style, Mood, Instruments, Production, Exclude, Form — because MyTunes, Suno, Udio and the rest take fields rather than paragraphs and weight the front of a box; a one-box paste order is given, with the warning that writing *"no drums"* into a style field is how you get drums. `music-prompts.md` gains a tool table keyed to the job (**Stable Audio** for the four themes, since the spec is a seamless instrumental loop; **Udio** for the two unrecorded songs, because inpainting fixes one mangled canonical line without costing the take, and its licensing is the cleanest of the song generators), plus the note that MyTunes' mp4 wrapper and badge are not the deliverable. `video-prompts.md` gains the same for Grok Imagine — good for roughs and for shots where the subject moves and the camera watches, capped at 720p and weak on the camera control the house signature is almost entirely made of, so **Runway Gen-4.5** for the camera-led scenes and **Veo 3.1** for the material ones. Sora 2 is flagged as deprecated so nothing gets built on it.

- **A regeneration worklist** (2026-08-20) in `story-bible/music-prompts.md` — every supplied file with a separate verdict for its audio and its card, since most have a keepable track inside a container that needs redoing. Seven of ten need only a new card; two already pass.

- **Ten supplied files read and recorded** (2026-08-20). Beyond the six above: *Hold Me Till Dawn*, whose title echoes *Baby Universe*'s published chorus closely enough to need a decision either way; *Aoife of Stars*, **the closest of the cards to the house target** and also the first depiction of a canon character who currently has no portrait at all, so draft-and-stop; and a Grok clip of shuffle dancing that flags a canon question — **low-gravity shuffle dance is marked in the 26 July intake as not existing in canon**, and the clip is full-gravity, which loses the only part that would be worth establishing.

- **`story-bible/video-prompts.md`** (2026-08-20) — the prompt-of-record for moving images, completing the images/audio/video set. Carries the house motion signature (the same three canon anchors as the audio), the **camera-is-a-witness** rule that follows from the corpus having no omniscient narrator, the diegetic-light and no-text-in-frame rules, delivery specs, a twelve-scene library and timed edit plans for two supplied tracks. Records what nothing checks: `src/video/` holds a file referenced nowhere, and `baby-universe.mp4` is 19 MB at 1 fps to show one still. Story-bible only; no published content or media changes.

- **Music direction amended** (2026-08-20, Dermot's direction) in `story-bible/music-prompts.md`: *beautiful, enigmatic, haunting, dramatic*. **Dramatic scopes the target rather than replacing it** — a footer loop and a film are different jobs, so the four edition themes stay deliberately quiet and everything a listener chose to play may build and arrive somewhere. The horror line does not move. Six supplied tracks recorded with their measured structures and their missing prompts, including the finding that **one is the recording already in `src/audio/`, bit-for-bit** (so the Ballad entry's 1:27 claim stands), that two others are previously unseen recordings with no home, and that three band cards contradict Slipwave's canon lineup and register. *Paper Galaxies* is the exception: `paper-galaxies-audit-dialogue.md` already describes that exact artifact — *a single held frame, a singer before a painted, swirling field of light* — so the still-over-audio format has an in-universe reading before it has an excuse.

- **`story-bible/music-prompts.md`** (2026-08-20) — the prompt-of-record for audio, the counterpart to `image-prompts.md`. Carries the house sonic signature (station hum, the *slipwave* detune, a pulse that arrives late), a shared preamble and negative, paste-ready briefs for the four edition themes and the four in-universe recordings, and the boundary rules: the codex entry is the lyric of record, external recordings are never generated, and the Krenyi absence stays unanswered. Records that all five files in `src/audio/` predate the file with no prompt kept, and marks that absence rather than inventing one. Pointers added in `images.md`, `open-questions.md` and CLAUDE.md. Story-bible only; no published content or audio changes.

- **The eight corps badges, designed as a set** (2026-08-19), in [Rank, Insignia, and the Ranger Uniform](src/lore/rank-insignia-and-uniform.md). **Two structural rules keep them clear of rank**: *rank is counted, a corps is singular* — every rank mark is a count of solid elements, every badge is exactly **one outline and never solid**, so a reader who is counting is reading rank; and **a branch sits inside its corps**, drawn within the outline, so containment carries the hierarchy. Rank owns bars, rings, chevrons, stars, discs and bands, so **the badges own polygons** and use no shape from that list. Two deliberate omissions: **colour distinguishes no corps** (it is already keyed to service track, and a monochrome set survives smoke and eyes that sort colour differently), and **position is not fixed by the standard** — a rule naming a shoulder assumes a shoulder, in a service with four non-human body plans and analytical chassis in it. **Each figure is derived and the derivation recorded**, because an unrecorded one drifts into decoration within a generation: Safety a closed square for a standard that completes, and **[Navigation](src/lore/star-rangers-navigation-corps.md) the same square with one side missing**, because its certificate expires where the hull's does not — two badges, one gap, and the distinction those entries spend paragraphs on is legible across a dock. **[Frontier](src/lore/star-rangers-frontier-corps.md) is a triangle inverted**, the only device pointing at its own ending, for the only corps whose mandate is built to terminate. The branch that proves the system is **Fold Transit Safety: two marks at opposite corners and nothing between them**, which is not a symbol but the finding the branch began from — *nothing has ever been lost inside a fold, only at the two ends of one.* Closing limit: **a badge never claims a hazard** — a Boundary Safety device is not a certification, because corps, rank and qualification fail independently. Drafted, not merged.

- **Corps and branch badges** (2026-08-19), Dermot's direction, added to [Rank, Insignia, and the Ranger Uniform](src/lore/rank-insignia-and-uniform.md): **each corps carries its own device, and branches within a corps carry theirs beneath it.** The entry already held that rank and certification *are deliberately never the same mark, because rank and qualification fail independently* — **the badge is a third mark on the same reasoning**, since an officer can be posted out of a corps and keep her rank, or command a section of a corps she did not climb through. **A corps badge is not a faction crest**, which is why the neutrality clause permits it: the clause forbids a mark giving a party a reason to read a Ranger as taking a side, and a corps device says which part of the Rangers arrived. **The rank tab's own colour rule — keyed to service track rather than corps loyalty — is preserved and scoped**: it governs the rank tab only, because it was written about the harder reader, someone outside the service for whom *which department* is a chart they have never seen. A badge is read by the people a corps turns up for, and a colony that signed a standing invitation to the [Frontier Corps](src/lore/star-rangers-frontier-corps.md) is entitled to see the Frontier Corps arrive. **Authority stays on the tab; belonging goes on the badge.** Badges obey every existing constraint — shapes not words, seated not sewn, no name, never confusable with the rank tab. Drafted, not merged.
