- **[The Eden Bureau Uniform](src/lore/eden-bureau-uniform.md)** (2026-08-19), Dermot's direction: **Eden Space Habitat's detectives are uniformed and wear rank insignia in plain view.** The corpus was silent on bureau dress, so this fills a gap rather than overturning anything. **The entry turns on who does the reading**, which is where it diverges from [the Ranger uniform](src/lore/rank-insignia-and-uniform.md): a Ranger's insignia is for *a colleague across a corridor who cannot look it up in time*, and withholds identity on purpose because **no Ranger's name is written on their clothing**; a detective's is read by **a resident at their own door being asked questions they did not invite**, who needs to know what the person in front of them is entitled to do, at the start of the conversation rather than the end. *The Rangers are a body that arrives; the bureau is a body that lives there.* **The marks borrow the [plainmark's](src/lore/plainmark.md) method rather than its grammar** — rank is a count, and the count band already says a small number without writing it, so one stroke to three and a filled block for the Superintendent, carrying the two survivability rules with it: colour never alone, and no letters or numerals. **So a resident who can follow the ochre rings to sealed air can read the collar of the officer at their door.** The cost is stated rather than hidden — a jacket that turns a corner ahead of you loses you the people who would rather not be found — and the bureau's answer is that *an officer who can arrive unannounced is an officer a resident cannot check*. **Three qualifications from Dermot the same day**: the obligation is **on the lower ranks** and thins going up, **an undercover officer does not wear it**, and **Commissioner ranks are not required to have one at all** — a Commissioner does not knock on doors, so the logic that puts a jacket on a detective takes it off a Commissioner. That also retired a problem: Oyelaran's and Albercombe's delivered portraits show ordinary jackets, and as a Superintendent and an Inspector neither is required to wear the uniform, so the art and the entry never disagreed. **Deliberately left open: whether the uniform carries any mark of individual identity**, which is a real question because the accountability argument runs straight at it. Drafted, not merged.

- **Prompts for all fifty-two outstanding lore illustrations** (2026-08-19), in `story-bible/images.md` Open work 5b — written in one pass, 1600×900. **The governing rule for the set: every abstract page gets a concrete anchor**, since roughly half are pages about a rule or an epistemology rather than a place, and an abstract page illustrated abstractly produces exactly the flat filler the house target rules out. Frames come from each entry's own argument: [the Frontier Corps](src/lore/star-rangers-frontier-corps.md) is **boot tracks leading away from a lit settlement**, because departure is the achievement; [what nobody certifies](src/lore/what-nobody-certifies.md) is **four framed certificates and a fifth empty frame**; [Wholecloth](src/lore/wholecloth-formcluster.md) is deliberately the least eventful image on the roster, because *nothing about it can be measured from here*; [Counterpane](src/lore/counterpane-archecluster.md) is **two identical cloths whose overlap makes a figure belonging to neither**. Four defaults flagged as failing quietly — the gold cryostat on [quantum computing](src/lore/quantum-computing-and-the-cavern-constraint.md), gibberish lettering on [the Plainmark](src/lore/plainmark.md), the tone line in both directions on [predatory entities](src/lore/predatory-entities.md), and the jellyfish cliché on [the Ollune](src/lore/ollune.md) — plus the set's own risk, which is sameness: judge as thumbnails and re-roll for variety. **One naming collision flagged**: the lore and character pages for Saint Aoife would both reach for `saint-aoife.jpg`, so the lore one is proposed as `cill-aoife-devotion.jpg`. Not generated; all proposals.

- **Portrait prompts for the remaining twenty-one pages** (2026-08-19), in `story-bible/images.md` Open work 1 — written in one pass, because a roster reads as a roster only if the frames were chosen against each other. Two shared blocks (a standing negative, and a Rangers service-dress block with geometric rank marks and no name tape, per [Rank, Insignia and the Ranger Uniform](src/lore/rank-insignia-and-uniform.md)). **Five belong to *Undercover Pets* and are deliberately off the house style**, since the runbook says weaving melancholy through that thread is a category error. Frames are chosen from each page's own argument rather than from the role: **de Courtney at a threshold she has never asked to be let past**; **Kane in civilian clothes at the back of a ceremony**, no uniform, because the tradition his career is counted in forbids one; **Zoe Smith in an ordinary corridor**, deliberately the least impressive frame, because her page's argument is that this rank is what the word means; **Aoife looking down at the water with no halo and no glow**, because the page is her refusal to claim. Two are flagged as the ones that will fight the generator: **Elvira**, whose *chalk, thread and water in vessels* is a witchcraft prompt read literally and whose page exists to say it is not one — carrying the roster's longest negative and a survey grid, folding rule and shut record books to make it survey work; and **Muffin**, which **should probably carry no image at all**, since eleven witnesses returned four different animals and drawing a specific adorable one contradicts the page in the first frame — prompted as the place on the [Eden Warden](src/characters/eden-warden.md) precedent, with the entity present and unresolved. Not generated; all proposals.

- **Portrait prompts for the three rescue machines, as a set** (2026-08-19), in `story-bible/images.md` Open work 1 — [Lucene-9000](src/characters/lucene-9000.md), [Xenon](src/characters/xenon.md) and [Lumbarian](src/characters/lumbarian.md). **What binds them is not a place** — Lucene is at Eden, the other two aboard Wender's ship — but a catalogue shelf: all three are classic designs out of production, which `xenon.md` already states. So the set is **a shared house block pasted verbatim into all three prompts**, since a generator carries nothing between frames. **All three are present-day frames**: the rescue-era framing was dropped because it would have put the part-empty cradles in shot, making an image carry the hint §7 keeps in prose. Lucene's is the risky one — *social gynoid* returns a photoreal woman by default — and her artificiality is carried by a seam at the jaw, a seam at the temple and lens eyes and nothing more, on the cyber-revenant precedent; the frame is her actual posture, **beside the interviewing officer, watching an answer arrive**. Xenon's centres on his hands, because *his personhood lives where his hands do*, working a machine with nothing wrong with it. Lumbarian's carries **scale and stillness** with a human-sized hatch for reference and no person in frame. One deliberate convention breach flagged: a bench task light is a tool, not a furnishing. Not yet generated; proposals.

- **A portrait prompt for [Anne Wender](src/characters/anne-wender.md)** (2026-08-19), in `story-bible/images.md` Open work 1. **Depicted as safety officer during the buildout, not as sheriff** — her page puts her in that post at Season 1's start, and more bindingly **there is no sheriff's insignia in canon**, so drawing a badge would invent an office's regalia in a picture, the same cascade the Calloway entry refused for a Compact uniform. The frame is a frontier yard at dawn with the fusion pad behind her and **she is counting something off-frame**, which renders her character note without a caption. *No poverty* is carried as a canon negative rather than a taste one, because [the Fusion Ceiling](src/lore/the-fusion-ceiling.md) says an early settlement's surface is *persistently misread as poverty when it is sequencing* and a generator would assert exactly that misreading by default. No family resemblance to Karla is specified, deliberately — her portrait establishes no features to match, so one could only be invented here and would bind her frame retroactively. Draft alt text included, to be checked against the frame. Not yet generated; proposals.

- **[Anne Wender](src/characters/anne-wender.md)** (2026-08-19), the last character page [A Person's Name](src/seasons/s01/e00/s01e00c04.md) unblocked and the only one still unwritten. Applies the #444 rulings: she went out to a [Cairn Trust](src/lore/cairn-trust.md) charter as a safety officer, the colony elected her, and **the settlement took her name at its constitution without her say** — *Anne Wender did not name the settlement, and could not have refused it.* Role follows Karla's model, with the election's course left *remains to be established in story*, and the page **never joins the two facts**: the wreck and the swearing-in sit in one history with no sentence connecting them, because the intake is explicit that the eldest survivor becoming the first person a world swears in *needs no commentary*. The machines' loss stays hinted at the level already published — eight down, five back, *and gave the two numbers to nobody* — written as a habit of counting rather than a loss. No portrait; a new character image is its own draft-and-stop item. Proposal.

- **Rulings on the remaining 28 July backstory decisions** (2026-08-19, #444), recorded in place in `story-bible/intake-2026-07-28.md` §10. **Four of the listed questions turned out to have been answered elsewhere and never brought back** — Anne's surname is published as **Wender** in [A Person's Name](src/seasons/s01/e00/s01e00c04.md)'s `canon_facts`, Xenon and Lumbarian are active aboard Karla's ship on both character pages, the caretaker mandate was closed by the 13 August addendum, and the corporation was named the same week. **Two are declined deliberately**: what the disaster was, since the chapter marks that absence inside a character's judgement (*it had not seemed, that night, like the missing fact*), and the *Lucy Anne* echo, already a decision to leave something open. **Ruled**: the settlement is named **Wender by the colonists at constitution rather than by Anne**, which preserves the inversion and improves it because it is done to her, rhyming with the intake hall's *one word, holding three people*; the election was **obstructed rather than contested**, on the lawful and possibly correct ground that it was premature, so the [Cairn Trust](src/lore/cairn-trust.md) never ran a candidate; the Senior Officer is **new**, with [Galen Kane](src/characters/galen-kane.md) as the man he calls, since Kane's page already defines the advisor's role and his own philosophy makes him the wrong shape for the post; the machines were **posted to the hull before Karla had any say**, so *Karla Wender's command* became true with nobody arranging it; and **all three machines remember the rescue from three vantages that make it three different events**. Andrew's question dissolved rather than resolving — the chapter has Lucene never leaving — and is replaced by the better one, that **nobody has ever asked her what happened**, for three different reasons. Story-bible only; no published content changes. Proposals.

- **[The Cairn Trust](src/lore/cairn-trust.md)** (2026-08-19), naming the 28 July intake's unnamed corporation (#445) — the concern that financed a frontier settlement and then found the colony had elected its own sheriff. **Its product is a schedule, not a commodity**: [fusion is sufficient everywhere and immediate nowhere](src/lore/the-fusion-ceiling.md), so the Trust underwrites the interval — passage out, the first rationed cores, the ten-to-twenty-year buildout — and recovers against the colony's own later output, which makes it **the party installing the reactor rather than stripping the world**. Sincerely aggrieved and partly right is made structural rather than asserted by the corporate form: its capital is held for settlers on the register awaiting passage, so **a company may forgive a debt whenever it likes and a trustee is forbidden to** — every refusal has a person behind it and they are never the person in the room. The [Frontier Corps'](src/lore/star-rangers-frontier-corps.md) self-terminating clause is written about the Rangers and lands on the Trust: the counterparty changes **from a document into a constituency in one afternoon**, and the only authority present the whole time is obliged to leave. The name inverts [Hyperfold's](src/lore/hyperfold-yield-combine.md) — a word that *can* be held to a meaning, and is: *a marker is of no use to the one who set it.* Name is a proposal; Anne, the world, the election and the Senior Officer are deliberately kept off the page, which stays structural so it seeds an unwritten arc without spoiling it. Drafted, not merged.

- **[What Nobody Certifies](src/lore/what-nobody-certifies.md)** (2026-08-18). The record certifies hulls, routes, people and minds, each to published standards with a body to complain to — and **nothing certifies a permission to be somewhere**. The entry establishes that this is a **decision rather than an oversight**: an office competent to review a settlement's right to be where it is must be able to **enter** and to **compel**, which are exactly the powers the Rangers were forbidden at founding. The [SSDC objected that those limits created dangerous gaps](src/lore/military-space-command.md) and the delegations replied that *a boundary-operations body with unrestricted right of entry would simply be the MSC wearing a different crest* — **both were right, and the record holds both without adjudicating**. The structure was already published and unnoticed: the invitation clause **fails in two opposite directions**, with [Fliade](src/lore/planets/fliade.md) having *nobody to issue* and [Corryn](src/lore/planets/corryn.md) *nobody to withdraw* — *one has no counterparty yet, the other had one and outlived it.* The working case is stated first, the Cerebraun withdrawal, because *a protection that is never tested is a claim; that one is a practice*. No verdict on the trade, and no reform proposed. Drafted, then merged.

- **[The Halvern Combine](src/lore/halvern-combine.md)** (2026-08-18), the Corryn charter-holder as its own entry. Descended from one of the [Imperium](src/lore/the-imperium.md)'s industrial patrons — the families holding the shipyards and fold-drive patents the fleet was *already answerable to* — and **it outlived the Imperium because it was never a government**: what ended in 2609 was a chain of command, and a patent portfolio, a set of yards and a drawer of sealed licences require no issuing authority to persist. The charters were neither upheld nor overturned — the MSC inherited a defence problem, the Consolidation constrained a military, the Rangers charter was argued over what it forbade — so *they were simply never the question in front of anybody, and a document nobody has jurisdiction to revoke is, for every practical purpose, valid.* **The spine is a parallel with the [Hyperfold Yield Combine](src/lore/hyperfold-yield-combine.md)**, and the difference is sharper than the parallel: Hyperfold was lawful and **fast**, ending at Dock Seven in 2831; Halvern is lawful and **slow**, with *no moment to point at* — so the Corps teaches the case that ended, *which is a fact about how institutions learn rather than about which case is worse*. Two absences marked: what became of the other patron holdings, and that **nobody certifies a charter** the way hulls and routes are certified. Drafted, then merged.

- **[The Corryn System](src/lore/planets/corryn.md)** (2026-08-18), the fix for #463 — the renamed Meridian block, with all six corrections applied and the one blank filled. **The colony is a remnant of the Old [Imperium](src/lore/the-imperium.md)** (Dermot's direction), chartered 2543–2609 by an authority that *regarded elected governance as a demonstrated failure*, backed by one of the legacy industrial holdings behind its fleet — whose successor is **the Halvern Combine**. That resolves the Military Space Command error and the unfilled corporation blank together, and **the date correction goes the other way round**: the block's *approximately thirty years* is the **expansion**, not the founding, so the settlement is two centuries older and the harm is recent. The Imperium fell in 2609, seven hundred light years away, where *the collapse of the chartering government was news rather than an event* — so the colony is lawful in the only sense available to it, holding **a valid charter from a government that no longer exists, with no office standing to review a document nobody can revoke**. **The name carries the hedge**: *The Sentinel → the Carillon*, since a set of tuned bells names the sound as patterned without claiming anyone is ringing it. Etheric co-location deleted for a flexure with an unidentified far side; the distress signal keeps its dreams and loses its sender (*the vision survives; the sender does not*); *Convergence Weaving* deleted. **The Spiralites became the entry's centre** — a people who speak in electromagnetic pulse and reproduce by it, under a colony degrading exactly that band, where the [sapience clause](src/lore/frontier-transformation-protocols.md) applies on the plain reading and the failure is not one of understanding but of an unsupervised registration seven hundred light years from anyone with standing to review it. Names are proposals. Drafted, then merged.

- **[The Kalypsis Dawn](src/lore/kalypsis-dawn.md)** (2026-08-18), the last of the 26 July intake's three worlds, drafted as the fix for #472. Every Overfold usage resolved to **fold transit** or **boundary-zone proximity**; the three refused tropes removed; both namings taken. **The shielding was the real rewrite and it improved the ship**: *shadow-matter shielding* assumed a hazard that arrives and can be deflected, and a boundary zone has none — **agreement fails, nothing strikes**. So the vessel is built to know the effect *by how much*, carrying several independent reference sets that share no design or failure mode, cross-checked continuously, where **the disagreement is the measurement**. It points at a published failure: [Threshold's forty-second discrepancy](src/lore/boundary-zones.md) sat eleven years as a calibration fault *because a single reference with nothing to disagree with looks exactly like an instrument needing adjustment*. The *Emergency Node-Hop Protocol* became **eighteen months of endurance** — *you do not jump, you wait* — since fold transit cannot be improvised. Certification hooks into both bodies, the [Safety Corps](src/lore/star-rangers-safety-corps.md) for the hull and the [Navigation Corps](src/lore/star-rangers-navigation-corps.md) for the route. Helion-3 is Kernel-compliant by charter and never decides meaning. **Warden-Class → Lee-Class**, the sheltered side, *not a defence and does not stop anything*. Naming is a proposal. Drafted, then merged.

- **[The Umbral Moon](src/lore/umbral-moon.md)** (2026-08-18), the second of the 26 July intake's unwritten worlds, drafted as the fix for #462. **Two of that issue's three problems were overstated and dissolve rather than needing decisions.** The neighbour membrane never needed naming — the record **never names the far side** at either documented boundary zone, saying only *a neighbour*, because the Interval carries no bearing or distance: *the record has instruments for measuring that a neighbour is close; it has none for asking which one.* So *Shadow Universe* is dropped rather than replaced, and **the coupling to *where shadow beings live* is broken** — they are meta-dimensional, extending across higher dimensions rather than residing next door, so the realm question has the wrong shape. The one real decision resolves by separating two questions the block had merged: the moon is a **Trojan at Earth–Moon L5** held by ordinary Lagrange dynamics, and the flexure merely shares the address — *why is it there* and *why is the place strange* are different questions, and no gravity tunnel could hold anything anyway at seconds to minutes. The block's detection story survives improved: the gravitational micro-pulses are the flexure, not the moon, which turns up in the follow-up *having nothing to do with it*. Drafted, then merged.

- **[Narrative Works and Their Adaptation](src/lore/narrative-works-and-their-adaptation.md)** (2026-08-18), Dermot's direction: a work of in-universe fiction is a **spine of scenes each carrying several viewpoints**, published with its apparatus — settled background, a register of terms, a chronology, and attributed source documents that may be partial or self-serving. Three in-world causes, none artistic in origin: a documentary culture that learned to ask who says so; the failure of the single credible narrator, taken from the archive's own hardest cases; and **modularity for adaptation**, the pressure that shows most. Audiovisual but not cinema — matte unlit surfaces read by ambient light, nothing projected. **Adaptation is years of named work** because no machine renders one people's mode into another's: the [Chthonari](src/lore/chthonari.md) case is the taught one, since a human work entering the Undersong is re-composed into a channel where the separation between a character's thought and the work's telling of it does not exist. An adapter may decline, on the [Ollune](src/lore/ollune.md) precedent. **The original is the work; the adaptation is the courtesy.** The entry never references this site or the resemblance — that was a deliberate craft constraint. Drafted, then merged.

- **The holodeck is refused** (2026-08-18), Dermot's ruling, added to [What the Record Refuses](src/lore/what-the-record-refuses.md) as a closing subsection of *The Furniture of the Future* plus a summary-table row. **Simulation is not refused with it** — [Virtual Reality](src/glossary/virtual-reality.md) is canon, rigs exist, immersive entertainment was never banned, and a Survey Corps navigator trains in one. What is refused is the walk-in room: matter where there is none, and a place indistinguishable from a real one. Three arguments, the middle one the load-bearing one — it inherits the hologram's missing medium everywhere at once; **the difference that matters is provenance rather than fidelity**, since a rig leaves a memory sourced (*four hours on the rig*) while an indistinguishable room manufactures experience a person genuinely had and cannot source, which an institution built around an Archive cannot keep; and the kernel refuses a simulated person who answers back without saying what it is, in the same words that refuse the universal translator. The glossary had already reached the same place by another route — immersive entertainment declined because a culture attentive to genuine emergence stopped finding recombination interesting. Drafted, then merged — it asserts about the world.

- **[Proverbs and Maxims of the Star Rangers](src/lore/star-rangers-proverbs-and-maxims.md)** (2026-08-18), a lore entry collecting the Corps' working sayings, sourced where the origin is documented and marked unrecorded where it isn't. The page turns on a tension already in the corpus rather than smoothing it: a service trained to write flatly, checkably, and low-context so its reports survive translation nonetheless runs on compressed idiom, and the rule that reconciles the two is that **a maxim is a mnemonic for a discipline, never a substitute for a finding** — taught in the college, inadmissible in the log. Most of the sayings are borrowed from the Survey Archive's [verification doctrine](src/codex/the-verification-doctrine.md), which is what Sen's [Three Disciplines of the Record](src/codex/three-disciplines-of-the-record.md) recommended in as many words. Two are new, from Dermot's direction of the same date: **"Quiet is not doubt; loud is not certain"** and **"The pleasing reading is checked first."** The closing section applies [Marked Absences](src/codex/marked-absences.md) to the page itself and declines to attribute the sayings whose origin the Archive cannot show. Drafted, then merged — it asserts about the world.

- **Humility as confidence, captured** (2026-08-18). Dermot's note — humility can be a sign of a deeper internal self confidence that does not require external validation, and distrusts flattery — added to `story-bible/life-lessons.md` and written up in `story-bible/ideas.md`. It is deliberately **not** a correction of *Humility can become invisibility* in The Limits of Virtue; the pair is the useful thing, because the outward conduct is identical and an observer cannot tell which one they are looking at, which is what lets a room misread a competent officer for years. The note surveys where the corpus already holds this ([Tissadelle Shepherd](src/characters/tissadelle-shepherd.md), Ranger practice in [The Institute](src/lore/the-institute.md), [Sofia Santos](src/characters/sofia-santos.md), Agent Barsik) and flags what is thin: every existing case is the good version, and nobody yet embodies the invisibility half.

- **[The Third Debt Is Mine](src/journal/the-third-debt-is-mine.md)** (2026-08-17), a journal entry on the rule that came out of writing the PR review process: technical and literacy debt get a repair drafted on sight, and creative entropy never does. The reason is not severity but checkability — the first two can be tested against something outside the author's head, while entropy and intention look identical from outside, so **creative entropy can be good** where a broken link never is. The entry lands on the observation that this is the story's own problem: [Marked Absences](src/codex/marked-absences.md) already argues in-universe that a record tidying away what it cannot account for has destroyed evidence and called it housekeeping, and the same test had been running on the repository unnoticed.

- **[A Proposal to Collar the Anstolik, Refused at Countersign](src/codex/proposal-to-collar-the-anstolik.md)** (2026-08-17), a Fliade survey working paper filed with its own refusal: an instrument specialist's prospectus for detection collars on Anstolik herds, and the survey lead's countersign withheld on four grounds. Codex, so it settles nothing — no `canon_facts`, and the question of whether anything is being taken on Fliade stays marked rather than answered.

- **[Fliade](src/lore/planets/fliade.md)** (2026-08-16), the first of the 26 July intake's three unwritten worlds to be drafted. A cold terrestrial world whose biodiversity lives in geothermally warmed cavern systems rather than on its frozen surface, and whose deep-network people — the **Pandoids** — the survey found before any transformation proposal existed, which is the rare case where the sapience clause arrived early enough to matter. The entry states the two facts ruled about them, that they do not travel in space and keep their record by speaking it, as facts rather than as a level, and says why an oral record is a different shape rather than a smaller one. It also marks two absences: the classification of the boundary feature the planet sits near, and **the Pandoids' own name for themselves**, since *Pandoid* is a survey coinage and not a name they gave. The closing section is the one the world is for — the charter's entry-by-invitation limit has nothing to grip on a world with no body that can issue or withdraw one, so the protection is thinnest exactly where the asymmetry is greatest.

- **[The PR Review](story-bible/pr-review.md)** (2026-08-17), a sibling process to the Benevolent Critic with the same three debts, the same four priority bands, and **the opposite default**. Only two things stop a pull request — a major critical flaw in the change itself, or a red CI check — and everything else a review finds is raised as an issue that does not hold the merge, including findings that are real and urgent. The reasoning is that a P1 in an adjacent file is urgent *and unrelated*: priority says when a thing gets fixed, while the blocker test asks only whether this particular change should wait. Its sharpest rule is that **the debt decides the remedy**: technical and literacy findings get a drafted fix on sight, because they have a correct answer that does not need the author's taste to find, while **creative entropy is never quietly resolved** — only the author can tell entropy from intention, and entropy is sometimes the good kind. Paired with a `pr-review-finding` issue template carrying the same contract.

- **Designed SPECIES title cards for the three remaining species pages** (2026-08-17) — [The Pelagene Littoral](src/lore/pelagene-littoral.md), [The Serephine Dunekin](src/lore/serephine-dunekin.md) and [The Veyr Basaltborn](src/lore/veyr-basaltborn.md), drawn by `make-emblem-card.ps1` and matching Chthonari's card rather than the square codex covers. Each takes a device that argues from the page — concentric **rings** for a people of layered depth bands, a **sundial** for a people who open twice a day between two lethal extremes, a **triad** for a body built as a truss rather than a frame — and its own tint, so four species cards in a row do not read as four printings of one. The epithets and qualifiers are authored, as the generator requires; they are not fields of any page.

### Changed

- **[Levrils](src/lore/levrils.md) restructured for readability.** The page front-loaded taxonomy and buried its two strongest passages past 70% of the scroll, and ran four bullet lists back to back — 20+ consecutive bullets, now a longest run of 8. *What a Levril Looks Like* moves up to answer the question the opening raises; *Functional Role* and *Operational Constraints* merge into one permitted/foreclosed table, which is the entry's actual thesis; *Two Occasions* moves ahead of the taxonomy. The `Distinction from Other Meta-Dimensional Beings` section — three subsections restating `meta-dimensional-beings.md` while linking to it, including one headed *Levrils* on a page about Levrils — is replaced by a short pointer. Verified against the classification page first: its Class III coverage is strictly fuller, so nothing was lost. Prose preserved paragraph-for-paragraph elsewhere. **No sub-page:** at 1,388 words this is 35th of 119 lore pages against a median of 1,133, and a summary already exists at [Levril](src/glossary/levril.md).
- **Krenyi senses include EM fields and harmonic conditions** (2026-08-18, Dermot's direction). Extends *The Whole Body Is the Instrument* in [Krenyi (Quiet-Built)](src/lore/krenyi.md). **This one needed a continuity check first**: *harmonic* is the coherence state governing teleportation and QSHW transit alike, so a people who feel it can feel a boundary zone — and `year-0-survey-team-arrives.md` has **Rook-7, a machine**, identify Threshold's anomalous resonance *within hours*, with **Syra, a Krenyi Boundary Analyst, on that team**. The resolution is a hard limit that makes the sense safe to have: **it produces no number** — no frequency, magnitude, bearing or name — so it is *a direction to look, and never a reading*. A finding still needs an instrument, and a Krenyi is the last person to offer a sensation as one, being unwilling to assert what they cannot support. Syra's silence becomes characterisation rather than a hole. The precedent belongs to another people, which keeps the Quiet-Built off a pedestal: [the Overfold](src/glossary/overfold.md) already has a trained observer feeling a wrongness *long before an instrument confirms it*, and **neither route produces a certificate** — a Krenyi sits the same boundary-analyst examination as anyone. Third reason for the published *field, a pressure, a turn of light* line. Psionics guard unchanged: EM and harmonic conditions are properties of a **place**, not a person. Drafted, then merged.

- **Krenyi sensitivity, reflexes and awareness** (2026-08-18, Dermot's direction). New *What the Body Notices* section in [Krenyi (Quiet-Built)](src/lore/krenyi.md), placed after Emotional Range because its payoff depends on those bounds. The cat comparison is **kept and framed** rather than avoided: the record's standing note holds that [likening a people to an Earth animal](src/lore/what-the-record-refuses.md) is *a fact about the observers*, so the cat is what humans reach for and a Krenyi names the distortion as they would any category. **The comparison then fails in one place, and that failure is the idea** — a cat is fast *because* it is alarmed, the startle being the mechanism, where the Quiet-Built have the reaction and not the startle: *they orient without flinching.* This re-explains their reputation on a bad deck, which had read as composure and is not — *there is nothing being mastered*, and **composure runs out where this does not**. The cost, per the page's pattern: they **cannot un-notice**, so a room conducting a small social fiction is legible from inside it and their honesty leaves no graceful way to join. Also retro-fits the Levril section merged earlier the same day, which rested on this apparatus without describing it. **A second section, *The Whole Body Is the Instrument*, answers what the apparatus is** (Dermot, same day): there is **no organ** — no eye, whisker or membrane a survey could photograph — and the whole body samples continuously. That retro-explains the entry's own opening line, since **movement is noise in your own readings**, so *no wasted gesture* is method rather than manner and *the stillness people read as composure is closer to a technician not breathing on a scale*. It also explains a published line nothing else accounted for: [levrils.md](src/lore/levrils.md) already had a Krenyi meeting *a field, a pressure, a turn of light* where others meet a figure — every other people gives it a shape, the Quiet-Built give it a **weight**. The psionics guard is written in on the record's own boundary, **texture never content**, and the resemblance to their body-wide immune discrimination is noted without being claimed. Drafted, then merged.

- **Kalypsis Dawn checked against canon, and it is the worst of the three** (2026-08-18). `intake-2026-07-26.md` block 3 rests on a **category error**: [the Overfold](src/glossary/overfold.md) is the Fellowship of Light's contemplative name for boundary-zone Etheric phenomena — *three names, one thing*, alongside Etheric and Intermembrane Bleed — and is **not a medium you travel through**. The block builds the ship's identity, certification, defensive suite and class history on Overfold corridors, ratings, turbulence and jumps, which would also be a third FTL channel where [the record allows exactly two](src/lore/what-the-record-refuses.md). **The original check was backwards**: it read *Overfold is already established canon (9 files)* as reassurance, when the word is established and means something else — counting files is not reading definitions. Three refused tropes are fitted to it: holo-displays, **stasis pods** against the outright cold-sleep refusal, and an AI that *handles* interspecies communication where the refusal permits only xenolinguists with AI support on an exact division of labour. Both original flags confirmed, one stronger — Kernel compliance is a **charter requirement**, not a *should probably*. The heading *WRITABLE AFTER TWO NAMING DECISIONS* is corrected in place and the block is tracked as **#472** — the strongest of the three P2s, since #462's block said *writable after three fixes* and #463's said *needs new names*, both understating, while this one affirmatively certifies itself as *Fits canon well*. What survives: the unarmed neutral-passage design, Tissadelle's verified Line Captain rank, and the modular multi-biology interior.

- **#463 re-checked against canon, and the Military Space Command date corrected** (2026-08-18). Five of the seven Meridian corrections confirmed; three needed correcting. **Item 1 is stronger than filed** — the Sentinel appears in published Season 3 chapter text, so the name collision would reach live prose rather than only an entry. **Item 3's date was wrong**: canon has the Consolidation Accords narrowing the MSC into the SSDC in **2722**, with the charter following in 2723, and both the intake and the issue said 2723. The contradiction is unaffected — a founding around 2796 postdates either — but the wrong year had propagated once and is fixed in place. **Item 5's verdict changes from FLAW to UNSUPPORTED**: [physics-comparison](src/lore/physics-comparison.md) holds consciousness emergent from neural complexity *and* that *the deeper nature of consciousness remains an open scientific question*, so the block asserts as explanation something the record holds open — the repair is to hedge it, not remove it. And **item 2 is a blank rather than a correction**, tracked in #445, so six corrections and one blank is the honest count. Priority unchanged at P2.

- **The Arilon reading stops at Old Earth** (2026-08-18). [Arilon](src/lore/arilon.md) now bounds the Krenyi reading rather than leaving its reach open: nothing in the record places any people but humans on Earth before spaceflight, contact history is uniformly late, and for a human community the pattern predicts a human Champion since selection operates on the beings available to be selected. Two reasons, the second general. **Evidential** — an unplaceable people is not a placeable one, and impossible-to-disprove is not supported, which corrects a subtlety in the previous draft that treated non-placement as making the reading permanent without noting it denies the reading any positive support. And **no people is the explanation for another people's history** — the refusal underneath the closed list of human-framed peoples and of a shared galactic biochemistry, each declining a tidier universe descending from one source. *A file whose founding renunciation is that it does not adjudicate between traditions cannot hand one of them a mechanical answer and call it neutrality.* The reading survives where it was always interesting, among the later accounts across star systems. **Recommendation and draft, not a decision taken.**

- **Krenyi understand human emotions without sharing them** (2026-08-18, Dermot's direction). New passage in the Emotional Range section of [Krenyi (Quiet-Built)](src/lore/krenyi.md), heading off the stock reading that a people without fury are a cold people. **It derives from canon already in place**: [empathy is re-derived](src/lore/what-the-record-refuses.md) as cognition rather than reception — *nothing arrives by antenna; everything arrives by attention* — so **understanding never required sharing, for anyone**. Four points: they are **not an unemotional people** (anxiety, annoyance, grief, and attachments held for centuries; the range is bounded at three extremes, and missing three extremes is not missing the register); comprehension without sharing, stated plainly; **one bounded advantage** — a human reads another's fear through their own and a Krenyi's instrument is not measuring something it is also doing, explicitly not a rank; and the **cost**, that human emotional grammar is learned, so they work from a very good model and a model is what a novel case defeats. Closes on the distinction that does the work — *logic is a method and clarity is an absence of ornament* — and the note that a Krenyi has never been recorded finding a human ridiculous for being afraid. Drafted, then merged.

- **The Arilon implication, drafted** (2026-08-18). [Arilon](src/lore/arilon.md) gains the reading that follows from the Krenyi being the readiest Champions: **a Champion of which people?** Filed as a refinement *inside* the Champion reading rather than a fourth peer to it, so the three-way Champion/avatar/incarnation list in [Arilonian](src/glossary/arilonian.md) stays correct. The fit is the pattern's own — *an outsider who arrives*, names what local authority will not, is opposed, and departs — and the Krenyi match it in every particular. **It is permanent rather than merely plausible**, because no filed homeworld, emergence date or timeline entry gives any chronology to test an account against: *a people who decline to be placed cannot be placed anywhere, including out of an account they were never in.* Two guards written in — it is **the deflationary reading**, no better evidenced than the devotional accounts it would displace, and the entry cites [the pleasing reading is checked first](src/lore/star-rangers-proverbs-and-maxims.md) against preferring it for tidiness; and nothing is adjudicated, the Fellowship filing it exactly as it files the Avatar exception. **Also states outright that the pattern is species-neutral** (Dermot's correction the same day): a Champion is a *sentient material being — organic or artificial*, so an Arilon-figure may be of any sapient kind and so may the community that received one. What is **not** neutral is the archive, and that produced the entry's sharpest idea — the filed pattern describes what survived transmission by low-context observers, so a Champion who looked broadly like the people visited is written down as a *person* while one who did not is written down as a marvel, a beast, a voice. **The accounts on the shelf are not the accounts that exist; they are the accounts that looked like accounts** — deliberately the [boundary-zone](src/lore/boundary-zones.md) record's own move about its two documented sites. The Krenyi over-representation is therefore a fact about the shelf and not about who is selected. Reciprocal pointer added from the Krenyi Champions section. Drafted, then merged.

- **Krenyi, Levrils and Champions** (2026-08-18, Dermot's direction). Two new sections in [Krenyi (Quiet-Built)](src/lore/krenyi.md), filed with the other resistances because it is the same faculty producing the opposite of what anyone expects. Least awe of any people toward a [Levril](src/glossary/levril.md), and fastest to answer one — **a single fact from two sides**, since *awe and attention compete for the same faculty, and the Krenyi have spent it all on attention*. Subtle influence is a sculpted gradient that must be **noticed** before it can be answered, and a witness occupied with being amazed is not reading it; the Quiet-Built read **pattern drift** professionally, which is the same instrument tilted at a different object. *They are not more obedient than other peoples. They are earlier, because nothing happens in them first.* **Cooperation is not deference** and a floor is stated — they are unenslavable, Cascade standing is not a lever, and a Levril drifting from its stated terms would meet the same quiet withdrawal anyone would. The closing beat is the record's own: since the aftermath of selection is *"mythic overstatement"* and *"misattribution as divine will"*, the people least willing to be read as symbol are the most often selected and so the most mythologised — able to name the distortion in the room, never in the story told afterwards by people who were not there. Drafted, then merged.

- **The Krenyi have little appetite for *human* entertainment** (2026-08-18, Dermot's direction, and his clarification the same day that the claim is about the **human forms** specifically). New section in [Krenyi (Quiet-Built)](src/lore/krenyi.md). The clarification changed the derivation: an earlier draft had these forms *returning nothing usable*, which applies to any such form and so quietly predicted the Krenyi have no equivalents. It is instead a **calibration problem** — human entertainment is tuned, with great skill, to an instrument they do not have. Human drama runs on dread, sport on partisan fury and the fear of losing, much music on holding a sorrow open, and **deep fear, fury and unresolving grief are exactly the three bounds the page already established**. Fiction's method is the one they decline everywhere else; team sport asks a person to become a category on purpose. They compete and train freely — *it is the stands rather than the field where nothing arrives.* Whether they have forms of their own is left open and becomes the interesting question, the absence being **theirs rather than the archive's**. [Narrative Works](src/lore/narrative-works-and-their-adaptation.md) takes the payoff: the species sharing almost the whole human body plan is the one human stories reach least, while peoples built nothing like us want the work done — *what a story is for does not travel with the shape of the body reading it.* Drafted, then merged.

- **Virtual reality's one live use is generalised** (2026-08-18, Dermot's direction). [Virtual Reality](src/glossary/virtual-reality.md) already named fold-scaffold visualization as the field's *"one enduring, unremarked-upon use"*; the exception is now **a class rather than an instance** — any measured structure a baseline sense cannot reach, with **alien communications and signals** named as the demanding case and the one it is most valued for. The hard boundary is recorded with it, because the two rules meet exactly: **a rig renders structure, never meaning.** It shows a xenolinguist that a figure recurs at an interval and breaks in a place; it never says what it means and never says anything in a voice — that remains years of translation work by named people with error bars, which is where the universal translator's refusal begins. Drafted, then merged.

- **A third option for an image that contradicts canon: refile it as Codex art** (2026-08-18). Dermot's direction — an image that contradicts canon but remains aesthetic may move into the Codex as in-universe artwork rather than be removed. It **completes** *absence beats a picture quietly making a claim* rather than overturning it: that rule governs a picture asserting in **Archive voice**, and a codex artefact asserts nothing, so the disposal options become fix it, relocate it, delete it. The Codex's required `author` field is what makes it work — an artwork's author is exactly what makes it valid-for-its-author, so the test is *could someone in this world have made it, and would they have made it this way?* Recorded in `story-bible/images.md` with its limits: it is **not** a file move (an unreferenced image fails validation, so refiling means writing an entry around it), it would **not** have rescued either Batch 3 deletion (both are photographs of identifiable real-world subjects, which a codex frame cannot cure), and **two absolute exclusions** were ruled the same day: **stock photography never qualifies, and neither do anachronisms.** One reason under both — the Codex can carry a wrong belief, never a wrong century or a real place, since an artefact is a physical object made inside this world and the author's fallibility covers interpretation rather than material culture. A deliberate historical depiction is not an anachronism, so the exclusion needs no exception. A **quality bar** was ruled the same day: only a high-quality image with artistic merit and no technical flaws qualifies — if it would not earn a page were canon no obstacle, it does not earn one as Codex art. A generation artefact is a flaw; a stylisation is not, the test being whether an in-world artist could have *chosen* it. Together these close the French dial (previously arguable, now excluded twice over) and empty the candidate pool: a blob check found the rejected originals were **never committed** — one content version each for `cerebraun`, `aldera`, `rook-7`, `nessa` and `orla-shepherd` — correcting an earlier claim in `images.md` that they were recoverable from git, and establishing that the live `cerebraun.jpg` is the architectural indirection rather than the grey-alien bust. The rule is therefore **prospective**. Two decisions remain open before anything is applied. `CLAUDE.md` deliberately not updated until they are.

- **The Meridian block's correction list is now one issue, #463** (2026-08-18). Seven items where the block's heading advertises one — three from 26 July (name collisions with Halyx's Meridian and Sentinel, the corporation's name, and a Military Space Command founding date that postdates the MSC's dissolution by a century), two from the #442 boundary-zone ruling, and two found while filing: the Sentinel's distress signal received as dreams by sensitives is a **refused psi trope** rather than a stretch of one — [What the Record Refuses](src/lore/what-the-record-refuses.md) holds that *"a dream is never evidence about who sent it: nothing did"* — and **Convergence Weaving** is an undefined term doing load-bearing work, the same shape as Convergence Point before #442. The risk named in the issue is not accidental drafting, which the naming blocks, but a **partial fix**: names changed, block assumed cleared, refused trope written in. Unpublished capture; no lore page changes.

- **The Convergence Point maps onto boundary zones** (2026-08-18, #442). Dermot's ruling: no new term — a Convergence Point is an **inter-membrane boundary zone**, the flexure case that [Boundary Zones and Concordant Edges](src/lore/boundary-zones.md) already describes, and the word stays out of `src/`. The mapping settles the degree question (*minor* becomes a **Boundary-State Class**), fixes the location grammar (a zone has sky coordinates but no distance to its neighbour), and rules out *fold* for the feature, since a flexure is not engineered transit. [Fliade](src/lore/planets/fliade.md) needs no edit — its marked absence was about the **class**, which a *suspected* narrowing genuinely leaves open. The two unwritten blocks do: the Umbral Moon's *Shadow Universe* is not canon and its moon suspended in a stable gravity tunnel contradicts a phenomenon canon defines as lasting seconds to minutes, and the Meridian block's *Ethereal Universes* asserts the Etheric is a place. Recorded in `intake-2026-07-26.md`; unpublished capture, no lore page changes.

- **_Wayland_ ruled not reusable as a corporate name** (2026-08-18, #445). The 26 July intake's *Wayland Space Corporation* collides with [Space Commissioner Zara Wayland](src/characters/zara-wayland.md), and the *Drithane* precedent does not carry: a retired title and an in-world planet are different kinds of thing, where these pair the same surname with the same word — *Space* — in the same domain. **No migration-map row**, on the guide's own precedent for declining one — the name never entered the corpus, so nothing is renamed. Recorded in `intake-2026-07-26.md`; the concern's actual name is still open, and is one edit with that block's existing Military Space Command date correction rather than two. The index also stopped conflating this corporation with the separate unnamed one in the 28 July intake.

- **Fold Transit Safety has an origin story** (2026-08-18, #430). [The Safety Corps](src/lore/star-rangers-safety-corps.md) names three largest branches and gave histories to two of them. The third now has two paragraphs, drawn entirely from what [Catastrophic Failure in Fold Transit](src/lore/fold-transit-catastrophic-failure.md) already establishes: the branch begins from a finding rather than an inherited programme — the failure surface is the aperture, not the fold — which makes the hazard a tolerance, and a tolerance is the kind of thing the 1894 method was built to certify. Its budget goes on comparative standards work rather than inspection because its hard case is a hull honestly certified to a weaker standard, lawful everywhere it goes. The founding year is left a marked absence, on the same page's precedent for the year *Solutions* was dropped. Drafted, then merged — it asserts about the world.

- **`CONTRIBUTING.md` no longer invites readers through a door they can't use** (2026-08-17, #432). The `## Issues` section was written to third parties — *"a short report with a URL is enough"* — while `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/config.yml` turns blank issues off and routes every reader to the comments repo. The two documents contradicted each other, and the reader met the contradiction rather than the author. The section now describes the tracker for what it is, the author's own backlog kept readable, and sends problem reports to the same forum the next section already names — which is what *"asking once in the right place is more likely to get an answer than asking in several"* asks for.

- **The humanoid refusal now turns on the frame, not the posture** (2026-08-16, #449). [What the Record Refuses](src/lore/what-the-record-refuses.md) said the Krenyi were the only other sapient *humanoids* and that the list was closed at one; it now says the only other people built on the **human frame**, and states why standing upright is a different claim. Independent origins converge on solutions, which is what a physical universe does; the costume constraint asked them to converge on a silhouette, which is the refused thing. The test becomes *"is this a human with features applied?"* rather than *"does it stand up?"* — strictly the same refusal, said in the terms it always meant. Ruled by Dermot after the Pandoid sapience ruling produced an apparent second exception.

- **The same sharpening swept to [Cross-Biosphere Taxonomy](src/lore/cross-biosphere-taxonomy.md)** (2026-08-16), which carried the claim in its own words — *"the only two sapient humanoids in the record"*. It now distinguishes the two: Endoskelia asks only for an internal skeleton, while the refusal asks whether a body could be mistaken for a person, so a third people arriving in that row upright is a taxonomic neighbour and nothing more. The page's own line — *a frame is a description, not a genealogy* — was already the argument.

- **Four Pandoid rulings recorded, and Fliade is nearly writable** (2026-08-16). `story-bible/intake-2026-07-26.md` now carries the settled facts — sapient; descended from a bear-like alien ancestor rather than anything terrestrial; not space faring; keeping their record orally, in cultural memory — with the two consequences worth having deliberately: contact is asymmetric because a non-spacefaring people is arrived at rather than arriving, and the Archive meets a spoken record where its own epistemology is documentary. The method for the second already exists and should be followed rather than reinvented — [Hymn of the Thin Places](src/codex/hymn-of-the-thin-places.md) files an oral tradition as a composite text whose variance is evidence, which is a Codex form and not a Lore one. Unpublished capture; no page in `src/` names Fliade or the Pandoids yet.

- **The ladder of technological levels is refused outright** (2026-08-16, #450). New closing subsection on [What the Record Refuses](src/lore/what-the-record-refuses.md), plus a summary-table row: capability is **a shape, not a height**, because a technology answers a question a world asked and no two worlds asked the same ones in the same order. A world with no ore never had a metals age to be behind on. Specific questions survive and matter — can they leave their atmosphere, can they hold a fold route — while *are they more advanced* has no answer, and contact doctrine turns on what a people is and consents to rather than on a rank. Three pages already refused the same ladder case by case ([the fusion ceiling](src/lore/the-fusion-ceiling.md)'s sequencing misread as poverty, [civilisation comparison](src/lore/civilisation-comparison.md)'s *post-comprehension*, [environmental design](src/lore/environmental-technology-design.md)'s advanced world that looks quiet); this states the rule they were all applying. Ruled by Dermot, and it dissolves #450 rather than answering it.

- **A name borrowed from an Earth animal is a fact about the observers** (2026-08-16). New passage and summary-table row on the same page: where the record calls a people bear-like, or files them under an `-oid` coinage, the comparison belongs to whoever did the naming — a first survey reaching for the nearest familiar shape — and says nothing about descent, since [life began separately on each world](src/lore/cross-biosphere-taxonomy.md) and no lineage outside Earth's biosphere has an Earth animal behind it. The record keeps such names, because they are what people say, while declining what they imply.

- **The open-questions index is now reachable from the documents it indexes** (2026-08-16, #441). `story-bible/open-questions.md` had no inbound references at all, which left it as undiscoverable as the prose it replaced. CLAUDE.md's `story-bible/` inventory now names it first, and `intake-2026-07-26.md`, `intake-2026-07-28.md`, `cascade-structure-and-limits.md` and `images.md` each carry a pointer back to it.
- **Class III "shadow beings" are now *incursives*** (Dermot's direction, 2026-08-21). The old name collided with [Membrane Shadows](src/lore/membrane-shadows.md), and the collision was live rather than theoretical — two pages carried explicit "not to be confused with" warnings and `membrane-shadows.md` recorded the two as "routinely misfiled". *Incursive* names the actual discriminator: a Class III being has **entered** material space and can be touched, where a Membrane Shadow is a gravitational imprint with nothing present. So a Membrane Shadow is not an incursive because nothing incurred, and the warnings become nearly unnecessary rather than merely relocated. Swept across 6 files; registered in the canonical glossary with a migration-map row. **Membrane Shadows were the other candidate and were left alone** — 15 files against 6, with their own lore entry, glossary entry, journal entry and existing guide rows, so renaming the smaller surface was the cheaper change.
- **The Unfounded sub-names are modes of failure, not kinds** (Dermot's ruling, 2026-08-21). *Demon*, *threne*, *beautiful monster*, *cute predator* denote no category the way a species or a Cascade tier does, because **nothing among the Unfounded exists by design** — a founded thing is created and defined by the strata above it, and that decision is what gives a kind its membership; the Unfounded are underwritten by no origin condition, so there is no decision for a category to record. Three consequences now on file: two things under one name need have nothing else in common; nothing is obliged to stay what it was filed as, and a reclassification is a correction to the file rather than an event in the world; and the counters are matched to modes rather than kinds, which is why they look unrelated to each other. The **Class II / Class III split survives** — sapience is an observed capability, not a claim about design — and Class I is untouched, Levrils being founded with real subclasses of a real tier. Reconciled in `glossary/unfounded.md`, `lore/predatory-entities.md` and `lore/meta-dimensional-beings.md`.
- **Codex viewpoints add flavour and in-character debate, never doubt about canon** (Dermot's ruling, 2026-08-21). Recorded in `CLAUDE.md` as a bound on the existing canon-for-its-author rule: an entry may be mistaken in its author's voice, but must not leave a reader less sure what is true. The test is the reader rather than the author. Applied immediately — *The Borrowed Silhouette*'s closing said the traditions holding a literal adversary "are not refuted by this paper", which kept an incoherent category live; it now states that the finding is settled and that a tradition's freedom to keep its own words is not a reservation about the record.
- **There is no chief of the Unfounded, and there could not be one** (Dermot's ruling, 2026-08-21). `glossary/unfounded.md` called the devotional adversary "the limiting case of the class", belonging to it "by definition rather than by observation" — "a classification with a standing member slot". That left a chief-shaped hole in the class and quietly reopened a door [What the Record Refuses](src/lore/what-the-record-refuses.md) had already shut ("the dark lord — curtailed… ecology, not theology"). The position on file is now **incoherence, not absence**: command needs somebody to issue it, and nothing performs the reading; something to obey it, and the Unfounded are a failure mode rather than a faction; and answerability, which is the class's own test. Such a being would have to be **founded in order to command and Unfounded in order to be the adversary**, and cannot be both. [The Borrowed Silhouette](src/codex/the-borrowed-silhouette.md) is rewritten to argue this rather than the weaker conditional it carried.
- **[The False Dragon](src/codex/the-borrowed-silhouette.md) is retitled *The Borrowed Silhouette*** (Dermot's direction, 2026-08-21). Renamed rather than removed, because the paper does the opposite of trafficking in the dragons-are-evil trope — it exists to hold real dragons apart from the adversary imagery, and deleting it would remove the one document making that argument. The problem was the *title*: in an index it put *dragon* beside the adversary, which is the association the body works to break. Old URL keeps working — redirect stub plus an `.htaccess` 301, the same pairing used for the Concordant rename — which matters because codex entries map giscus by pathname, so a bare rename would have orphaned the discussion thread.

### Fixed

- **Three consistency defects in the planetary-physics set, and the Tír na nÓg/Drithane habitability tension underneath one of them** (audit, 2026-08-22 — findings appended to `story-bible/canon-consistency-audit-2026-07.md`). [The Cost of the Crossing](src/lore/the-cost-of-the-crossing.md) flatly called Tír na nÓg "the one confirmed world in the catalogue a human can walk on unassisted", which [Drithane's](src/lore/planets/drithane.md) canonical breathable-with-acclimatisation atmosphere contradicts — restated on Tír na nÓg's own canonical classification, *naturally human-compatible*, with Drithane named as the gentlest case elsewhere; [tir-na-nog.md](src/lore/planets/tir-na-nog.md)'s parallel "dome, mask, or engineering" sentence (the pre-existing root of the tension) adjusted the same way. [The Ledger and the Truce](src/lore/the-ledger-and-the-truce.md) claimed Fliade's surface as "the driest in the settled record" — a superlative no canon supports, softened to "among the driest". [Weather on Other Worlds](src/lore/weather-on-other-worlds.md) claimed "exactly one new storm-severity classification in its history" — canon says only that the Four Islands *needed* a new classification, so the count is dropped.
- **Five of seven editions were rendering no hero slideshow at all** (found 2026-08-21). Every edition but `pets` inherited the default cast, and every character in it is filtered out on a narrowed domain — so `sciencefiction`, `starquest`, `fellowship`, `fellowship-archive` and `church-space` all fell back to the static hero image, correctly and silently, for as long as their narrowing has existed. Fixed by the casts above; `sciencefiction` needed its own ruling first, since it carried no character page to cast. **All seven editions now render a hero.**

- **A broken image on the Drithane lore page** (found 2026-08-21, live since 2026-08-17). `src/images/lore/planets/drithane.jpg` was the only image in the corpus in a `planets/` subdirectory while its front matter named a bare filename, and `lore-entry.njk` builds `/images/lore/` + the value — so the page requested a file that was not there. Moved flat, where every other planet's image is; `story-bible/images.md`'s slug corrected with it.
- **A broken slide in the homepage hero on every edition but undercover-pets.com** (found 2026-08-21). `heroCharacterIds` may name a character with no `image:` — 24 of 76 character pages have none, Elvira among them, and she is in the default cast — which rendered `<img src="…/images/characters/">`, a request for the directory. It also counted toward the crossfade's `--nN`, so the animation timed a slot for a slide that could never appear. A new `withImages` filter drops them before the count. Silent until now because a hero slide is decorative and `aria-hidden`.

- **Contrast failures on five palettes** (2026-08-21), found by the new checker and measured rather than eyeballed. **undercover-pets.com — the children's domain — had the worst contrast on the site**: its accent measured 2.32:1 on badges against a 4.5 floor, and its canon-facts control 2.13:1. Also `fellowship`, `church-space`, `sepia` and `light`, mostly on muted text and status badges sitting on `--color-surface-2` two steps darker than the page. And the `fellowship` palette's hover was a *lighter* gold than its link colour, so pointing at a link made it harder to read — 2.98:1 against 6.00 at rest. Every palette but the exempt `solarized` now clears the floor on all thirteen checked pairs; the colours moved as little as the arithmetic allowed.

- **A `SITE_NOINDEX` build no longer emits a sitemap.** A testing or staging domain ships `robots.txt` with `Disallow: /` and `noindex, nofollow` on every page, and then shipped a `sitemap.xml` enumerating those same pages. Unreachable rather than harmful — robots.txt omits the `Sitemap:` line and disallows the file itself — but a list of URLs the domain is actively hiding is the wrong artifact to leave in a document root. Found while verifying a test subdomain build. Same shape as the `ranksAt` case already handled in `src/sitemap.njk`, now sharing one condition.
- **Documentation described a cPanel interface that no longer exists.** cPanel retired its separate *Subdomains* and *Addon Domains* pages and folded both into one **Domains** interface, so `TECHNICAL-README.md`'s "created via cPanel's own addon domain setup" and `cpanel-deploy.sh`'s "create the addon domain" pointed at icons that are gone — reading as though the feature had been removed rather than renamed. Both now describe **Domains → Create A New Domain**, the own-document-root choice that separates a build from an alias, the DNS case where nameservers are not cPanel's, and the fact that the same page is where an alias is finally re-pointed. Written as actions rather than icon names, since this interface has already moved once.
- **Two Aethelrock findings from the Benevolent Critic** (2026-08-20), both raised as issues on the day the clan-head portraits went up and both closed here. **Rhiannon Ceridwen's page counted the objections from the wrong clock** (#499): *"nine years of being told, at every Ridgemoot since"* — but nine years is her headship, from 2817, while the objections run from first contact in 2824, which against the story present of 2826 is two. Elapsed time has one correct value, so the fix is the fact and not the framing; the nine survives eight lines above it, where it belongs. **Cormac Dubhghlas chaired a Ridgemoot five years before he was a clan head** (#498): 2806 against a headship taken in 2811, at a body `aethelrock.md` defines as a gathering of *heads*. Repaired additively rather than by moving a date — he chaired **as his father's proxy** — which costs one clause, keeps both dates, and quietly establishes that Dubhghlas has been arguing this case across two generations, which *"has never once required updating"* already implied.


- **The lettering-ban failure applied back to the prompts written this week** (2026-08-19). #487 recovered the rule that **the lettering ban cannot beat the scene**; **seventeen prompts written on 19 August had the shape it forbids** — a text-bearing object plus an instruction to leave it blank. Fixed by changing scenes, never by strengthening negatives, using the three moves now recorded under Prompt craft: **remove** (Vexar's counter cleared of forms, Drey's desk bared, Strozzi's cards gone, the founding table's papers gone, Harrow's folder gone), **close** (Emma's notebook shut and her pencil down, Kate Ukrainka no longer mid-sentence but with the work shut and a mug in both hands, the Institute's notebook shut, the narrative-works volumes all shut, Halvern's wallets tied), and **substitute** — [what nobody certifies](src/lore/what-nobody-certifies.md) went from *four framed certificates, each one blank of any writing* to **four struck metal seals in wall niches and a fifth niche empty**, which keeps the whole idea and removes the writing surface rather than arguing with it. [The Plainmark](src/lore/plainmark.md) is the one whose subject cannot be moved, so it gets the opposite handling recorded instead: describe the marks as shapes and never name the function, keep nothing else markable in frame, and if glyphs still appear **crop tighter rather than add negatives**. **The prompt-craft rule itself was wrong and is corrected**: its *Ban lettering explicitly* bullet offered *plain unmarked folders* as its own worked example, which is precisely the shape that fails.

- **The Reeves emblem is confirmed deliberate, and the rule it looked like it broke is scoped** (2026-08-19). The 19 August audit flagged `reeves.jpg` as an abstract emblem sitting oddly beside the 12 August rule that *AIs get portraits like everyone else*. **The flag was wrong about the decision and right about the file**: it was settled on 13 August in #415 and carried consistently into both `image_alt` lines, and nothing in `images.md` or `image-prompts.md` said so. Now recorded in both. **The rule's scope is the resolution** — it answers how to depict an AI *that has a body*, so a generator's photoreal default cannot stand in for one, and never required inventing a body for a system with none; [Lucene-9000](src/characters/lucene-9000.md) is *a mobile AI humanoid* where [Reeves](src/characters/reeves.md) is *investigative support intelligence*. Three worked cases settled the same day: the Eden Warden became the habitat, and the two Reeves became a deliberate pair. **The lesson underneath is general and now written down: the lettering ban cannot beat the scene** — the earlier Eden brief asked for a case-file interface and banned lettering in the same breath, and came back reading `CASE FILE: ALPHA-7`. The fix is to change the scene, never to strengthen the negative. **And the pair's difference is content, not variation**: Eden's pattern is *half-found and not yet claimed*, Threshold's is a ring almost closed and deliberately not closed.

- **`images.md` audited for stale counts; three sections were wrong and one of my own was duplicated** (2026-08-19). **Open work 0** said *28 images* replaced with placeholder cards; **six have since been replaced with real images and were never marked** (`petra-voss`, `brother-daire`, `ilsabet-marrowtide`, `rasa-oyelaran`, `eden-warden`, `reeves`), leaving **22 still carded** — separated by shape (cards are 1600×900 at 52–77 KB, portraits 1200×670 at 96–217 KB) and then **confirmed by opening a file at each end**, per the file's own rule against reasoning from filenames. **Open work 3**'s *contemporary-stock-headshot cluster (11 files)* describes images that no longer exist — all eleven became PENDING cards on 12 August — and its `validate-images: on` block passes anyway because the files exist, which is **exactly the drift the section's own closing note predicted**, four days after it was written. **Open work 6**'s alt-text figures are stale in the good direction: *68 pages under 80 characters* is now **7**, and *40 at 120+* is now **112**, across 135 illustrated pages. **And *The ten worth doing first* was duplicated by my own 19 August passes** — eight of its files were prompted a second time because both new lists were derived from pages lacking an `image:` and this section was never checked against them. Reconciled in place: the newer brief governs for six, **Open work 6's brief governs for `predatory-entities`** because a vacated habitat compartment holds the tone line better in-setting than a woodland clearing, and the older Aoife brief's **keep the face concealed** — canon reasoning the newer entry missed — is adopted into it. Sections that check out unchanged: *The seventeen replaced on 12 August* (17, all present) and Open work 4's New London defects (still 1408×768).

- **Open work 5 listed delivered lore illustrations as a queue** (2026-08-19). The *Missing lore illustrations* section was headed *19 pages*; **23 of the 30 slugs it names already exist**, and the seven that do not were named in passing and never prompted. Retitled as archived, prompts left in place as the record for the images they produced, and the true outstanding count re-derived: **52 lore pages**, most of them written since July. Same failure as Open work 1, found the same way.

- **Open work 1 listed thirty-four delivered portraits as a queue** (2026-08-19). `story-bible/images.md`'s *Missing portraits* section was headed *28 pages*, listed **34**, and had **all 34 already shipped** — the count was wrong, the label was wrong, and finished work read as outstanding. Retitled and dated, with the audit method recorded; **the prompts stay in place**, since they are the prompt of record for the images they produced and deleting them to tidy a status line would destroy provenance. A true outstanding list of **25 pages** is added at the end of the section, none of them overlapping. Also flags a stale instruction inside those archived prompts: most end *Portrait orientation*, which predates the settled 1200×675 16:9 convention that 42 of the 52 delivered files actually follow.

- **The rescue chapter's `andrew` pov id matched no character** (2026-08-19). `s01e00c04` used `::: pov andrew` while [Andrew Falkorian](src/characters/andrew-falkorian.md)'s page carries `id: falkorian`, so his scene-POV page resolved to no portrait and no link back to him. Synced to `falkorian`, moving that one scene-POV URL with it; the chapter's own note had pre-authorised the sync (*the ids may need syncing*) and the page was six days old. **`anne` could not sync the same way** — the surname form is Karla's and an `id` must be unique for the portrait lookup — so Anne's page carries `id: anne` deliberately.

- **The Pandoid sapience question is answered, in place and sourced** (2026-08-16, #443). The note had asked it since 26 July while #443 and the index both recorded it as settled — *sapient but low-tech* — on a ruling that appeared nowhere in the repo. Dermot confirmed the sapience half directly: the Pandoids are sapient and one of very few humanoid-like aliens, so Fliade is a first-contact world under the FTP sapience clause. Written into `intake-2026-07-26.md` dated. Their technological level was **not** confirmed and stays open, and the humanoid half collides with a published refusal — see below.

- **A humanoid collision is flagged before it can be written into canon** (2026-08-16). [What the Record Refuses](src/lore/what-the-record-refuses.md) states, in prose and in its summary table, that the Krenyi are the only other sapient humanoids, and calls that refusal the load-bearing one. Sapient humanoid-like Pandoids would be a second exception. Nothing is broken — Fliade is unwritten and the Pandoids appear nowhere in `src/` — but the first page describing them would contradict a live canon page. Three readings are recorded in `intake-2026-07-26.md`, `story-bible/species-design.md` carries a flag against its own premise, and **no page was changed**: the choice is authorial and gates writing Fliade.

Collapsed back to one.

## [1.22.0] — 2026-08-16

A release about the machinery for noticing things. Two doctrines that looked
opposed turned out to govern different objects, and stating the boundary
between them produced a named review process, a public backlog to file its
findings in, and the first three findings themselves. Alongside that, the
Safety Corps gained an internal structure, Kieme gained three titles it can be
translated by, and one domain's deploy stopped failing silently.

The through-line, if there is one, is that **silence is the expensive failure**
— a cron that reports nothing, a gap nobody marked, an untidiness filed as a
fault. Most of what is below is an attempt to make one or another kind of
silence legible.

### Added

- **Journal: [Kieme Means Gill](src/journal/kieme-means-gill.md)** (2026-08-16). The naming problem written up as craft rather than as a fix. The entry's argument is that the mistake was about *which kind of problem it was* — not that `Kieme` reads as a fish organ in German, but that Conseleme had a living translatable devotional name and Kieme's was marked legacy, leaving one tier of three exposed to translation with nothing to land on. Hence the principle it ends on the way to: **titles translate, coinages transliterate** — a translator meeting *the Everlasting Ground* renders the sense, a translator meeting *Kieme* gets a sound and whatever that sound already means where it lands. And the closing turn, which is the reason the entry exists: having three names for one thing looked like untidiness to be reduced, and writing down *why* the tier has several produced the best sentence in the glossary. *"I went in to clean up a mess and the mess turned out to be the evidence."*

- **Kieme gains three titles, and the reason it has several becomes part of the entry** (2026-08-15). `Kieme` is the ordinary German noun for a fish gill — checked and deliberately kept on 2026-08-04 with a recorded revisit trigger. Revisiting it found the real gap was structural rather than linguistic: **Conseleme has a living translatable devotional name (the Everlasting Ground) while Kieme's translatable name, Holy Triumvirate, was marked legacy**, leaving Kieme the only Upper Structure tier with no current name that survives translation. Hence the fish.

  The repair is **additive, not a rename**. Three titles in three registers: **the Silent Origin** (living devotional name, direct counterpart to the Everlasting Ground, taking the constraint for the name — the tier does not speak and never has); **the Undivided** (the title, standing where *Most Holy Triumvirate* stood, refusing the count without refusing the shamrock, since one/three/many are rival images rather than rival answers); and **the First Condition** (Archive register, deliberately undevotional). *Holy Triumvirate* stays synonymous and pre-retirement filings read as written — its weakness being that a triumvirate is three men ruling, which is both a count and a committee, and this tier is neither. **`Kieme` remains the term of art**: no migration, the `-eme` pairing with Conseleme undisturbed, no corpus sweep. Titles translate where coinages transliterate, so this fixes every language rather than German alone.

  The entry now also says **why** the tier carries several names, which is the more interesting half. Nothing here has ever spoken, it permits no identifying intervention, and it is inferable only through invariants — so **no tradition was ever told what to call it**, and each named it from what it could see from where it stood. *A tier with exactly one settled name would be a tier somebody had been told about.* Extended per Dermot to other species, which name the tier or the whole Cascade out of their own psychology, sociology and language; those appear translated under the record's existing default, so a name kept untranslated is a species making a point by it. And the striking part survives translation: **the names agree about almost nothing and the constraints agree almost exactly**, which is what one would expect of something real that has never spoken.

- **The reading plan gains a narrator, and the record gains a list of its own gaps** (2026-08-16).
