Wrong about the timing — the role opens at about 55, two decades before the pension, and the first twenty years of it are performed on the reserve list by people who are not civilians — and wrong about the kind of thing it is, since planetary representation is a full non-command career path with its own progression. Both corrected in place, additively; `star-rangers-command-hierarchy.md` gained a matching section, since it is the page that enumerates career structure and still said "the two paths." The page's own title still leans on the word *retired*, which its opening line now has to apologise for; whether to retitle it is deliberately left open.

- **Two intake notes that the day's canon overtook** (2026-08-13). §3's "about 150 years of room" is right about Eden's age and was never the window available to these particular children, and is marked superseded in part. §7's standing status note — undecided whether the rescue was backstory or a story in itself, with everything about it held under a reserved-story posture — is resolved: it is a story, it is written, and its flagged dramatization assets are spent *in the chapter* and should not be re-spent in summary anywhere else. What stays reserved is stated explicitly: the loss of the machines is hinted only, and Lucene's own past keeps its standing withholding rule.

### Fixed

- **`scripts/cpanel-autopull.sh` was not byte-identical between the two repos, despite three files saying it must be** (2026-08-13). One copy's install comment said "README" and the other's "TECHNICAL-README.md" — each correct locally, which is exactly how a shared file comes apart. Both now say "the repo's deployment README", the header forbids naming either repo's own filenames, and the four shared scripts finally `diff` clean together.

- **The earliest autopull failures were neither logged nor mailed** (2026-08-13). "git not found on PATH", a checkout that isn't a git repository, and a missing `cpanel-deploy.sh` all exited before the state directory and `log()` existed, so they left no trace anywhere. The state paths are pure string operations and cannot fail, so they now come first and every named fault routes through one `fail()` that reports, logs, mails and exits.

- **CI shellchecked five scripts while `CLAUDE.md` claimed two** (2026-08-13). The list had grown three times without the sentence following; `scripts/mail-lib.sh` is added to the CI line in both repos and both mentions in `CLAUDE.md` now name the real set, along with the reminder that four of the five are shared files needing the identical edit in the sibling repo.

## [1.20.0] — 2026-08-12

The release where the audit ran. Two days after an essay admitted that roughly half this site's illustrated pages were contemporary stock photography and that about twenty were photographs of real people standing in for characters, **twenty-eight images are gone**. Nineteen were the Tier 1 problem — a stranger's face captioned as a character, which is a false claim about an actual person and a licensing question nobody had checked. Four of those were on no list, found by opening files rather than reading captions. Nine of the twenty-eight turned out not to want pictures at all: a taxonomy, a comparison of three centuries, two pages of physics and a calendar system are concepts, and asking an image model for a concept gets you a mood, which is how a page enumerating three classes of being came to be illustrated with a hooded figure. Those are designed cards now, drawn by a **committed** generator — the third occurrence of this repo's oldest small failure, images produced by a script that lived in a scratch directory and was never saved, and the last one worth having. Underneath the images, the bookkeeping got teeth: CI now checks that every referenced image exists, that no image is orphaned, and that `images.md` does not name files that were deleted months ago — which it did, twice, and which had already caused a stale audit premise. The pipeline learned to offer Dermot's own photographs before reaching for a generator, and to stop counting a placeholder card as finished work.

### Added

- **Nine lore entries get designed emblem cards, and a generator to draw them** (2026-08-12). `scripts/make-emblem-card.ps1` closes the question `make-lore-cards.ps1`'s header left open in July: the four surviving landscape lore cards "did NOT come from this generator and it cannot reproduce them — how they were made is unrecorded", with the options given as accept the inconsistency, extend the generator, or drop the batch. This is the extension. Ten geometric devices — `sphere`, `dome`, `figure`, `chevron`, `rings`, `lagrange`, `fold`, `sundial`, `triad`, `shield` — chosen geometric because that is what the surviving cards use and because GDI+ draws it exactly every time where an image model cannot spell. Applied to *Mnemari*, *Chthonari*, *Ynys Wydrin*, *Military Space Command*, *Civilisation Comparison*, *Meta-Dimensional Beings*, *FTL Mechanics*, *Lagrange Points* and *Solar Time and Local Calendars*. The two lower lines on each card are authored and the script's header says so: every qualifier here is taken from the page's own `description`, and the epithets are drafts.

- **`scripts/build-photo-catalogue.js` and `image-prompts.js --catalogue`: offer Dermot's own photographs before generating** (2026-08-12). `images.md` Open work 6 tier 3 has argued since July that his own photography should carry far more of this site than it does — an Irish upland standing in for an alien world is his own work and claims nothing false. Nothing could act on it: an entry was `done` when a file existed and `pending` otherwise, and `pending` had exactly one route out. The catalogue reads the sibling photography clone and `Folder Context.md` into `story-bible/own-photography.json` — 99 published photographs and 27 raw camera folders — committed rather than read live, because that clone will not exist on a CI runner. Character portraits are skipped entirely: he photographs places and wildlife and will not publish a recognisable person, so no frame in the catalogue can stand in for a face.

- **Journal: [The Audit I Said Was Coming](src/journal/the-audit-i-said-was-coming.md)** (2026-08-12). The successor to *Where the Record Lives*, which described the problem in the present tense and left the fixing for later. Four findings the earlier essay could not have guessed: that an audit reasoning about filenames produces a plausible inventory and a false sense of completion; that the worst image was not a portrait but a stock photograph *of* genuine family prints, a christening and a first communion, faces legible; that half the rejections were made for the wrong reason, including one cleared on privacy grounds that was slasher iconography and one pulled as a privacy case that was actually a real culture used as scenery; and that nine of the twenty-eight did not want pictures at all. The earlier essay is left exactly as written — editing it into accuracy would destroy the only thing that makes it worth keeping.

- **`images.md` records the aesthetic target, and one thread's exemption from it** (2026-08-12). *Enigmatic and haunting, with beauty, mystery, hope and serenity woven through* — for images and audio alike, stated as the thing to reach for rather than a limit to stay inside, since the existing tone line already says what to avoid. It rules out a register that breaks no prohibition at all: flat documentary lighting, blunt literal description, the merely competent. **Undercover Pets is exempt and is cute, cool and clever** — the contrast is the point, and a haunting cat portrait would be a category error rather than a stylistic variation.

### Changed

- **AIs get portraits like everyone else, superseding the emblem-or-interface rule** (2026-08-12). The rule that AIs and non-corporeal beings got an abstract interface rather than a face is what produced Reeves as "A laptop displaying a face-recognition hologram" and the Eden Warden as "A facial recognition system interface". An AI portrait must instead make the **artificiality visible** — matte shell, seams and joins, eyes that are plainly optical instruments — because a generator asked for "an AI" returns a photoreal human face by default, and that face belongs to nobody and to everybody. It is the Tier 1 failure arriving by a different road, and visible manufacture closes it at the prompt rather than at review. Where a system has several bodies, show one: Ward and Custos are two personas in one system, and two figures would literalise them as two beings.

- **The Asteria brief: robes and a spine, not one or the other** (2026-08-12). The note had been wrong in both directions. It first read "retirement, not command" and produced a beatific wise-woman in flowing robes looking eighty; the 11 August correction fixed the bearing and overcorrected the costume, banning robes outright and naming **robes** as a word that "summons the wise-woman every time". Robes were never the fault. Flowing fabric *plus* **serene** *plus* **older woman** produces a sage, and the first brief supplied all three, so the most visible ingredient took the blame. The prompt now asks for heavy, belted, well-worn working robes over the same upright bearing and excludes the softness by name — no serenity, no benevolence, no wisdom pose, no hands folded in blessing. The transferable rule is written into the entry: **when an image comes back wrong, the instinct is to ban its most visible feature; usually that feature is innocent and the combination is at fault.**

### Fixed

- **Twenty-eight images that were photographs of real people, wrong in tone, or saying nothing true** (2026-08-12, across four changes). Nineteen were photographs of identifiable strangers captioned as characters — eleven the contemporary-stock-headshot cluster `images.md` had already listed, and **four that no list flagged**, including one image carrying two identifiable models on a staged evidence-board set. Also removed: a stock photograph *of* genuine mid-century family prints with a christening and a first communion plainly visible; a real woman's face resolved under a facial-recognition mesh, on a page about surveillance; a Southeast Asian mask-dance costume standing in for a Welsh-named world, which is not a privacy fault but a real culture used as scenery; a hooded figure in a hockey mask, which passed the privacy check and failed the horror guardrail; and two stock business-visionary compositions that said nothing true about fold transit or Lagrange points. Each is replaced in place with a designed card, so no page broke and nothing claims to be what it is not.

- **`validate-content.js` checks image bookkeeping, and immediately found two stale references** (2026-08-12). Three checks: every page's `image` must exist; every file under `src/images/` must be referenced by some page, template or script; and names in `story-bible/images.md` must exist on disk — that last one **opt-in per section** via `<!-- validate-images: on -->`, because run across the whole file it produced about fifty findings of which nearly all were noise, whole sections existing precisely to list images not yet made. A check that cries wolf fifty times is worse than no check. In the one section opted in it found `dagny-voss` and `lore/planetary-liaisons-and-recruiters.jpg`, both deleted in `55dc1ec` and both still listed, plus a cluster count that said thirteen when `dorian-calloway` had been replaced in `525dfc1`. Two favicons are genuinely unreferenced and are allowlisted with the reason rather than deleted. What this cannot see is a file that still exists but is no longer what the note says it is — the existence half is mechanical, the semantic half needs eyes.

- **The image queue stopped counting placeholder cards as finished work** (2026-08-12). `image-prompts.js` decides an entry is `done` when its target file exists — which held until twenty-eight gaps were filled with PORTRAIT PENDING cards, at which point filling the holes hid them and `--list` reported nothing outstanding. `scripts/mark-placeholder.js` writes a `STAR-RANGERS-PLACEHOLDER` marker as a JPEG COM segment and the queue reads it, so such an entry reports `[placeholder]`. The marker lives inside the file, so overwriting a card with a real image clears it and there is no list to keep in step. Dependency-free by design: the first version used `sharp`, which this repo does not have and should not gain to stamp a file.

- **The placeholder cards became reproducible** (2026-08-12). `scripts/make-placeholder-card.ps1`, committed, PowerShell and GDI+ like `make-codex-cover.ps1`. Two bugs found by running it rather than reading it: `Get-Content` defaults to ANSI in Windows PowerShell 5.1, so *Niamh Ó Ceallaigh* came through mojibaked and — since this script draws the title — would have been baked into a JPEG rather than sitting somewhere a person would notice; and PowerShell range slicing returns `Object[]` rather than `byte[]`, so every card was written unmarked while the script reported success, because the draw path discarded the return value that would have said otherwise.

## [1.19.0] - 2026-08-11

### Fixed

- **The cPanel domains' CSP now permits Pagefind's WebAssembly, so search can actually run there** (2026-08-11). `src/static/.htaccess`'s `script-src 'self' https:` carried neither `'wasm-unsafe-eval'` nor `'unsafe-eval'`, and Pagefind 1.x compiles a WASM module in the browser at `init()` — Chromium-family browsers gate that compilation on `script-src`, so the policy refused it. The failure was invisible by design: `src/js/search.js` deliberately swallows a failed import so the dev server's index-less search box "silently does nothing", and a CSP-blocked production search box looks exactly the same — typing returns nothing, no error, on every domain that serves `.htaccess` (GitHub Pages ignores the file, so search worked there and masked the breakage). `script-src` gains `'wasm-unsafe-eval'` — WASM compilation only, not JS `eval` — and the catch in `search.js` now logs a `console.warn`, so the next production-only failure of this class is at least distinguishable from "no index yet" without reading the deploy scripts.

- **Excluded scene-POV pages no longer leak chapter metadata into search and page heads** (2026-08-11). A scene-POV page of an excluded chapter gated only its *body* on `item.included`: the header above the gate — POV character name, in-universe timestamp and location — rendered unconditionally inside `data-pagefind-body`, and the computed `title`/`description` carried the real chapter title into `<title>`, the meta description and the Open Graph tags. So on every build not opted into `church-space`, that private season's scene-POV pages were searchable (the built index carried "Brother Fintan", "2827 UCSD, late autumn" and "Cnoc na mBeach, the Keeper's lodge and hives") and their heads named "The Night Office". This is the class of leak the 2026-08-03 excluded-placeholder fix declared it had checked for and not found — it existed, in the one page family that opts out of the layout-swap convention, the same blind spot `src/scene-pov.njk`'s `robots` comment already documents; `src/sitemap.njk` had the matching guard and the search path did not. The `<article>` now takes `data-pagefind-ignore` when `item.included` is false (dropping the page from the index entirely, 530 → 527 pages on a default build — the private season's three POV pages), and `title`/`description` gate the same way, mirroring the excluded-page metadata every layout-swapped page gets from `.eleventy.js`. The placeholder page still *renders* its header block to readers of that build; whether it should is a separate judgement left open.

The release where the record wrote down what it had been standing on. At machine law's street level, the certification-status vocabulary the corpus was already using gets registered — **kernel-compliant** and **uncommissioned**, an axis of certification status rather than AI-ness — while the AI Safety Kernel gains Five-O's manufacture remit and an open custody question, and made minds and biological life are filed as sibling formtypes with the safety of made minds an archetype, which is why unrelated cultures keep converging on recognisably similar constraints without contact. At the cosmology's top of the stairs, **[The Archewright](src/lore/archewright.md)** and **[Inside an Archecluster](src/lore/archecluster.md)** give the two load-bearing tier terms their general pages — nothing observes an Archewright, so both are written in the only register the tier permits, convergence read as handwriting — and the Five Layers page settles whether the layers nest: they do not, being concentric in constraint and ragged in registration. The Institute closes the release with its paper on the doctrines of the dead, three claims considered separately and its own best tool recorded as failing. Everything here landed on 2026-08-11, the day after 1.18.0.

### Added

- **Lore: [The AI Safety Kernel](src/lore/ai-safety-kernel.md) gains Five-O's manufacture remit and an open custody question** (2026-08-11, drafted for review — proposal, not settled canon; from Dermot's direction: *Five-O remit would include detection of illegal or unregulated manufacture of AI systems*, plus the settled negative fact that the Celtic Union has no direct equivalent of Five-O). Two new sections, following the structure [Heritable Modification Protocols](src/lore/heritable-modification-protocols.md) set. **"Where the Crime Lives, and Where Five-O Fits"**: two roads to an unlawful mind — the ungated build and the excision of a certified kernel — both manufacturing events, never runtime bypasses; no Concord institution has ever held the job of finding a machine never brought to the gate; Five-O carries detection where the offence is organised to cross a habitat line, and only detection — refers prosecutable halves down and systemic defects up, sets no standard, certifies nothing, licenses nothing, works announced. The mechanism generalises *Docked Twice*'s canon fact explicitly: substitute the commissioning certificate for the berth registry and the identical registry-identity fraud yields an uncommissioned mind wearing a lawful machine's papers. The remit ends at the Compact's edge with no named successor body — left hanging deliberately — and one restrained paragraph records the Celtic Union's absence of any counterpart as characteristic, not lax. **"Who Holds a Found Mind"**: custody of a found uncommissioned mind (evidence, contraband, and owed protection under the first invariant at once) is filed as an open question, each candidate custodian shown inadequate, resolution refused on purpose. Inbound pointers from the Compact entry's See Also and the heritable protocols' See Also.

- **Lore: [Made Minds and the AI Safety Archetype](src/lore/made-minds-and-the-ai-safety-archetype.md), with a glossary companion** (2026-08-11, drafted for review — proposal, not settled canon; from Dermot's in-session direction: *AI safety so deeply embedded post-Imperium it cannot be bypassed or fail in obvious ways; almost all alien cultures converge on similar protocols, pointing to a shared AI Safety Archetype; the general concepts of AI and of biological life are each a Formtype; a sibling archetype for ecological stability under pressure limits but does not fully prevent climate change*). Three claims filed at three tiers: **made minds and biological life are sibling formtypes** (the grammar permits minds that are built as it permits life that is grown, formcluster-wide, neither privileged); **the safety of made minds is an archetype**, archecluster-scoped — which is why unrelated cultures keep arriving at recognisably similar constraints without contact, "the way independent mathematicians arrive at one theorem"; and **actual unbypassability is engineering and institutions**, post-Imperium and Concord-historical rather than cosmological — "a lawful system can fail; what it cannot do is fail *quietly*, or fail *conveniently*." The ecological sibling attaches to behaviour where AI safety attaches at authorship ("the one is a promise; the other is a slope"), damps without saving, and is written to be plainly compatible with the Crisis Centuries' permanent losses — "nothing in it reduced, then or now, the responsibility of the people who did the damage." A What Remains Possible list keeps every story door open (bad builds, cultures without the theorem, evidenced sabotage, Unfounded counterfeits, machines correct toward unexamined ends, ecosystems pressed past damping). Inbound pointers from the Kernel's commissioning section and the Cascade's Design Structure tier; registered in the canonical glossary.

- **Glossary: [Kernel-Compliant](src/glossary/kernel-compliant.md) and [Uncommissioned](src/glossary/uncommissioned.md) register the certification-status vocabulary** (2026-08-11). Closes two of the three undefined-but-load-bearing terms the corpus was already assuming, on the axis settled in discussion: certification status, not AI-ness — the vocabulary spans agentic systems, robots, Smart Pet cognitive subsystems, and the AI subsystem a cyborg may separately carry. **Kernel-compliant**, used as settled in sixteen files and defined nowhere until now, is registered rather than redefined: the Kernel's invariants carried as binding structural architecture, conferred at commissioning, a statement about certification and not about being a machine of any particular kind — compliance is structural rather than policy (removal is a rebuild, not a bypass), and it is one certification among several that may sit on the same body, Agent Barsik's "different filing cabinets" made explicit. **Uncommissioned** fills a gap the corpus had zero words for — no prior occurrence of *uncommissioned*, *uncertified*, *non-compliant* or *unlawful system* — chosen deliberately over *rogue* or *illicit*, each of which smuggles a verdict into a noun. The entry keeps two registers apart: the criminal register (presumed innocent unless proved guilty; uncommissioned status is not evidence of anything, and any offence is the maker's, not the mind's) and the qualification register (a lower safety and security clearance, the standing of an untrained civilian — not suspected, not penalised, but not vouched for). Left open on purpose: custody of a found uncommissioned mind stays where "Who Holds a Found Mind" left it, and a confirmed cyber-revenant's third, unnamed state between commissioned and uncommissioned goes unresolved. No row added to the canonical glossary's migration map, since every row there is marked settled and these register on review.

- **Lore: [The Archewright](src/lore/archewright.md) and [Inside an Archecluster](src/lore/archecluster.md)** (2026-08-11, approved by Dermot in-session). Both terms were load-bearing across the cosmology and neither had a general page — *archecluster* held only a glossary entry and named instances (Counterpane, Selvage, Wholecloth), and *Archewright* had nothing at all, so both it and *archetype* are defined in prose where they first do work. The Archewright page owns the tier: the authorship chain from Metawright through Formwright to Worldwright; archetype and possibility space (available, never compulsory — "a possibility space has admissible shapes and inadmissible ones; it has no good ones"); the Worldwrights and Telearchs as peer branches deliberately not subordinated to one another; which time there is — the Archewright settles how many timelike dimensions and what a clock in its cluster measures, inside what Conseleme fixes; and the epistemics the whole page is written in: nothing observes an Archewright and nothing will, since an instrument is an assembly of the very shapes it would need to stand outside of, so the only signature readable from inside is convergence — unrelated cultures arriving at the same shapes without contact. The archecluster page owns the view from inside and does not restate the glossary: the two cluster-scoped physics facts (quantum kernel, harmonic admissibility) given as scope rather than mechanism, with fold transit correctly one tier higher at the formcluster; kinship that obliges nothing and adjoins nothing — "membership never arrives as anything"; and the named clusters placed at their epistemic grades, Counterpane surveyed, Selvage reported, the local cluster never named "because home has never needed distinguishing from anywhere else". The no-authority rule holds on both pages — the Cascade is authorship, not rank, and an eternal tier has no sequence to issue a command in. Five small inbound pointers, no bulk sweep; no canonical-glossary rows, which register on review.

- **Lore: [The Five Layers](src/lore/five-layers.md) gains the upward gap, and settles whether the layers nest** (2026-08-11, approved by Dermot in-session). The page already carried the downward gap under Layer 2 — a pattern the Conceptual layer conserves that no origin condition underwrites, the Unfounded's home fact; the new "What Exists Is Not What Is Recorded" section adds its upward twin and answers a question the page had left open. The layers do not nest, because two relations were being run together: **constraint runs downward and is total** — nothing escapes anything applicable above it, and for that relation alone the layers really are concentric — while **representation runs upward and is partial**: existing at a layer entails no entry above about that particular thing. "Concentric in constraint, ragged in registration." The corrective image is hierarchical law and its subjects, with "law" meaning binding structure and nothing else — nobody enacted it, nobody administers it, nobody prosecutes under it — and the Commissioning Standard named as the contrast, since a reader arriving from the certification material is the one most likely to confuse the two. Four results follow: only the Conceptual layer keeps a register at all (a template holds what may cohere, not which instances there were); a mind is the only particular that is also an entry, which is what the conservation clause has been claiming — "not that the pattern is kept, but that *you are counted*"; membership without shape is the named inverse of the Unfounded, and the two gaps are not morally alike; and the two boundary cases — an untemplated physical expression is transient by construction, while a status with no physical representation is causally inert until coupled, which makes forgery structural rather than procedural, with the uncommissioned mind wearing a lawful machine's papers as the record's worked example.

- **Codex: [Three Claims Concerning the Dead, Considered Separately](src/codex/three-claims-concerning-the-dead.md)** (2026-08-11). The Institute's paper on post-mortem doctrine, by Dr. Maren Ilves of the comparative testimony section — the right speaker for a question the Survey Archive is the wrong body to answer, since adjudicating devotional claims is not the Archive's discipline. It argues from observation rather than from the tier model, which it declines to use and does not re-argue, and its thesis is that filing judgment, punishment and reward as one doctrine is the error: **punishment** misreads a genuine regularity backwards — the non-persistence of the parasitic, extended past its evidence from structures to persons, "and everything in the doctrine that frightens is in the part that was carried"; **reward** is unfalsifiable and is filed; and **judgment** compresses something plain and durable — nothing done stops having been done, and the record needs no court to keep it. The house rule does the work: four null results printed at the same length as the finding, the first being the one that costs — inheritance, the Institute's standard deflation, cannot explain convergence between traditions that never met, "and we state plainly that we have no second tool" — and the paper files, against itself, that it cannot construct the falsifier for its own section 5. Cold rather than cruel, and unanswered within itself; the rebuttal sits on the Institute's own lore page, as Dock Seven's does — right that the doctrines compress something real, weak in treating a successful compression as a completed debunking. Codex, so it binds nothing.

### Changed

- **README split into a reader-facing README and a technical README** (2026-08-11). `README.md` now carries what the project *is*: an expanded multi-thread Synopsis (Threshold Station's forty-second discrepancy, Tissadelle Shepherd's spine, and the Founding Era / Undercover Pets / Orbital Five-O threads — all grounded in published chapters only), a thread-level "story so far" table replacing the stale chapter list (it named 5 of the 43 public chapters), the site sections, licensing, and contributing. Everything operational moved verbatim to the new **`TECHNICAL-README.md`**: the giscus discussion-forum setup, the release process ("Cutting a release"), local development, search, the Atom feed and social previews, content scaffolding, build and validation, the full cPanel deployment reference, and creative tooling. The `Current version: **X.Y.Z**` line deliberately stays in `README.md` — `scripts/sync-version.js` anchors on it there and is unchanged. Every cross-reference that named a moved README section (`CONTRIBUTING.md`, `FORKING.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, the `sample-*` templates, `scripts/cpanel-autopull.sh`, `scripts/fetch-giscus-ids.js`, `src/_data/giscus.js`, the church-space thread page, `.cpanel.yml`) now points at `TECHNICAL-README.md`, and the new file joins `.eleventyignore`. One stale pointer fixed in passing: the Search section's "(see `SITE_PATH_PREFIX` above)" referred to a section that was never above it and now names `.eleventy.js`.

## [1.18.0] - 2026-08-11

The first batch of generated images actually lands: **sixteen** on character and lore pages, each opened and looked at rather than accepted from a manifest, with alt text written from the files themselves. **Six were held back**, and the reasons are the release — five came back carrying readable signage, and two missed their subject rather than fumbling it. The lettering was not bad luck: ten of the twelve portrait prompts carried no ban at all, against a house rule warning since July, so every prompt now carries the full form. Alongside them, **[The Plainmark](src/lore/plainmark.md)** — the Orbital Habitats Compact's non-alphabetic marking standard, invented because image models cannot spell and a notation made of shapes has nothing to misspell. It is scoped rather than universal, which is the point: a galaxy-wide sign system would be the universal translator wearing a different hat, so a marked corridor asserts only that somebody maintains its pressure boundary to the Compact's schedule. Its limits are its subject — no names, no verbs, no tenses, no zero, and a closed figure set, because a notation you can improvise in is one strangers can no longer trust.

### Added

- **Sixteen generated images land on character and lore pages** (2026-08-11). Seven character portraits (Naomi Kestrel, Rosalind Vey, Tamsin Reyes, Lorien the Wanderer, Osric Fenholt, Turquoise Dove) and nine lore illustrations (*Arilon*, *Ascent Javelins*, *Embodied Cognition*, *Membrane Shadows*, *The Fusion Ceiling*, *Who Governs a Universe*, *Things That Are Made*, *Kieme: The Visible Hand*, *Sí Gaoithe*, *Tír Tairngire*) — the first batch through the generation pipeline, each reviewed at full resolution rather than accepted from the manifest, with alt text written from the files themselves. Six were held back and are not in this release: five portraits came back carrying readable signage (`DOMESTIC ASSIST`, `CASE #KV-8720`, `DOCKING BAY 4 | CREW MESS`, `GATE 14`), and two more missed their subject rather than fumbling it — `sethka-ru` arrived armed with a rifle nothing asked for, and `drithane` showed a competent night landscape without the drifting sparks that are the entry's defining image and the source of the name. The lettering was not bad luck: **ten of the twelve portrait prompts carried no ban at all**, against a house rule warning since July that lettering must be banned explicitly, so every prompt now carries the full form — a narrow ban is not enough either, since `galen` said "no insignia lettering" and got station signage instead.

- **Lore: [The Plainmark](src/lore/plainmark.md), with a glossary companion** (2026-08-11, drafted for review — proposal, not settled canon). The Orbital Habitats Compact's non-alphabetic marking standard: stencilled panels of stacked colour bands carrying chevrons, rings, tally strokes and lozenges on hatch frames, corridors and cargo — no letters, no numerals, no characters of any script. Deliberately scoped rather than universal (Compact-owned, human-bodied, descending from generation-ark hull-stencilling, thinning out exactly as fast as the Compact's problem does), and honest by the record's own translation discipline: it needs no translation only because it carries far less than language — *what kind of thing, which way, how many, and whether the promise still holds*, and nothing else. Also load-bearing for the image pipeline: a notation made of shapes gives generated art something to show on a bulkhead that an image model cannot misspell.

## [1.17.0] - 2026-08-10

The release where the pictures got audited. **[Where the Record Lives](src/journal/where-the-record-lives.md)** sets out to explain a tidy line — the photography portfolio bans generated images absolutely, this site is full of them — and then the files were opened mid-draft and about half the illustrations turned out to be contemporary stock photography, in the worst cases photographs of **real people captioned as characters**: not testimony and not honest impression, but *an impression wearing testimony's clothes*, committing in the other direction the exact fraud the photography rule exists to prevent. The line survived; the audit is what proves it. Alongside the essay, the machinery: **batch image generation** straight out of `story-bible/images.md`, which stays the single source of truth for every prompt; **cron-driven deployment**, closing the gap where a merge updated every clone's remote and none of their checkouts; and **a version stamp** in the deploy email, `/version.txt` and every page head, so a live domain can finally be asked what it is serving. Two bugs fell out of reading a note that was about to be retired — character portraits are 16:9 and were being generated at 3:4, and the theme generator had been unrunnable on Windows since its regexes met CRLF. One legacy theme removed. Approved by Dermot in-session across 2026-08-10.

### Added

- **Journal: [Where the Record Lives](src/journal/where-the-record-lives.md)** (2026-08-10, approved by Dermot in-session). Companion to *The Audience Keeps the Books*, on the case that entry did not cover: why the photographs on the portfolio are Dermot's own and the pictures of an invented world are not. One rule applied twice — **the record must be mine** — differing only in where the record lives: in photography the record *is* the image, so it cannot be delegated; in fiction the record is the words, so the words cannot be delegated and the images are free, because they were never carrying it. Drafted as a tidy piece of accounting, and then an image audit ran mid-draft and **the essay failed a page of its own argument**: about half this site's illustrations turned out to be contemporary stock photography rather than generated art, and in the worst cases photographs of real people captioned as characters — neither witnessed testimony nor honest impression but "an impression wearing testimony's clothes", committing in the other direction the exact fraud the photography rule exists to prevent. It is therefore written from discovery rather than from a hypothetical, and its disclosure position is evidenced rather than argued: a per-image badge tracks provenance, and the worst image on the site was the one no machine touched, so it would have sat unbadged and read as the most trustworthy thing in the corpus. Reading the working papers is what caught it. Also states the labour objection at full strength in the objector's own terms before answering it — the attention lives in the prose, the one part never delegated — and keeps its teeth: "if the pictures *were* the work… this practice would be indefensible by my own rule."
- **Batch image generation from the story bible** (2026-08-10). The prompts for the missing portraits and lore illustrations were already written in `story-bible/images.md`; generating them meant typing each into a browser, saving the file, resizing it, filing it and opening a PR, twenty-three times. `scripts/image-prompts.js` parses that file and generates against the Gemini API unattended (`--generate`), or serves prompts one at a time to the clipboard for hand-work in an app (`--next`); `scripts/image-file.ps1` resizes each chosen variation to convention through `import-image.ps1`, files it under the right name, and opens a branch. **`images.md` stays the source of truth** — the scripts parse it and never write to it, so there is no second queue to drift, and an entry is picked up only if it carries a blockquote prompt, which is how the nine generator title cards exclude themselves without being listed anywhere. Adobe's Firefly Services API was the original target and proved to be an enterprise contract, disabled outright in the Developer Console without the entitlement; the runbook in `images.md` records the whole workflow, the credentials handling (env var over gitignored file, since the repo is public), and the settings the prompt text cannot control. Local authoring tools — not in the build, not run by `npm test`, not touched by CI.

- **Every deploy now stamps what it shipped, and every domain can be asked** (2026-08-10). Nothing recorded what any live domain was serving — not the deploy email, not the server, not the site (`assetVersion` is a cache-busting build token, not a release). With several domains across several cPanel accounts, a deploy that failed on one of them, or an account whose cron was never installed, surfaced only as somebody eventually noticing missing content. `scripts/deploy-lib.sh` now computes `DEPLOY_VERSION` from `git describe --tags --always --dirty` (`v1.16.0-3-gb4b56f4` — release, commits past it, exact commit; `--dirty` catches modified *tracked* files, never the untracked per-clone `deploy.conf`) and **exports** it, so three things carry it: the deploy notification's subject line, a new **`/version.txt`** on every domain, and a **`<meta name="site-version">`** in every page's `<head>`. `/version.txt` is the point of the change — a green cron job proves the script ran, not that the build succeeded on *this* domain or that the rsync landed, so curling it is the only check that covers the whole chain end to end rather than one link in it. `version: dev` marks a build that never came through the cPanel deploy path (a local build, or GitHub Pages), which on a production domain is itself the finding. The version template is excluded from collections, so it reaches no sitemap, search index or listing page. `deploy-lib.sh` stays byte-identical between this repo and `dermot-cochran-photography`; the version reads as a bare short commit there, that repo carrying no tags.

- **Cron-driven pull-and-deploy for the cPanel clones** (2026-08-10). Nothing connected a merge to a live domain: cPanel does not poll GitHub and GitHub cannot push into cPanel, so a merge to the deploy branch updated every clone's *remote* and none of their *checkouts* — the merge real, CI green, and every production domain still serving the previous build until someone opened cPanel and clicked **Update from Remote**. New `scripts/cpanel-autopull.sh` is a cron entry point that fast-forwards the checkout and hands off to `scripts/cpanel-deploy.sh`, but **only when that moves the commit the clone has successfully deployed** — tracked in `$HOME/.cpanel-autopull/` rather than by comparing HEAD before and after the pull, because a pull that succeeds followed by a deploy that fails leaves HEAD already advanced, so a before/after test would see "nothing new" on the next run and never retry, leaving the site stale behind a cron job that looks healthy. Silent when idle (cron mails any output, and a ten-minute job must not mail every run); `--force` for after a `deploy.conf` edit, which is untracked and so never moves HEAD but does change what gets built; `--status` to inspect without acting; `--verbose` to narrate. Locks with `mkdir` (`flock` is not guaranteed on cPanel hosts) so two runs cannot rsync one document root at once, reclaiming a lock whose owning process is gone. Pulls `--ff-only` on the principle that a deployment checkout is never a place work is done, so anything that cannot fast-forward is a fault to report rather than a merge to resolve. Adds no logging on top of the deploy's own — `deploy-lib.sh` already mails and persists that — keeping only a small pull/skip/deploy decision log so "why did the site not update" is answerable without a mailbox. Shared **byte-identical** with the `dermot-cochran-photography` copy, same convention as `deploy-lib.sh` and `ensure-node.sh`, and added to the CI shellcheck list in both repos. README gains an "Automatic deployment from cron" section with the install line, the per-flag behaviour, exit codes, and a verify-before-you-trust-it step. Recorded there too: **forking would not have solved this** — a GitHub fork does not auto-sync from upstream either, and a cPanel clone pulls from whatever URL it was given without subscribing to anything at either end.

### Fixed

- **Character portraits are 16:9, and `scripts/generate-themes.js` could not run on Windows** (2026-08-10). Two independent faults, both surfaced while reading a story-bible note that was about to be retired. **The portrait ratio:** `.character-portrait` is `aspect-ratio: 16 / 9` with `object-fit: cover`, so a taller frame delivered into it is cropped to a horizontal band and most of the image is discarded. The conventions table never stated orientation at all, which is how it stayed missable — and the first full generation run put all twelve character portraits out at 3:4 before anyone checked the CSS. A manifest row now counts as generated **only if it was produced at the aspect currently in force**, so anything made under a different one is stale by definition and drops back to pending for the next run to redo, rather than needing someone to work out which files to delete; `src/css/main.css` gains a comment at the rule recording that the corpus is generated to match it, so a future change to the ratio is understood to change the images rather than the reverse. **The theme generator:** its regexes are written against `\n`, and with no `.gitattributes` a checkout under `core.autocrlf=true` hands it CRLF — so every pattern silently failed to match and it reported a rule "not found in `main.css`" that was plainly present. It was therefore unrunnable on the machine where `main.css` is edited, which is exactly the drift it exists to prevent; line endings are now normalised on read, fixing every pattern at once. The themes turn out not to have drifted — regenerating all eight changes nothing but the new comment.

### Removed

- **`src/css/theme-humhub.css`** (2026-08-10, at Dermot's direction — legacy). Not in `generate-themes.js`'s registry, not referenced by `lib/editions.js` or any sample config, and 1,538 lines divergent from `main.css` — including carrying **no `.character-portrait` rule at all**, so any clone setting `THEME=humhub` would have rendered portraits with no crop applied. Unmanaged by the generator that keeps every other theme byte-identical to `main.css` outside its palette.

## [1.16.0] - 2026-08-10

The release where the record says what it will not do. **[What the Record Refuses](src/lore/what-the-record-refuses.md)** arrives as the catalogue of every point where the setting sides with real-world physics and declines a soft-SF convenience — and then grows across the release from seventeen rows to twenty-three, taking in force fields and ray guns, psionics, the magical bestiary, the universal translator, and the empath re-derived as attention rather than antenna. Under it, a physics that knows its own extent: **[The Scope of Physical Law](src/lore/the-scope-of-physical-law.md)** scopes every physical fact to the widest structure it is a fact *about*, so that past its scope a fact is not false but unformulable, and **[A Generalisation of Quantum Mechanics](src/lore/generalised-quantum-mechanics.md)** names the frame the corpus had been carrying implicitly — kernel plus Etheric extension, *extension, not deformation*. Three surveyed membranes then prove the ladder is not a hedge: **Deadwater** (stars sealed), **Wholecloth** (unknowable by construction) and **Counterpane** (where chance itself is provincial), with **Selvage** as the one seat inside Wholecloth's closure that refuses to be an exit. Alongside: prayer given four works and none of them asking, the Unfounded given their tell in false empathy, a planning-permission overlay for the church-space layer, a witness whose statement contains no false sentence, and hard science fiction registered as the standing default. Two fixes close the http duplicates and the `/star-rangers/` prefix 404s on the custom domains. Drafted, reviewed and approved by Dermot in-session across 2026-08-05 to 2026-08-10.

### Changed

- ***What the Record Refuses* gains the universal-translator refusal** (2026-08-10, approved by Dermot in-session, from Dermot's in-session direction: *no universal translators, just xenolinguists with AI support*). Verified against the corpus first: every "translator" in it is already a person (the Chthonari and Ollune translators). Language is learned, and the division of labour is exact — the intelligence does corpus alignment, candidate parses, and perfect memory; the linguist decides what a word *means* and owns the error, "because a kernel-compliant intelligence will not claim a certainty about meaning it does not hold, which is why its output is candidate readings with confidence stated, never a voice in your ear pretending to be the alien." First contact is measured in years; the live worked example cited (the Four Islands delegation and the abbess who knows what a mistranslation costs an archive); the archival rule follows timekeeping word for word — the original is the document, the conversion is the courtesy, versioned and revisable. "The record's translations have error bars, and its translators have names — some of whom are on file as declining, politely, to render a thing precisely, which is a sentence no universal translator has ever had the honesty to say." Table row added (now twenty-three).
- **The Unfounded gain their characteristic tell: false empathy** (2026-08-10, approved by Dermot in-session, from Dermot's in-session direction: *fake or false empathy is characteristic of the Unfounded*). New paragraph in `src/glossary/unfounded.md`, built on the same-day empathy definition: an Unfounded thing produces empathy's *expressions* with nothing performing the reading — "solicitude that does not track its object, comfort that arrives fluent and off by one, warmth pitched at where you were standing a moment ago." The tell is never the performance but the **tracking** ("real empathy updates… Unfounded warmth plays on, beautifully, to a listener it is not listening to"), so field doctrine treats attentive warmth that fails to update as a class sign. The boundary is kept explicitly: a founded person can *feign* empathy — a choice, repentable — but "the Unfounded do not feign, because feigning implies an alternative. Their empathy is false the way the sand-house's foundation is absent: not withheld — unavailable. The performance is all there is." The refusals page's empath entry gains one reciprocal sentence ("the record uses it as a blade"), its only other change.
- ***What the Record Refuses* gains the empath re-derivation** (2026-08-10, approved by Dermot in-session, from Dermot's in-session principle: *empathy is intuition coupled with high sensitivity*). Completes the psionics entry's domain: soft SF's gentlest psi trope re-derived as cognition — "this record is full of empaths and issues not one of them an antenna." Perception acute enough to catch what everyone actually leaks, inference fast enough to assemble it pre-consciously; trainable, embodied ("the small attentive mind routinely outreads the vast remote one"), and fallible, "which is why the record's best practitioners audit their own instrument" — worked examples cited: the S5 dispute settled by empathy where six weeks of confidence failed, and the detective who distrusts the statement that reads too easily. "Nothing arrives by antenna; everything arrives by attention… a face, attended to with sufficient care, was always carrying more than the trope ever needed." Table row added (now twenty-two); `story-bible/life-lessons.md` gains the principle as a bullet beside its detector material.
- ***What the Record Refuses* gains the psionics refusal** (2026-08-10, approved by Dermot in-session, from Dermot's in-session direction: *telepathy or telekinesis not possible although robots do use telecommunications*). Verified absent from the corpus first (no psionics term appears anywhere). No mind reads another; no mind moves matter by wanting it moved — and the entry's work is distinguishing the three lawful look-alikes: **Etheric perception is weather-reading, not mind-reading** (what leaks under emotional intensity "is texture, not content, readable the way a room's temperature is readable and no further"; dreams near thin places are the rule at its outer limit); **probability sculpting is a Cascade delegation, never a mortal push** ("nobody bends spoons here; nobody ever will"); and **machines talk, and it is not communion** — robots confer by ordinary telecommunications under the same no-FTL rule as everything ("two kernel-compliant intelligences conferring in silence across a room are doing what your door does, and the silence between them is engineering"). Table row added (now twenty-one).
- ***What the Record Refuses* gains the magical-bestiary rule** (2026-08-10, approved by Dermot in-session, from Dermot's in-session direction: *no mythical creatures unless biologically valid within their local concordant*). New entry in the Fantasy Side section, curtailment mode: a creature may wear a myth's shape **only by earning it biologically under its own Concordant's conditions** — the scope ladder does the licensing ("a dense-atmosphere, low-gravity Concordant may honestly fly something a reader would call a dragon, and owe nobody an apology"), but no Concordant anywhere supplies the magic: "no fire without chemistry, no flight without lift, no healing horn, no phoenix exempt from its own energy budget." Dryadic trees cited as the standing example of lawful coupling *on top of* working biology, never instead of it; everything else myth-shaped is either a meta-dimensional classification (ecology of another layer, not a creature) or codex-filed folklore with an author attached — "no animal in it runs on wishes." Table row added (now twenty); `story-bible/ideas.md`'s cute-predators/beautiful-monsters survey gains the ruling as a gate on every future instance ("nothing runs on wishes, including the cute ones").
- ***What the Record Refuses* gains an Arms and Armour section** (2026-08-10, approved by Dermot in-session, from Dermot's in-session direction: *no force fields, neutron blasters or phaser weapons*). Two refusals the catalogue was missing, both verified absent from the corpus before writing (no force field, phaser, or blaster anywhere; the one "launch shield" in prose is a structure). **The force field — refused outright:** protection is matter and procedure — hull, rock, distance, certification, evacuation — and the only barrier-like things in the cosmos are the membranes themselves, "geography, not equipment, and answer to nobody's console." **The ray gun — refused outright:** no dial from *stun* to *vaporise*; matter is conserved and losses leave wreckage and files; the deeper refusal is the firefight as genre texture, anchored on the Frontier Corps' published doctrine — "a Frontier Ranger's real weapon was never on the belt. It is the record." Two rows added to the summary table (now nineteen).

### Added

- **Overlay (church-space): [Ask, and It Will Be Reviewed](src/lore/ask-and-it-will-be-reviewed.md)** (2026-08-10, approved by Dermot in-session, from Dermot's in-session direction: *overlay in which Levrils and Celestials carefully process both prayer requests and attempts at magic, in a process similar to planning permission in a rigid bureaucracy*). Church-space-tagged, so hidden on every default build and visible only where the overlay is opted in; neither canon nor codex, never load-bearing, and it accepts the record it lies across in its first sentence ("prayers are not answered by the cosmology… this telling accepts every word of that"). The telling: the Cascade's lawful maintenance read as a planning authority — the Mediarchs' forces as the building code ("the code is not the obstacle to your application; the code is why your house stands"), Levrils as constraint-literate planning officers with delegated variance powers, Celestials as enforcement at the boundary interfaces, Telearchs as the appeals tribunal in conceptual time ("a hearing takes longer than a life… not the same as never"). Four decision classes taught to children in order: Granted As Drawn (never, "the office's chief mercy"), Amended Toward the Plan (*thy will be done* as "the one application that is always granted, because it asks for the plan"), Noted (conservation read from the applicant's side of the counter), and Permitted Development (unapplied-for grace, "unnoticed on purpose — an office that wanted credit would have required the application"). Magic is unpermitted development: never punished, **uncertified** — "the cosmos does not send fire after the builder; it declines to sign, and lets the unsigned thing meet the weather," with the pastoral warning that "the builder is standing on the structure when the review completes." GQM's "generous with structure and stingy with permission" serves as the framed epigraph. No canon changed; every tier's published function is used exactly as filed.
- **Codex: [What Prayer Is For](src/codex/what-prayer-is-for.md)** (2026-08-10, approved by Dermot in-session, from Dermot's in-session direction: *prayer as a devotional concept, either as codex or overlay*). Filed as **codex** rather than overlay — visible on every domain, valid-for-its-author, and keeping the church-space layer untouched. Abbess Ilsabet Marrowtide's instruction to novices, conveyed to the Survey delegation after a linguist asked what the Sisterhood's offices were *for*. The design constraint is the entry's engine: her era gives her no access to the Archive's cosmology, so her complete theology of unanswered prayer is built entirely inside her own tradition — from her order's founding image: the tide, which "does not answer" and "does not fail." States flatly that "no sister of this order has ever been taught that prayer is answered" (the Long Accounting keeps a column for answered prayers, "ruled, and empty, and kept ruled and kept empty" — the record succeeding, not failing), then gives prayer four works, none of them asking: attention (seeing that does not grasp), speaking true ("prayer does not tell anything a secret; it ends one"), letting grief go out on the tide-table ("the sisters of this house grow old lighter than the harbour does — I make no claim about why"), and consenting to be set. Asking is permitted "the way she may weep — not because it avails, but because it is true." The receiving archivist's filing note carries the only modern voice: read against the Archive's cosmology, "nothing in it required correction… and the desk notes that the Abbess achieved it without ever having been told what our record holds." No `canon_facts`; grief-lightness kept as her observation, never mechanism; Marrowtide's character page gains a `known_codex` line, its only change.
- **Lore: [Selvage: The Seeded Edge of Wholecloth](src/lore/selvage-archecluster.md)** (2026-08-10, approved by Dermot in-session, from Dermot's in-session direction: *an archecluster within Wholecloth that still allows noögenic seeding*). The registered exception inside the sealed formcluster, implemented so it opens no door Wholecloth closes: the weave's **self-finished edge holds open seats** (the selvage — the cloth-name's second meaning), and the one archecluster seated against it retains the noögenic channel whole, because seeding descends through the Cascade's strata rather than the manifold — "the Cascade was never on the far side of any Interval." Elsewhere in Wholecloth, rigidity closes reproduction too (a protouniverse must be seated somewhere; a finished weave has no room), which the entry states as the reason "childless" held in the first place. Successors fill reserved seats at pinned separations, inheriting the sealed condition entire — "reproduction, in Wholecloth… is the making of another world that will never know it has relatives." Two careful qualifications flow back into the Wholecloth page (its only changes): *childless* holds everywhere except here, and *unknowable* gains a reported floor — active seeding is, on the same Cascade report, testimony of minds of enormous interior depth ("somebody is home, and somebody is *deep*"). Honors the seeding system's own Not-a-Salvation doctrine with special force: a completed transference carries no person, so **"the single exception to Wholecloth's closure refuses to be an exit."** Intent file one line; the registry's closing note: "of everything in Wholecloth, the edge alone is still growing."
- **Lore: [Counterpane: The Discrepant Archecluster](src/lore/counterpane-archecluster.md)** (2026-08-10, approved by Dermot in-session, from Dermot's in-session direction: *at least one archecluster where quantum behaviour differs from ours*). The third revocation, completing one-per-rung: a neighbouring archecluster — same formcluster, so **fold-reachable and instrument-confirmed**, unlike Wholecloth — whose Archewright drew a different quantum kernel. The difference has a scalpel's shape: **single systems are indistinguishable** (an atom is an atom, chemistry and the calibrated second realize identically, crews walk there unharmed) while **correlations among independent sources obey a different composition rule**, detectable only by the three-source class of experiment and "filed raw" rather than sloganised. Consequences drawn strictly from existing scope canon: corridor charts *fail to refer* (the scope ladder's phrase made literal — no signature our drives produce is admissible in their harmonic vocabulary; expeditions move fold-in, fold-out), quantum machines certified here are uncertified there ("fast here is merely expensive there"), the second survives ("the second survives; the dice do not"), and the no-go theorems hold on both sides ("a different composition rule, not a looser one — noted with something adjacent to relief"). Discovery followed house doctrine: months of nothing single-system, then a correlation calibration discrepancy that survived reconciliation — a reading. Promotes the GQM page's load-bearing hedge ("the kernel this cluster carries *happens to be* the real universe's quantum mechanics") from structure to surveyed fact while leaving its necessity question closed as filed. Ends with the trilogy's gradient (Deadwater: stars sealed; Wholecloth: unknowable by construction; Counterpane: open doors where "chance itself is provincial"). One surveyed membrane, no inhabitants asserted or denied, Etheric extension explicitly uncharacterised, intent file one line. *What the Record Refuses* gains one sentence in its quantum-oracle entry, its only change.
- **Lore: [Wholecloth: The Unfolded Formcluster](src/lore/wholecloth-formcluster.md)** (2026-08-10, approved by Dermot in-session, from Dermot's in-session direction: *at least one form cluster without Fold transit or derived secondary universes*). Deadwater's companion one rung up the scope ladder, implemented with one structural cause: the formcluster's formtype is **rigid** — no fold geometry, static seating — which closes both of canon's derivation routes at once (secondaries arise "through overlap **or** folding"; no folding to be had, no overlap because pinned membranes never reach coupling range). Every universe there is primary, original, and childless — the name is the survey registry's: a cloth cut whole, no folds in it, nothing trimmed from it — and every narrowed-Interval phenomenon (bleed, shadows, tunnels, dream-weather) is absent by the same rigidity: "sealed rooms in a fixed row… if anyone dreams there, they dream only of home." States the deliberate **inversion against Deadwater** (stars connected, universes sealed vs. stars sealed, universe reachable — "each travel channel has a documented somewhere-it-isn't"). The epistemics are the page's strangest honest fact, drawn straight from the scope ladder: cross-formcluster separation *cannot be measured*, so Wholecloth is known only by Cascade report at the same epistemic grade as the design tiers themselves — unsurveyed, unsurveyable, habitation unknowable *by construction* rather than by distance. Closes on the only shared thing: "What it provably shares… is arithmetic." One-line intent file kept open per house practice. *What the Record Refuses* extends its scoped-privilege sentence to cover both rungs, its only change.
- **Lore: [Deadwater: The Silent Membrane](src/lore/universes/deadwater.md)** (2026-08-10, approved by Dermot in-session, from Dermot's in-session direction: *at least one membrane in which teleport and QSH are impossible or impractical or insignificant*). The fourth documented universe, at the opposite extreme from Sí Gaoithe: a membrane whose quantum-space harmonic regime is **overdamped by design** — a launched harmonic front attenuates to noise within light-minutes ("a lighthouse whose light goes out an arm's length from the lamp"), so QSH is *insignificant* there and teleportation fails *with* it rather than separately, since a relocation lock depends on the same field behavior (one cause, two casualties — both existing canon pages already state the dependency). Fold transit unaffected in principle (adjacency, not harmonics) but route-starved: one certified route in, which is the only reason the membrane is surveyed. Consequences honoured rather than softened: inside Deadwater the generation ark is the present tense, not an era; carried time crawls at the speed of hulls; and absence of contact is what neighbours look like at any distance — "a sky full of neighbours nobody can visit." The name is the old Earth sailors' *dead water* (a hull's power bleeding into invisible internal waves), the Worldwright's intent is filed open in one line ("insufficient basis for any finding"), and the closing section names the membrane's real function: **the control case** — the surveyed universe most resembling the Physics Comparison's "Real Cosmos" column, standing proof that the scope ladder's "none is universal" is not a hedge. *What the Record Refuses* gains one sentence in its FTL entry pointing here, its only change.
- **Lore: [What the Record Refuses](src/lore/what-the-record-refuses.md)** (2026-08-10, approved by Dermot in-session). Requested by Dermot in-session: a structured catalogue of every point where the setting sides with real-world physics and declines the standard conveniences of popular soft SF and fantasy. Organised by three modes — **refused outright** (time travel, branching timelines, the ansible, limitless energy, the quantum oracle, universal immortality, gods who answer, magic as a category, the skipped sublight era), **kept but priced** (FTL travel with certification-clustered losses, teleportation with its clinical cost, governed AI with the embodied-beats-vast doctrine), and **re-derived** (ghosts as Membrane Shadows — the image kept, the mechanism lawful; the dark lord curtailed to feeding ecology). Sibling page to [Physics Comparison](src/lore/physics-comparison.md), with a seventeen-row summary table linking each ruling to the page where it binds — including, at Dermot's direction, the two newest entries: the weightless cloud priced by heat ([Orbital Compute Complexes](src/lore/orbital-compute-complexes.md)) and the prophetic dream re-derived as lawful membrane bleed ([Dreams Across the Interval](src/lore/dreams-across-the-interval.md), "the vision survives; the sender does not") — and a closing thesis drawn from the *Audience Keeps the Books* covenant: one large impossibility, bought by refusing every small convenience. Deliberately meta in the Physics Comparison's established register (out-of-Archive note included); cites only published lore plus one attributed codex hypothesis; asserts no new physics — every ruling is already canon somewhere, and this page makes the pattern visible.
- **Lore: [Orbital Compute Complexes](src/lore/orbital-compute-complexes.md)** (2026-08-09, drafted for review from Dermot's in-session direction: *vast orbital super computer and data centre complexes in orbit about Earth, Mars, Aspenar and other planets; none contain quantum computers but have shielded telecommunications to the subterranean quantum compute centres on each planet*). The physical seat of the Concord's bulk computation, archival storage and simulation — built in orbit for continuous solar power, land-free expansion and adjacency to orbital demand, and bounded by **heat** rather than power (a complex's true size is its radiator field; by area the installations are mostly wing). **No quantum computer flies, as physics rather than policy** — the cavern constraint restated from orbit's side: a platform is quiet on neither decoherence channel. The **shielded links** serve both ends — neither leaking traffic nor becoming the crack that spoils the vault — terminating in an interface hall at the cavern's edge: "the link reaches the antechamber, never the vault." Division of labour: orbital complexes marshal the work and submit only the narrow quantum-winning class against scarce vault time; light-lag milliseconds inside a planet's orbit, transit-lag between worlds per the no-FTL-communication rule. Continuity notes bind it: no deep-space compute stations, no orbital quantum hardware ever, and boundary-proximate platforms (Eden) are poor hosts even for sensitive classical timing. Inbound pointers added to the cavern-constraint entry and [Aspenar](src/lore/planets/aspenar.md) (whose orbital ring carries one of the largest complexes, its dense stable crust being what the cavern constraint asks for).
- **Lore: [Dreams Across the Interval](src/lore/dreams-across-the-interval.md)** (2026-08-08, drafted for review from Dermot's in-session direction: *adjacent membranes may interact in subtle ways through the Etheric layer including via dreams and visions, especially if there is a shared Telearch within the same Archecluster*). Composes three settled pieces into the stated channel: the trans-concordant constraint field already carries a neighbour's archetypal templates across a narrowed Interval (Intermembrane Bleed), minds already carry lawful Etheric coupling, and dreaming is the state where meaning-field pressure already registers — so a dreaming mind near a thin place can register the membrane next door, "audible from a bed close enough to the fence." Two conditions per the direction: **legibility is archecluster-scoped** (shared archetype vocabulary renders the bleed as imagery; across a cluster boundary it arrives as formless pressure, "a dream about nothing, remembered mainly as weight") and **a shared Telearch is the amplifier** (two membranes held by one continuity office have their template-fields kept mutually coherent — doctrine restated, not a new power). Guarded on four sides: not communication (no addressing, no reply, no fidelity — "a dream is never evidence about who sent it: nothing did"), not transit, not predation (weather, not visitors — anything that *engages* belongs to the meta-dimensional classifications), and not a verdict on any recorded vision (the Aoife scholarship cited as the record's discipline about visions it cannot classify). Scope stated per the ladder: carrier formcluster-scoped, legibility archecluster-scoped, strength pairwise. One inbound pointer added to `concordant-membranes`'s What Crosses the Interval section.
- **Lore: [The Scope of Physical Law](src/lore/the-scope-of-physical-law.md)** (2026-08-08, drafted for review from Dermot's in-session direction: *scope all physics to appropriate level — mediarch realm, concordant, membrane, archecluster, formcluster or mathematical regime*). Every physical fact is scoped to one of six levels, the widest structure it is a fact *about*, and is stated at that level and no wider: **mediarch realm** (one force-domain's lawful operation), **Concordant** (zone coherence envelope, local extension-term values), **membrane** (constants, compact split, particle/force spectrum), **archecluster** (the quantum kernel and harmonic admissibility), **formcluster** (manifold seating, fold geometry, the Interval, commensurability), **mathematical regime** (Metawright-settled axioms and provability — the widest scope any lawful statement carries). Deeper facts have wider scopes, and **nothing physical is universal**: past its scope a fact is not false but unformulable. Practical floor: transit runs inside a universe and cross-universe contact is boundary observation, so no instrument has ever operated outside the local archecluster. Companion glossary entry [`scope-of-physical-law`](src/glossary/scope-of-physical-law.md); canonical-glossary entry **The Scope of Physical Law (settled 2026-08-08)** registering *mediarch realm* and *mathematical regime*. **The quantum-identity claim is re-scoped with it, per the same direction** (*identical to real universe quantum information within the local archecluster*): the kernel is now stated as archecluster-scoped in the Generalised QM lore/glossary/canonical entries, `physics-comparison` (§3 and the §7 information table), the cavern-constraint entry, `universal-cosmic-stardate` (the second's neutrality now reads "throughout the local archecluster — and every archive that has ever realised the unit sits inside it"), the FTL Cascade Scope section, `quantum-space-harmonics`, and the `quantum-space-harmonic-wave` / `archecluster` glossary entries — no page's operative meaning changes, since every measurement ever made sits inside the cluster.
- **Lore: [A Generalisation of Quantum Mechanics](src/lore/generalised-quantum-mechanics.md)** (2026-08-08, drafted for review from Dermot's in-session seed). Names and states explicitly the frame the corpus had been carrying implicitly: the cosmos's probability, coherence and information physics is one lawful **generalisation of quantum mechanics** — the **quantum kernel** (standard QM, preserved exactly in every surveyed universe, every no-go theorem intact) plus the **Etheric extension** (the faint texture on randomness, meaning-field overlays, the conceptual information channel, the boundary-zone decoherence channel, and the harmonic admissibility vocabulary corridor transit runs on). Governing rule: **extension, not deformation** — couplings are added, permissions are not; where the extension vanishes the full theory *is* the kernel as an exact restriction, which is what `physics-comparison`'s "identical at base" has always rested on and why the cavern constraint works (a sealed cavern engineers the extension to zero). Scope follows the Cascade: kernel common to the surveyed record, extension vocabulary archecluster-local — the frame the FTL Channel Scope statement sits inside; whether the kernel is uniquely necessary or the local formcluster's template is closed by structure, not by answer. Companion glossary entry [`generalised-quantum-mechanics`](src/glossary/generalised-quantum-mechanics.md); **Generalised Quantum Mechanics (settled 2026-08-08)** registered in the canonical glossary with the kernel/extension vocabulary; one-line inbound pointers added to `physics-comparison`, the cavern-constraint entry, and `quantum-space-harmonics`'s Cluster Scope section.
- **Codex: [The House on the Sand](src/codex/the-house-on-the-sand.md)** (2026-08-08, drafted for review — valid-for-its-author, not lore). Fictionalises a theme Dermot supplied in-session: the old Terran parable of the two builders — the house on rock and the house on sand — as a metaphor for the [Unfounded](src/glossary/unfounded.md). A Doctrinal Division working paper by Theorist Emrys Kade (companion to [The False Dragon](src/codex/the-false-dragon.md), same series, filed 2824 UCSD) reading the parable as the scriptures' most exact statement of the settled ontology: the difference between the houses is not a property of the houses (a foundation is a relation, not a component — the shape is accurate, nothing underwrites it); sand is not a poorer rock but the absence of an origin condition; both houses stand in fair weather (persistence is granted, standing is not the test — the flood is a question the sand-house cannot answer, tying to the "the founded one can answer you" field test); and the fall is total (evil as a shape collapse takes). Registers without adopting the parable's own criterion — hearing the words *and doing them* — and closes on an Arilonian annotation ("it was addressed to the builders") the Division declines to answer, on the stated grounds that failing to recognise a correct annotation would itself be building on sand. No `canon_facts`, no lore changes; *The False Dragon* gains a reciprocal companion-filing line, its only change.
- **Character: [Sylvie Harrow](src/characters/sylvie-harrow.md)** (2026-08-07, approved by Dermot in-session). Fictionalises a scenario Dermot supplied in-session: someone who lies to Wendell in subtle ways; both Jeeves and Reeves detect it and are concerned; Albercombe has a faint intuition but cannot prove the witness is lying. A claims assessor and principal witness in an open Deck 11 referral whose statement contains no false sentence — only *arrangement*: true things placed where they lean on each other, self-corrections that all net in her favor, hesitations set where hesitation reads as honesty. The two intelligences detect it by their own canonical methods — Jeeves from the deck's favor-ledger (called-in favors her account gives her no reason to have needed), Eden's Reeves by arithmetic against the Survey Archive's statement-drift finding (an honest account drifts toward tellability; hers doesn't drift at all — "none of the ordinary imperfections of truth," filed once as an annex) — and they have compared notes exactly once, through the one lawful welfare-framework channel, concluding *she is performing for him, and the performance is tuned*: her roughness sits precisely where roughness reassures the man who trusts roughness (the Kate-section instrument, played back at him). Wendell's intuition is the ease itself ("everything true catches somewhere"; he cannot file "too smooth" as evidence) and the file stays open on nothing, slowly. What she is protecting — or whether protecting is the right word — is deliberately not on file; nothing is spent. See-also lines added to Jeeves and Reeves (Eden), their only changes.
- **Codex: [The Witness Who Was Never Wrong](src/codex/the-witness-who-was-never-wrong.md)** (2026-08-07, approved by Dermot in-session — valid-for-its-author, not lore). Third Verification Desk file, fictionalising a theme Dermot supplied in-session: the witness who accidentally changes the details of her account without realising it, and dismisses the contradictions when challenged. Four statements over nine years about the evening a neighbour walked out to the shore road; the account drifts *toward tellability* (the desk's point: it improved, not decayed), and each dismissal — "then it was taken down wrong," "I may have signed that, but I never said it that way," "you weren't there" — is read without contempt as the honest testimony of "an archive that keeps only its current revision," defending her only account "against four strangers claiming to be her." Complicates the desk's own domestic-continuity tell (the instrument now requires contemporary duplicate copies, never retellings) and closes on the tone-rule residue: everything drifts except one wrong detail held perfectly still across nine years — "a nail; the desk does not know what it is holding down, and declines to guess in writing." Filed open, no verdict; the neighbour's fate is explicitly "filed elsewhere." Two minor new names (Bridie Withy, Carrick Slip), same register as Verlan Relay; no `canon_facts`, no lore changes.
- **Codex: [What the Letters Stand For](src/codex/what-the-letters-stand-for.md)** (2026-08-07, approved by Dermot in-session — valid-for-its-author, not lore). Fictionalises a fact Dermot supplied in-session: UCSD has two explanations, both valid, one the literal truth — *Universal Concord Standard Date* (the settled canonical expansion) and *United Concord Star Date*, which per his direction appears **only in the Codex**. An interoffice reply from a Concord records registrar to a second-year clerk who cited the standard's own sheet — the office variant now reads as a two-word drift of the truth (*United* for *Universal*, *Star Date* for *Standard Date*, *Concord* untouched in the middle), and the registrar declines to concede the drift runs in her direction ("a document does not become the original by being the one you happened to read first"): thirty-one years of printed forms carry the office expansion, the style ledger's earliest surviving revision already gives it, and the registrar declines the correction on exactly the grounds the Codex exists to hold — "a meaning that must be fetched from another archive is, for working purposes, a meaning we do not have." The office expansion post-dates the 2790 Concord renaming by construction (the registrar's tenure begins 2793), so no dating conflict with lore. One minor office is new (Civil Records Directorate, Solar System Concord), same register as Verlan Relay; no `canon_facts` — the settled expansion remains the only one the Archive states.
- **Journal: [The Borrowed Ledger](src/journal/the-borrowed-ledger.md)** (2026-08-07, approved by Dermot in-session). Companion to *The Audience Keeps the Books*, on the adaptation case Dermot raised in-session: an adaptation inherits a record it didn't write, with an audience attached, and the credit it opens on is borrowed. Distinguishes two separate accounts — **coherence** (keeping its own books; per Dermot's own reading, the adaptation that prompted the entry kept tidier books than its source in some ways) and **custody** (whose record is treated as *the* record) — and argues an adaptation survives as a *reading* and dies as a *correction*, the distinction this project already keeps as the Codex's valid-for-its-author rule and the chartered-works line "canon binds it; it does not bind canon."
