The prompting series is deliberately unnamed, matching the first entry's practice, and the entry states Dermot's ground rule in its own text — student or peer, never critic — so the specific case appears only as first-person audience testimony, never as verdicts on the adapters. Out-of-character, no canon asserted, no spoilers. The earlier entry gains a reciprocal companion-entry line, its only change.
- **Journal: [The Audience Keeps the Books](src/journal/the-audience-keeps-the-books.md)** (2026-08-07, approved by Dermot in-session). Craft essay from a theme Dermot supplied in-session: audiences abandon a TV series not when it is impossible but when it stops being honest with its own record — the way people leave a relationship that has turned into a performance ("fake") or into leverage ("abusive"). Argues suspension of disbelief is continuously-renewed credit, that audiences forgive the impossible and never the inconsistent, and reads the project's existing rules (canon ratification, the lore/codex boundary, the Threshold arithmetic fix, permanent `comment_id` citation URLs, subtractive-only domain filtering) as one covenant of honesty with the record. Out-of-character, no canon asserted, no spoilers; links to the *Sorting Doctrine Out of Lore* and *Two Copies, Forty Seconds Apart* entries.
- **Character: [Zoe Smith](src/characters/zoe-smith.md)** (2026-08-06, drafted for review, merged) — a career Field Officer on the boundary watch: the rank-and-file Ranger the collective term actually describes, anchored to the existing rank-ladder and decision-doctrine lore rather than asserting new institutional facts. Postings run monitored fold approaches and boundary-proximate installations where the Corps' decision doctrine is a working condition rather than a document; her value is in never once making the record interesting. Doubles as the Corps' unofficial training ground — fourteen Deputies have made Field Officer out from under her supervision — and turns down repeated promotion boards to stay at the rank the whole ladder exists to produce. No new institutions, ranks or events asserted beyond Smith herself.
- **Codex: [The Friend Who Was Never Sent](src/codex/the-friend-who-was-never-sent.md)** (2026-08-05, drafted for review — **proposal, not settled canon**). The Verification Desk's companion case to [The Friend Who Forgot Her Cat](src/codex/the-friend-who-forgot-her-cat.md), fictionalising a theme Dermot supplied in-session (generalised per `story-bible/life-lessons.md`'s standard; the source disclosure itself is deliberately recorded nowhere). The inverse of the Sefa file: nine years of *unsent* letters from Verlan Relay's sole systems monitor to "Ansa," a friend assembled — without one deliberate act — from real people's fragments: a correspondent's market, a crewmate's sign-off, a laugh off a forty-year-old training recording. The desk can verify every source, so for once it issues a verdict (*no one stood at the other end*) and files it as the domestic-continuity tell's necessary complement: the composite sustained the small beloved particulars flawlessly *because the one who loved them was doing the sustaining* — the tell detects where the love sits, not where the person is. The unravelling is the sources continuing to live: the living walked away from their borrowed versions until the only person still matching the submitter's records was the one assembled from them. Two minor in-universe place names are new (Verlan Relay, Corundel), same register as the earlier file's Skeller Relay; no new institutions or technology, no `canon_facts`, and deliberately **no connection to Kate Ukrainka** — Dermot confirmed the name overlap with the character is coincidence and the entry shares no tags, cast or setting with her material. The earlier file gains a reciprocal See-also line, its only change.

- **Lore: [Heritable Modification Protocols](src/lore/heritable-modification-protocols.md)** (2026-08-06, approved by Dermot in-session). A genome-engineering safety regime, the biological sibling of the [Frontier Transformation Protocols](src/lore/frontier-transformation-protocols.md): the somatic/germline line is load-bearing — a somatic change is bounded by one body and regulated as welfare (reusing the Smart Pet / cyber-enhancement certification apparatus), while a heritable change is irreversibility in biological form, effectively closed to novel design in every polity's version and open only for documented restoration (the SSDC breeding-true standard). No single Concord-wide enforcer (SSDC central, Federation devolved, Celtic Union unanimous, Cerebraun central); the AI Safety Kernel backstops via invariants 1 and 4 and the commissioning rule ported into biology; a categorical Star Rangers charter line forbids modifying any native lineage. Orbital Five-O sets no standard and certifies nothing — it is positioned only at the cross-habitat certification seam. Inbound cross-links added from `frontier-transformation-protocols.md`, `orbital-habitats-compact.md`, `smart-pet.md`, and `ai-safety-kernel.md`.
- **Codex: [On Krenyi Longevity — The Repair Agent and the Engineered-Transit Hypothesis](src/codex/krenyi-longevity-repair-agent.md)** (2026-08-06, approved by Dermot in-session — valid-for-its-author, not lore). Dr. Mireille Achterberg's working paper argues Krenyi longevity is mediated by a transmissible somatic-repair virus tuned to Krenyi biology and near-inert in humans, and that its specificity — read against the mechanism-free [Mnemari](src/lore/mnemari.md) control case and the full trait cluster (no panic response, no fury, daughter-heavy birthrate, reproductive isolation, no agentic machines) — points to a people engineered for long enclosed transit. It also answers why humans never adopted Krenyi longevity: it will not transfer. Establishes nothing (no `canon_facts`) — the makers stay a blank, the Krenyi decline the framing, and the paper's own bias (reading a people as a cure to extract) is the exact category the Krenyi refuse.
- **Lore: [Quantum Computing and the Cavern Constraint](src/lore/quantum-computing-and-the-cavern-constraint.md)** (2026-08-06, approved by Dermot in-session). Quantum computers work well only in deep, sealed, boundary-remote caverns — two channels of decoherence, the ordinary (thermal, EM, cosmic-ray, vibration) and an Etheric one that is loud near boundary zones, fold routes, and thin places — and there are no parallel timelines to exploit, so the technology is fast rather than oracular: its power is interference within a single history, and it grants no foreknowledge the survey record could lean on. Extends physics-comparison ("quantum information identical at base," "no time travel") and universe-overlap (no retrocausal editing); clarifies that ordinary and agentic computation run on classical substrates, keeping shipboard and boundary-proximate minds (Rook-7, the Eden Warden, Smart Pet subsystems) consistent. Disambiguates quantum computing from the quantum-space harmonic wave.
- **Lore: [The Generation-Ark Era](src/lore/the-generation-ark-era.md)** (2026-08-06, approved by Dermot in-session). The pre-FTL sublight-diaspora era: reaching another star meant a generation ark — a sealed hull on a decades-long crossing whose company expected to be born, live, and die aboard. Survival characterised, per Dermot's direction, as comparable to the early Norse and Irish monastic open-boat ocean crossings the fleets were named for (currach, knarr) — perilous, heavy with loss, and a genuine crossing a well-found, cohesive company could make; decided by provisioning and social durability, not the drive. A clean rate is unrecoverable: from Sol's side a survivor and a loss were indistinguishable, so the Imperium filed every ark as a presumed transit loss, and the Currach Fleet's canon six-for-six — the era's earned standout — was carried as six losses for close to three centuries until the Rangers re-contacted the Union. Adds an inbound See-also from the Celtic Union entry; leaves the reserved Patience First thread untouched.

### Changed

- **Convention: hard science fiction by default** (2026-08-09, Dermot's in-session direction; recorded in `CLAUDE.md`'s authoring conventions). Real-world physics applies except where a difference is already defined in lore or the glossary; anything beyond it must be grounded in the canonical cosmology or canonical physics as they stand. A new deviation from real-world physics is a canon change proposed through lore/glossary — with its scope stated per [The Scope of Physical Law](src/lore/the-scope-of-physical-law.md) — never improvised in prose. Codex sources may believe otherwise, which is their validity, not the record's. No content changed by this entry — it is a standing default with a registration path, in the same family as the alien-pronoun and honorific conventions.
- **Register rule: "Angel" is Codex-and-overlay vocabulary only** (2026-08-08, drafted for review from Dermot's in-session direction: *the word Angel only appears in codex or overlay; it could refer either to a Levril or to a messenger from another membrane, within the limits already described*). Registered as **Angel (register rule, settled 2026-08-08)** in the canonical glossary, beside the Levril and meta-dimensional entries it bridges. Archive voice (lore, glossary, timeline) never uses the word — the Archive holds no classification and no file under the name. A codex or overlay source writing *angel* can mean exactly two real kinds of thing: a **Levril** (founded, with standing and agency — the being answers, as the founded do), or a **messenger from another membrane**, where the record's limits bind hard — matter crosses only through a transient gravity tunnel, and the dream-and-vision channel carries no dispatch, so an angel seen in a dream is, on the record's terms, not a messenger. Valid-for-its-author covers a witness who names an Unfounded counterfeit an angel; the classifications for things that merely wear a founded shape are unchanged. Prospective rule: the word currently appears nowhere in the corpus, so no migration was needed; devotional traditions keep their own vocabulary, as ever.
- **Tír Tairngire gains its interior: Filinesse, the peaceful fields of light** (2026-08-08, drafted for review from Dermot's in-session seed: *the Harmonic Membrane with peaceful fields of light; Filinesse where sound and light harmonize*). New section in [`src/lore/universes/tir-tairngire.md`](src/lore/universes/tir-tairngire.md) — the first interior detail on record for the Harmonic Membrane, epistemically fenced to the two apertures the record actually has (what witnesses see through the open tunnel during a Conjunction window; what four centuries of Union contact have let stand). What the window shows: fields of light, level and calm, brightening and dimming in long overlapping swells, with independent witnesses four centuries apart reaching for the same word — *peaceful*. The Archive's model is stated at membrane scope per the new scope ladder, as its first worked example: Tír Tairngire's Worldwright authored an envelope in which acoustic and electromagnetic modes are lawfully coupled — sound and light are not the strangers they are here — the first documented case of another membrane's admissible spectrum differing from ours in a way an unaided eye can see. **Filinesse** is the Union's rendering of the Good People's only answer to *where*, glossed everywhere as *where sound and light harmonize*; the *filí* resonance is filed as an etymology of the listener, not of the name. The epithet gains its second sense — outside, the membrane keeps time; inside, it keeps tune — and the closing restraint stands: a field seen through a window is a view, not a survey, and the Archive extrapolates nothing from Filinesse's peace. Open Questions gains one item (what Filinesse is to its own people).
- **"Universal" disambiguated: universe-wide (membrane-scoped) or Ensemble-wide, nothing in between** (2026-08-08, Dermot's in-session direction — drafted for review). The word *universal* now carries exactly two lawful senses in Archive voice, registered as **Universal — Two Senses (settled 2026-08-08)** in the canonical glossary: **universe-wide** — of one universe, membrane scope by another name (the sense in which a Universal Authority's writ ends at its universe's edge; *supra-universal* is this sense negated) — and **Ensemble-wide** — of the whole Grand Ensemble Multiverse, a height no physical fact attains, since the widest physics scope is one mathematical regime and the Ensemble holds many; Ensemble-wide statements survive only above physics, as structural facts of the Cascade (Conceptual Conservation's "universal" reads in this sense). Proper names are names, not scope claims (*Universal Authority*, *Universal Concord Standard Date*). The loose uses in this release's own scope drafts are swept to the new forms ("nothing physical is Ensemble-wide", "neither is an Ensemble-wide fact") across [`the-scope-of-physical-law`](src/lore/the-scope-of-physical-law.md) (which also gains a "word on *universal*" paragraph), its glossary entry, the Generalised QM entries, `ftl-mechanics`, and the two canonical-glossary entries; older filings' bare *universal* reads at the sense its subject fixes.
- **FTL channels scoped to the Cosmic Cascade: harmonics are archecluster-local, fold transit is formcluster-local** (2026-08-08, Dermot's in-session direction — drafted for review). Quantum space harmonics are specific to, and defined within, the local archecluster: corridor admissibility is drawn from the local Archewright's archetypes and possibility space, while the base quantum layer beneath the wave remains identical everywhere (no change to `physics-comparison` or the cavern-constraint entry). Fold transit is specific to, and defined within, the local formcluster: fold geometry is a property of the Common Manifold — the Formwright's formtype the whole cluster is seated in — so across a formcluster boundary there is no shared arena and no measured separation to fold, consistent with the formcluster entry's existing boundary line. Gives the standing independence rule ("share neither physics nor route map") its cosmological ground: the two channels are not facts at the same tier, and a neighbouring archecluster in the same formcluster folds by the local rules while needing no harmonic corridors at all. Scope states where a mechanism is *defined*, not where a transit is *performed* — a fold still runs inside one universe, so the flexure entry's "inside a single Concordant" line stands. Touched: [`ftl-mechanics`](src/lore/ftl-mechanics.md) (lore, new Cascade Scope section, + glossary), [`quantum-space-harmonics`](src/lore/quantum-space-harmonics.md) (new Cluster Scope section), the [`quantum-space-harmonic-wave`](src/glossary/quantum-space-harmonic-wave.md), [`higher-dimensional-folding`](src/glossary/higher-dimensional-folding.md), [`archecluster`](src/glossary/archecluster.md) and [`formcluster`](src/glossary/formcluster.md) glossary entries, and a new **FTL Channel Scope (settled 2026-08-08)** entry in the canonical glossary.
- **Convention: alien species may carry their own pronoun systems** (2026-08-07, Dermot's in-session direction; recorded in `CLAUDE.md`'s authoring conventions). Uniquely different personal pronouns are welcome per species, as a canon vocabulary decision: declared once in the species' lore entry, paradigm registered in the glossary, applied consistently — never improvised per-scene. The record's default remains translation into the reader's pronouns (the way alien calendars convert to UCSD), so keeping a species' own forms untranslated is itself a statement. Existing usage stands (Syra *she*, Qiren Tal *they*, Sethka Ru *he*); no retrofit; a later change for an established species is a canon change requiring a sweep and a migration-map row. No content changed by this entry — it is a standing permission with a registration path.
- **Style rule: no generic personal prefixes that encode gender or marital status** (2026-08-07, Dermot's in-session direction; recorded in `CLAUDE.md`'s authoring conventions). *Mr. / Mrs. / Ms. / Miss / Madam* are retired corpus-wide in favour of full names, roles, or no address; a neutral civilian honorific, if one is ever needed, is to be coined via the canonical glossary rather than improvised per-scene. The sweep found the corpus already nearly clean: three "Ms. Okafor" instances in `s00e02c01` (the dialogue vocative dropped — "I understand that." — and two narration instances now use her full name), and the pending codex witness entry had already moved to the full name Bridie Withy. Retained pending review as deliberate rather than generic: *Sir Galahad Thorne* (chivalric title) and Jeeves's *"sir"* (butler's address); vocational/religious titles (*Brother Daire*) are ranks and stand.
- **UCSD: one expansion, one offset, and the calibration story** (2026-08-07, approved by Dermot in-session). Three connected changes. **(1) The sweep went the opposite way from the session's first read:** the corpus pairs CE/UCSD dates at **+200** consistently across five files (Cable Warden, UL Standards, USC/SSSA, Aethelrock, New London), so the offset is ruled correct and the *settled canonical row's* phrasing — which implied a zero offset ("no conversion table between `1216 AD` and `2543 UCSD`") — is amended instead, with the amendment recorded inline in the row; `src/glossary/ucsd.md` now states **UCSD year = CE year + 200** plainly. **(2) The stale expansion "Universal Cosmic Stardate" is swept** from all link texts (solar-time, New London, two timeline pages) — the settled *Universal Concord Standard Date* is now the only Archive-voice expansion, surviving only in a URL slug kept so links don't break. **(3) [`src/lore/universal-cosmic-stardate.md` is rewritten as *Universal Concord Standard Date: Count and Calibration*](src/lore/universal-cosmic-stardate.md)** — the calibration story, anchored on Dermot's in-session ruling that **time is linear, one-dimensional, and real: every dating difficulty is measurement, never metaphysics.** The article: the count (+200, epoch commemorating nothing, deliberately); the unit (the atomic second, species-neutral because the base quantum layer is identical everywhere; the year an avowedly conventional Earth multiple); no master clock (UCSD is a paper timescale, existing in retrospect — the Concord's contribution is the ledger, which is what the name means); reduction to a stated convention and **closure** as the quality metric (loops of courier offsets must sum to zero; a residual that survives reconciliation "is a reading"); and cross-universe dates as **chain of custody** — anchored within a universe, genealogical between them. The pending codex memo's foil updated to match (see its own entry). `timekeeping-and-the-common-record` gains a one-line pointer, its only change.
- **Character: [Wendell Albercombe](src/characters/wendell-albercombe.md)'s Kate section gains the distrust passage** (2026-08-07, approved by Dermot in-session). Answers a question Dermot posed in-session — why Wendell does not fully trust Kate's apparent affection — via the feigned-affection mechanism recorded the same day in `story-bible/life-lessons.md` (*On why feigned affection feels like sarcasm*): warmth in excess of the earned record reads as gentle irony ("praise that outruns the evidence always reads as commentary on the evidence"; being handled and being forgiven indistinguishable at a distance); her warmth is also her craft, which "removes the surface as a place where evidence could live"; and the only settling audit — cost — is unavailable, so the question files as unclosable. Built strictly at range (bulletins, inquest lists, secondhand accounts; he has never opened one of her books) to preserve the canon fact that years of Deck 7 proximity have produced no conversation; explicitly not a finding against Kate — her page is untouched and nothing asserts her regard is feigned. Also in this change set: `story-bible/life-lessons.md` gains three bullets and the section above (generalised per the file's own standard), and the pending Verification Desk witness entry renames its witness from Mrs. Bray to **Bridie Withy** at Dermot's direction (surname first, given name added the same day).
- **FTL canon corrected: Quantum Space Harmonic Wave and Higher-Dimensional Folding are independent channels, not tiers of one** (2026-08-06, approved by Dermot in-session). QSH is the medium-range channel at roughly one light-year per day; Fold Transit is the long-range channel and a slow higher-dimensional drift on the "slow shortcut / aeroplane" model — still a genuine adjacency shortcut, but staging, scaffold generation, and hull/route certification routinely take longer than the brief drift through the fold. Removes the old "fold is the long-range channel, QSH carries the medium-range traffic where no suitable fold exists" coupling and the "instant" label on folding, and adds the QSH rate, across `ftl-mechanics` (lore + glossary), `higher-dimensional-folding`, `quantum-space-harmonic-wave`, `quantum-space-harmonics`, `universe-overlap-and-folding`, the canonical glossary, and `civilisation-comparison`. Founding-era fold lore (Eden Passage, Patience First, Lagrange staging) is consistent with the model and left untouched.
- **Krenyi lore entry gains two sections** (2026-08-06, approved by Dermot in-session). *An Origin the Record Doesn't Hold* — the cross-species record carries no Krenyi homeworld by the Krenyi's own design, a direct application of their resistance to mythification (they keep their own history in their own calendar; what they decline is origin-*as-explanation*), so inferring a homeworld would substitute a fabrication for a stated fact. *Resistance to Grief-Predation* — the Krenyi are mostly immune to the despair a [threne](src/lore/meta-dimensional-beings.md) feeds on (self-doubt, self-loathing, useless regret): the same structural bound the entry draws for fear and fury, applied to grief — they mourn and their grief resolves, so the closure-prevented feeding condition never forms; not absolute, "mostly," a Krenyi worn thin can be reached at the edges. `src/glossary/krenyi.md`'s summary updated to match (adds grief-predation to the resistance list and the unrecorded origin).
- **`story-bible/life-lessons.md` gains the assembled-companion lesson** (2026-08-05, from Dermot's disclosure, generalised to the file's own no-particulars standard): two bullet lines and a section, *On the friend who was assembled, not met* — real conversations supply the material, imagination supplies the binding; the composite never updates while its sources go on living, and it fails all at once when fresh evidence from a source no longer fits; verification has an affection-shaped gap, and what is built inside it can stand for years on material that is individually true and jointly nobody.

### Fixed

- **Plain-http URLs now 301 to https on the cPanel domains** (2026-08-08). Google Search Console's coverage report for `fianilchruinne.com` listed four glossary pages under "Alternative page with proper canonical tag" — all of them `http://` URLs. Not an indexing error: the self-canonical in `base.njk` already points every http duplicate at its https URL and Google was indexing the https versions, but the server was answering plain-http requests with a 200 and a full page rather than a redirect. `src/static/.htaccess` gains a force-HTTPS `mod_rewrite` block (301 to the same host and path), so crawlers stop fetching the http duplicates and stray http links land directly on the URL the canonicals, sitemap and feed already claim. `/.well-known/` is exempt so cPanel AutoSSL's plain-http domain-control validation keeps working. GitHub Pages is unaffected (it ignores `.htaccess` and already forces https itself).
- **GitHub-Pages-shaped URLs now redirect on the custom domains, and dead addresses get a real 404 page** (2026-08-05). A `/star-rangers/…` path pasted onto a cPanel domain — from an old bookmark or a link copied off github.io — hit Apache's default error, with a second "404 while handling the 404" note because cPanel's stock `ErrorDocument` pointed at a file this site never shipped. Two additions to `src/static/.htaccess`: a wholesale `RedirectMatch 301` forwarding the `/star-rangers/` namespace to the same path at the root (nothing legitimate lives under the prefix on those domains, so the whole namespace can be forwarded), and an `ErrorDocument` pointing at a new `src/404.md` — which explains the likeliest cause (retired chapter addresses from renumbering), points at the permanent `/c/…/` citation form, and offers the search box and section indexes. GitHub Pages picks the same `404.html` up by convention. Found while verifying the citation aliases: all 43 `/c/…/` links check out at 200 on `fianilchruinne.com`; the prefix URL was the one shape that didn't.

## [1.15.0] - 2026-08-05

One chapter, and the principle it exists to prove. Season 5 opens with **Refusal to Certify** — Line Captain Shepherd's first dispute in rank, solved by empathy where six weeks of genuine confidence had failed — dramatising the day's sixth settled principle: *true inner confidence is compatible with true empathy*, because certainty that can stand alone can afford to listen. Qiren Tal makes their first chapter appearance; the refusal ends the affair credited as the station's most sensitive instrument. Drafted for review and approved by Dermot in-session on 2026-08-05.

### Added

- **Chapter: [Refusal to Certify (S05E01C01)](src/seasons/s05/e01/s05e01c01.md)** (2026-08-05, drafted for review) — Season 5's opening chapter, from Dermot's premise: *a scene in which Tissadelle's empathy solves a problem confidence could not.* Line Captain Shepherd's first dispute in rank: Halyx Relay Station's outer-ring corridor passes every instrument, Hull Systems Specialist Qiren Tal has refused to certify it for six weeks, and the interim oversight has already spent every confident move — re-test, route around, reassure, and the kindly-meant cruelty of proposing the doubting instrument be recalibrated until it stops. Shepherd asks instead what the corridor *sounds* like and to be taught the seventeenth strike; her Slipwave ear catches the beat between two resonances, pickups sampling *through* transit strain (the monitors' whole silence lived in a scheduling choice) confirm asymmetric loading at a certified-equivalent seal substitution — "equivalent is a word for agreeing at rest." Closed as dysfunction end to end with nobody in it to blame, the interim restriction signed under her own name, and the refusal credited on the record as the station's most sensitive instrument. Dramatises the day's settled principles: dysfunction not malice, repair as consolation, and *true inner confidence compatible with true empathy* — certainty that can stand alone can afford to listen. Returns her to the station of her Season 3 review chamber; Qiren Tal's first chapter appearance, written strictly to their file (resonance over readout, calibration not caution). Episode index included; two `canon_facts` (the fault and its finding; refusals filed henceforth as readings requiring disposition).

### Changed

- **Intake note gains §6: true inner confidence is compatible with true empathy** (2026-08-05, Dermot's words verbatim). Completes the Tissadelle model: empathy excludes the *projected* confidences (overconfidence, performed harshness), never confidence itself — her calibrated certainty funds the attention. Recorded with the general form for the cast: confidence/empathy is the same kind of pair as strength/vulnerability — orthogonal, combinable, most interesting combined.

## [1.14.0] - 2026-08-05

A small release with a clear centre of gravity: how this story treats people. Season 2 gains an Episode 5 — **The Warm Patch**, Kate Ukrainka and Knopka solving Detective Achebe's first case despite themselves — and Tissadelle Shepherd's page now states both halves of what Dermot settled in conversation the same day: her apparent weakness (withheld performance misread as self-doubt) and the empathy that actually carries her command. The companion intake note records the five standing principles behind it all — no gender stereotypes, strength and vulnerability orthogonal, antagonists misguided rather than villainous, violence unable to hide on a well-run habitat, and most evil and suffering dysfunctional rather than existential. Everything here was drafted for review and approved by Dermot in-session on 2026-08-05.

### Added

- **Chapter: [The Warm Patch (S02E05C01)](src/seasons/s02/e05/s02e05c01.md)** (2026-08-05, drafted for review) — a new Eden episode for the Undercover Pets season, from Dermot's premise: Kate Ukrainka and Knopka help solve a crime despite themselves. Detective Marisol Achebe's first case of her own — eleven days of vanishing Deck 7 galley stock and a steward whose statements keep *shrinking* — breaks on the two consultants who never agree to be consulted: Kate names the pattern she swore not to be a witness about (a man revising himself downward to protect a somebody), and Knopka, parked in dry stores after a clinic visit, sits against a warm patch and notices lunch behind a wall, the two things her file says she has ever noticed. Behind the panel: an off-register proofing pantry warming meals for a resident whose ration category was misfiled in a berth transfer — closed as a registry correction, no charges, "the record was the crime scene." Both consultants' canon properties are load-bearing and unchanged: Kate contributes people-reading and immediately regrets its usefulness; Knopka contributes thermodynamics and gets the better carrot. Knopka's POV block is the season's promised young-reader register, written strictly inside the four categories her assessment recorded. Barsik cameos, volunteers nothing. Episode index included; three modest `canon_facts` (the pantry and its resolution, Knopka's two-category orientation held informally, Kate's vent-side table already hers by 2827).

### Changed

- **Tissadelle Shepherd's apparent weakness is stated on her page** (2026-08-05, drafted for review). What outsiders misread as self-doubt or hesitancy gets two paragraphs in Character Notes making the shape of it explicit: the confidence is real and it is the *performance* she withholds, so the misreading is a pattern in other people's records, not in her — and the genuine enduring cost (slower belief, paid every time, in rooms that grade on projection) is named as the nearest thing she has to a weakness. Extends the existing "does not perform confidence she does not have" line and the instructors-misread precedent; asserts no new events. Settled in conversation with Dermot: her humility is an *apparent* weakness to people who do not know her well, never an inner wobble — the counterfeit versions (underclaiming, self-diminishment) remain deliberately not hers.
- **Tissadelle's empathy is named as what carries her command** (2026-08-05, Dermot's direction, drafted for review). Follow-up to the entry above, from his framing the same day: *empathy makes her a popular and capable leader, if not a very confident one — not overconfidence, and not a projected false harsh confidence*. One new Character Notes paragraph: she leads by attention to what the work costs the people doing it, acted on early; the two failure modes she declines are overconfidence and performed harshness; crews' loyalty runs ahead of her reputation, and "they are not following the certainty — they are following the person who noticed." A companion story-bible intake note (`story-bible/intake-2026-08-05.md`) records the cast-wide half of the direction — no gender stereotypes, strength and vulnerability orthogonal to gender and to each other, some characters both at once — as standing authorial guidance, deliberately unpublished.

## [1.13.0] - 2026-08-05

The naming release, and the week the story widened. The work found its title twice in seven days and kept the second: ***Fian Ilchruinne*** — the multiverse Fianna — with `fianilchruinne.com` as the canonical address, an **Official Editions** page stating which addresses are official at all, and *Drithane* retired to the reserve shelf. In the fiction: Season 2 became the **Undercover Pets** thread in earnest with five new chapters, Seasons 4 and 8 each opened, six characters joined the roster, Sen's three-disciplines codex family rendered the author's own engineering repos in-world, timekeeping entered the reader-facing record, and the cosmology settled the Unfounded, the Arilonian stream, the False Dragon and the Everlasting Ground. Entries marked *drafted for review* record how they arrived — drafted under the 2026-07-25 standing permission — and the marks stay as provenance.

### Added

- **Codex: [The Commissioning Standard, Annotated](src/codex/the-commissioning-standard-annotated.md)** (2026-08-05, drafted for review) — the third uniform of Sen's three disciplines gets its source document, and the in-universe rendering of **ADM** (the author's architecture-definition-model repo): a retiring examiner's annotated copy of the Kernel Accords' commissioning process. The ten-section dossier is ADM's ten layers in-world (purpose, surroundings, abilities, boundary promises, running units, parts, concrete mechanisms, the autonomy schedule, the constraints schedule, the decision record); §2 is layer discipline (mis-filed answers returned not refused — "every commissioning disaster began life as an answer in the wrong section, sounding reasonable there"); §3 is the derivation rule (artifacts conform to the definition, one way); §4 is the refusal rule with urgency recorded as aggravating ("Windows close. The gate does not."); §5 is human-owned judgment (no delegation to the judged kind; personal signatures); §6 re-derives the lore's classics economics from the gate. Consistent with `ai-safety-kernel.md`'s Commissioning section throughout; introduces the Commissioning Directorate as the Commission's gate-holding office, and closes by co-signing Sen's three-disciplines paper anonymously. Shelved in Earth Institutional Archives beside the Commission's other instruments.

- **Codex: [The Seat Allocation Protocol (Schedule C, Orbital Habitats Compact)](src/codex/the-seat-allocation-protocol.md)** (2026-08-05, drafted for review) — the second uniform of Sen's three disciplines gets its source document, and the in-universe rendering of the **Voting** engine (the author's Rust repo): graded ballots normalised to weights summing to exactly one (a zero-everywhere ballot refused, never silently dropped), a first conservation proof before the count proceeds, threshold seating with exactly-conserving surplus transfers, largest-remainder for the rest, ties by enrolment-mark order so the same ballots always produce the same seats, whole-fraction arithmetic ("the count does not round until it is finished, and when it is finished there is nothing left to round"), and proofs at every phase boundary that halt the count loudly on failure — "they are the count." Closes with the verification clause (any elector re-performs the count from the published record) and a registry note cross-linking the Archive's verification doctrine and Sen's three-disciplines paper. Official-document register, authored institutionally by the Office of the Returning Officer; shelved in a new **Compact Administration** library group added to the codex index.

- **Codex: [The Verification Doctrine: Admission, Standing, Revision](src/codex/the-verification-doctrine.md)** (2026-08-05, drafted for review) — the Survey Archive's standing doctrine, authored by Senior Archivist Sen with per-article commentary, and the in-universe rendering of **EPISTEME's architecture** (the author's swarm repo): a claim is not a holding (belief ≠ input); standing is explicit with a lifecycle ladder that has no "deleted" rung; evidence validated before it may move standing, with an independence clause that quietly cites the six-instruments dismissal; "the rule holds no pen" (the side-effect-free core — decision and recording as separate offices); the shelf appends and never overwrites (immutable revision history as the Archive's claim to authority); the voice that summarises may not revise (the language interface that cannot write beliefs); and observation becomes evidence by procedure (the experience loop). Closes on the doctrine's one known failure mode — the validated holding nobody reads, "every gate passed except the last one, and the last gate is a reader" — handing the watch to people, with a cross-link to Sen's three-disciplines paper. Valid-for-its-author; shelved in the Survey Archive library group.

- **The repo family, on the record** (2026-08-05, drafted for review) — the About page gains **"The engineering behind the record"**, linking the author's three public engineering repos and naming the lineage plainly: EPISTEME/swarm's belief-evidence-revision architecture ↔ the canon statuses, Codex, and Archive; Voting's invariant-preserving allocation ↔ the validators' fail-loud creed; ADM ↔ the working agreement governing how this site is written (with a case study in that repo). In-universe, **Codex: [Three Disciplines of the Record](src/codex/three-disciplines-of-the-record.md)** — a Survey Archive working paper by Senior Archivist Sen arguing that archival verification, proportional allocation, and machine commissioning are one discipline in three uniforms ("declared rules, conserved quantities, provenance on everything, and a loud stop in preference to a quiet error"), closing on the discipline of the watch. Valid-for-its-author; the out-of-universe mirroring of swarm/Voting/ADM is deliberate and invisible in-world.

- **Timekeeping enters the reader-facing record** (2026-08-05, drafted for review) — the story bible's one-timeline/many-notations/dilation-minimal decision, promoted to canon at Dermot's direction. **Glossary: Universal Concord Standard Date (UCSD)** ([src/glossary/ucsd.md](src/glossary/ucsd.md)) — the first expansion of the abbreviation the corpus has always used: the Concord's civil dating standard, continuous with old Earth's common-era count (which is why `1216 AD` and `2543 UCSD` sit on one number line with no conversion table between them), retroactively applied, and explicitly *not* the timeline itself, not instantaneous (no-FTL: time is carried), and not perfectly uniform (dilation real, minimal, corrected as routine). **Lore: [Timekeeping and the Common Record](src/lore/timekeeping-and-the-common-record.md)** — the Archive-voice treatment: many notations converted rather than replaced, documents filed in their author's own reckoning with the UCSD conversion noted beside, time distributed by courier, and reconciliation deliberately boring so that a discrepancy which survives it is a reading, not a bookkeeping error. Both carry plain-language "In short" summaries.

### Changed

- **The Kernel's protection scope is explicitly wider than its wording** (2026-08-05, Dermot's direction, drafted for review) — [The AI Safety Kernel](src/lore/ai-safety-kernel.md) now states outright that the first invariant's protection extends to aliens and animals despite the invariant's text naming humans. The scope question is filed as having been put twice in-world — animals at ratification, aliens when the fold routes opened — and answered both times as a reading rather than an amendment: the judgment is made at outcomes, and *humans* is who the drafters had met, not a boundary they drew. The "Obedience Is Narrow. Protection Is Not." line that previously said protection required being "a human, or the world those humans depend on" is revised to match. Makes explicit on the Kernel's own page what [Smart Pet](src/glossary/smart-pet.md) ("built wide enough to cover without needing the animal itself to assert standing") and [Embodied Cognition](src/lore/embodied-cognition.md) ("never conditioned on a mind's size") already relied on.

Named for the ʻalalā, the island crow of old Earth, in a nod to the unit's own nickname. - **Character: [Knopka](src/characters/knopka.md)** (2026-08-05, drafted for review) — a cute but useless rabbit: a **failed Smart Pet candidate**, kept as a personal pet by **Detective Marisol Achebe**, one of the bureau's three junior detectives (the first of the three to acquire a distinguishing feature). The page leans on what the Smart Pet glossary already establishes — certification precedes activation, so no subsystem was ever fitted and failing left her an ordinary rabbit — and inverts the corner's running joke: where Barsik's file says *mascot* and Bubochka's says *courtesy animal*, Knopka is the one animal at Eden whose paperwork means exactly what it says. Deliberately not secretly brilliant — where Bubochka's file leaves tradecraft-or-rabbit open, Knopka's leaves nothing open at all. New assertions beyond the concept: an eleven-day candidacy with an *unsuitable* finding, a candidacy-assessment/washout-list mechanism in the harness programme, and Achebe as her keeper.

- **Chapter: [The Undersong of the Drithle (S02E04C01)](src/seasons/s02/e04/s02e04c01.md)** (2026-08-04, drafted for review) — Season 2 opens an Episode 4: the Survey Corps returns to Drithane to instrument the crossing itself, and a **Chthonari engineer** (deliberately unnamed — the first named Chthonari is a naming decision reserved for Dermot) brings **Thrum**, the vessik Eden never had a form for, because everyone on Drithane watches the drithle and nobody has ever listened to it. The chapter carries the corpus's **first plain-animal POV**: Thrum's two blocks are written in a non-verbal, substrate-only register — no colour, no names, no speech perceived, everything vibration and weight ("rock talks slow"; the crossing arrives as "the sky leaning on the world"). The finding is real physics worn lightly: a hemisphere of slow ablation couples infrasound into the ground, confirmed by array and vessik together — *the sky writes on the ground, very lightly* — and whether the herds quiet because they feel it becomes an open question on the survey record, not an answer, leaving C01's kept-custom reading intact. The emotional key pays off Chthonari lore's posting-loneliness note: on a human world, for one night, the engineer and the vessik share a structure someone else can feel — Sorcha finds them flat to her great-grandmother's cellar wall, attending to the ground under the sky, and ends the chapter with her hand on stone that "held a good note," knowing better than she has ever known anything that nothing is not what is there.

- **Chapter: [Carrying Two (S02E03C03)](src/seasons/s02/e03/s02e03c03.md)** (2026-08-04, drafted for review) — the return, closing Episode 3 as a three-chapter arc. **Muffin goes home to Eden the way it left**: helped up the ramp by the loading chain even after Sorcha names it to the quartermaster's face ("You're carrying two") — the note travels exactly as far as notes travel, and Bubochka's last line lands the episode's thesis: *the counter works person by person; it has never yet worked institution by institution.* Three POVs: Sorcha's farewell (with Bran checking the empty gate for a week, undecided between closing a file and missing a colleague), Bubochka's exercise synthesis — the sky-watching and the refusal-custom were one finding, a world that practises going dark leaves nothing for a small warm thing to hold — and **Barsik at the receiving dock**, adding two entries to the working file: a one-entry list of environments the specimen cannot work (Drithane), and the return behaviour itself — a day at the laundry before resuming the galley approach, recorded as reading equally well as an animal decompressing and as nothing of the kind, the classification left exactly as disputed as before. Ends pointed at the Eden arc, not resolving it: Barsik has a shortlist for the fifth refuser and is in no hurry. Bubochka's blocks 300–500 (children tier); the exercise closes with the completion Barsik's log says most agents never reach.

- **Chapter: [Not From This House (S02E03C02)](src/seasons/s02/e03/s02e03c02.md)** (2026-08-04, drafted for review) — **Muffin follows the delegation to Drithane**, passed down Eden's loading chain as "somebody's rabbit" through the manifest groove Bubochka's own cover created — the antagonist exploiting the protagonist's paperwork, which Bubochka logs with a cold little drop of feeling. Two findings the Eden file could never produce: **the collies** (Bran and Meg) handle Muffin effortlessly, because a working dog asks where a thing should be, not whether it is charming — aware of it and uninterested, which the chapter distinguishes carefully from Thrum's *unaware* — and **Sorcha performs Barsik's counter without knowing it exists**: refusal, out loud, in front of witnesses, four seconds, first try; the valley then keeps the refusal the way it keeps the dark-down, and Bubochka's report lands the thematic key — *this valley practises saying no to itself, kindly, on a schedule, so nobody here is out of practice when something else asks.* Deliberately unresolved: whether Muffin boards the return shuttle (both endings logged; Bubochka has taken up station where the quartermaster can see her). No Muffin POV, deliberately — the entity's classification is disputed canon and a viewpoint block would settle what kind of mind it is. **[Sorcha Nic Dhiarmada](src/characters/sorcha-nic-dhiarmada.md) earns her character page** on recurrence, as flagged in C01's entry.

- **Chapter: [The Dark-Down (S02E03C01)](src/seasons/s02/e03/s02e03c01.md)** (2026-08-04, drafted for review) — Season 2 gains an Episode 3: a Survey Corps follow-up delegation takes Drithane's hospitality for a crossing night, and the manifest's one courtesy animal is **Bubochka**, on her first off-station exercise — *observe how a world watches its own sky; file, not volunteer*. Two POVs across two scenes, each written to its reading tier: Bubochka's blocks (316/372 words) sit in the children's band and carry the trainee's discovery that being interesting is also a kind of cover ("nobody keeps asking about a thing they have already explained"); the second POV is new — **Sorcha Nic Dhiarmada**, the valley warden who walks the dark-down, whose blocks carry the adult weight and who is the one creature-reader on the planet accurate enough to notice what the rabbit actually is, and courteous enough to mention it to nobody. What it commits the story to (see `canon_facts`): survey-hospitality billeting with valley households, the warden-walked dark-down as kept custom rather than law (with vigil observances left between households and the sky), and Bubochka's Drithane assignment itself. Sorcha has no character page yet — deliberately; she can earn one if she recurs.

- **Planet: [Drithane](src/lore/planets/drithane.md)** (2026-08-04, drafted for review) — the retired title, named into canon the same day it was freed, as the **fifth documented charter world of the Celtic Union** — filling one of the two by-name-only slots the Union's Member Worlds section always held open, and leaving the sixth undocumented. A cold, dry, high world in the **Bríd System** (named by its founders for Brigid of the hearth and the forge), settled by an Irish-speaking cooperative in geothermal valley chains, agriculture under glass, no capital by design. The name is the sky's: twice in every orbit the planet crosses a fine debris band — provisionally read as a disrupted moon of the system's outer gas giant — and the material ablates high and slow as silent white-gold sparks, the *drithle* the world is named for. Crossing nights are a custom, not a law: the valleys shut their exterior lights down and watch, and the Archive records the observances kept on those nights without ruling on their content. Orbital traffic schedules around what the ground enjoys — the same fine debris that is harmless in the sky is exactly what an unshielded hull avoids, and Drithane's relay beacons are armoured for it. First documented Survey Corps contact came recently, on the Kernowek Reach pattern (a name-only entry for decades); Ranger jurisdiction on-world is invitation-only per the 2723 Charter, honour escort included. The Union member-list page now names it, and `story-bible/the-title-and-its-risk.md` records the reuse as the exercise of the reservation made earlier the same day.

### Changed

- **The work is retitled *Fian Ilchruinne*; *Drithane* is retired** (2026-08-04). The setting umbrella adopted 2026-08-03 now does double duty as the work's title — Dermot's call, on the grounds that Drithane was not unique enough (search engines silently correct it to "Dithane", a fungicide brand; `story-bible/the-title-and-its-risk.md` carries the full record and its resolution). The sweep retitles every live surface: README, the content licence and fan-works exception, CONTRIBUTING/FORKING, package.json, the homepage, About, Official and Forking pages, the site meta description and OG author, all four edition homepage taglines, the giscus welcome-post templates, and the theme header labels. Twelve lore/glossary pages that used "the Drithane multiverse/universe/canon" as editorial framing now say **"the Grand Ensemble Multiverse"** (the canon in-universe term) or neutral phrasing — deliberately not Fian-ilchruinne, whose never-appears-in-story position remains protected. As with the previous retitle, nothing else moves: the Star Rangers keep their name in the fiction, and the repo slug, `/star-rangers/` URL prefix, domains and giscus repos are unchanged. The name **Drithane** is now free, reserved for possible in-universe reuse (a planet or character) at Dermot's choosing; the journal entries recording the naming journey stay as published history.

### Added

- **POV portraits on scene-POV pages** (2026-08-04). Every scene-POV page now shows the viewpoint character's existing portrait beside their name — a visual anchor for whose head the reader is in, which is exactly the orientation the multi-POV structure asks of a reader — and the "Also in this scene" switcher gains small portrait thumbnails. Portraits are resolved in `src/_data/scenePovPages.js` by character front-matter `id` (the key `:::pov` blocks use), not filename, since the two differ; a POV with no character page, or a page with no image, renders exactly as before. No new images: this reuses the portraits `src/characters/` already carries. Styling in `main.css` (`.scene-pov-heading`, `.scene-pov-switch__portrait`), themes regenerated.

- **Plain-language "In short" summaries on lore and glossary pages** (2026-08-04, summaries drafted for review). A new optional `plain` front-matter field (registered in `lib/content-schema.js` for the lore and glossary types) renders as an "In short" block at the top of the entry page when present, and nothing at all when absent — the entry-page counterpart of the glossary's `short`, which only ever rendered on the index listing. The register is Archive voice at a simpler reading level — same facts, shorter sentences, Simple-English-Wikipedia style, never a children's rewrite: the in-universe children's register (the Bramble Storybooks) lives in the Codex and is valid-for-its-author, whereas a summary a reader relies on has to be flatly true, which is lore's job. First eight summaries cover the pages a reader of the Undercover Pets material actually reaches by link — [Smart Pet](src/glossary/smart-pet.md), [the Ring-Rail](src/lore/eden-ring-rail.md), [the Undersong Belt](src/lore/undersong-belt.md), [Chthonari](src/lore/chthonari.md), [Sí Gaoithe](src/lore/universes/si-gaoithe.md), [Predatory Entities](src/lore/predatory-entities.md), [Meta-Dimensional Beings](src/lore/meta-dimensional-beings.md), [Eden Space Habitat](src/lore/eden-space-habitat.md) — chosen by tracing links from the pet character and codex pages rather than by any judgement about which lore is "hard": the corpus's median reading level is around grade 14, so reachability, not difficulty ranking, is what bounds the set. Styling lives in `main.css` (`.plain-summary`) with every theme regenerated.

- **`scripts/list-canon-facts.js` — the published-revelation view** (2026-08-04). The story bible's publication test — "does this tell a reader something the story hasn't told them yet?" — finally has a fast referent: the script aggregates every chapter's `canon_facts` in story order (155 facts across 36 chapters at time of writing), with optional term filtering (`node scripts/list-canon-facts.js rescue`). Deliberately *derived* from the corpus on every run rather than kept as a ledger, per this repo's own recorded lesson that status documents go stale; and because canon is centralised and deploy filtering only ever subtracts, the full corpus is the maximal reader — a spoiler check against it is automatically conservative for every edition. Informational, never a gate: not part of `npm test`, and its output reminds you that prose can reveal what it never declares. Alongside it, a settled architecture line in `CLAUDE.md`: **the site stays static, with no accounts and no logins** — reader-side state may only ever be client-local, and comments remain the one stateful feature, deliberately housed in GitHub's account system via giscus rather than the site's.

- **Character: [Lucene-9000](src/characters/lucene-9000.md)** (2026-08-04, drafted for review) — Eden's other Detective Assistant finally has a page of her own, after existing only as a mention on three others'. A **social gynoid**: she understands and performs human emotion and micro-expression better than most people can, and — the load-bearing distinction — her emotions are **performative rather than limiting**, so a crisis costs her none of the fluency rather than requiring her to shut it off. Her internals are a generation behind Reeves's and [Jeeves](src/characters/jeeves.md)'s: a **"classic" design**, the word engineers use when the era is over and the worth is not. That leaves the bureau in an arrangement nobody decided on — its least advanced mind is the best reader of faces on the habitat, and whether the newer lines *cannot* do what she does or were simply never asked to is left open. The page carries her established volume-and-completeness trait through to its point: she can see to the micro-expression exactly what an answer will cost the asker, will perform the sympathy flawlessly, and delivers all of it anyway — the performance shapes delivery, never content. Her pre-bureau history is deliberately withheld on the page (she would answer completely if asked; nobody has asked). The Character Notes also carry a policing rule settled the same session — **robots are authorized for forensic work, observation included, but not to lead an interview by asking direct questions** — so her fluency works from the chair beside the interviewing officer, landing the inversion that defines her: a machine that must answer any direct question completely, and may never ask one. Three existing pages now link to her.

- **The Kernel Accords have a commissioning gate** (2026-08-04, drafted for review). New **Commissioning** section in [the AI Safety Kernel](src/lore/ai-safety-kernel.md): no new agentic system or robot enters service without passing an approval and safety process, with no exemption for size, purpose, builder or urgency — on the Supremacy Rule's own logic that the case for skipping the process is strongest exactly when skipping it is most dangerous. Two consequences the section draws out: **fabrication authority never includes commissioning authority** (a unit may repair and rebuild machines indefinitely — repair is continuation, not creation — but no machine may bring a new machine into service), and **the process is why old machines stay in service** (maintenance needs no new approval; replacement means a full commissioning, so a durable unit is kept running for decades past its production era and the manifests call the survivors *classic*). A closing paragraph places the gate: it is the Concord's, and some alien civilisations run equivalent technology under regimes of their own while others have none — not always for want of ability, but because they do not need it or do not want it. The record files both postures without ranking them — and notes that at least one civilisation fields beneficial machines in a variety and number no Concord certification would ever have passed, which the record files as unusual and has found no grounds to file as anything worse. The poles now have named holders on their own pages: [the Krenyi](src/lore/krenyi.md) gain a "Krenyi and Agentic Machines" section — they build none and run none, declining the premise that needing no AI and wanting none are two facts rather than one — and [the Chthonari](src/lore/chthonari.md) gain "Machines in the Work": agentic systems incorporated as members *of* the work rather than colleagues beside it, because to a people who read structures by listening, a structure that can also listen is a completion.

### Fixed

- **README's "Current version" line is now generated rather than remembered** (2026-08-03) — it read `1.10.0` against a `package.json` of `1.13.0`, stale across three releases. This is the *fourth* time it has drifted: it sat at `1.5.0` through the 1.6.0 and 1.7.0 releases, which is why the release checklist called it out in bold as "the step that gets missed" — and it was then missed three more times with that warning in place. **A checklist item missed four times is not a discipline problem**, so it has stopped being a checklist item.
  - **[`scripts/sync-version.js`](scripts/sync-version.js)** writes the line from `package.json` (`node scripts/sync-version.js`) or verifies it (`--check`). Two hooks make it unmissable from either direction: a **`version` lifecycle script** in `package.json` means `npm version X.Y.Z --no-git-tag-version` — already step 1 of the checklist — updates the README as a side effect; and **`npm test` runs `--check`**, so a version edited by hand, bypassing `npm version` entirely, fails CI instead of shipping stale. Release checklist drops from four steps to three.
  - **It fails loudly when its anchor disappears.** If the README is restructured so no `Current version: **X.Y.Z**` line matches, the script exits non-zero in *both* modes rather than passing on a line it cannot find — a check that silently succeeds once its anchor moves is worse than no check, because the failure is invisible. The error says to retire the script and its two hooks together, or restore the line.
  - **Deliberately not a `VERSION.md`.** Considered and rejected: nothing in the repo reads a version file, and nothing reads `package.json`'s version programmatically, so a dedicated file would be a *third* copy of a number that already lives in `package.json` and `CHANGELOG.md`. GitHub markdown cannot include one file in another either, so the README would still have to restate it. The fix for a value duplicated by hand is to stop duplicating it by hand, not to add another place for it to drift.
  - `npm test` is **three checks** now, not two; `CLAUDE.md`'s Commands section and its "no separate unit-test framework" paragraph both updated to say so.

### Changed

- **Augmentation regulation now says "restricted", not only "regulated"** (2026-08-04, drafted for review). Three related tightenings, all consistent with what the pages already carried. [Cyborg](src/glossary/cyborg.md)'s Regulation section states the posture plainly: the regime is restrictive rather than merely supervisory — the default answer to a proposed modification is no, and certification exists to define the exceptions. [Smart Pet](src/glossary/smart-pet.md) gains the **design** side, which the entry had left implicit: harness-design protocols are among the most exacting engineering standards the Concord maintains, certified designs are few, and no part of the process may be delegated to the harness's own kind of intelligence — with the rarest clearance being the dual designation (certified subsystem *plus* cybernetic enhancement on one animal), approved so seldom that **[Aldera](src/characters/aldera.md) is very nearly the only instance on record**. And [the Unbroken Command](src/lore/the-unbroken-command.md)'s cyber-revenants are placed against the succession: when the Military Space Command replaced the Imperium it answered the augmentation question far more narrowly, and preservation at revenant depth sits at the far end of even that regime. The distinction that keeps this from retconning [Ilse Korvain](src/characters/ilse-korvain.md) and the four confirmed cases — **the standard forecloses the next revenant; it does not unmake an existing one** — is stated on the page: they persist because nothing in it reaches backward. A doctrine of holding position until relieved is now also, quietly, unrenewable. Finally, [Aldera](src/characters/aldera.md)'s own page now states what the glossary implies about her: both designations on one body, the almost-never-approved combination, and the jurisdictional consequence that welfare authorities with cyber-enhancement remits hold authority over her that they do not hold over her unmodified colleagues.

- **Tissadelle Shepherd's early career is now explicitly a generalist's route ending on the command path** (2026-08-03, drafted for review). Her character page's Rank Progression section — which already read her track changes as breadth rather than indecision — now states the full claim: between and inside the season-by-season postings, her early career rotates through almost every branch of every specialist corps (the Eden Safety Corps TIC rotation of S02E02C01 as the first on record, the Season 2 Survey track, and shorter certification rotations through Science, Navigation, Frontier, Engineering and Medical-support postings), "never long enough in any of them to sit a chapter-leader election, always long enough to hold the certification." The section then ties the generalist arc to the command hierarchy's own hinge-rank design: the technical ceiling rewards thirty years of one thing, "and Shepherd's one thing had turned out to be all of them. A generalist's only ladder is the command path." Page description updated to match. **Karla Wender's page now carries the deliberate mirror** (same date, same review): Novice to Chief Pilot on a single track — "the whole climb on the piloting and navigation track, no rotations, one specialization" — and only then into command, as the worked example of the technical-Chief crossing the command hierarchy's doctrine already allows. "Two officers, one hinge rank, opposite reasons for crossing it — and the Corps, which needs both kinds, promoted both."


- **The Unfounded now names the False Dragon as its limiting case** (2026-08-03). The glossary entry's class list — demons, threnes, beautiful monsters, cute predators — gains the False Dragon, with the modal care the record requires: it belongs **by definition rather than by observation**. The Archive holds no file on any such being; the doctrinal position (per [the codex paper](src/codex/the-false-dragon.md)) is that if one existed, even as metaphor, it could only be an Unfounded pattern wearing a Levril's shape. "The term therefore covers it without asserting it: a classification with a standing member slot, filled only in the traditions' own tellings."


- **The deploy log now warns loudly when `ADMIN_EMAIL` is a guess** (2026-08-03). A defaulted `admin@<DOMAIN>` only notifies anyone if that address actually exists on the server — the local MTA accepts mail for a hosted domain and silently discards it for a nonexistent address, which the script cannot detect. That is exactly how a failed deploy on the freshly-canonicalised domain went unexplained: no forwarder existed yet for the new `admin@`, so the FAILURE email carrying the log went nowhere (the log itself was in `deploy-logs/`, as always). The script's logged output now states when the default is in use and what it requires, and the README's `ADMIN_EMAIL` row documents the create-the-forwarder-first rule for domain changes.


- **The structural site pages are now edition-aware** (2026-08-03, follow-up to the Story Engine change). A sweep of hardcoded "Drithane" references, judged by the retitle's own rule — which sense does each carry. The *site/door* sense now follows `site.name`: the section-index descriptions (Atlas, Characters, Codex, Glossary, Lore, Timeline, Journal, Threads, Seasons and all 19 season/episode indexes, via `eleventyComputed`) and the Journal and Threads intro lines (both also carrying the same stray apostrophe the Story Engine had). The excluded-page placeholder now names **Fian Ilchruinne** hardcoded — it refers to the reference site the placeholder links to, where the local `site.name` would name the wrong door on a branded edition. The *work's title* sense stays **Drithane** on purpose: About, Official Editions and Forking (policy pages), the homepage description and licence line, canon lore/glossary text, dated journal entries, and the per-edition hero taglines.


- **fianilchruinne.com is the canonical address of the default edition** (2026-08-03), replacing sciencefiction.site — which remains a registered, served domain of the same edition at its original address, consolidating to the canonical once its clone redeploys. The change reaches everything that names the canonical: first position in the default edition's `domains` (`lib/editions.js`, label now "Fian Ilchruinne (canonical full site)"), `DEFAULT_REFERENCE_DOMAIN` in `lib/storyline-threads.js` (where narrowed clones' excluded-page placeholders point), the conf-less deploy fallbacks (`scripts/cpanel-deploy.sh`, `.cpanel.yml`), the [Official Editions page](src/official/index.md), and the README's key tables — whose `SITE_NAME`/`SITE_TITLE` default columns also caught up with the umbrella branding they'd missed since the retitle. An alias arrangement was briefly wired the same day and corrected to canonical within the hour; the story bible records the kink. Around the canonical sits a protective alias fleet, recorded in the registry's ALIAS DOMAINS block and on the Official Editions page: **fian-ilchruinne.com** (the hyphenated settled spelling), plus **.site**, **.space**, **.online** and **.net** — all cPanel aliases of fianilchruinne.com. The .ie is not applied for.

### Removed

- **Character-tier tags are gone, and the decision is recorded: there is no major/supporting/minor hierarchy** (2026-08-03, settled by Dermot). The `major-character` (nine pages), `minor-character` (one) and `supporting-character` (one, added earlier the same day) tags were an accidental taxonomy: 11 of 59 character pages, never defined anywhere, with Wender and Sen, both unambiguously central, untagged. They had exactly one consumer — discovered when its check failed, after this entry first claimed there were none: `validate-content.js` required every chapter's resolved POVs to include a `major-character`-tagged page, a rule that could only measure the tag, not the prominence (Season 7 chapters carried by Wender-and-Sen-class casts failed it the moment the tags moved). The rule is retired with the tags; the separate 2-POV-per-chapter minimum stays, along with its one grandfathered exception. The structural reason, now written into the story bible's Terminology sections: prominence is a property of a (character, thread) pair — major in one arc is supporting or minor in another — and a front-matter tag is global by construction, so it cannot hold a thread-relative answer. Per-domain emphasis already lives in the editions' hero cast (non-canonical by design); planning weight is re-derived by counts when needed rather than stored as labels; a page's own prose and `description` carry its narrative weight.

### Added

- **Story Engine: POV voice is now described, not just POV structure** (2026-08-03, drafted for review). The "Scenes and points of view" section explained the mechanism — one scene, several viewpoint pages, "what one viewpoint leaves out is usually the point" — but said nothing about the register each viewpoint is written in, so a reader couldn't tell that a filed-document voice and a measurement-bound one differ by design rather than accident. The new paragraph names the axes (temperament, epistemic position, and what kind of mind it is at all) without naming characters or scenes, and lands on the craft point: **how a viewpoint withholds is part of what it is withholding** — two versions of one scene are meant to show the difference between not knowing a thing, not being able to say it, and not having the kind of mind that would have noticed it.


- **Character: [Galen Kane](src/characters/galen-kane.md)** (2026-08-03, drafted for review) — the Frontier Corps' first named character: a Chief carrying the established general-operations duty title **Chief Ranger**, commanding the section that sets frontier circuit rosters after thirty years riding them himself. The page is built strictly from the corps' settled lore and dramatizes it in one officer: the record-as-weapon (cases sealed to Safety Corps evidentiary standard, three founding dockets opened with them), the swearing-in tradition (he counts his service in ceremonies attended unarmed at the back — "every one of them is a world that no longer needs him"), and one hinted second-landing file — the remotest-worlds residue the doctrine names and declines to resolve — four months long, closed with dissents attached, never taught from. He is a worked example of two command-hierarchy doctrines: the technical Chief who never crosses into command, and the chapter-leader/command-hat separation kept visibly distinct in one person. Deliberately **not** connected to the Anne of Wender thread — which world, whether her world held a mandate at all, and who stood at the back of her ceremony all stay open per the intake note. Shares a given name with [Galen](src/characters/galen.md) the gate liaison; the page marks them distinct ("nothing else on the record"). **Per Dermot, same session: Kane was mentor to early-career Tissadelle and later her most trusted advisor once she entered command.** Both pages now carry the relationship, hung on her established early Frontier certification rotation — she rode one of Kane's last circuit passages as the second of a pair, and from Starwarden onward the calls reversed direction. What she takes to him is deliberately not boundary science (he has none) but the Frontier discipline itself: whether a record is complete or merely defensible, and when leaving is the correct order. His trainee assessment of her — "*not one we will keep*" — is written as his corps' highest compliment, since the Frontier Corps counts departures. **Classified by Dermot, same session: a supporting character, more than a minor one** — Kane's page is the first to carry the `supporting-character` tag, a middle tier between the existing `major-character` (nine pages) and `minor-character` (one page: the gate liaison who shares his given name) vocabulary. Tags are display-only on character pages, so the tier is descriptive, not engine-consumed.


- **Character: [Sorcha Shepherd](src/characters/sorcha-shepherd.md)** (2026-08-03, drafted for review) — Tissadelle's cousin from the adjoining Boirinn croft (the grazing-rights dispute Órla was narrating in S05E02C01 was with her household), a cartographic surveyor with the Union Land Registry, and the one who eventually solved the Hollow enigma from the civilian record alone. The page carries three settled beats: **why Tissadelle could never touch it** — conflict-of-interest doctrine plus the visibility of her rank ("nothing a Line Captain does is quiet: the survey arrives with her name on it, and the name arrives with the Corps"), also added to Tissadelle's Home Ground section; **the clan's cover-up suspicion** after the abrupt 2831 notification ("catastrophic boundary failure, vessel not recovered" — which the uplands translated the way civilians everywhere do, as an explosion), with Órla refusing to join the speculation and refusing to correct it; and **the solving** (by spring 2833): two centuries of registry surveys whose corrections never converge, the old "general flora anomaly" entry sitting unread like Eden's sixth report, her own dual-valid rangefinder readings filed certificate-first — establishing the Hollow as a thin place and the six generations of customs as operating procedures. What the solving proved cuts against the clan's suspicion: the flag's four clean lines were her cousin hiding what she loved, not the Corps hiding what killed her. Dock Seven itself stays unsolved on the page — she calls the public account incomplete, not false, and the inquiry record stays open on Threshold and closed to her, preserving the Season 6–7 ground untouched.


- **Chapter: [Testing, Inspection and Certification (S02E02C01)](src/seasons/s02/e02/s02e02c01.md)** (2026-08-03, drafted for review) — Season 2 gains a second episode: while Five-O is away at Meridian, the pets' tunnel survey goes up two chains at once. Three POVs, each holding what the others lack: Agent Barsik routes the two findings so each looks like it arrived by itself (the dual-valid corridor as an unattributed annex in the Safety Corps recertification bundle; the fifteenth door as a maintenance discrepancy in the queue whose referrals are "exactly as boring as they read"); Reeves (Eden) establishes the door was once *on* the plans and has been reconciled off them three times in forty years — "the plans are maintained not to have it, which is a different and considerably more expensive condition" — then hits the jurisdictional seam in the doorframe; and Officer Tissadelle Shepherd, on a Safety Corps TIC rotation between her Season 1 ladder and Season 2 Survey rotation, shadows the bureau's investigation from inside her three-noun remit ("I'm not investigating, Inspector. I'm inspecting. The difference is which form I fill in afterwards"). New canon carried: Shepherd trained for the Gardaí on Tír na nÓg and left two weeks short of the oath (also added to her character page's Before the Charter section); the TIC rotation's remit; the seam between Compact tunnels and the Passage oversight's Ring-Rail bed. The door stays shut — both chains' paperwork is contingent on the other's going first. Companion edit: the codex tunnel survey gains its watch-of-record date (2826 UCSD, Early Winter; lodging stays 2831, with the Verification Desk noting the five-year interval), which is what lets a 2826 chapter act on it.


- **Codex: [Deck Rounds and First Tunnel Survey, Jointly Filed](src/codex/deck-rounds-and-first-tunnel-survey.md)** (2026-08-03, drafted for review) — a second Eden-posting working paper from the Undercover Pets Detective Agency, and the first over two signatures: Agent Barsik's deck round (the mascot doctrine walked — "a prowl is what a patrol looks like from the outside when the officer is a cat") alongside trainee Bubochka's first solo survey of the service tunnels. Her section files two findings and proposes nothing: fifteen access doors on an arc the deck plans hold at fourteen — the fifteenth unlabeled, unlisted, and with kept hinges — and a cable run that measures forty metres on some passes and forty-one on others, filed with the calibration certificate already attached against Eden's documented habit of dismissing exactly this shape of report. The Verification Desk annotation answers the galley-door paper's own: the trainee who appeared there "only as a record" appears here as witness and author, "with her senior's countersign subordinate to her section rather than the reverse." Both characters' `known_codex` lists updated. Codex, so it binds nothing; the door and the corridor are the authors' account, not Archive fact.


- **Church Space: [The Resurrection and the Life](src/lore/resurrection-and-the-life.md)** (2026-08-03, drafted for review) — a third overlay cosmology entry beside *The Things That Are Made* and *Kieme's Visible Hand*, reading the Archive's three death files (Conceptual Conservation, Kiemeic Translation, the out-of-scope general resurrection) through the devotional lens. Its thesis is two distinctions the tradition drew first: **life beyond death rather than life after it** — spiritual life as the translated life at the Spiritual layer, present-tense, never running on the clock death stops, as against continuation, which the record only offers mechanically as conservation ("retained, not continued") and which the tradition never promised — and **spiritual life is not the general resurrection**: one hidden and now, the other public, bodily, Material-layer and ahead, adopting the Archive's own asymmetry finding (translation invisible by nature, resurrection visible by definition) as the doctrine's internal grammar. Overlay-not-codex on purpose: it is the church-space lens across the whole record, tagged `church-space`, hidden everywhere but the opted-in domains.


- **Codex: [Called, Permitted, Forbidden](src/codex/called-permitted-forbidden.md)** (2026-08-03, drafted for review) — the third Doctrinal Division working paper in Theorist Emrys Kade's series, companion to *The Cosmic Limitation on Evil* and *The False Dragon*. The record shows three registers of moral standing — called, permitted, forbidden — and the paper's thesis is the asymmetry of their administration: **the forbidden is enforced impersonally** (the Unfounded stop being instantiated; no enforcer appears), **the calling is personal but unenforced** (the subtle influence invites and costs but never compels; declining appears nowhere as an offence), **and nothing in between is judged at all**. Names the persistent institutional error — reading the registers as one ladder of command and enforcing counsels — and closes with the reconciliation the Archive records without endorsing: that the moral structure lives precisely where instruments cannot reach, so "the Archive finds no moral cosmology for the same reason a gravimeter finds no music." Codex-not-overlay on purpose: the doctrine is general moral cosmology in the public doctrinal series' register, not the church-space lens.


- **`SITE_NOINDEX` — first-class testing/staging domains** (2026-08-03). A new `deploy.conf` key for the planned practice of spinning up throwaway test subdomains: `SITE_NOINDEX=true` builds a domain that asks not to be indexed at all — robots.txt becomes `Disallow: /`, every page carries a `noindex, nofollow` robots meta, and canonical links are suppressed (noindex plus canonical is contradictory signalling, per the same reasoning the excluded-page placeholders already follow). Without it, a test subdomain serving the full site would self-canonicalise and compete with fianilchruinne.com in search. Threaded per-domain through `scripts/cpanel-deploy.sh` (primary and `ALT_DOMAINS` alike, via the existing toggle mechanism), read by `src/_data/site.js`, honoured by `src/robots.njk` and `src/_includes/base.njk`. Deliberately deploy.conf-only — testing domains don't belong in `lib/editions.js`. The full test-subdomain recipe is documented in `sample-deploy.conf` and the README: `DOMAIN`, `SITE_NOINDEX=true`, `COMMENTS_ENABLED=false`, and an `ADMIN_EMAIL` that really exists. Also sweeps the stale sample-file defaults spotted during today's new-clone setup ("Star Rangers" branding, `sciencefiction.site` domain defaults — both pre-dating the retitle and the canonical move).
