- **Journal: [Almost Despaired](src/journal/almost-despaired.md)** (2026-08-03) — the companion piece to *The Name Was Never Mine*: that entry was about losing the book's name, this one is about finding the setting's. The public account of the Fian-ilchruinne naming day — the drift-cluster collisions, the term-level discoveries (*Kieme* is German for gill; an unrelated fan wiki independently coined both a Levril and a Frenar), the turn from coining to compounding Irish, and the "almost" in the title doing the entry's real work. Deliberately silent on the title tier's own open risk file, which stays in the story bible.

### Fixed

- **Excluded-page placeholders no longer pollute site search** (2026-08-03). Every "Not included in this edition" stub sat inside `data-pagefind-body`, so a narrowed edition's Pagefind index carried dozens-to-hundreds of identical placeholder results (matching "archive", and latterly "Fian Ilchruinne"), and even the full site indexed its church-space placeholders. One attribute on `src/_includes/excluded.njk` (`data-pagefind-ignore`) empties them out of the index: the full build drops 444 → 434 indexed pages, a `TOPICS=undercover-pets.com` build drops to 159 — only genuinely included pages. Real excluded titles never leaked (only the generic stub text was indexed), so this is de-noising, not a privacy fix.

### Written earlier in the same release — 2026-08-03

*1.13.0 was written up twice. This section was drafted on 3 August, more work
landed before the tag went on, and `[Unreleased]` was renamed to `[1.13.0]` a
second time on 5 August — so both passes shipped under `v1.13.0` (tagged
2026-08-05 10:49, thirty minutes before v1.14.0). Kept as a nested section
rather than merged, so nothing is lost and the two-pass history stays visible.
The duplicate `##` heading it used to carry was found by
`scripts/check-changelog.js` on 16 August (issue #439).*

A grounding, and a naming. The canon half of this release closes a loop the cosmology had left open since the Cosmic Limitation on Evil was first filed: the Layer 1/2 distinction now *grounds* the predator taxonomy instead of sitting beside it — the Unfounded are patterns nothing underwrites, the False Dragon is the counterfeit of the largest founded thing, and Conseleme's devotional name stopped implying the one thing its definition denies.

The front-of-house half is the naming day. The setting umbrella was hunted, vetted, and adopted in a single sitting — through the Drythane and Driftane collisions, a term-level sweep that exempted *levril* and *Kieme*, an interim *Grand Ensemble Multiverse* tab title that lasted a few hours, and four spellings of one Irish compound — landing on **Fian-ilchruinne**: the multiverse Fianna. The tab now carries the setting, the header keeps the work's title, and each branded edition finally shows its own name over its own door. The full vetting doctrine — three naming tiers, three gates including the new radio test — is recorded in the story bible so none of it is ever re-walked.

### Added

- **Lore: what Layer 2 records, Layer 1 does not found** (2026-08-02, #270). The Conceptual layer conserves structure without auditing it, so patterns of harm persist there like any others — which is why predatory entities sort into *classes* rather than arriving each time as something new. What such a pattern never acquires is Layer 1: the Spiritual layer holds origin conditions, and a parasitic pattern has no origin, only a host. Written as a **category fact rather than a moral one**, which keeps it consistent with the no-moral-cosmology invariant — evil is a shape collapse takes, and a shape needs something to be the shape *of*. Two consequences the record now leans on: it explains why cute predators are patterns rather than persons (catalogued but unaddressable — every attempt to negotiate fails *unanswered*, not refused), and it finally gives [the Cosmic Limitation on Evil](src/codex/cosmic-limitation-on-evil.md) its mechanism: an entity in service of evil never had grounding of its own, so when the borrowed purpose goes it does not die — **it stops being instantiated**, which looks identical from outside.
- **Glossary: [the Unfounded](src/glossary/unfounded.md)** (2026-08-02, #273) — the Survey Archive's collective term for demons, threnes, beautiful monsters and cute predators, **derived from the Layer 1/2 distinction rather than invented beside it**: patterns the Conceptual layer conserves that no origin condition underwrites. A finding, not an insult. What marks them is **counterfeit** — each class wears the shape of something founded without being a member of the kind, which is why animals detect them more reliably than instruments: a creature that declines without needing a reason is reading the membership, not the shape. Deliberately excludes Levrils, dragons included — those are founded, and *the founded one can answer you*.
- **Glossary: [Arilonian](src/glossary/arilonian.md)** (2026-08-02, #273) — the broadest term for the stream of devotional belief descended from the Arilon accounts, named for the figure and **deliberately silent on what the figure was**: Champion, avatar, or the incarnation of Kieme — every reading is an Arilonian reading and the word endorses none. Scales on purpose (Arilonian traditions → a body like the Fellowship of Light → a single chapter), filling the gap between *devotional tradition* (every faith) and named organisations. The first draft carried a `church-space` tag, and the validator's private-thread boundary check correctly rejected a public codex entry linking into it — the term is public vocabulary and the tag was wrong.
- **Codex: [The False Dragon](src/codex/the-false-dragon.md)** (2026-08-02, #273) — per the standing rule that the devil concept lives in **codex or overlay only, never canon or lore**. A Doctrinal Division paper (same author and series as the Cosmic Limitation on Evil) on the adversary of the Arilonian codices: the Archive holds no file on such a being, and the paper exists for the narrower problem the imagery causes — **dragons are real, and founded.** If an adversary existed even as metaphor it would be a **false dragon**: an Unfounded pattern wearing a Levril's shape, a counterfeit of the largest real thing the old scriptures remembered. The traditions holding him real are not refuted and know it — *"You have proven that if he existed he would be a liar. We had noticed."*
- **Site: [Official Editions page](src/official/index.md)** (2026-08-02, #275) — the complete list of official deployments, linked from every page's footer. The one-line contract: **if the address you are reading is not on this list, you are not reading an official copy.** A fork cannot be prevented — the engine is MIT and forking is invited on purpose — so the defence against a contaminated fork is making an unofficial copy distinguishable, not impossible. The forks note restates the welcome for legitimate forks in the same breath, so the page reads as provenance rather than territoriality.

### Changed

- **The default site brand is now *Fian-ilchruinne* in both slots** (2026-08-03, superseding the *Grand Ensemble Multiverse* tab title shipped earlier the same day in #278). The setting umbrella was adopted in its final form — Old Irish *fian* (the warrior-band) + *ilchruinne* (Irish for multiverse), "the multiverse Fianna" — and `src/_data/site.js` now carries it in both defaults: `SITE_TITLE` as the settled hyphenated **"Fian-ilchruinne"** (browser tab), and `SITE_NAME` as **"Fian Ilchruinne"**, the spaced display variant chosen for on-page branding (header logo, footer, homepage heading), replacing "Drithane" there. The work is still titled *Drithane* — that name now reaches the default build through the meta description and OG author rather than the header. Front-of-house only: **"Grand Ensemble Multiverse" remains the canon in-universe name of the multiverse**, which is why the default meta description still says it — the description speaks in-world, the chrome speaks front-of-house. Per-clone/per-edition overrides are untouched.

- **The branded editions now carry their own site title and homepage heading** (2026-08-03). `lib/editions.js` gains `siteName`/`siteTitle` on three editions — **Orbital Five-O** for the StarQuest domains (exact phrase vetted unowned; the Hawaii Five-0 echo is deliberate), **Undercover Pets Detective Agency** for undercover-pets.com, and **Fellowship of Light** for the four fellowshipoflight domains — and the homepage `<h1>` in `src/index.md` changes from a hardcoded "✦ Drithane" to `✦ {{ site.name }}` so the heading follows each domain's own brand. The default edition renders identically ("✦ Drithane"). Edition ids and themes are unchanged (see the migration-safety note in `lib/editions.js`), and `deploy.conf` still wins wherever a live clone sets `SITE_NAME`/`SITE_TITLE`, so nothing changes on a domain until its own config defers to the registry.

- **The default browser-title brand is now *Grand Ensemble Multiverse*** (2026-08-03). The setting umbrella — the canonical name of the whole continuity, per [the lore entry](src/lore/ensemble-multiverse.md) — was adopted as the working umbrella name and now fronts the default edition's tab title: `SITE_TITLE`'s repo default in `src/_data/site.js` changes from "Drithane" to "Grand Ensemble Multiverse", and the default meta description now reads "…an interactive science-fantasy novel *of the Grand Ensemble Multiverse*…". `SITE_NAME` — the header and footer brand — stays **"Drithane"**: the header carries the work's title, the tab carries the setting. Per-clone overrides via `deploy.conf`/`lib/editions.js` are untouched, so branded editions only see the change where they inherit the default. The umbrella is exactly the canon form — no variants — and is interim by decision: it stands until a shorter word or phrase passes vetting.

- ***Grand Demiurge* is retired; Conseleme's devotional name is the Everlasting Ground** (2026-08-02, #274). The stronger argument was internal rather than aesthetic: `conseleme.md`'s own definition says *origin condition, not a character or moral authority*, and a demiurge is precisely a character with intentions — the one label guaranteed to make a reader import agency where three entries deny it, dragging old-Earth speculative baggage ruled out of canon besides. The replacement keeps the pattern (an older devotional name beside the structural one, as Kieme keeps *Holy Triumvirate*) and connects to the week's canon: the Unfounded are what nothing underwrites; Conseleme is what any mathematics and any time must satisfy — **the ground**, named by the traditions centuries before the Archive formalised what it grounds. Recorded in the migration guide with the standard dating rule. *Frenar* was considered alongside and deliberately kept. (#274)
- **The Fan Works exception is now explicitly additive-only** (2026-08-02, #275). `CONTENT-LICENSE.md` covered adding stories alongside canon but never quite said that **altering existing entries and republishing them changed** remains a derivative use the licence does not permit — which is precisely the contamination case the Official Editions page exists for. Now it says it.

### Fixed

- **Journal entries are now filtered per edition, like the Codex** (2026-08-02, #271). `classifyContentPath` already classified journal pages, but `isContentIncluded` had no branch for them, so journal entries fell through to the unconditional `return true` — every branded edition published all of them regardless of its own `TOPICS`/`CHARACTERS`/`THREADS` filters. Journal entries are out-of-character notes about *making* the work, not the work itself, so the branded doors have no reason to carry them. The gap was visible in search: a query for the book's name surfaced the naming journal entry on `fellowshipoflight.org`, a narrower-audience edition, ahead of the unbranded site. Filtered with the same one line used for codex entries. Worth noting for future checks: excluded pages render as the stub rather than disappearing, so the file count is identical either way and a count-based check alone won't catch a gap like this one.

### Security

- **The Safe Browsing flag on `sciencefiction.site` is cleared** (2026-08-02). Google's re-review came back successful — the domain "no longer contains links to harmful sites or downloads" — and the user-facing warnings are being withdrawn. The flag was never about this site's content: it was earned in 2020 by a compromised WordPress installation under a previous occupant and had sat on the domain unseen ever since, which is why Search Console could show no sample URLs. What 1.12.0 changed was the *evidence a crawler had to work from* — hundreds of stale WordPress permalinks answering `200 OK` with this site's homepage, which said the old site was alive and well (#263, now `410 Gone`), and a missing root `/favicon.ico` leaving the previous occupant's WordPress logo attached to the property (#264). Recorded here because the clearance is the outcome of that release and nothing in the repo changed to earn it, so it would otherwise have no entry anywhere. **What it does not settle:** it is Google's judgement on one domain at one moment, not a clean bill of health for any other domain served from this repo, and none of it would have been found without claiming the Search Console property — the [journal entry](src/journal/nothing-was-broken.md) is the account of why.

## [1.12.0] - 2026-08-01

A new species, and a repair job. The two halves have nothing to do with each other, which is itself the character of the release.

The **Ollune** and their world **Cirrane** are the substantial addition: a Federation species evolved in a gas giant's upper atmosphere, whose politics fall out of its physiology like every other entry on the roster.

Everything else is the domain's own history being cleared out. Registering the site with Google Search Console for the first time surfaced a **Safe Browsing flag inherited from a previous occupant** — the domain served generated spam in 2020, years before it was this one, and the flag had been sitting unseen ever since. Pulling that thread found WordPress permalinks still answering 200 in the site's name, and four of six property icons wrong. None of it had ever broken; that is precisely why none of it had ever been found. The journal entry **Nothing Was Broken** is the account of what that was like, and its companion **The Name Was Never Mine** covers the retitle that started the week.

### Added

- **The [Ollune](src/lore/ollune.md) and their world [Cirrane](src/lore/planets/cirrane.md)** (2026-08-01) — a Federation species evolved in a gas giant's upper atmosphere, with a matching [glossary entry](src/glossary/ollune.md). Written to the roster's existing rule that a species' politics falls out of its physiology, and every trait here descends from one constraint: in a hydrogen atmosphere there is no lighter gas to float on, so an Ollune floats on a *warmer* one and pays for its own lift metabolically, hourly, for life. Hence sleep is communal (an unconscious Ollune sinks, and is carried), possession is a permanent metabolic charge rather than an asset, and a people whose word for themselves means *the held* treats trust as a load being borne by named individuals rather than a sentiment. Cirrane has no free oxygen, so **nothing on it has ever burned** — no fire, no smelting, no metal, no launch vehicle, and no route by which the Ollune could have presented themselves to anyone. **The two-channel split is the load-bearing idea.** Pressure sound (**the far word**) is fast, public, unblockable and gone the moment it is uttered; chemical marking (**the near word**) is slow, close-range, attributable to a body and durable. Ollune law gives them opposite jobs — the far word binds nothing, so there are no oaths and no verbal contracts, while the near word binds everything. The consequence is that **raising an alarm is free**: warning and committing are separate organs, not two uses of one, so no Ollune has ever stayed quiet because speaking up would mean owning the problem. Correspondingly a *false near word* is their gravest offence while lying aloud is unremarkable, which is the inverse of the human arrangement and has cost individual Ollune badly in commercial dealings. Two hooks into existing canon, both chosen to avoid ground already held by other species: their zonal bands make **proximity and access different things** — a shoal a thousand kilometres away in the same band is unreachable forever, one three kilometres up is a regular partner — which is the first principle of fold transit, worked out from weather rather than from corridors, leaving the Prismeri their astrogation; and their contribution to the Ranger compact is neither material nor expertise but **procedure**, the discipline of drafting agreements that hold between parties who cannot confer, which is the Federation's own structural problem under no-FTL-communication. The [Safety Corps](src/lore/star-rangers-safety-corps.md) separation of a free, unattributed reported concern from a signed, permanent finding is noted as the same principle the Corps argued its way to over centuries and the Ollune have as anatomy. Cirrane is also the clearest test of the Federation's founding sentence, since it is the one member world whose people could not have proved themselves to anybody, and its delegate is generally not in the room.

  **Volumetric cognition, and why the obvious version of it is the boring one.** The expected reading — surface species think in two dimensions, atmosphere species in three — is stated and then set aside, because what actually distinguishes the Ollune is that they have no privileged *plane* and a ferociously privileged *axis*. A surface species' vertical is the cheap direction with nothing at either end; the Ollune vertical carries every resource, every neighbour, every hazard and **both** available ways to die, while their horizontal is free, infinite and socially empty. Hence no maps — a map projects onto the plane where nothing happens — and a position notation of **depth, bearing and phase** in which the time term is not optional, because on a world where every reference body moves at a different speed a position without a time does not underspecify a location, it fails to denote one. There is no Ollune expression for a place that does not include when you will be at it.

  **Trade runs on carriage, not goods.** A hull crosses in an hour what a shoal waits a generation for, so any visiting trader has a connectivity no native possesses, and the valuable cargo is carriage of the near word — constituting agreements between shoals that could not otherwise exist. That makes the Rangers' charter role as the courier both sides trust the load-bearing member of Cirrane's economy rather than a piece of institutional design. The physics cuts one way only: a near word is attributable to the body that made it, so a carrier cannot forge one, and readable by anyone in proximity, so a carrier can read everything they carry. **Integrity is guaranteed and privacy is impossible** — hence the Ollune have no concept of a confidential agreement and read a non-disclosure clause as a description of an agreement that is not there. And since anything imported must be lifted permanently by whoever accepts it, **the only imports worth having on Cirrane are weightless**: a merchant who understands the place arrives empty and leaves full.

  **Freyari** (2026-08-01) is the Ollune name for the temperate shell — the habitable band itself, not the body it wraps. *Cirrane* remains the Federation survey catalogue name for the whole planet, and the two deliberately do not denote the same object: Cirrane is tens of thousands of kilometres deep, all but a sliver of it irrelevant to everything alive, and Freyari is the sliver. In ordinary usage it doubles as the Ollune word for *everywhere*.

  **Relationship with the [Krenyi](src/lore/krenyi.md)** (2026-08-01). The pairing xenosociology expected to fail — Krenyi do not use social deception, Ollune hold that a falsehood in the far word is unremarkable — and it does not fail, because the Krenyi were already asking for what Ollune anatomy supplies: a species that moves directly to material terms meets one with a dedicated channel for them. The Krenyi are also close to the only species that can accept the far word's standing without hearing a moral defect in it, since *architecture, not virtue* is exactly how the Krenyi describe their own bounded emotional range. **The one serious hazard belongs to the Krenyi**: a far word contradicting a near word is pattern drift by the Krenyi definition, and the Krenyi answer to pattern drift is quiet withdrawal — aimed at someone who has broken no law of their own, who will not be told, and who can only be reached at a passing. The failure mode is not an argument but a Krenyi going silent, correctly by their own lights, over nothing; the fix is the practice they already use against mythification. On fear the two are opposite answers to one question — Krenyi have no deep-fear response to cascade, Ollune have alarms that cost the raiser nothing — and neither quite believes the other's method works. Also pays off a running risk in the entry: the Ollune are tired of being told their body is somebody else's moral achievement, and the Krenyi are constitutionally incapable of telling them so.

- **Journal: [The Name Was Never Mine](src/journal/the-name-was-never-mine.md)** (2026-08-01, #260) — the out-of-character account of the retitle, beside [A Name You Have to Argue With](src/journal/a-name-you-have-to-argue-with.md). Records the reusable part of the method: OR-ing candidate names into one query produces false negatives, because a name with modest presence vanishes behind one with none — which is how two already-taken names were both cleared before individual exact-phrase searches caught them. Also settles publicly what *Drithane* means, and that it means nothing in-story: **a spark and a drift, no character has said the word, and it is not going in the glossary**, because a title that stays outside the story gets to be about all of it. And why the corps kept its name while the book did not.

### Changed

- **The giscus welcome-post drafts carry the new title** (2026-08-01, #259). Three occurrences in `scripts/giscus-welcome-posts.md` still named the work *Star Rangers*, one of them wrapped across a line break — which is why the retitle sweep's grep missed it. Three of the four drafted starter posts have never been posted, so leaving these would have reintroduced the old name into a public forum whenever they went up. The one live post, in **Fan Creations**, was corrected directly on GitHub: Discussions sit outside the repo, so no sweep could reach it, and it had been telling fan authors to tag work `Star Rangers (Dermot R. Cochran)` while the About page said `Drithane (Dermot R. Cochran)`.

- **Legacy WordPress permalinks now return 410 Gone** (2026-08-01, #263). `sciencefiction.site` ran WordPress under a previous occupant, and a static server ignores query strings it does not understand — so every stale permalink (`/?p=417`, `/?cat=3`, `/?m=202001`) was resolving **200 and serving the homepage**. To a crawler the old site was not gone at all: alive, responsive, and inexplicably now a science fiction novel. That soft-404 pattern is the likeliest reason Google still classified the domain as the WordPress site it used to be. **410 rather than 404 is the point** — 404 means "not found, might return" and gets retried for months; 410 means permanently gone. Scoped to the site root and numeric values only, so it cannot match anything this site serves.
- **`/favicon.ico` is served at the site root** (2026-08-01, #264). It returned **404 on every domain**. `base.njk` links the SVG and PNG icons and browsers honour those, but Google's favicon crawler, feed readers and link-preview generators request the conventional root path and were getting nothing — so **four of six** Search Console properties showed a wrong icon, for three different reasons: `sciencefiction.site` kept the previous occupant's **WordPress logo** from cache, `star-rangers.site` and `undercover-pets.com` showed a placeholder having found nothing, and the rest were correct only because Google happened to read the HTML tags. One 404 that had never inconvenienced a human being. The file is a multi-size ICO (16/32/48) embedding the same PNG bytes `src/images/icons` already ships, so root and linked icons are identical. `src/static/` has no directory-wide passthrough, so it needs its own line in `.eleventy.js`.

### Fixed

- **The retitle session date** (2026-08-01, #267). The whole session ran on 1 August and had been recorded throughout as 31 July — twenty-six occurrences across the release heading, its dated entries, the journal entry's front matter, `CLAUDE.md` and `src/_data/site.js`. Verified as a correction rather than a rewrite: every occurrence fell inside this session's own sections, none near 1.10.0 or earlier.
## [1.11.0] - 2026-08-01

The retitle release, and the one that pinned down the top of the Cascade.

The work is now ***Drithane***. A prior-art search turned up three standing claims on *Star Rangers* as a title — Andre Norton's 1953 novel foremost — so the site would have been permanently second in search for its own name. The corps keeps its name inside the fiction and the repo slug, URL prefix, alias domains and comment repos are all deliberately untouched; only front-of-house branding moved.

Behind that, the cosmology's upper tiers stopped being implicit. What Conseleme fixes and what each tier below settles is now stated rather than inferable: where number begins, what a conceptual realm is, what a formcluster and a formtype are, why the Concordant Zones tile a membrane's interior, and why the past cannot be edited and the future is not yet there to visit. Two institutions were added — the **Navigation Corps** and the certification regime it shares with the Safety Corps — and one charter reading that had never been written down, on what an officer owes and is owed on personal leave.

The through-line is smaller than the list suggests. Almost every entry here records what the Archive *cannot* establish alongside what it can: the tiling is the design account and not a survey finding, the Holy Spirit doctrine is confirmed by stance rather than measurement, a formtype is inferred and never observed, and the invariants say what the Cascade admits rather than what anyone in it believes.

### Changed

- **The work is retitled *Drithane*** (2026-08-01, #247). A trademark/prior-art search turned up three collisions on *Star Rangers* as a title — Andre Norton's 1953 novel of the same name (still in print), a 1987–88 comic with an uncomfortably similar premise, and assorted unrelated media reusing the phrase — so the site would have been permanently second in search for its own name. *Drithane* is a coinage from Irish *drithle* (spark, glimmer) with no exact match in any medium. **Front-of-house branding only:** site name/title/description, homepage H1, theme-generator labels, and prose/frontmatter lines naming the work's title all changed. **Deliberately unchanged:** the Star Rangers remain the in-universe corps throughout (~298 occurrences, including the Charter, the Anthem and the founding history), plus the repo slug, the `/star-rangers/` URL prefix, the alias domains, and the giscus comment repos — see `CLAUDE.md`'s opening note on telling the two senses apart.

- **The Cosmic Cascade is scoped to the multiverse, not to one universe** (2026-08-01, #249). `cosmic-cascade.md` places universes as a *rung on* the Cascade (`Worldwrights -> Universes with Concordants -> Telearchs`) and `ensemble-multiverse.md` calls the Grand Ensemble "the infinite collection of universes produced under the Cosmic Cascade" — so Cascade > multiverse > universes, and describing the Cascade's authority as holding "in the Drithane universe" had quietly placed it below its own top tier. Seven lines move to *multiverse* (both Cosmic Cascade pages, `meta-dimensional-beings`, `predatory-entities`, `levril`); three stay *universe* on purpose, because `higher-dimensional-folding`, `quantum-space-harmonic-wave` and `ftl-mechanics` all depend on the local 3+7+1 structure the Grand Ensemble explicitly calls "a local fact rather than a cosmic constant"; two drop the word entirely, since AUC is an economic measure and `lore/index.md` spans both scopes.
- **The Five Layers have a scope split, and it falls where the Upper Structure sits** (2026-08-01, #249). **Layers 1 and 2 are multiverse-wide; Layers 3 to 5 are local to this universe** — Etheric extent runs through this universe's compact dimensions, Physical law under local Concordant boundary conditions, Material local by definition. Which is why Kieme and Conseleme are named for exactly those two layers and no tier is named for the lower three. Gives the Survey Archive's quoting rule three settings rather than two: universal at Layer 1, realm-bounded at Layer 2, universe-bounded at Layer 3 and below.
- **Concordant Zones tile a membrane's interior — an infinite jigsaw** (2026-08-01, #252). The image lands on a distinction `concordant-membranes.md` already drew in its own table: two **membranes** are separated by the [Interval](src/glossary/interval.md); two **zones inside one membrane** meet at an ordinary internal edge with *no Interval at all*. A jigsaw's pieces touch, which makes it exactly right for a membrane's interior and exactly wrong for two membranes, so this is written as the picture the existing distinction was already implying rather than as new machinery. Two consequences, both usually assumed the other way round: **there is no unclaimed interior** — no neutral space between zones, no third condition a region can occupy, nothing a survey could file as belonging to no zone; and **a zone's extent is not a property it owns**, since in a jigsaw no piece's shape is independent of its neighbours, so an internal edge is where two rule sets disagree lawfully rather than a wall either built or could shift alone — which is why an edge yields instrument drift and timebase mismatch rather than law failure. Both sets are holding, and the disagreement is what holding looks like from the seam. **Filed as the design account and confirmed as such**, from the strata that author membranes rather than from anyone who has stood at an edge: `concordant.md` continues to decline the question of how many zones a universe holds, because from inside, a few unbounded zones and endlessly many merely vast ones are indistinguishable. The agnosticism is not weakened anywhere, only attributed — a jigsaw no one has ever seen a single edge of.
- **The Holy Spirit doctrine is belief-conditioned, not simply undetectable** (2026-08-01, #249). The Subtle Influence section had it as flatly undetectable, which is not what the traditions holding it claim and read as the Archive dismissing them. Kieme influences people **and events** directly but subtly, breaching no law of physics and no aspect of the Cascade, invisibly and unverifiably **except to those who choose to believe it** — so confirmation is a matter of *stance rather than measurement*, stated openly rather than caught out. Nothing in the Cascade forbids a claim of that shape; nothing in the Archive's method can engage one; the disagreement is durable because the two positions cannot reach each other. **Contested events accordingly get a three-way reading, not two** — divine influence, a purely physical account with nothing left over, and a dispute of the transmission itself, that third position being the one usually dropped.
- **Kieme's threefoldness is devotional interpretation, not structure** (2026-08-01, #250). The entry asserted that "Kieme is itself understood to be threefold in nature". Kieme stands above the concept of number, so *one*, *three* and *many* are rival pictures rather than rival answers, and **the teaching image is the shamrock** — one leaf, three lobes, nobody being asked which number is correct. What the three aspects *are* is therefore not a hard question but the wrong shape of question, which is a stronger statement than the "cannot settle" the entry made before. The image is kept, on the same terms as the name.
- **Gravity is the safety variable shared by teleportation and harmonic transit** (2026-08-01, #249). `teleportation-limitations.md` already had teleportation depending on "the same lawful field behavior" as QSHW transit, but nothing said why one is routine commercial infrastructure and the other a Medical Corps event. A relocation lock is held against the local harmonic field and a gravity gradient distorts it continuously, so the **existing three-condition set falls out as consequence rather than stipulation**. Written deliberately as an explanation of those three conditions and **not as a fourth**, since `S01E02C05` canonises the rule as having no exception clause. `ascent-javelins.md` already had a surface-to-orbit jump failing all three at once, so the account was latent there and is now explicit: distance is not what makes a jump dangerous, standing on something massive is.
- **Route clearance now names the Navigation Corps** (2026-08-01, #249). `lagrange-fold-points.md` and `universe-overlap-and-folding.md` both vested it in "the Survey Corps navigation authority"; both updated, with the new Corps entry recording that older protocol documents still carry the old name.

### Added

- **Glossary: [Formtype](src/glossary/formtype.md), and the Common Manifold placed at the Formwright tier** (2026-08-01, #256). Settles three structural questions that had been answered only by implication.
  - **A Worldwright makes the vessel and therefore its membrane, but not the manifold the membrane sits in.** A membrane is what a universe occupies *by virtue of being one*, not a skin fitted to a finished vessel — which is also why membrane-hood is **not** a Worldwright privilege, derived universes receiving no Worldwright and occupying membranes regardless. The anchor was already in the entry: the manifold's 20+ band encodes boundary conditions Worldwright and Telearch operations must *satisfy*, and a condition something must satisfy is not a thing it built.
  - **Three tiers make the manifold between them.** [Conseleme](src/glossary/conseleme.md) fixes that **seating obtains** — universes distinct, separated, the separation able to carry geometric strain, causal timing and template propagation — which settles that there must be a manifold and nothing about which. A **Metawright** settles the mathematics one could be expressed in. A **Formwright** instantiates the thing itself as a **formtype**. This extends the ladder the Conceptual layer already follows by one rung: *Conseleme fixes what any mathematics must satisfy and a Metawright settles which there is; Conseleme fixes that seating must obtain and a Formwright settles which manifold there is.* An earlier draft placed the manifold in the Upper Structure and was wrong — a manifold is a mathematical object, mathematics is settled one tier down, so "it is shared, therefore it is above the realms" begs the question.
  - **A formcluster is a common *seating*, not only a common origin** — its members are not merely drawn from one vocabulary, they are laid out in one arena, which is the deeper reason a shared cluster explains why two universes are commensurable at all. It also fixes what a cluster boundary is: two universes in one formcluster have an [Interval](src/glossary/interval.md) between them however vast, and two in different formclusters have **no measured separation at all**, no shared arena existing to measure it across. Descent stays an Archewright fact; **position is a Formwright one**.
  - **`formtype` gets its own entry**, defined against the two things it is constantly confused with. It is **not an archetype** — an archecluster's archetypes are a vocabulary, formtypes are the grammar that permits it — and it is **not a physical law**, which is the Worldwright's work three tiers down. A formtype does not say what happens or even what may happen; it settles what shape a thing that happens is permitted to have. The Archive uses the word sparingly and records why: nothing at Material scale has observed a formtype and nothing will, an instrument being a thing built inside the grammar and unable to be turned on it.
  - **And the entry's own title is parochial twice over.** *Post-11* records where the Corps was standing when it started counting; ***Common*** records how far the Corps can see. Every universe it has reached is seated in this manifold, which is a claim about the Corps' reach rather than about the Grand Ensemble. The word is kept and no longer defended.
- **Lore: [Catastrophic Failure in Fold Transit](src/lore/fold-transit-catastrophic-failure.md)** (2026-08-01, #249) — chosen over a *Wrath of the Dragons* codex entry, and absorbing it. A codex would have documented one disputed event; the lore entry explains the class it belongs to and gives all three readings something concrete to disagree about. **Premise:** folding is geometrically lawful and nothing is lost *inside* a fold, so the failure surface is aperture formation, stability and collapse — an engineering tolerance, therefore certifiable, therefore certifiable badly. Losses concentrate on hulls uncertified or certified against a weaker standard, and **the Safety Corps cannot compel any polity to adopt its own**. Built from existing canon rather than invention: the Safety Corps was already the fold-adjacent certification authority with its Underwriters Laboratories lineage, the Hyperfold Yield Combine was already the lawful-but-appalling teaching case, and the Institute already publishes its own null results — so its unexplained residue is in character rather than a concession. *Dragons are low-ranking Levrils* does the heaviest lifting: agency is available to the devotional reading under the Cascade, so this is two well-founded accounts plus a transmission dispute, not credulity against physics. The founding event is left unspecified on purpose.
- **Lore: [The Star Rangers Navigation Corps](src/lore/star-rangers-navigation-corps.md)** (2026-08-01, #249) — **lineage, not a new invention.** Written as the Survey Corps' own navigation authority separated out, on the same founding principle that produced the Science and Safety Corps ("a body whose conclusions matter cannot answer to the command chain those conclusions might embarrass"), applied one turn further to a body whose conclusions could embarrass *itself*. **The Safety Corps certifies the hull; the Navigation Corps certifies the route.** A fold route is certified *as of a date* and drifts away from the survey that cleared it, so route certificates expire where hull certificates do not — producing the failure class the fold-transit entry could not previously express, a properly certified hull on a **lapsed route**, both certificates genuine and nothing evaded. Mutual recognition with sister organisations takes **centuries**, because a mature standard encodes what its authors never had to write down and neither body will accept an audit it did not perform; three outcomes, none framed as success or failure — merger, alliance, and neutral standoff (commonest, and published as an incomplete audit rather than a breakdown). Recognitions recorded: the Solar System Concord, the Celtic Union of Planets, the Federation of Sentient Beings. **Charter limits held throughout** — no jurisdiction beyond invitation, so outside Concord space the Corps publishes what it surveyed and what it did not, and clears nothing.
- **Lore: [Shore Leave and the Neutrality Constraint](src/lore/shore-leave-and-neutrality.md)** (2026-08-01, #249) — the charter's neutrality clause was drafted against *Solar System* politics because in 2723 that was the politics there was, so **an officer on personal leave in a member confederation beyond the Concord is a gap the drafters never addressed**, covered since by practice rather than text. The hard case is never an officer campaigning, which has an obvious answer; it is an officer helping her family, because training does not switch off at a gate and in a small polity a precise question about why a rule exists is inseparable from who benefits from it existing. **Ranger status works like diplomatic accreditation, and its exact reciprocal is the power to declare an individual holder unwelcome** — nobody can be an accredited neutral and a citizen with an unconditional right of return at once, so the status displaces the citizenship and a home world may expel its own, costing standing in property and inheritance, a voice, and the right to be present at a family matter. That also explains the refusal to contest an expulsion, which would otherwise read as indifference: contesting asserts that Ranger status confers rights *against* a polity, the precise claim the charter disclaims. No rule has ever been written because a rule strict enough would require officers to stop going home.
- **Glossary: [Formcluster](src/glossary/formcluster.md)** (2026-08-01, #249) — the set of archeclusters tracing to one Formwright, built from the lawful templates that Formwright instantiates, following `archecluster.md`'s shape exactly since it is the same authorship fact one tier up. Completes the design-tier ladder: **conceptual realm -> formcluster -> archecluster -> universe.** Named plain `Formcluster` rather than "Formcluster Ensemble" deliberately and confirmed by Dermot — *Ensemble* already names the totality (the Grand Ensemble Multiverse), and reusing it for a proper subset would put the word on two scopes at once.
- **Cosmic Cascade: conceptual realms, and two new Global Invariants** (2026-08-01, #249).
  - **Conceptual realms.** Multiverse-wide is not the same as uniform. The Conceptual layer divides into realms, one per Metawright, each settling its own system of mathematical axioms and foundations within the constraints Conseleme sets but not determined by them — Conseleme fixes what any mathematics must satisfy, a Metawright settles which mathematics there is. Universes beneath different Metawrights differ in **what can be proved**, not only in physical law.
  - **Number begins below the Upper Structure.** Hyperomnium, Kieme and Conseleme are neither singular nor plural, standing above the concept of number altogether, so counting them is a category error rather than an open question; countability starts at the Metawrights, who are individuals. The same fact as conceptual realms rather than a separate one — number is defined *inside* a realm and cannot reach above the tier that settles realms.
  - **No literal theophany.** No stratum above the Levrils appears, speaks or manifests to a time-bound witness as itself. Generalises constraints the glossary already carried per tier, with the two exceptions already canon: **Avatars**, and **Levrils acting as representatives of higher strata**. Neither is an unmediated appearance, which is what makes them exceptions rather than breaches.
  - **A framing note on what the invariants are and are not**, added because the theophany rule was open to being read as the Archive settling the question against the traditions. Each invariant states what the Cascade *admits* and what invariant-only inference can establish, **never what anyone in the setting believes**: devotional traditions hold theophanies real while rejecting magic, others treat magic and the paranormal as unremarkable, and nothing in the list adjudicates them — a document that cannot detect a thing has established the limits of its method, not the limits of the world. Also makes visible that *devotional tradition* is the Archive's own deliberately flattening term for religions, faiths and cults alike.
- **Glossary: the `-eme` etymologies, recorded as a devotional reading** (2026-08-01, #250) — *Kieme* glosses as "ruler of the Spiritual layer" and *Conseleme* as "ruler of the Conceptual layer", on a shared **-eme** ruler-marker that was invisible in the repo. Taken structurally the gloss contradicts both entries' standing line that Upper Structure tiers are non-anthropomorphic, since a ruler decides and an origin condition does not — so it is recorded the way `kieme.md` already handles *Most Holy Triumvirate*: material the Archive registers without adopting. The Kieme note ties it to the election-into-the-Spiritual-layer doctrine already in that entry, both attributing a decision at exactly the layer the name points to. The Conseleme note observes where the marker stops: **Hyperomnium takes no such ending and is named for no layer**, read as significance by devotional tradition and as absence of evidence by the Archive. **Hyperomnium keeps its name** (confirmed by Dermot) rather than becoming "Hyperpaneme" for consistency — that absence is load-bearing, and the Cascade is already etymologically hybrid throughout (`Formwright` Latin + Old English, `Mediarch` Latin + Greek).
- **Cosmic Cascade: two new Global Invariants, and a `### Past, Present, and Future` section** (2026-08-01, #254). **The future is open** in the quantum sense — genuinely branching, none of it yet actual; those possibilities **resolve at the present**; the **past is static**, admitting no revision — what changes about the past is how it is remembered, interpreted and understood, and that happens in the present. **No time travel follows from the asymmetry rather than being stipulated**: there is nothing behind the present to alter and nothing ahead of it yet actual to visit, which is a stronger position than a rule, since a rule invites an exception and this does not. The new section works the implication through: **the asymmetry is fixed by Conseleme; the physics of time is not** — archeclusters vary timelike dimension count and what a clock measures, same tiering shape as the Conceptual layer's mathematics/Metawright split, so there is no cluster to go looking in for an exception; **branching futures are not the Grand Ensemble** — nothing produces a universe by quantum branching, Ensemble universes are Worldwright-authored or derived through overlap and folding; the design strata fix possibility space rather than which branch resolves, so this is **not fatalism**; and the three-years-late cross-boundary correction stays what the three time registers already predicted — two clocks disagreeing about one event's ordering, not causality reversing. The prohibition previously existed only mechanism-by-mechanism (`higher-dimensional-folding` says folding "permits distance traversal, not timeline revision") and was never stated at Cascade level before this.
- **Glossary: [Formtype](src/glossary/formtype.md)** (2026-08-01, #256) — settles which tier makes the [Common Manifold](src/lore/post-eleven-dimensional-manifold.md), a question three existing entries left implicit. **Not a Worldwright**: creating a vessel creates its membrane, but not the manifold that membrane is seated in — the manifold's outermost band encodes boundary conditions Worldwright and Telearch operations must *satisfy*, and a condition something must satisfy is not a thing it built. **Not an archecluster either**: seating and descent are separate axes, so the manifold belongs to no archecluster and traces to no Archewright. **Three tiers resolve it**, one rung added to the ladder the Conceptual layer already follows — Conseleme fixes that seating must obtain and nothing about which; a Metawright settles the mathematics a manifold could be expressed in; a Formwright instantiates the manifold itself, as a **formtype**, a lawful template satisfying Conseleme's condition in that realm's own mathematics. Makes a formcluster a **common seating** as well as a common origin, the deeper reason `formcluster.md` already said a shared cluster "explains why they are commensurable at all," and fixes what a formcluster boundary is — an [Interval](src/glossary/interval.md) inside one, no measured separation at all across two. `archecluster.md`, `formcluster.md` and `worldwright.md` each gain a cross-reference recording the placement, and `post-eleven-dimensional-manifold.md` gains a "Nobody Made It" section carrying the full argument, including the corollary that **nothing can be moved**: seating is not a thing anyone at Worldwright level does, so a boundary event is discovered rather than caused, and the record has never produced a party to hold responsible for one — not a failed investigation, a category that does not apply at this tier.

- **Three Eden characters and a second Kate Ukrainka codex story, all pointed at the Smart Pet material** (drafted 2026-07-30 at Dermot's direction — **proposals, not settled canon**).
  - **[Thrum](src/characters/thrum.md), an alien pet** — a *vessik*, a burrow commensal from the [Undersong Belt](src/lore/undersong-belt.md), left on Eden by a rotating [Chthonari](src/lore/chthonari.md) fold-scaffold engineer. Built from the Chthonari page's own physiology rather than invented alongside it: it reads substrate vibration and has no apparatus at all for a face or a voice. **The point of it is a negative capability** — it is not resistant to social pressure, it is *unaware* of it, and only the second of those cannot be worn down. Carries no cognitive subsystem and no enhancement, so it is not a [Smart Pet](src/glossary/smart-pet.md) and falls outside every welfare framework Eden has — the gap that glossary already flags for Barsik and Bubochka, one step further out.
  - **[Muffin](src/characters/muffin.md), the antagonist** — a **cute predator**, which the corpus already had: [Predatory Entities](src/lore/predatory-entities.md) classifies them as Class III, non-sapient, feeding on micro-consent collapses, and states outright that the detective agency's animals detect them early because their asymmetry detection isn't distorted by politeness. Muffin is an instance of the existing *lamb-mask* type, so **no lore page needed changing to make room for it**. Written to the classification's own terms: it does not plan, does not avoid the Smart Pets, and gets nothing from them — Barsik, Bubochka and Thrum are a control group, not a defence. What it costs a deck is not injury but the habit of refusal, surfacing as monitoring-officer sign-offs that stopped being returned for correction. The cute name is the hazard: no one can file a compliance report containing the word *Muffin*, and everyone who has tried has discovered that privately and put the form down.
  - **[Kate Ukrainka](src/characters/kate-ukrainka.md) now has a character page**, placing her on Eden and giving her the Smart Pet children's books alongside the Earth-diaspora work [already on file](src/codex/the-domovyk-who-stayed.md). Additive, not a retcon: *Tales from the Old Hearth* is untouched.
  - **[The Cat Who Would Not Say](src/codex/the-cat-who-would-not-say.md)** — her second codex entry, and **a deliberate demonstration of what "canon-for-its-author" is for.** The story is emotionally exact and technically wrong: it renders a certified cognitive subsystem as "a small quiet friend who lives behind the eyes," which is precisely what a governed component is not. The annotation records two welfare inspectorates' objection *in full and unanswered*, and records Eden readers' assumption about what the thing by the door really was as an assumption. A children's book that got the regulation right would have had to be filed as something other than one author's account.
  - **Eden's cast joined `undercover-pets.com`.** `undercover-pets.com` narrows by tag, so being written about Eden was not enough to appear there — [Oyelaran](src/characters/rasa-oyelaran.md) was tagged and her own [DI Albercombe](src/characters/wendell-albercombe.md), her bureau's [Reeves](src/characters/reeves-eden.md), [Jeeves](src/characters/jeeves.md), [Commissioner Wayland](src/characters/zara-wayland.md), [Mayor Petrakis](src/characters/imogen-petrakis.md) and the three junior detectives were not, so the domain showed the pets without the institution they work inside. All seven now carry the tag. Filtering still only ever subtracts: nothing about these pages differs between domains, only whether that domain shows them.
  - **Kate and [Albercombe](src/characters/wendell-albercombe.md) have a shared past**, written onto both pages from each side. A few months, some years ago, that did not end so much as thin out — his replies got slower, he decided nothing at any point, and she reached the end of what she was willing to make small. He feels a small, infrequent guilt, specifically at having been a man who reads a silence expertly in a witness statement and let one run for a year in his own messages; he has no wish to reopen it, and neither has she. **Deliberately no unfinished business**, because the interesting residue is professional rather than romantic: it is where her eye for a person quietly asking for less than they need comes from, which is every animal in the Smart Pet books.
  - **Muffin is semi-sapient, at roughly the order of a cat — and no lore page changed to allow it.** `predatory-entities.md` and `meta-dimensional-beings.md` both state flatly that cute predators are Class III, non-sapient, instinctive pattern-matching. Rather than reopen a class definition that carries counter-strategies for the whole class, **what is now in question is Muffin's filing, not the classification**: it was entered as a lamb-mask by a duty officer, from a description, on the strength of the feeding pattern — which does fit — and nine months of observation do not. The corpus already had the precedent and it is cited rather than invented: [Sí Gaoithe's crossers](src/lore/universes/si-gaoithe.md) "resist clean Class II/III sorting altogether," recorded there as a case the system wasn't built to sort rather than a gap in it. Muffin is the second, and the first that could be **calibrated**, because Eden is the first place it turned up four metres from two certified benchmarks for cat-order cognition. **Settled 2026-07-30: the class definition stays as written and is not to be reopened on this evidence.** The specimen-level dispute is the whole of the change — widening it to the class would put semi-sapience behind every cute predator in the corpus and behind the counter-strategy the class is given, which is a much larger claim than one Eden file supports.
    - What semi-sapience buys: it learns a door (three wrong ones first, which instinct does not do), has a favourite it has never once worked, gets bored, and stopped trying Barsik in the second month — not avoidance, which would be strategy, but the way any cat stops at a door that has never opened. It never resolves into anything organised enough for Class II either.
    - **The antagonism gets worse rather than sharper.** A non-sapient hazard is a thing you remove. An animal of about Barsik's order, carrying no subsystem and covered by no welfare instrument, is the same gap that leaves Barsik, Bubochka and Thrum outside their frameworks — arriving a third time from the direction nobody allowed for, the predator. Barsik's counter is unchanged and he now asks for it on the record knowing what he is asking to have done, and to what.
  - **[On the Filing of the Galley Door Specimen](src/codex/filing-of-the-galley-door-specimen.md)** — the contested argument, put in the Codex where contested material goes, authored by **Agent Barsik** (non-human authorship has precedent in `rook-7-first-week-log.md`). Written to fail in the way a codex entry should: Barsik states his own instrument problem at greater length than his finding — a cat is not a disinterested judge of whether a thing is as clever as a cat — and the Archive annotation flags the blind spot he does not state, which is that the paper's entire evidence base is Bubochka's log and never once treats her as a witness rather than a record.
  - **Kate loves cats and has never kept one.** Three, each lost to something ordinary and different — the Deck 4 service voids, a neighbour with better hours, a family who packed it off-habitat in good faith. **Written so the set refuses to become a pattern**: every individual loss has a boring explanation that is almost certainly the true one, nobody has ever laid the three side by side, and the first two predate her moving her mornings to Deck 7 — which forecloses the tidy sinister reading a reader who has just met [Muffin](src/characters/muffin.md) will reach for first. Nothing on Muffin's page mentions the cats and nothing should; the unease has to come from the reader assembling it and being wrong. The current cat is five weeks in and unnamed, and she has noticed herself not naming it. Closes on the one thing she will not argue about: she has never written a cat that is not found by the end of the book.
  - **No portraits or title cards yet.** `image`/`image_alt` are optional on both types and are deliberately left unset rather than pointed at a file that doesn't exist; the codex card wants `scripts/make-codex-cover.ps1`, which is Windows-only.
- **`undercover-pets.com`'s content narrowing is now in the registry** (`lib/editions.js`) as `topics: ["undercover-pets.com"]`. Every other registered domain's identity moved into the registry on 2026-07-30; this one key did not, so the `pets` edition resolved no narrowing at all and a clone trimmed to the two-key minimum `deploy.conf` would have **silently served the full unfiltered site**. Quiet, and in the permissive direction — the worse one to leave to a default. The tag being the domain name is deliberate: `undercover-pets.com` is what a page carries to opt *into* that deploy, so the filter and the tag cannot drift apart the way a curated list would. `deploy.conf` still wins wherever it sets `TOPICS`, so nothing changes for the live clone until that line is removed there. Verified via `scripts/resolve-edition.js`: the domain now resolves `RESOLVED_TOPICS='undercover-pets.com'`, and `sciencefiction.site` still resolves none.

### Added

- **Glossary: [Archecluster](src/glossary/archecluster.md)** — names a grouping the cosmology has been using without a word for it: every universe tracing to one Archewright, sharing that Archewright's archetypes and possibility space. **Deliberately drawn as authorship rather than authority** — it inherits the settled protouniverse position (an adult child, "answerable to it in nothing", kinship permanent and authority temporary) and the `Worldwright` bound (Worldwright authority exists only in primary universes), so cluster membership records provenance and never establishes standing. Two distinctions it exists to prevent: an archecluster is **not** a Worldwright's universe set (RTS-9's three coupled universes are one architecture *inside* a cluster, not the cluster), and it is **not** adjacency (membranes and the Interval are physical separation; a cluster is common origin). A cluster's **reference universe**, where it has one, is the primary universe holding the whole record — a place to look things up, not a seat.
- **`CLAUDE.md` gained an "Authority and review boundary" section** — the internal counterpart to `CONTRIBUTING.md`'s external one. The boundary was already operating (technical fixes merge when green; new lore waits for Dermot) but existed only as practice, inferable from scattered rules rather than stated anywhere. Now three explicit tiers — merge when CI is green, draft-and-stop, never-without-instruction — plus the reasoning that fixes where the line falls: **the gates prove structure, not judgement.** `validate-content.js`, the dry run and the link/related checkers can show a page is well-formed and fully resolved; nothing in the toolchain can show a sentence is true in this world or in the house voice, so mechanical correctness is delegable and assertions about the world are not. Written after weighing a full Architecture Definition Model for the repo and deciding against one — that methodology governs generative-AI *systems* while this site ships static HTML, but its agent-authority question was the part with a real object here: the authoring pipeline, not the artifact.
- **`sample-deploy-minimal.conf`** — a copyable two-key template (`CPANEL_USER`, `DOMAIN`) tracked alongside the full `sample-deploy.conf`, giving the "minimum viable `deploy.conf` is two lines" state a file rather than only a paragraph inside a 300-line one. Its header says what a registered domain now resolves for itself out of `lib/editions.js` and what deliberately stays server-side (`ADMIN_EMAIL`, the raw `GISCUS_*_ID` values, `CUSTOM_CSS_FILE`, `ALT_DOMAINS`), and points at the full template for the rest. No behaviour change: `scripts/cpanel-deploy.sh` reads the same `deploy.conf` whichever template it was copied from. `README.md`'s setup step, `FORKING.md`'s cPanel bullet and `CLAUDE.md`'s deploy-mechanism note name both.
- **`CONTRIBUTING.md`** — the project's contribution and support policy, which until now existed only as an unstated assumption. Third-party pull requests are not accepted (creative control of a single-authored novel, and because a merge is a permanent maintenance commitment rather than a one-off); forks are encouraged, need no permission, and are unsupported; reader questions are welcome in the discussion forum, triaged, with no promise of coverage. GitHub surfaces this file in the "open a pull request" and new-issue flows, which is the point — it reaches someone at the moment they'd otherwise spend an evening on something that was never going to merge. Linked from `README.md` (new "Contributing and support" section) and `FORKING.md`'s opening.
- **The Imperium's High Council and its Convenor** (settled 2026-07-30) — [`the-imperium.md`](src/lore/the-imperium.md), with a term entry in the [canonical glossary](src/lore/glossary/canonical-glossary-and-migration-guide.md). **Additive, not a rename:** `Administrator-Supreme` is untouched and remains the Imperium's actual apex office throughout its span.
  - **The page already gestured at this institution without naming it.** The Decline section described "outer-station representatives who had gained provisional consultative status in the Imperium's final decade" — the High Council is that mechanism, named, and the Convenor chairs it. Late Imperium only; there is no High Council in the founding or middle period.
  - **Advisory, never executive**, which is what keeps it consistent with everything already written. No Council resolution bound an Administrator-Supreme and no Convenor ever issued an order, so [The Unbroken Command](src/lore/the-unbroken-command/) still turns on a stand-down order only an Administrator-Supreme could have given, and the "authority concentrated at the top" characterisation stands. What the Council spread was the *appearance* of responsibility at the point where the reality had become unbearable to hold alone.
  - **Its significance is what it admitted rather than what it achieved:** a government founded on the proposition that consultation caused the Coherence Wars built itself a consulting chamber and seated the settlements it had spent two generations punishing. The Convenor's chair is the first seat in Solar System governance since the Consortium's collapse that a civilian could hold without a service record.
  - **It also explains a continuity that was previously a coincidence.** The MSC's advisory councils are now modelled on the High Council and inherit its flaw — a chamber that may be consulted and an executive that need not listen — which is the same finding the Outer Stations Consolidation Hearing spent three months reaching sixty years later.
- **Recorded plainly that the Imperium had no emperor and never claimed one.** The corpus never said otherwise, but it never said so either, and the name invites the assumption: no coronation, no succession by descent, no throne. The apex was a serving officer's office filled from fleet seniority.

### Added

- **Permanent citation aliases for chapters at `/c/<comment_id>/`** (2026-07-30) — [`src/chapter-aliases.njk`](src/chapter-aliases.njk), one redirect stub per chapter, plus a "Citing this chapter?" line at the foot of every chapter page so the aliases are actually discoverable.
  - **The problem is worse than link rot.** A chapter's URL is not permanent — episodes get renumbered in place to keep story chronology in order, which reassigns a URL like `/seasons/s00/e02/s00e02c01/` to *entirely different content*, and that has already happened once. An external wiki or citation pointing there doesn't 404 afterwards; it silently starts pointing at something else, which is strictly worse because nothing signals the breakage to either side.
  - **Nothing new had to be invented: the repo already solved this once, for giscus.** `comment_id` is required on every chapter, permanent by policy, carried forward with the *content* rather than the slot when a chapter is renumbered, and unique by build-time check (`validate-content.js` fails on collision). That is exactly the property set a citable identifier needs, and all 35 are plain lowercase slugs needing no escaping.
  - **Static stubs rather than server redirects**, because an `.htaccess` rewrite doesn't exist on GitHub Pages and this repo deploys to both. Same head as the two existing rename stubs. `noindex` + `canonical` is correct *here* — for a redirect the two agree, where for an excluded placeholder they conflict (see the canonical entry below).
  - **Built from a new unfiltered `allChapters` collection** so an alias resolves on **every** domain, including one that hides that chapter — where it lands on the `excluded.njk` placeholder that points onward. An alias that vanished on the narrowing clones would break the very links the feature exists to preserve. Filtered by `inputPath`, not `layout`, since `layout` is rewritten to `excluded.njk` for exactly those chapters. Verified: 35 aliases build on a `THREADS=founding-era` clone, and every one resolves to a real built page.
  - Scene-POV pages get no alias, deliberately — derived ids, derivative views, ~92 stubs earning nothing. Excluded from the sitemap, and the scheme is documented in `/llms.txt` so an agent cites the stable form.
- **`<link rel="canonical">` on every indexable page, self-canonical per domain** (2026-07-30). Each domain declares itself the canonical home of its own URLs rather than pointing at `sciencefiction.site`. Built from `page.url` + `site.url`, so it matches `og:url` exactly and picks up `SITE_DOMAIN` per clone with no per-domain configuration.
  - **Self-canonical is right here *because* the domains are meant to diverge.** A cross-domain canonical says "this page is a copy, rank the other one" — consolidating ranking signals into one host, and in exchange asking search engines not to rank the independently-branded domains at all. That trade is worth making for duplicates and is exactly wrong for editions carrying their own framing, cast and copy. The decision followed from the plan to diverge, not the other way round.
  - **Deliberately not emitted on a page this build hides.** `robots` is `noindex, follow` precisely then, and noindex plus canonical is contradictory signalling — one says don't index this, the other says index this URL instead. A placeholder has nothing worth canonicalising; the reader-facing pointer to the domain that *does* have the page is the link in its body. The condition tests for `noindex` in `robots` rather than for `robots` being set at all, so a page that opts into some other directive via front matter still gets its canonical.
  - The two redirect stubs (`glossary/dynarch.njk`, `lore/solar-system-concordant.njk`) are unaffected — they hand-write their own head and keep canonical + noindex, which is the conventional pairing for a *redirect* rather than for a placeholder.
  - **Verified as a partition, not just as a presence check.** Full build: 424 pages, 415 canonical, 11 noindex, the 2 stubs in both, and **zero pages carrying neither**. A `THREADS=church-space` narrowed build: 51 canonical, 373 noindex, again zero gaps. Also confirmed three different `SITE_DOMAIN` values each produce a canonical naming themselves.
- **A minimum viable `deploy.conf` is now two lines: `CPANEL_USER` and `DOMAIN`** (2026-07-30), plus `ALT_DOMAINS` for an account serving several. `lib/editions.js` gained the deploy config itself — `theme`, `threads`, `characters`, `topics`, `siteName`, `siteTitle`, `giscusProfile`, `commentsEnabled` — and `scripts/resolve-edition.js` looks it up **by domain** so `cpanel-deploy.sh` fills in whatever a clone leaves unset.
  - **`deploy.conf` still wins wherever it sets a value; the registry only fills gaps.** That is not just migration cover. `deploy.conf` is untracked and lives on the cPanel account, so live configs cannot be migrated from the repo and a registry that overrode them would silently re-skin a live domain. It is also the honest ordering: **the alt-domain entries in the registry were inferred from `sample-deploy.conf`'s commented examples**, since the real file can't be read from here. The deploy log prints one `[edition]` line per key naming its source — check those on the first deploy and correct `lib/editions.js` against what each domain actually sets.
  - **Resolution happens in the deploy script, not in the Node consumers, and the blast radius is why.** Every downstream reader is already env-var driven — `content-filter.js` reads `CHARACTERS`/`TOPICS`/`THREADS`, `site.js` reads `SITE_NAME`/`SITE_TITLE`, `giscus.js` reads `GISCUS_PROFILE` — so resolving in bash and exporting the same variables leaves all three untouched. Teaching each of them its own edition fallback would have meant editing three modules that currently have one input each.
  - **This does not weaken private-thread opt-in; it strengthens it.** `threads` can name `church-space`, and that is still explicit opt-in by naming — now recorded in a tracked, reviewed, versioned file instead of an untracked one on a server. What remains forbidden is opt-in inferred from the *shape* of a domain string; a registry entry is a decision, pattern-matching a hostname is not. It also closes the footgun where a church-space domain that forgot `THREADS` would serve the full site minus its own storyline.
  - **`EDITION` is threaded through and exported separately from `THEME`.** Falling back to `THEME` covers a pre-registry clone, but the axes are independent now — a domain whose edition id differs from its palette (`EDITION=my-site THEME=sepia`) would otherwise resolve its copy as `editionFor("sepia")`, find nothing, and silently ship the default tagline. Verified end to end.
  - `validateEditions` now also rejects a **domain claimed by two editions** (resolution would pick one and the other would quietly serve wrong branding forever) and a `theme` with no matching `src/css/theme-*.css` (the deploy silently keeps `main.css` on a miss, so a typo shipped as "unbranded" rather than failing).
- **`editions.local.json` — independent hosting without a fork.** Untracked, gitignored, with a tracked `sample-editions.local.json`, exactly the pattern `giscus.local.json` already establishes. An entry whose `id` matches a tracked edition overrides it field by field; a new id is added. Domain matching tolerates scheme, `www.`, port, path and case.
  - **It cannot add story content, and that is the point.** There is no field for a lore page, chapter or glossary entry, because canon is centralised. That protects an independent host as much as the record: nothing they put in that file can be mistaken for this story's canon.
  - This is also the seam that makes the config split coherent. `GISCUS_PROFILE` stays repo-side because a profile name is meaningless outside this registry; the raw `GISCUS_*_ID` values stay server-side because they are exactly what an independent host supplies via their own `giscus.local.json`.
- **`lib/editions.js` — a registry of per-domain copy, so `theme` goes back to meaning only "palette"** (2026-07-30). "Edition" is the site's own existing word for a per-domain build, not a coinage: `excluded.njk` has said "Not included in this **edition**" since narrowing was introduced. Resolved from an `EDITION` env var, **falling back to `THEME`** so every untracked live `deploy.conf` keeps working with no edit.
  - **The governing rule is a constraint on the file, not a note about it: canon is centralised, and variants are non-canonical** (settled 2026-07-30). Nothing an edition carries may assert a fact about the world. `src/seasons/`, `src/lore/` and `src/glossary/` are identical on every domain; every field here is framing — a tagline, a hero cast, an audio track. The test for a proposed field is not "is this nice for that domain?" but "**could two domains now disagree about something true?**" This is also what makes the multi-domain deploy coherent rather than merely convenient: filtering only ever *subtracts*, so a narrowed clone shows a subset of one record and never a contradiction of it. No fifth canon status is added — an edition is the shop window, not the archive.
  - **Why `theme` had to stop doing this job.** It was carrying palette *and* identity, and `sample-deploy.conf` already breaks the one-to-one that requires: four `fol*` entries share `THEME=fellowship`, two `churchspace*` share `THEME=church-space` — six domains, two identities. A fifth domain wanting its own tagline couldn't have one, and a domain wanting the `sepia` palette *plus* its own copy couldn't ask. Verified the fix: `EDITION=pets THEME=sepia` now yields pets copy on the sepia palette, which was previously inexpressible.
  - **It also inverts the direction copy is organised in.** The old `{% if theme == %}` branches put one domain's identity across `src/index.md` and `base.njk`, so edit points grew as domains × templates. Now it's one entry per edition, however many templates read it. `editionFor()` merges over `DEFAULT_EDITION`, so an edition declares only what it overrides — `church-space` is registered with no overrides at all, precisely so its first flourish is a one-line edit here instead of a new template branch.
  - Migrated the existing four looks (`default`, `fellowship`, `starquest`, `pets`) plus a registered `church-space`. **Content verified identical** for all four against pre-refactor snapshots: same subtitle, same audio file and label, same hero cast.
- **Codex entries now say on the page that they aren't canon.** `codex.njk` renders a short notice under the byline: a primary source, not the Archive's own voice, canon *for its author*, possibly partial or self-serving or contradicted by settled lore, and to be cited as an account rather than as established fact. It names the entry's own `author` inline, which is possible on every entry because `author` is required precisely so there is someone to attribute the claims to.
  - **Why on the entry and not just the index.** `/codex/`'s intro already warned that "some are incomplete, biased, or built to mislead", but most readers never see it — a search result, a cross-link from a lore page, or an external citation all land on the entry directly. The four canon statuses are the easiest thing on this site to flatten, and flattening them turns a named source's account into the Archive stating fact.
  - Reuses the `.canon-facts` box treatment deliberately, so a reader who has met one of those on a chapter already reads the shape as the Archive talking *about* a text rather than *in* it. Carries `data-pagefind-ignore` for the same reason the breadcrumb and footer do: identical boilerplate on all 32 entries would otherwise return 32 indistinguishable hits for "primary source" or "canon". `npm run generate-themes` re-run, so all nine generated themes stay in sync.
- **Chapters can carry their own image, and social cards gained the tags they were missing.** `image`/`image_alt` are now optional chapter front matter (`lib/content-schema.js`), with `chapters` added to `OG_IMAGE_DIRS`; files live in `src/images/chapters/` and `chapter.njk` renders one on the page, on the same pattern as `lore-entry.njk`.
  - **The gap this closes was a social-sharing one, not a design one.** Chapters had no image field at all, so **147 pages** — every chapter plus every scene-POV page, the most shareable things on the site — fell back to one site hero in their Open Graph tags and produced visually identical cards. The fallback stays for any chapter without an image.
  - New tags in `base.njk`: `og:image:alt` and `twitter:image:alt`, `og:image:width`/`height`, `og:locale`, and `article:published_time` on article pages.
  - **`og:image:alt` follows the image, not the page** (`computeOgImageAlt`). Once the fallback hero is in use, a page's own `image_alt` describes a file that isn't in the card, and reusing it would caption the wrong picture — the exact failure the July 2026 audit found on-page. Verified on an excluded page: it falls back to the hero and the hero's own alt, leaking neither.
  - **`article:published_time` reads its guard and its value from different places, and has to.** `date` in a layout is the raw front-matter string, so it answers "did the author set one?"; the value comes from `page.date`, Eleventy's parsed Date, because `dateToRfc3339` uses `DateTime.fromJSDate` and renders the string as empty — which is how the first attempt shipped an empty tag. Testing `page.date` instead would have stamped every lore entry with a publication time it never had, since Eleventy falls back to file mtime.
  - **`lib/image-size.js`** is new: a memoised JPEG/PNG header reader for the width/height tags. No new dependency — this repo ships zero runtime `dependencies`, and `sharp` would pull per-platform native binaries for two integers sitting in the first few hundred bytes of every file. Only JPEG and PNG are handled (the only formats `src/images/` contains); anything unreadable or unparseable returns null and both tags are omitted, because a guessed dimension makes a platform reserve a box the image doesn't fill.
  - Verified end to end by temporarily giving a chapter an image: Open Graph switched to it with correct alt and real dimensions, it rendered on the page, and validation accepted the new fields. Test artifacts reverted.
- **`/llms.txt`** ([`src/llms.njk`](src/llms.njk)) — an orientation index for language models and agents reading the site, per the llmstxt.org convention. Plain Markdown, generated from the same **filtered** collections `sitemap.xml` uses, so a narrowed clone advertises only what it serves and a private thread stays absent.
  - **It carries the canon model, which is the only thing on this site a crawler cannot infer and the main reason the file exists.** Four canon statuses flatten to one under naive reading, and the consequence is not cosmetic: an agent that quotes a codex entry as settled fact has misread the archive. `llms.txt` states that chapters/lore/glossary are canon, that each codex entry is canon *only for its named author* and may be partial or contradicted, that contested material lives in the Codex by design, and that an overlay is neither. It also warns that a POV block is one character's understanding rather than a narrator's assertion, that terminology is versioned with a migration map, and that story content is CC BY-NC-ND while the engine is MIT.
