  - **It is a map, not an inventory, and that was a correction mid-build.** The first version enumerated every chapter, lore entry, glossary term, character and codex entry with descriptions: 352 lines, 66 KB, ~16k tokens spent before the reader reached anything it wanted — and duplicating `/lore/`, `/characters/`, `/glossary/`, `/codex/` and `/timeline/`, which already enumerate their own sections in HTML, plus `sitemap.xml`, which is the complete URL list. The shipped file is **102 lines, 9.7 KB**: orientation, the canon rules, start-here links, per-section links with live counts, and chapters named inline (the one section whose story order isn't recoverable from URLs by anything that hasn't decoded the `sNNeNNcNN` scheme).
- **`scripts/make-lore-cards.ps1`** — a batch driver over `make-codex-cover.ps1` that generates the title cards for the nine lore entries lacking an image, with the card table inline. Local authoring tool: Windows-only, not part of the build, not run by `npm test`, not linted by CI (the shellcheck job covers the three `.sh` files only).
  - **Why a script rather than nine pasted invocations.** The nine cards are data, not decisions — the decisions are already recorded in `images.md` Open work 5. `make-codex-cover.ps1`'s own header gives the rationale: the original codex covers "were produced ad hoc and never scripted, so a broken or missing cover had no reproducible way to be rebuilt." That reasoning covers *which* cards exist as much as how one is drawn. Same shape as `generate-themes.js` — a mechanical derivation belongs in a script so nobody hand-maintains its outputs.
  - **Existing files are skipped unless `-Force`**, so a re-run cannot clobber a card since replaced by hand. `-List` previews the table without generating; `-Only <substring>` regenerates one row.
  - Two constraints found by reading the generator rather than guessing: subtitles are **not** auto-fitted (only titles are), so the driver fails the whole batch up front on any subtitle over 34 characters rather than emitting a card with text running off the canvas; and `Institution`/`Author` are empty on every row, because codex covers carry them for a named in-universe source and lore is the Archive's own voice with no author to name.
- **Seventeen lore entries gain a worked example, a dramatised cross-reference, or both** (2026-07-30). A sweep prompted by a simple observation: only 9 of 97 lore pages linked to a chapter, and several of the most rule-heavy pages read as regulation with nothing behind it. Nothing here changes a fact — every addition is drawn from an existing chapter's `canon_facts` or from settled lore already on file, and no new canon was created.
  - **The direction of reference is deliberate and one-way: lore points at chapters, never the reverse.** A chapter has to stand on its own for a reader who arrives at it first, so nothing was added to `src/seasons/`. The links are all outbound from the reference material, which is the direction a reader already goes when a rule raises a question.
  - **The physics cluster gets its numbers back.** [`teleportation-limitations.md`](src/lore/teleportation-limitations.md) states its three-condition rule and now records where the rule was written and why it carries no exception clause — Thorne argued for one, having just authorised a jump on a thin margin, and was talked out of it. [`quantum-space-harmonics.md`](src/lore/quantum-space-harmonics.md) gains the Threshold coupling as a worked case: three traces overlaid, a 3:7 band coupling, and a forecasting capability of 18–26 minutes rather than a fix. [`boundary-zones.md`](src/lore/boundary-zones.md) grounds Class II in the one figure it always had available and never quoted — forty seconds, eleven years, carried as a calibration fault.
  - **Two pages gained the counter they were missing rather than a link.** [`predatory-entities.md`](src/lore/predatory-entities.md) listed a "how to counter them" for Cute Predators only; Court-Fae and Gilded Saints now have theirs, and the Gilded Saint entry says plainly that the obvious counter is the wrong one — refusing comfort exhausts the person practising it and inconveniences nothing. [`seed-mind-lifecycle.md`](src/lore/seed-mind-lifecycle.md) gains **the stall**, the state between Phase 6 and a completed Phase 7 that the phase list could not name because it is not a phase.
  - **One addition exists to stop a misreading rather than to illustrate one.** [`noogenic-seeding-system.md`](src/lore/noogenic-seeding-system.md)'s "Not a Salvation" section holds that a completed transference carries no person and nobody wakes up in a successor universe. That is unchanged and still correct — and a stalled seed is a different state in which somebody is demonstrably in there. The two are now distinguished on the page, because a reader who meets both without the distinction concludes one of them is wrong.
  - Also: [`cerebraun-hegemony.md`](src/lore/cerebraun-hegemony.md) (what unambiguous authority costs the official holding it — accountability for a reversal independent of whether the reversal was correct), [`cerebraun.md`](src/lore/cerebraun.md), [`levrils.md`](src/lore/levrils.md) (two occasions, one tier constraint — what differed was what was permitted, never what was possible), [`saint-aoife.md`](src/lore/saint-aoife.md), [`dryadic-trees.md`](src/lore/dryadic-trees.md), [`celtic-union-of-planets.md`](src/lore/celtic-union-of-planets.md), [`orbital-habitats-compact.md`](src/lore/orbital-habitats-compact.md), [`habitat-threshold.md`](src/lore/habitat-threshold.md), [`the-fusion-ceiling.md`](src/lore/the-fusion-ceiling.md), [`planets/tir-na-nog.md`](src/lore/planets/tir-na-nog.md), [`kieme-visible-hand.md`](src/lore/kieme-visible-hand.md).
- **`planets/tir-na-nog.md` records the Boirinn Hollow, and `dryadic-trees.md` records it as an unsurveyed instance.** Both were derivable from [`s05e02c01`](src/seasons/s05/e02/s05e02c01.md)'s `canon_facts` and neither page had them. The entry earns its place by what it establishes about the organism rather than about that holding: the two field markers are consistent wherever an anchor of this type occurs, so **the survey record's coverage is a record of where instruments have been allowed, not of where the trees are** — the same selection effect `boundary-zones.md` already names about the two Solar System sites, arriving from a second direction.

### Changed

- **`story-bible/images.md` gains Open work 5: the nineteen lore entries with no image** (audited 2026-07-30). Open work 1 had enumerated missing *character portraits* since July; nothing had ever enumerated missing *lore* illustrations, so the gap was invisible rather than deferred. None blocks a build — `lore-entry.njk` guards the image behind `{% if image %}`.
  - **The section's one editorial contribution is splitting the nineteen by job.** Nine are institutions or factions and belong on designed title cards from the generator, which letters text with a font engine where an image model cannot be trusted to spell. The remaining ten are places, phenomena, technology and cosmology, and get generated images with prompts written to the standing rules — era stated, lettering banned, sheen named rather than substance. (The first version of this entry also claimed the split was *descriptive* of how four existing lore cards were made. It wasn't — see **Fixed** below.)
  - Two prompts carry an explicit constraint about what they must *not* show. `arilon` must not read as a portrait of one figure, since the entry exists to establish that Arilon is a recurring pattern and not a person. `membrane-shadows` must read as an unexplained physical imprint and not as a threat approaching — nothing is coming through, which is the entry's whole point and also where the tone line bites hardest.
  - Also flagged, deliberately as *not* defects, so a future audit doesn't re-derive them: `predatory-entities.jpg` and `teleportation-limitations.jpg` have thin-but-accurate alt text.

### Deprecated

- **`deploy.conf`'s `CUSTOM_LORE_FILE`** (2026-07-30). Still honoured — the deploy logs a warning rather than failing, because `deploy.conf` is untracked and lives on the cPanel account, so a live domain relying on it cannot be migrated from the repo and a hard failure would silently drop that domain's page. `CUSTOM_CSS_FILE` is **not** deprecated, but the reason given here originally — "it is cosmetic and cannot assert a fact" — was wrong and is corrected under **Fixed** below.
  - Two reasons, and the second is the binding one. It keeps story prose outside the repo — unversioned, unreviewable, unseen by `npm test` and both check scripts, outside the CC BY-NC-ND scope `CONTENT-LICENSE.md` describes, and lost with the hosting account. And it writes into `src/lore/`, which is **canon** — making it the only mechanism in the system that could have two domains disagree about a fact rather than show different subsets of one record. Removing it closes the last route to per-domain canon.
  - There is deliberately **no replacement for injecting lore**. `lib/editions.js` replaces the legitimate use (per-domain framing) and cannot express the illegitimate one. A domain needing a page of its own gets a non-canonical one; if material is worth being true, it is worth being true everywhere and belongs in `src/lore/` on every domain.

### Fixed

- **The glossary was never actually sorted, and its A–Z navigation quietly depended on it being sorted** (`.eleventy.js`, `src/glossary/index.md`). The `glossary` collection was `getAll()` plus two filters with no `.sort()`, so it inherited Eleventy's own ordering — alphabetical for the first 22 terms and unordered for the remaining 31.
  - **The page is built entirely on the assumption of a sorted list.** It emits a letter heading whenever an entry's first letter differs from the previous entry's, which is correct for sorted input and nonsense otherwise: **44 headings for 53 terms, with 13 letters appearing more than once** as the sequence flipped back and forth. The A–Z jump bar *is* deduplicated, so each letter anchored to its **first** occurrence and every later group of that letter was unreachable from it — four of the five N terms could not be reached by clicking N. The bar itself rendered in the collection's order (`A B T C E H K M N U W F S O I L Q V G P`) rather than alphabetically.
  - **Leading articles are ignored when filing** (settled 2026-07-30): *The Interval* files under **I** and *The Common Manifold* under **C**, standard printed-glossary practice and where a reader actually looks. The cost is that a heading letter no longer always matches the first character shown, which is the accepted trade.
  - **Order and heading now come from one function.** `glossaryAlphaKey` drives the collection sort, and the new `glossaryAlphaLetter` filter drives both the jump bar and the headings, so the letter a term files under is by construction the letter it sorted by. Comparison uses `localeCompare` with `sensitivity: "base"`, which keeps the four `Noö…` terms together and in order.
  - **Deliberately presentation-only.** `related:` terms resolve through `glossaryUrl` by *exact* title match, leading articles included, so stripping an article for filing cannot change which page a related link reaches. The collection's other two consumers are order-independent (`| length` in `src/llms.njk`, a title lookup in `glossary-entry.njk`). After: 20 headings, none repeated, jump bar identical to the headings and in A–Z order.
- **Home page hero went blank on any deploy whose slide count wasn't 5 or 6** (`src/css/main.css`, `src/index.md`, all `theme-*.css` regenerated) — reported as a missing image on `undercover-pets.com`'s home page, which is the domain the bug was built to catch first.
  - **The slide count is a property of the *deploy*, not of the edition.** `src/index.md` resolves `lib/editions.js`'s `heroCharacterIds` through `charactersByIds` against the **filtered** characters collection, so a narrowed clone drops any hero character its `CHARACTERS`/`TOPICS`/`THREADS` excludes. `main.css` carried crossfade rules for exactly `--n5` and `--n6`, the two counts the registry lists. At any other count no slide got an `animation-name`, every one of them kept the base `opacity: 0`, and the hero rendered as an **empty bordered box** — losing all the portraits, not the one character that was filtered out.
  - **One missing tag on one character page was enough to trigger it.** `undercover-pets.com` narrows by the `undercover-pets.com` tag and is the only edition with a recast five-character hero cast, so its hero sits one tag away from a count of four — and this release's own changelog records a pets-relevant page found *without* that tag. Reproduced directly: `TOPICS=eden` gives four slides, `TOPICS=detective-agency` three, and before this fix both rendered nothing.
  - **Fix is in the stylesheet, where the promise was being broken.** Crossfade variants now exist for 2–8 slides (one 6s slot each, 1s crossfade — the same geometry as the original two, which are unchanged), `:nth-child` delays extend to 8, and a `:first-child { opacity: 1 }` fallback shows one still portrait for a single slide or any count past the range, so a blank box is no longer reachable. `npm run generate-themes` re-propagated all of it, including to `theme-pets.css`.
  - **And when *no* hero character survives the filter, the page now falls back to the site hero image** rather than rendering no image at all — the previously untested case, and the one that leaves the page every reader lands on first with nothing on it. Uses the page's own computed `ogImage`/`ogImageAlt`, so the card preview and the page show the same picture with the same description.
- **Corrected a false claim about `CUSTOM_CSS_FILE`, and added a deploy-time warning for it.** Three places in this release described that key as "cosmetic" and as unable to "assert a fact" (`CHANGELOG.md`, `sample-deploy.conf`, `scripts/cpanel-deploy.sh`). That does not survive scrutiny. The accurate claim is narrower: **it cannot change the record.**
  - **CSS here can inject text.** `content:` on a `::before`/`::after` puts arbitrary prose on a page — an assertion delivered by stylesheet. Nothing restrains it: the site sets no CSP at all, and this file is appended **last** to the built `main.css`, so it overrides the theme and everything else.
  - It can also **hide** content — `display:none` on `.codex-entry__status` suppresses the "not canon, cite it as an account" notice added earlier in this release; on `.site-footer` it hides the CC BY-NC-ND attribution — **reorder** what a human reads relative to the DOM via flex/grid, and **reach external hosts** via `@import`, `url()` and `@font-face`.
  - **What bounds all four is that they affect rendering only.** The DOM is untouched, so crawlers, chatbots, screen readers, reader mode, the Atom feed and `llms.txt` still get the real content. So the canon rule **holds structurally** — nothing CSS does enters the record — and **leaks perceptually**, for a sighted human on one domain. It cuts both ways: `content:`-injected text is invisible to search engines and to an LLM fetching the page, so an injected "fact" reaches nobody else.
  - **The conclusion is still to keep it server-side**, for a narrower reason than originally given: the legitimate use is real and small, hand-edited `theme-*.css` files get overwritten by `generate-themes`, and the realistic risk is not sabotage but forgetting — hiding one of those boxes months from now while tidying something you no longer recognise.
  - `check_custom_css_powers()` in `scripts/cpanel-deploy.sh` now **warns** on the three constructs that cross the line, naming only the elements actually mentioned so the warning never explains something you didn't do. It never fails the deploy: `content: ""` is ordinary pseudo-element decoration, and a false positive that blocks a deploy is worse than a log line. Exercised against seven cases — innocent tweak, `content: ""` and `content: ''`, text injection, hiding the notice, hiding the footer, an external `@import`, `display:none` on an unrelated selector, and all three at once — with silence where silence was wanted.
- **The homepage hero subtitle was invalid HTML, and the class it names was inert.** `src/index.md` wrapped the subtitle in `<p class="home-hero__subtitle">` and the Markdown pipeline then emitted `<p>` elements *inside* it. Browsers auto-close a `<p>` on encountering a nested one, so `.home-hero__subtitle` (1.1rem, muted, `max-width: 55ch`, centred) was applied to an empty paragraph while the visible text rendered as default body copy. Collapsing the `theme ==` branches into a single `{{ edition.heroSubtitle | safe }}` removed the blank-line structure that caused it, so the markup is now one correctly-nested paragraph.
  - **This is a visible change on every domain's homepage** — the subtitle finally picks up its intended styling — and it is called out because it was a side effect of the editions refactor rather than something asked for. The `latestLore` sentence also joins the subtitle as one paragraph instead of becoming a second one, which is what the template always intended.
- **`scripts/check-internal-links.js` now scans `src/` and `lib/`** (`.md`/`.njk`/`.html`/`.js`) rather than `src/` alone. Moving the homepage taglines into `lib/editions.js` took 4 links out of the script's coverage silently, which is the failure mode the script itself exists to catch.
  - **Scanning by root, not by a list of exceptions.** The first version of this fix was an `EXTRA_FILES` list naming `lib/editions.js`; that shipped and is now replaced. A hand-maintained list of exceptions goes stale — the next authored file with links outside `src/` would not have been added to it and nobody would have noticed. Same reasoning that consolidated four drifting image notes into one `images.md`.
  - **Verified safe rather than assumed:** `src/js/pov.js` and `src/js/search.js` contain no `/star-rangers/` strings at all, and `lib/content-filter.js`'s three occurrences are in comments and a regex literal — none href/src/markdown-link shaped, so `linkRe` cannot match them. Page derivation still comes from `src/` only; a `path.relative(SRC, …)` on a `lib/` file would have invented pages like `../lib/…`.
  - **One consequence, arguably a feature:** an illustrative URL written in attribute form inside a code comment is now checked like a real link. It caught a made-up example in `editions.js`'s own comments the day this landed. Fake paths should be described in prose, not quoted as attributes.
  - The summary line now counts files actually **read** (360) rather than every file walked under `src/` (579) — the old figure included images and audio, so it was always larger than the set of files that could hold a link. Verified end to end: a break in `lib/` and a break in `src/` are each reported against the right file, and both exit non-zero.
- **`lib/editions.js` validates itself at build time** (`validateEditions`, called from `.eleventy.js`), throwing on a duplicate edition id or a `themeAudio.file` missing from `src/audio/`. The audio filenames used to be literal `src="…/audio/x.wav"` attributes that the link checker verified; they are now bare strings assembled by a template, which the checker correctly skips as templated — so a typo would have shipped a player pointing at nothing. Duplicate ids are checked for the same reason `validate-content.js` guards `comment_id` collisions: the map would quietly keep the last one.
- **Hidden pages are no longer indexable.** A page this build hides still returns HTTP 200 with a real placeholder body — that *is* the design, so no cross-link ever 404s — which meant every hidden page was advertised to crawlers as ordinary content. `base.njk` now emits `<meta name="robots">` when a `robots` value is set, and two places set it to `noindex, follow`.
  - **`follow`, not `nofollow`, deliberately:** the one useful thing on a placeholder is its link out to the reference domain, and that should still be traversed.
  - **The effect on the public site is larger than the narrowed-clone case that prompted it.** `church-space` is a private thread hidden on *every* build including the default full-site one, so the main site was already publishing 9 indexable "Not included in this edition" pages. Those are now `noindex`. On a narrowed clone the count is 376.
  - **Driven off `isContentIncluded` rather than `data.layout`**, per the hazard documented at the top of `.eleventy.js`: `layout` is itself one of the overridden computed keys, so reading it from inside another computed field can see the already-rewritten value. That exact mismatch caused a real bug once before.
  - Included pages get **no** `robots` tag at all rather than an explicit `index, follow`, and any page may still opt in via its own front matter. Verified both directions: 376 placeholders and 376 `noindex` tags on a `THREADS=founding-era` build with zero gaps; an included lore page and an included scene-POV page each carry none.
- **Scene-POV pages were the blind spot in both the new `noindex` and the existing sitemap filter** — 92 hidden POV placeholders on a narrowed build, and one of them listed in `sitemap.xml` as real content. One root cause: **scene-POV pages opt out of the layout-swap convention.** They keep their own layout and gate their body on `item.included` (set per character in `src/_data/scenePovPages.js`), so anything keyed to the swapped layout misses them — and because they are generated from `src/scene-pov.njk`, `classifyContentPath()` sees that as their `inputPath`, matches none of its content dirs, and passes them through as included.
  - Fixed in the two places that own the decision: `src/scene-pov.njk` sets its own `robots` from `item.included`, and `src/sitemap.njk` gained a second test alongside the layout check. This is precisely the failure mode `CLAUDE.md` warns about for a new page type, arriving from the opposite direction — an *existing* page type that a new field forgot.
  - **Not changed, and flagged rather than silently decided:** `sitemap.xml` lists only **1 of 92** scene-POV pages even on a full build, because Eleventy represents a paginated template once in `collections.all`. Whether ~92 derivative POV views of existing chapters belong in a sitemap at all is an editorial call about duplicate content, plausibly deliberate, and not one to make as a side effect of a `noindex` fix.
- **`story-bible/images.md` Open work 5 shipped with a false claim about how the existing lore cards were made** (introduced in #232, corrected here). It stated that `cerebraun-hegemony`, `celtic-union-of-planets`, `orbital-habitats-compact` and `levrils` were produced with `scripts/make-codex-cover.ps1`, and listed `federation-of-sentient-beings` and `united-space-consortium` alongside them as more of the same. Both halves were wrong.
  - **The error came from reasoning about `image_alt` strings instead of opening the files** — the exact failure mode that file already warns about in its own Auditing section ("To check whether an image matches its description, **read the file**"). Reading them settles it: the four cards are **1600×900 landscape**, individually tinted, and carry a device inside a ringed seal, while `make-codex-cover.ps1` emits **square 1600×1600** in one fixed blue palette with no emblem motif at all — only `rules`, `dissolution`, `none`. It cannot have produced them. `federation-of-sentient-beings` (1200×1509) and `united-space-consortium` (1200×800) are photographs, not cards.
  - **The correction surfaces a real gap rather than just fixing a sentence: the emblem-card recipe is unrecorded and currently unreproducible.** All four landed in Release 1.7.0 (#187) with no entry in `image-prompts.md` — precisely the rule that file exists to enforce, and precisely the failure the Prismere cluster prompted it over. A fifth card in the same family is referenced from `uniforms-and-insignia.md`. Now recorded as open work with three named ways out: recover the original tool and log it; extend `make-codex-cover.ps1` with aspect, palette and seal support (noting every positioning constant in it is tuned for 1600×1600, so this is more than a parameter); or accept the codex look for lore and treat the four as legacy.
  - **Consequence for the new script, stated in both its header and `CLAUDE.md`:** its nine cards will read as codex-style, not like those four, and that inconsistency is deliberately left unresolved — it is a call to make before generating nine cards, not after.

## [1.10.0] - 2026-07-29

The naming release. Every substantive change in it is about a name rather than a fact: a Cascade tier renamed, a Ranger rank restyled, a second rank finally recorded under its full style, one charter clause rewritten so its rank floor cannot be misread, and a journal entry about the single tell the whole set had in common.

**That tell is the release's actual content**, so it belongs at the top. Each entry touched here carried a paragraph whose only job was explaining what its own name did *not* mean. `Dynarch` named a tier after the forces it is least able to alter — the rule-sets are the Worldwright's — and the entry spent a section on the gap. `Starwarden First Officer` named a rank after a relationship it does not have, and its own bullet admitted so in its opening clause. In both cases the explanation was *good*, which is exactly why it survived for months. A well-argued defence of a bad name is a decent piece of writing and a permanent tax on every reader who arrives after it.

**The two renames needed opposite machinery, which is this release's one genuinely load-bearing distinction.** `Dynarch → Mediarch` is the Archive correcting its own vocabulary: no in-universe register ever used the word, so once retired it names nothing, migrates on sight, and takes no dating rule. `Starwarden First Officer → Archwarden` is an institution renaming its own rank in **2833 UCSD**, so both styles are correct for their own periods and pre-2833 records are read as written rather than corrected. The consequence worth having in the record: **not one word of canon prose was altered anywhere in this release.** The two migration rows now sit next to each other in the canonical glossary making opposite claims about the past, and each points at the other so neither can be applied with the wrong rule.

**`MINOR`, and this is the first release where that classification needed an argument.** Earlier entries could justify it with "nothing was removed, renamed or moved" — this one renames two things and moves a page's URL, which reads like that criterion failing. It isn't. `MAJOR` in this project has always concerned the **engine's compatibility surface** — `deploy.conf` keys, themes, build outputs, defaults — and none of those changed. The single moved URL keeps a redirect stub at its old address, and the retired `dynarch` tag is deliberately retained on the renamed entry so any clone narrowing by that topic keeps matching it. Nothing 404s and no configuration breaks, which is the substance the older phrasing was reaching for.

**Tagging.** `v1.10.0` is cut at this release's own merge commit, which does not exist until the release merges — so the tag is always the last step and always separate from this file. The GitHub-automation path used for most changes here cannot publish `refs/tags/*`; where no local clone is in the loop, that is where the backlog recorded under `[1.7.0]` and `[1.8.0]` came from.

### Changed

- **The rank above Deputy and below Senior is recorded as `Field Officer`** (settled 2026-07-29) — the ladder entry previously gave only the short form **Officer** and described the rank without naming it in full. Same rung, same duties, no reordering: full field-qualified rank, the first tier that can act and be posted independently.
  - **Three live forms, and the reason they coexist is worth the paragraph.** Formal style **Field Officer**; short form **Officer**; colloquially just **Star Ranger** or **Star Ranger officer**. Unlike the three Archwarden styles retired above, none of these is deprecated — the entry keeps all three and explains which register each belongs to.
  - **The colloquial form is genuinely ambiguous, and the entry now says so rather than smoothing it.** "A Star Ranger" names *this rung specifically* and *everyone from this rung upward* — a Line Captain is a Star Ranger and so is the newest Field Officer aboard her vessel. Filed not as a defect but as what happens when a rank is the **threshold of belonging** rather than a step inside it: the rung at which a Ranger stops being supervised and starts being one of the people the word is for. The previous wording called *Star Ranger* a collective term "rather than a rung of its own," which is half the truth — it is both.
  - `Deputy` gains its full style **Deputy Officer** and `Senior` its alternate **Senior Star Ranger**, from the same pass. Recorded in [`star-rangers-command-hierarchy.md`](src/lore/star-rangers-command-hierarchy.md), with `field-officer` added to the page's tags.
- **The Field Triumvirate clause gains a fallback composition** (settled 2026-07-29). The clause previously specified exactly one body — the ranking Line Captain, the nearest vessel's Archwarden, and the next most senior Starwarden reachable — and said nothing about what happens when that cannot be assembled, which left the charter's emergency provision silently unavailable in the circumstances most likely to need it. It now has **two forms in strict order of preference**: the named composition where it can be reached, and failing that **the three most senior officers available, none below the rank of Officer**.
  - **The floor is `Field Officer`, and it is the only rank test the clause makes.** Field Officer is the ladder's full field-qualified rank and the first tier that can be posted and act independently; below it — Deputy Officer, Cadet, Novice — a Ranger works under another officer's supervision by definition, and a body of supervised officers authorising emergency action would be a contradiction, since the supervision is the thing being bypassed. The floor is therefore structural rather than a seniority ornament: it is the line between *can act on their own judgement* and *cannot*.
  - **The clause uses the full style deliberately, and this is load-bearing.** "The three most senior officers available" uses the ordinary word; *none below Officer* would collide with it, and *none below Star Ranger* would collide with the collective term for everyone from that rung upward — which would read as no floor at all. **Field Officer** is the only form of the name that cannot be misread in either direction. Same lesson the Archwarden restyling records, applied to a clause before it cost anything rather than after.
  - **Fallback, not alternative** — an officer cannot prefer it for being quicker to assemble or likelier to produce an agreeable third voice; where the named composition is reachable in the time available it is the only lawful one. **`Available` carries the third condition's own clock:** reachable in time to take part in the decision actually being made, so an officer who could join in an hour is not available to a decision that has minutes. And **seniority decides with no discretion** — the three most senior, in order — because a rule permitting selection permits a convening officer to assemble a body that will agree with them.
  - **What the fallback gives up is stated in the entry rather than concealed.** The named composition is independent by construction: a Line Captain, another vessel's Archwarden and a Starwarden on relay are three different commands, none owing its posting to the others. The fallback has no such property and on one hull can be a captain and two of their own crew. That weakening is accepted because the alternative is a body that cannot convene while people are dying — and the safeguards were never compositional: they are the three conditions, each standing on its own, plus the reporting and review that follow every convening.
  - **Below three eligible officers there is no Field Triumvirate**, and the clause manufactures nothing out of two. What one officer may do at the scene stays with the existing [decision doctrine](src/lore/star-rangers-decision-and-communication.md) — authority sitting with whoever is closest and holds the relevant rank — answered for personally, and never recorded as a Triumvirate.
  - **Nothing retroactive.** The 2831 Dock Seven convening reached the named composition in full and is now noted as the standing example of it; the fallback has never yet appeared on a record anyone has had to review. Recorded in [`star-rangers-command-hierarchy.md`](src/lore/star-rangers-command-hierarchy.md).
- **The force-governance tier is renamed `Dynarch` → `Mediarch`** (settled 2026-07-29) — a pure rename, with **no change of meaning, rank, property or constraint**. Every statement the corpus filed about a Dynarch stands unaltered about a Mediarch, which is why this is filed as Changed rather than as a settlement: nothing was decided about the tier here except what to call it.
  - **The old name pointed at the wrong thing, and the corpus already said so.** *Dynarch* (from *dynamis*, force) named the tier after its subject matter — and the tier's first listed constraint, unchanged since it was written, is that it governs the *operation* of a force and not its design: the rule-sets are the Worldwright's, and no Mediarch can rewrite a zone's physics. The name emphasised the one thing the office is least able to alter.
  - **The new name records what the 2026-07-26 settlement established.** *Mediarch* (from *medius*, the middle) names the mediating office — the Telearch line reaching inside a universe by proxy, standing between a continuity branch native to nowhere and the inside of the thing that branch has to reach. "A Mediarch is a proxy Telearch" now reads as an unpacking of the name rather than as a fact arriving from elsewhere.
  - **`Exarch` is untouched and still co-canonical.** The older devotional and provincial form was already naming the same mediation — a delegated governor holding a province from a distant throne — so the rename brings the formal name into line with the devotional one rather than displacing it. **No in-universe register keeps `Dynarch`**, which is why there is no quoted-as-written exception of the kind the Solar System Concord row carries: devotional sources say *Exarch*, and [The Reading Before a First Vigil](src/codex/the-reading-before-a-first-vigil.md) needed no change beyond its archive note.
  - **Recorded as terminology law**, per the standing rule that a cosmological rename means the canonical-terms list *and* a migration row *and* a corpus sweep: the [canonical glossary](src/lore/glossary/canonical-glossary-and-migration-guide.md) gains a `Dynarch → Mediarch` migration row and a `The name` block, and its "higher celestials" row now notes that the term has been migrated **twice** — `higher celestials` → `Dynarch` → `Mediarch` — so a legacy reading lands on the current name rather than on the intermediate one.
  - **Swept across the corpus in one pass**, hierarchy spines included: [`glossary/mediarch.md`](src/glossary/mediarch.md) (renamed from `dynarch.md`), `telearch.md`, `celestials.md`, `concordant-principal.md`, `high-celestials.md`, `glossary/cosmic-cascade.md`, `lore/cosmic-cascade.md`, `who-governs-a-universe.md`, `physics-comparison.md`, `concordant-membranes.md`, the codex archive note, and `story-bible/canon-consistency-audit-2026-07.md`. Where a page explains the tier's naming history rather than merely using the name — `lore/cosmic-cascade.md` and `who-governs-a-universe.md` — it now records all three names and why each was replaced, so the rename is legible from the record instead of only from this file.
  - **The old URL does not 404.** `/glossary/dynarch/` becomes a redirect stub ([`glossary/dynarch.njk`](src/glossary/dynarch.njk)) pointing at `/glossary/mediarch/`, on the same pattern as `lore/solar-system-concordant.njk`: canonical link, `noindex, follow`, meta refresh, and a sentence saying what moved and why. **`dynarch` is also kept as a tag** on the renamed entry alongside `mediarch`, so any cPanel clone whose untracked `deploy.conf` narrows by that topic keeps matching the page.
  - Verified with `npm test`, `check-internal-links.js` (1832 links, all resolve) and `check-related-terms.js` (204 terms, all resolve) — the last of which is the check that matters here, since `related:` resolves by page **title** and a stale term would have silently degraded to `/glossary/` rather than failing.
- **The rank above Starwarden and below Line Captain is restyled `Starwarden First Officer` → `Archwarden`** (settled 2026-07-29; **2833 UCSD** in-universe). A vessel's second-in-command, one rung above Starwarden and one below Line Captain — **seniority, duties and ladder position all unchanged**. Only the words on the tab moved.
  - **The old style was the most misread title on the ladder, and its own entry said so** in its opening clause. *First Officer* named the post — first officer **of a vessel** — and never meant first officer *to* a Starwarden, but that is how it read to anyone meeting it cold, and the two ranks are consecutive rungs rather than a commander and a deputy. The entry answered this with a paragraph of explanation, which is a tax on every reader rather than a fix. **Archwarden** says senior warden and needs no paragraph. Three written forms are also retired with it — `Starwarden First Officer`, `Starwarden First Class` and `Executive Starwarden First Class` — since one rank carrying three styles was half the problem.
  - **Where the old style actually cost something: the Field Triumvirate clause.** It names a warden-rank and a Starwarden in one breath, so the previous wording read as *the Starwarden First Officer … and the next most senior Starwarden* — implying a chain of command between the two that does not exist, in the one clause where three officers have to know who is who under pressure. Recorded as the reason the Provost track's standing objection was actioned. The 2833 restyling amended that clause and every other regulation naming the rank; **the composition itself did not change.**
  - **No canon prose was altered, by design.** This is an *institution renaming its own rank on a date*, not the Archive correcting its own vocabulary — so both styles are correct, each for its period, and the restyling is dated **after every published chapter**. [`s05e02c03`](src/seasons/s05/e02/s05e02c03.md) is right as published: Shepherd's 2831 Field Triumvirate and the officer who leaves on the last shuttle both keep the older style, quoted as written. Same treatment the 2723 charter preamble gets under the Solar System Concord row.
  - **The two renames in this release need opposite machinery, and the migration map now says so explicitly.** `Dynarch → Mediarch` has **no** dating rule — no in-universe register ever used the word, so once retired it names nothing and migrates on sight. `Starwarden First Officer → Archwarden` **has** one, because the old style was correct until 2833. The rows sit next to each other in the [canonical glossary](src/lore/glossary/canonical-glossary-and-migration-guide.md) making opposite claims about the past, which is correct; each row points at the other so neither is applied with the wrong rule.
  - Recorded in [`star-rangers-command-hierarchy.md`](src/lore/star-rangers-command-hierarchy.md) (ladder bullet, restyling note, Field Triumvirate clause and wording note) and the canonical glossary (new `Archwarden` term entry with its dating rule, plus a migration row). Character pages carry the `Canonical Term (formerly Legacy Term)` first-mention form per the guide's own deprecation policy: [`tissadelle-shepherd.md`](src/characters/tissadelle-shepherd.md)'s Season 4 progression and [`karla-wender.md`](src/characters/karla-wender.md)'s open progression both name the rank currently while flagging the style she held it under. `archwarden` is added to the hierarchy page's tags alongside the retained `starwarden-first-officer`.

### Added

- **Journal: [A Name You Have to Argue With](src/journal/a-name-you-have-to-argue-with.md)** — the craft entry for both renames above, and the one observation that connects two changes from opposite ends of the setting: **each entry carried a paragraph whose whole job was explaining what its own name did not mean.** The rank's bullet flagged itself in its opening clause; the cosmology entry's gap was subtler because the explanation was doing real work. The rule it ends on is that a well-argued defence of a bad name is a decent piece of writing and a small permanent tax on every reader who arrives after it.
  - Covers what the changelog entries cannot: that the cosmology rename was **the name lagging a settlement already made** (the proxy-Telearch finding relocated the tier three days before the word caught up), that the devotional register had the better name the whole time, and that the two renames turned out to need **opposite migration machinery** — the point nearly blundered past, since applying the Archive-correction rule to a dated institutional restyling would have "corrected" a published chapter that was never wrong.
  - Also records the engine half briefly, which is journal-appropriate rather than lore: why a moved URL is a broken link on four production domains, and why `check-related-terms.js` is the check that matters after a rename — `related:` resolves by page title and a miss falls back to the glossary index instead of failing, so a stale term sends readers somewhere plausible and wrong rather than breaking the build.
- **Title card for [The Reading Before a First Vigil](src/codex/the-reading-before-a-first-vigil.md)** — the one codex entry shipped without one, closing the loop opened when it merged. Same designed template as the rest of `src/images/codex/`: `DOCTRINAL RECORD` category line, `rules` motif, a tilted `DEVOTIONAL` stamp, and *Fellowship of Light · Contemplative Chapters* under the title.
  - **Rendered from a faithful port of `make-codex-cover.ps1`, not by an image generator** — same 1600×1600 canvas, same gradient stack and alphas, same coordinates, same tracking rules, same auto-fit title (landed at 106px). The `.ps1` is GDI+ and Windows-only, so it cannot run in a Linux session; the port reproduces its geometry exactly and the text is still font-rendered, which is the property that matters — the template exists precisely because generators cannot spell.
  - **One deliberate deviation, worth knowing before regenerating:** Georgia and Consolas are Windows fonts and are not available here. Georgia was substituted with **Gelasio**, which is metric-compatible, so the auto-fit title geometry lands where Georgia's would; Consolas was substituted with **DejaVu Sans Mono**, for which no metric clone exists, so the small tracked lines differ very slightly in width. Re-running the `.ps1` on Windows will produce a near-identical card with the true faces.

### Fixed

- **`package-lock.json`'s version had drifted to `1.8.0`.** The 1.9.0 release bumped `package.json` and the README's "Current version" line but not the lockfile, whose two `version` fields sit outside the README's release checklist and so were never part of the step that "gets missed" — they were never part of any step. Both now read `1.10.0`, bumped with `npm version --no-git-tag-version` rather than edited by hand so the two files cannot disagree, and **the checklist's first step now names the lockfile** so this does not silently recur. Found while cutting this release, which is the only moment anyone ever looks.

## [1.9.0] - 2026-07-29

The Dock Seven release. The event every Season 6–7 chapter reaches backwards for had no chapter and no POV of its own — `narrative-gaps-checklist.md` had it as the one genuinely unwritten item in the whole Tissadelle arc — and it has both now, in **Season 5** rather than at the S5/S6 seam, appended with no renumbering.

Its spine is that **the event is written once and then refracted through every institution that had to account for it**, none of which can see all of it: a claims adjuster who can write *dragons* in the box marked Proximate Cause because settling a bill requires no cosmology, an Institute paper whose section 4 prints the four observations that undo its own section 3, a lawful commercial concern that was never charged with anything, a comparative cross-reference withdrawn before submission, and a eulogy that declines to concede the death it is held to mark. The Corps' reputation ends up resting on a generous, secular, entirely wrong account of why its people survived — while the competence itself is real and on the page four hours earlier.

The other half of the release is **expand, don't replace**, made explicit: `canon_facts` were added to four published S6–7 chapters and **not one word of prose was altered**, so the six chapters stay canon exactly as written and now carry the *why* that was never written under them. Three deliberate non-changes are recorded as decisions rather than left to look like oversights, so a later pass doesn't "fix" them.

`MINOR` per the changelog's own rule: the release is additive surface area — one chapter, four codex entries, two lore entries, and front-matter insertions. Nothing was removed, renamed or moved, so nothing 404s and no `deploy.conf` key, theme or build output changed.

**Tagging gap closed.** `v1.7.0` and `v1.8.0` were cut from a local clone at their release commits (`3577221` and `9f69f24`) and pushed, clearing a backlog both of those release notes had recorded as pending; `v1.9.0` was cut at this release's own merge commit, which is why it could not go up with them. The "not yet tagged" notes under `[1.7.0]` and `[1.8.0]` are superseded, and are **left in place deliberately** as the record of why those two were late rather than edited away. The GitHub-automation path used for most changes here still cannot publish `refs/tags/*` — tagging remains a local step, and the backlog is what happens when no local clone is in the loop.

### Added

- **Chapter: [S05E02C03, "What Came Off the Ship"](src/seasons/s05/e02/s05e02c03.md)** — **the Last Stand, written.** `narrative-gaps-checklist.md` had it as the one genuinely unwritten item in the whole Tissadelle arc: every S6–7 chapter reaches it backwards as "Dock Seven", and the event had no chapter and no POV of its own. It has one now, in **Season 5** rather than "end of S5 / opening of S6" — 2831 Mid-Autumn, nineteen days before `s06e01c02`, appended to the existing episode with **no renumbering** and a freshly generated `comment_id`.
  - **What it commits the story to.** The sixteen-year chronometer discrepancy marked a real narrowed Interval, and a licensed commercial concern — the Hyperfold Yield Combine — located it and worked it industrially, holding a fold aperture open four months past its transit to take Class III boundary fauna for fold-transit stabiliser. **Industrial unauthorised folding is what tore the boundary**, not anything gestating in the dock. Shepherd convenes a **Field Triumvirate** by the clause in `star-rangers-command-hierarchy.md` and in the open, evacuates eleven crew in forty-one minutes by shuttle and chartered Farline courier, and stays with the *Sufficient Cause*.
  - **The strike is a Celestial enforcement action under Telearch delegation**, which `src/glossary/celestials.md` already covered verbatim (unauthorised Higher-Dimensional Folding breaching a Concordant boundary). Levrils are present only in canon-permitted roles — detection, containment, perimeter isolation, the `threnos-omega.md` precedent — and **at no point reach in**, which preserves the tier constraint stated as binding `canon_facts` in three published chapters and carrying the S7 climax. Every witness records **dragons**; nothing corrects the impression, and no Ranger present is told anything at all.
  - **The Rangers are not spared, they are not included.** Enforcement scopes to the unlawful process, so everything outside it is untouched without any finding about anyone's conduct. **The fauna are still filed Class III afterward** — "predatory, entropic, or ecologically disruptive", no Cascade standing, no protection — and the classification is not revised. Shepherd dies defending things the Archive calls a hazard, and nobody in the text says so.
  - **Five POVs — Shepherd, Syra, Wender, Rook-7, Tobble — and none of them can name what they saw.** Tobble's is the last, and is the first canon appearance of a Tobble viewpoint: not load-bearing at the moment of compression, and therefore the member left with structure to spend. Pronouns they/them, still unset.
  - Ends on the grey-then-gold morning that opens `s06e01c01`, so the two chapters meet at the seam without either changing.
- **Codex: ["Statement of Proximate Cause — Dock Seven"](src/codex/dock-seven-loss-adjustment.md)** — a Farline Courier Guild loss adjustment, and the only contemporaneous account of the action by somebody with no stake in the Corps' version. A commercial claims officer has no standing to adjudicate Cascade questions and no interest in acquiring any, which is exactly why the entry can write *dragons* in the box marked Proximate Cause and settle a bill around it. Carries **no `canon_facts`**, per the codex rule. Its live disagreement — two vessel masters hold they were let go; the third holds they were never taken up, and that being spared and being no part of the thing are different — is the decision above, argued by people who cannot settle it.

- **Lore: [The Institute](src/lore/the-institute.md)** — the secular, sceptical counterweight to devotional readings of boundary phenomena, and the source of the Dock Seven account most of settled space actually believes. **Not atheist, and deliberately not a strawman:** its published position is that no claim about meaning, intention or moral order has ever survived an instrument, and it *declines* the Cascade rather than denying it. Its house rule — **it publishes what it failed to find**, at the same length as the finding — is why the Survey Corps cites papers whose philosophy it rejects.
  - **Its reading of Dock Seven is correct about the mechanism.** Instability from overused, miscalibrated fold equipment held against an already-anomalous boundary is exactly what tore that boundary; the reported dragons are read as structured discharge along a strain gradient, seen through a viewport with no instrumentation. What the Institute does is take a correct account of a *cause* for a complete account of an *event* — which it states up front that it will always do.
  - **On dragons it says the Rangers are not lying, they are quoting** — dragon-talk in the Corps read as inherited devotional vocabulary carrying no observational content, since the Fellowship had the imagery first, the memorial repertoire was inherited rather than commissioned, and even *warden* was picked up from older guardianship traditions. What it grants is large: read as metaphor the tradition is very nearly exact, and the Institute teaches it in its own fold-transit safety courses, because a crew taught to imagine something enormous and patient behind a held aperture treats it with exactly the caution the physics warrants, faster than a crew taught the tensors. Filed as **superstition in form and wisdom in content**. Strong on the inheritance, which is documented; weak in the next step, treating an inherited word as evidence its referent is unreal.
  - **It attributes the Rangers' survival to superior protocols and practical boundary knowledge.** Careful, generous, entirely secular, and wrong: they were outside a perimeter drawn around a process rather than a party. **This is the account that established the Corps' reputation**, so that reputation rests on a version of their competence the instrument record does not support — while the competence itself is real and on the page four hours earlier.
- **[`star-rangers-safety-corps.md`](src/lore/star-rangers-safety-corps.md): "The Voluntary Standard"** — the Star Rangers are the **de facto regulator of boundary-proximate and fold-adjacent operations across settled space, and the regulation is entirely voluntary.** The entry had described only internal scope; everything it listed binds Rangers and, outside the Corps, binds nobody. **Local governments and corporations remain fully autonomous** — a world governs itself, a licensed concern answers to whoever issued the licence, and the Corps cannot fine, suspend, board, compel a filing or revoke anything.
  - **The mechanism was already in the file and had never been drawn out:** Underwriters Laboratories held no legal power over any manufacturer in 1894 either. It had independence and a method, insurers wanted evidence rather than assurances, and the market did the rest. Neutrality and self-funding are what make it work — a standards body with a commercial interest is a competitor with a rulebook.
  - **The Corps declines the word *regulator*, doctrinally rather than modestly**: accepting the title means accepting an authority the charter forbids, and it forbids it because the outer-station delegations of 2723 would not vote for a boundary body with compulsory power, having concluded it would be the MSC under better branding.
  - **What it costs was paid in 2831.** A voluntary standard is one the single operator who most needs it can decline, and the Combine declined it. Not an oversight in the design — the design, with the argument for it fully aired at founding. The Safety Corps has not proposed amending the charter, and its president's published reason runs to one sentence: *a corps that acquires the power to prevent this acquires, in the same motion, the power to permit it.*
- **Lore: [The Hyperfold Yield Combine](src/lore/hyperfold-yield-combine.md)** — the concern that worked the boundary, written so the uncomfortable thing about it is that **it was not a criminal enterprise**. Licence, counsel's opinion, audited product, a market that wanted more than it could supply, and every part of it lawful up to the moment it was destroyed.
  - **The loop is the point:** stabiliser makes apertures cheaper to hold, cheaper apertures make more boundary reachable, more boundary means more feedstock. Its own filings project the curve out four decades without remarking on it. Every part of the cycle closed except the aperture, which was the only thing in it supposed to.
  - **Three things made it untouchable, none of them a loophole** — the fauna have no Cascade standing so any argument on their behalf fails at the first line; the permit was silent on collapse and counsel's reading of that silence was *correct*; and **the only body competent to judge it had no power over it**, since it held no Safety Corps certification, was under no obligation to, and could not have been made to. What remained was a formal finding, which required a named officer to put her judgement on a second-guessable record, against a concern in good standing, on behalf of animals with none. For four months every authority had a reason not to look, and every reason was a good one.
  - **Two things left open, and neither is the expected one.** No insurer has corresponded at any address since — the ownership chain terminates in instruments that are lawful, opaque, and under no obligation, and since the destruction was not a crime anyone was charged with, no authority has had cause to compel an answer. And **the product shipped**: four months of industrial rendering, all of it sold, with where it went unestablished because a loss event generates no discovery. The licence framework was never amended, because the officer preparing the finding did not come back.
- **Codex: [A Material Account of the Dock Seven Event](src/codex/dock-seven-material-account.md)** — the Institute paper itself. Its **section 4 prints, unhedged, the four observations that undo its own section 3**, including that the losses sorted by *registry*, which no strain model can make a physical property. The strongest argument against the Institute is published by the Institute, which is the point.
- **Codex: [Shepherd Among the Comparanda](src/codex/shepherd-among-the-comparanda.md)** — the Arilon cross-reference, prepared and **withdrawn before submission**. Part One establishes the match on all five elements of the pattern and says outright it is the strongest comparandum this desk has ever assembled; Part Two is three people declining to send it, for three different reasons, recorded as a disagreement rather than smoothed into one voice.
  - **Cael:** element four is not satisfied, it is *assumed*. The pattern needs the namer absent when the record catches up — and a signal is still iterating at the failure point. So indexing the cross-reference would not record a match, it would **complete** one, handing the Council the finding Wender has refused for two years to sign, by a route the Council never had to take.
  - **Wyn:** the filing consoles, and that is the whole objection. A shape that fits perfectly, arrives as comfort, and cannot be checked is precisely what `s07e01c02` warns about — it would do in a comparative index what the citation does on a wall.
  - **Sen:** the comparative archive takes submissions from *named* correspondents, so the one correction this desk cannot make quietly is this one. Declines, and refuses to let a better reason stand in for the true one: not yet willing to pay what signing costs. **This is the story bible's "chose not to annotate" failure mode written as its own document** — and it is retained rather than destroyed, deliberately, because an absence in an archive is indistinguishable from a thought nobody had.
  - Marginalia gets the last word, and notices what the others didn't: the name is already at the top of the page.
- **Codex: [Address at the Official Funeral of Line Captain T. Shepherd](src/codex/wender-funeral-address.md)** — 2832 Mid-Autumn, eleven months after Dock Seven, just before `s07e01c01`. **Wender gives the eulogy having never signed the confirmed-loss citation, and says so from the podium.** The document grieves without once conceding the death it is held to mark, and refuses both consolations in the same breath — she will not say Shepherd is dead and will not say she is out there, having a finding for neither. Then holds both unresolved, and notes who taught her how. The ceremonial record omits the second half; three newsnets printed it whole, and it is the second half that gets quoted.

### Changed

- **Tobble uses he/him** (settled 2026-07-29), swept the same day across [`tissadelle-shepherd.md`](src/characters/tissadelle-shepherd.md) — which now states it outright, since being mis-recorded is his entire institutional situation — [`plural-minds.md`](src/glossary/plural-minds.md), `s05e02c03`, and the three story-bible notes that recorded the pronouns as unset. The they/them used before that date is **superseded, not an alternative**.
- **[`cosmic-cascade.md`](src/lore/cosmic-cascade.md): a "Who Accepts This Model" section** — the entry had stated the framework for its whole life without ever saying how widely it is held, which let it read as consensus. It is not: sceptical, contemplative and devotional traditions each decline or reorder it, and most people hold no position at all. Two consequences recorded — a cosmology with no virtue, reward or punishment **has nothing to console anybody with**, which limits its spread independently of whether it is right; and the existing Partial Observation rule cuts both ways, so disagreement here is not error to be corrected. A statement about *reception*, not about truth, so the canon/record split holds and lore stays internally consistent.
- **[`ballad-of-the-stars.md`](src/codex/ballad-of-the-stars.md): the second reading, filed 2832** — **and no retcon was required**, because the entry already had Tissadelle on vocals *pre-enlistment*. The surviving members of Slipwave reissue the recording with a reading attached: *she went to the stars* first meant she left the band for the Rangers, and now means both, **and they decline to choose**. They are equally explicit that the song foresaw nothing. Sen's second note draws the distinction that keeps this clear of the closure-prevention the later `baby-universe-ballad` is flagged for: a record with two entries in it is precise, not vague.
- **[`fellowship-of-light.md`](src/lore/fellowship-of-light.md): Dock Seven settled the neutral-broker argument** — rivals had put the case against Ranger neutrality and boundary competence on the record first, and the record went on to answer it. The sharpest detail is that **the Farline Guild's own claims file undercuts the Guild's own argument**: a vessel master came when a Ranger asked and negotiated the rate afterward, and the adjuster wrote it down against interest.
- **Three more `canon_facts` on [`s07e01c03`](src/seasons/s07/e01/s07e01c03.md)**, where the contested-record theme already lives: the Institute's material account is settled space's majority version; the Corps' reputation rests on an unsupported account of why its people survived; and the Cascade is not majority opinion. Prose untouched, as with the rest.
- **`canon_facts` added to four published S6–7 chapters; not one word of prose altered.** This is the expand-not-replace decision made explicit: the six chapters stay canon exactly as written and now carry the *why* that was never written under them. `git diff` on `src/seasons/s06` and `src/seasons/s07` shows front-matter insertions only, and no deletions.
  - [`s06e01c02`](src/seasons/s06/e01/s06e01c02.md) — the drift marked a real narrowed Interval that a commercial concern worked for four months before Survey Corps classification caught up; and **the closure also ended an unauthorised operation nobody had managed to stop**, which the confirmed-loss report buries along with everything else. That second fact makes the Oversight Council's hurry to close the file considerably more motivated, and more damning, without altering a line Wender says.
  - [`s06e01c01`](src/seasons/s06/e01/s06e01c01.md) — **the largest reframing in the set, done entirely in front matter.** What persisted did so on a substrate, the lost vessel's own archival stores; the Boirinn Uplands interior was **preserved by Tobble rather than generated by the stall, and only partly preserved.** The clearing stops being a floating dream and becomes a located thing.
  - [`s07e01c01`](src/seasons/s07/e01/s07e01c01.md) — the surviving witness record says dragons, nothing corrects it, and no Ranger authority ever established what standing the entities held: the same question the Union's scholars left open over Aoife's thorn well. Deliberately does **not** assert the Celestial basis here, so this chapter's in-universe contestedness survives intact.
  - [`s07e01c03`](src/seasons/s07/e01/s07e01c03.md) — a levril's inability to reach into a stalled seed is a **tier constraint, not a local circumstance**; what differs between Dock Seven and the warm edge is what was permitted, never what was possible.
- **[`celestials.md`](src/glossary/celestials.md): enforcement scope attaches to the process, not the persons** — bystanders are spared *structurally*, never assessed and found worthy, because a Celestial no more adjudicates worth than a Levril does. Makes explicit at the tier that actually acts what `levrils.md` already said as "enforcement tiers are structural, not moral". Closes with the observation that Material-layer witnesses routinely read the distinction backwards and nothing has ever been obliged to correct them.
- **[`metafold.md`](src/glossary/metafold.md): *hyperfold* recorded as commercial branding** — the same error sold rather than mis-reported, in an entry already categorised as a Misconception. The distinction kept is the useful one: the journalist writing *metafold* is guessing in good faith, while a concern that puts *hyperfold* on a hull has chosen a word that cannot be held to a meaning, and chose it on advice.
- **Recorded as decisions rather than left to look like oversights** — three deliberate non-changes, so a later pass doesn't "fix" them:

The **Register rule** in `canonical-glossary-and-migration-guide.md` already licenses exactly this — chapters and characters are voices, lore and glossary are the Archive — so there is **no new canonical term, no migration-map row, and no corpus sweep**.

It also flags a precision trap for future sessions — the levril constraint is on *initiating this enforcement* and on *completing another mind's process*, **not** a blanket "levrils never act unbidden", which would contradict three published chapters. `narrative-gaps-checklist.md` ticks the Last Stand and answers the question that entry itself posed; `story-bible-summary.md`'s season spine is corrected to put the event in S5.

## [1.8.0] - 2026-07-28

A cosmology-and-canon release, and the largest single sweep of Cascade terminology the project has done. Its spine is one recurring defect rather than a theme: **each of the 2026-07-26 Cascade settlements had been recorded where it was decided and never carried to the term on the other side of it.** Four instances turned up, and chasing them exposed two questions the corpus had been implying without answering — what crosses the Interval, and why physical law is reliable at all.

Also here: the Solar System Concordant becomes the **Solar System Concord**, retiring the last collision on that word; a new Season 1 chapter; and the first codex entry written to read a settled mechanism devotionally without contradicting it.

**Not yet tagged**, and neither is its predecessor — see the note under `[1.7.0]`. **`v1.7.0` and `v1.8.0` both need cutting from a local clone**, at each release's merge commit; the automation path used here cannot publish `refs/tags/*`.

### Added

- **Character: Sorcha** (`src/characters/sorcha.md`) — an itinerant, institutionally unaffiliated healer who works boundary-proximate settlements, carrying ordinary medicine in one half of her satchel and chalk, thread and a notebook in the other. **Constraint-literate in the same self-taught tradition as [Elvira](src/characters/elvira.md), with one difference: Elvira reads Etheric structure expressed through a *place*, Sorcha reads it as expressed through a *person*.** Three canon decisions worth recording: **(1)** she explicitly does **not** heal "the spirit" — Layer 1 is an origin condition without agency or intervention semantics, so nothing there can be treated; her work sits at the Conceptual and Etheric layers, and the page says so while allowing that the people she treats call it whatever they like (the register rule, applied). **(2)** Her reason for going toward pain is mechanical rather than sentimental: unresolved grief is a *feeding condition* for [Threnes and Gilded Saints](src/lore/meta-dimensional-beings.md), whose whole method is closure-prevention — so a closure practitioner is in direct functional opposition to a class of meta-dimensional predator. She does not know this, has no Survey Corps record, and needs neither to work. **(3)** No origin, training, homeworld or season placement is asserted; those are left open rather than invented. Portrait added at `src/images/characters/sorcha.jpg`.
- **Sorcha's weakness: central fatigue** — and the term is canon rather than a coinage. [Teleportation Constraints](src/lore/teleportation-limitations.md) already documents it as a consequence of repeated jump exposure, [Dr. Iona Vale](src/characters/dr-iona-vale.md) gates jumps on it (*"if the crew member shows unresolved central fatigue markers, the jump does not happen"*), and two Season 1 `canon_facts` establish that repeated exposure raises the markers and that Threshold Station adopted **mandatory screening** for them. Sorcha runs the same measurable deficit from a different cause — sustained constraint-literate perception of distressed people, with no off switch, because caring is not incidental to her method but the instrument itself. The sharp end is institutional rather than sentimental: **the protocol Iona Vale fought a room to establish covers Rangers, and Sorcha is not one** — the measure, thresholds and mandatory intake all exist, and the one practitioner whose whole method is a sustained draw on that reserve sits outside every one of them. Recorded as an open thread rather than a plot: her practice starves predators that feed on prevented closure, *and* spends down a reserve rest doesn't replace, so her most depleted hours are the ones she earns by working. Whether anything has ever waited for that is explicitly not established.

- **Chapter: [S01E03C04, "The One He Did Not Name"](src/seasons/s01/e03/s01e03c04.md)** — the morning after the grove. **Galahad Thorne met Elvira at Dún Rí in 2806 UCSD, sixteen years before any other record places her there, and she has not changed since.** He says nothing. He tests her instead, feeding her own private vocabulary back to her without attribution and watching whether she receives it as *familiar* or as *impressive*.
  - **It reaches back into an already-published line rather than adding one.** At their first causeway meeting (E02C01) Galahad says *"the layer underneath — the pattern substrate,"* and Elvira's look is written as *"Where did you learn that language"*; the next line is *"He chose not to answer the implied question."* That phrase is now hers, given to him in 2806 — so the moment she revised her model of him upward, she was being impressed by her own words. Not one word of E02C01 changed.
  - **Built to resolve nothing.** His memory is the only source: no image, instrument reading or third-party record corroborates it, he enters none of it in the survey file and states no reason, and whether Elvira remembers is explicitly not established. It is the first hard data point on the standing "What is Elvira?" thread and it deliberately stays a sample size of one.
  - **Answers E03C03's closing note without answering it.** Elvira ends that chapter writing *"That should have been harder. Find out why it wasn't."* Galahad has a reason, and it is unfalsifiable, unfileable and his alone.
  - **Inverts the season's own mechanic.** Season 1 turns on naming a thing correctly (E03C02, "The Right Question"); this closes it on a name deliberately withheld. Aldera sees the whole test, reconstructs the method, and files it unspoken under the same volunteered-information protocol that made her useful two chapters earlier — noting only, and without recommendation, that the last time everyone in the sector waited to be asked it cost three years.

- **Glossary entry: [Council of Harmonarchs](src/glossary/council-of-harmonarchs.md)** — the composition the 2026-07-26 settlement made load-bearing had no reader-facing page. Worldwright, Telearch, Dynarch, Celestials, High Celestials, Concordant Principal and Universal Authority all had one; the Council, which is *what a Universal Authority is made of*, existed only inside the canonical glossary and other entries. The tell was `universal-authority.md`, which linked **Consensus Field** to the whole canonical-glossary page with no anchor, because there was nowhere else to send a reader.
  - Covers the four things that only lived in the reference doc: the Council is **not a Cascade tier** (the same minds in their second seat, which is why it appears nowhere in the spine); the **Council is not the Authority** (Authority = Council + presiding seat, and neither half is an Authority alone); decisions come through a **Consensus Field** rather than a vote count; and **two seats** — a Principal's writ ends at its zone, the Council's is universe-wide, and a Harmonarch outvoted in council is bound at home regardless. Keeps the canonical glossary's own comparison to the Star Rangers' **Council of High Captains** (`star-rangers-command-hierarchy.md`), noting the resemblance is structural rather than borrowed.
  - Cross-linked from `universal-authority.md` and `concordant-principal.md`; the canonical glossary's Council entry now points at it. **Lead Harmonarch** and **Founder** are covered inside it rather than given pages of their own — both are seats rather than tiers.

- **Redirect at the old Concordant URL** — `/lore/solar-system-concordant/` now points at `/lore/solar-system-concord/` by two mechanisms, because no single one covers every host this repo deploys to. A **`Redirect 301`** in [`src/static/.htaccess`](src/static/.htaccess) serves the cPanel production domains; mod_alias resolves it before the filesystem lookup, so it wins wherever Apache is in front. A **meta-refresh stub** at [`src/lore/solar-system-concordant.njk`](src/lore/solar-system-concordant.njk) covers GitHub Pages and anything else that ignores `.htaccess`, and carries `rel="canonical"` plus `noindex, follow`.
  - The stub is a `.njk` rather than a `.md` on purpose, and that decides three things at once: `validate-content.js` scans only Markdown, so it isn't schema-checked as a lore entry; the `lore` collection filters on `layout === "lore-entry.njk"`, so it never appears in a listing; and it carries `eleventyExcludeFromCollections: true`, which keeps it out of `sitemap.njk`'s `collections.all` loop — a redirect has no business in a sitemap. It also has no `data-pagefind-body`, so Pagefind skips it (401 of 405 built pages indexed).
  - The stub's links are written with the ordinary hardcoded `/star-rangers/` prefix rather than being special-cased, so both prefix mechanisms handle it unchanged: GitHub Pages serves it as written, and `cpanel-deploy.sh`'s `sed` step rewrites it to `/lore/solar-system-concord/` along with every other page.

### Changed

- **Codex: [The Reading Before a First Vigil](src/codex/the-reading-before-a-first-vigil.md)** — the devotional half of the law's grounding, filed where a devotional reading belongs. A Fellowship of Light address read aloud to a novice on the night of their first watch at a thin place, answering the question every novice has and none asks: whether it will hold. Its answer is that it holds because **the Exarchs keep faith** — the same invariance `dynarch.md` grounds in design, read as fidelity.
  - **Written so it cannot contradict the lore, because it declines to try.** The reading names the surveyors' account outright — that an Exarch is *made* so, that nothing is being chosen and therefore nothing is being kept — instructs the novice not to argue with it, and answers only: *a thing made faithful is faithful.* Same fact, different reading, no competing claim. That is the lore/codex boundary working rather than being managed.
  - **In the Fellowship's own register**, which the corpus already established: **Exarch** for Dynarch (recorded as "the older form still preferred in devotional and provincial records") and **Overfold** for boundary-zone Etheric phenomena. It engages with none of the mechanism — no bands, no Interval, no Telearch line — which is authentic to a contemplative order rather than an omission.
  - **Author is `Traditional — no chapter claims first authorship`**, following the precedent of [Hymn of the Thin Places](src/codex/hymn-of-the-thin-places.md); the Fellowship's cross-chapter oral tradition is itself the stance, and no new named figure or chapter house was invented to carry it. Deliberately **not** attributed to the Communion of the Called, which is a `church-space`-tagged page — an entry authored from there would inherit the overlay's privacy and be hidden on every public domain.
  - No `canon_facts`, per the codex rule. **Title card still to do** — `make-codex-cover.ps1` is Windows-only, so the entry ships imageless for now, which several existing codex entries already do.

- **Why physical law is predictable: Dynarchs are stable by design** (settled 2026-07-28) — answering a question the corpus had already half-asked. `physics-comparison.md` has said for some time that "causal structure is **maintained** rather than merely emergent," which implies a maintainer and never named one. It names the Dynarchs now, and grounds the reliability in **design rather than in conduct**: the Worldwright designs the rule-sets *and* the office that keeps them, invariance included. A Dynarch is built to be invariant in the same sense a constant is.
  - **The proxy structure leaves no room for it to be otherwise.** Continuity is what a Dynarch substantially *is*, so there is no separate faculty of reliability that could fail on its own while the rest of the office carried on. **Drift is not forbidden to a Dynarch; it is undefined for one.** That is what keeps the claim from making physics contingent on anybody's will.
  - **The measurable consequence is no measurable consequence, and that is the design working.** Physics inside a universe is indistinguishable from physics in a universe with no Dynarchs at all: constants measure as constant, experiments repeat, nothing in a laboratory result points upward and nothing needs to. The maintained case and the merely-emergent case are experimentally identical, which is why the distinction is cosmological rather than experimental.
  - **Boundary anomalies are not counterexamples**, and the corpus already had the sentence for it: boundary zones produce *lawful disagreement, not law failure*. Threshold's forty-second discrepancy has stood unexplained for eleven years without once implying a force did anything other than what it does.
  - Written into [`dynarch.md`](src/glossary/dynarch.md) and [`physics-comparison.md`](src/lore/physics-comparison.md). **A devotional reading of the same invariance — as character and integrity rather than design — is deliberately not filed here**, per the lore/codex boundary: it is a named source's account, and it awaits its source.

- **What crosses the Interval, generalized — and why it is Telearch business** (settled 2026-07-28). Gravity's reach across a narrowed Interval was inferable from three separate pages and stated on none. It is now one rule rather than three exceptions: **a thing crosses the Interval exactly to the extent that a band of the Common Manifold carries it.** The manifold has three bands and each carries one thing — **12–15** geometric strain (**gravity**: Membrane Shadows, transient gravity tunnels), **16–19** causal timing (timebase disagreement), **20+** Etheric archetypal templates (Resonance, Intermembrane Bleed). Everything else is membrane-confined: matter, ships, beings, and the other force-domains — **electromagnetics and Nature have no band and therefore no far-side reach**. This is why "nothing crosses the gap" and "the far side's mass is measurable here" are both true of the same event.
  - **Gravity is not a special case; it is the visible one.** Gravity is geometry and the 12–15 band is the geometric one, so gravity is the single force whose nature matches what the between is made of. Neither "emergent per membrane" (which the Membrane Shadow forbids) nor "purely higher-dimensional" (which ignores its ordinary local behaviour — Lagrange points, high-gravity worlds, ascent javelins).
  - **The governance has the same shape as the physics, and not by coincidence.** Every force-domain divides into a **local** aspect, governed by the zone's Concordant Principal, and a **continuity** aspect that runs up the Telearch line — because continuity across membranes is a trans-membrane fact and the Telearch branch, native to no universe, is the only tier that is itself trans-membrane.
