The 20+ band already encodes "the nonlocal boundary conditions that Worldwright and Telearch operations must satisfy," so the continuity branch was already documented as operating where the between is. **A Dynarch's dual obligation is that division restated from the physics side**, and it is why continuity prevails on conflict: the local aspect is the one that stops at the edge.
  - Written into [`concordant-membranes.md`](src/lore/concordant-membranes.md) (new section, *What Crosses the Interval, and Why*), with the rule cross-stated in [`post-eleven-dimensional-manifold.md`](src/lore/post-eleven-dimensional-manifold.md), [`dynarch.md`](src/glossary/dynarch.md), [`telearch.md`](src/glossary/telearch.md) and the canonical glossary's Dynarchs entry.

- **Noögenic descent is an axis, not a category** (settled 2026-07-28) — closing a gap the taxonomy had carried silently. **Primary / secondary / derived classifies a universe by how it was *made*; noögenic descent describes who it came *from*.** A seeded universe is neither primary (no Worldwright) nor derived (it does not arise from the interaction of primaries), and it is not a fourth entry on that list, because it is not answering that list's question. Previously it was defined only negatively, by the one line saying it receives no Worldwright.
  - **Both ends of the relation are free.** A parent universe may itself be **primary, secondary, or derived** — seeding requires a mind capable of it, not a pedigree — and a matured noögenic universe's own standing is not set by its parent's.
  - **Maturity is the entire difference from *derived*.** A derived universe is permanently subordinate: its physics stays a function of its source primaries' constraints and it never stops running on inherited authority. A protouniverse is subordinate only *while unfinished*, and parent Telearch jurisdiction ends the moment it stabilizes a Universal Authority of its own. **What it becomes is the adult child of its parent** — grown, independent, answerable in nothing, with its own Council, its own founder presiding, its own continuity to keep. The kinship is permanent and carries no authority; the authority was temporary and is finished. *Proto* is a stage, not a class: it never acquires a Worldwright and never needed one, because what it was owed was a start, not an author.
  - Recorded in [`universe-overlap-and-folding.md`](src/lore/universe-overlap-and-folding.md), [`noogenic-protouniverse.md`](src/glossary/noogenic-protouniverse.md) and a new canonical-terms entry. Two pieces of superseded phrasing went with it: the protouniverse entry's "generate its own governing intelligences" (the mind-for-body error, same as above) and its "Concordant-equivalent authority", which the migration map had already retired in favour of *independent Universal Authority*.

- **A Universal Authority is a governance *body*, not a governance *intelligence*** — wording only; the 2026-07-26 composition is unchanged. That settlement made the Authority "a **body**, not a separate mind installed above the zones," and never reached the definition sentence four lines above it, which still opened *"the native governance **intelligence** of a universe as a whole."* `universal-authority.md` then closed by saying the term "names the universe-level governing **mind**" — the same page denying it is a mind and asserting it is one.
  - **This was not a judgement call:** the canonical glossary already carries a migration row retiring *"'Universal Authority' as a singular mind above the Principals"* in favour of *"the Council of Harmonarchs plus its presiding seat."* The term's own definition was on the wrong side of its own migration rule.
  - Corrected in [`universal-authority.md`](src/glossary/universal-authority.md) (short, lead, legacy note), [`who-governs-a-universe.md`](src/lore/who-governs-a-universe.md), the [canonical glossary](src/lore/glossary/canonical-glossary-and-migration-guide.md)'s Role Clarification and Definition, and the migration row that repeated "governance intelligences". `concordant.md`'s legacy note now says "governance office" rather than "governance minds."
  - **Keeps the asymmetry visible, because it is the point:** a Concordant Principal *is* a mind; the Authority those minds constitute is not a larger mind but a council. Both revised pages now say so in as many words.

- **The Telearch↔Dynarch relationship is recorded from the Telearch side too** — the 2026-07-26 settlement ("a Dynarch is a proxy Telearch") landed on the Dynarch page and in `who-governs-a-universe.md`, and never crossed over. `telearch.md` still carried the *pre*-settlement framing — co-created, stands under both, continuity prevails — reproduced as three bare assertions on the page best placed to explain them, and never said a Dynarch **is** a proxy Telearch at all.
  - Sharpest form of the gap: `telearch.md` already documented how a Telearch reaches inside a universe *by Avatar* — the occasional, personal route — while omitting the Dynarch tier, the **standing, structural** one. New section, *How a Telearch Reaches Inside a Universe*, gives both and says why there are two: a Telearch is native to no universe, and a force must be administered from within the thing it runs through.
  - The canonical glossary's **Telearchs** entry was two lines (a one-sentence definition and a protouniverse note) against a full `Nature (settled 2026-07-26)` block on the Dynarch side. It now records the continuity branch and Worldwright peerage, native-to-no-universe, and both routes inside.

- **"A membrane is a universe" tightened to "a membrane is universe-scale"** — phrasing only; the 2026-07-26 settlement is unchanged. That sentence stated an *identity* where it meant a *scale*, and sat awkwardly beside the definition two lines above it, which has a universe **occupying** its membrane. A thing cannot both be X and occupy X, and the corpus leans on the occupancy reading elsewhere — `membrane-shadows.md` has a mass staying "within **its own** membrane," which only parses if a membrane is an envelope. Corrected in [`concordant-membranes.md`](src/lore/concordant-membranes.md), the [canonical glossary](src/lore/glossary/canonical-glossary-and-migration-guide.md)'s scale rule, and the migration-map row that repeated it.
  - **Also records what the two words are actually for**, which is the question the wording invited: *universe* and *membrane* name the same object and differ in which way the sentence faces. **Universe** is the thing from inside — its contents and its governing authority. **Membrane** is that same object as the Common Manifold sees it: bounded, with neighbours and an Interval between. Inside-facing statements take the first, anything measured across takes the second, and that is why a Concordant Zone sits inside a *universe* while a bleed event happens between *membranes*.
  - No migration-map row, because nothing is renamed and no legacy usage becomes wrong. The `[1.7.0]` entry below keeps its original "A membrane is a universe, not a zone" heading — that is the record of what was settled that day, and released entries are not rewritten.

- **Concordant Zone gains two synonyms with declared registers** (settled 2026-07-28) — **coherent cosmic region**, the Survey Corps' plain-language gloss for first mention and cross-species records, exact and clumsy in prose; and **megaexpanse**, the popular word, recorded together with why it is imprecise: it names the *size* and drops the *internal consistency*, which is the whole content of the term. A megaexpanse is merely enormous. Neither replaces the canonical term, and the Archive's own voice keeps using it. Follows the existing Harmonarch/Exarch pattern, where a synonym earns its place by carrying a register rather than by being interchangeable. Recorded in [`glossary/concordant.md`](src/glossary/concordant.md) and the [canonical glossary](src/lore/glossary/canonical-glossary-and-migration-guide.md), with a migration row that applies **only** to Archive voice — both words stand in dialogue, popular sources, and first-mention glosses.

- **The Solar System Concordant is now the Solar System Concord** (settled 2026-07-28) — the last collision on the word *Concordant*, and the one the July sweep left standing. That sweep moved the governance sense to **Universal Authority** and left the compact holding a borrowed cosmological word, managed by a three-senses disambiguation in [`glossary/concordant.md`](src/glossary/concordant.md) and two sections of the entry itself. Managing an ambiguity in prose forever is what the canonical glossary exists to stop, so the name went instead. **`Concordant` now has exactly one live sense: the cosmological zone.**
  - **Done as an in-universe restyling, not a retcon.** The compact was founded in 2543 UCSD *as* the Solar System Concordant — the overreach was the point, a body of law with no enforcement mechanism naming itself after the largest structure in the sky — and was restyled **the Solar System Concord in 2790 UCSD**, keeping the root and giving the word back. Nothing about the institution changed: no clause, no commission, no signatory. The founding story survives intact, which is what the alternative (pretending it was always called Concord) would have cost. New section: *The Restyling of 2790*.
  - **The old name is now a date stamp rather than an error.** Pre-2790 documents carry it correctly and are quoted as written — the Star Rangers' 2723 charter preamble in [`formation-of-star-rangers.md`](src/lore/formation-of-star-rangers.md) still reads *"the limits of Solar System Concordant coherence"*, and is the one deliberate instance left in the corpus. Post-2790 usage is the tell of a document retyped from an older source without attention.
  - **Swept the corpus, not just the entry.** 24 files: the era (*the Concordant period* → **the Concord period**), the adjectival forms (*Concordant-wide*, *Concordant standards*, *Concordant baseline*, *Concordant-certified*, *Concordant personhood standards*), the civilizational sense (*"in the Concordant"*, *"the Concordant's engineers"*), and the in-universe institution names (**Concord Governance Archive**, the document header on two codex entries). Chapter prose needed no changes — every season-file use of the word is cosmological (*Concordant phase oscillation*), which is the result the rename was aiming at.
  - **Page moved** from `/lore/solar-system-concordant/` to [`/lore/solar-system-concord/`](src/lore/solar-system-concord.md). Since giscus maps non-chapter pages by pathname, any existing discussion thread on the old URL will not follow the page.
  - Canonical-terms entry and two migration-map rows added to the [canonical glossary](src/lore/glossary/canonical-glossary-and-migration-guide.md); the superseded ruling in `story-bible/canon-consistency-audit-2026-07.md` corrected in place rather than left to go stale.

### Fixed

- **Elvira's Dún Rí prequel was dated four years too early in two places** — `src/characters/elvira.md` said Season 1 Episode 0 covered Dún Rí *"roughly four years before her arrival at the outpost,"* and `s01e00c01.md`'s description said *"Years before Elvira ever reaches the Marsh Causeway."* E00 is Year -4, Late Autumn; she reaches the causeway Year -3, Early Spring — about **six months**. Someone read "Year -4" as "four years before the outpost" rather than four years before Year 0. Both now say what the timestamps say. Found while checking whether a twenty-year-old meeting fit her established chronology; it does, but not for the reason the character page implied.

- **Misdirected cross-link in [The Crisis Centuries](src/lore/crisis-centuries-terran-wildlife.md)** — the "now credited" link on *the standing authority* keeping Earth's unmanaged biomes healthy pointed at [The Celtic Union of Planets](src/lore/celtic-union-of-planets.md), which is not an Earth environmental authority and has explicitly declined SSDC jurisdiction. The authority in that clause is the **Solar System Defence Command**, so the link now goes to [Military Space Command](src/lore/military-space-command.md), the page documenting the MSC's narrowing into the SSDC and the established anchor for it elsewhere in the corpus. The link resolved and so passed both `npm test` and the internal-link checker — a stale *target* under valid link text, the same failure mode `check-related-terms.js` exists to catch on `related:` lists. The likely origin is the sentence's echo: the Celtic Union entry states the same "healthier than at any point since the early industrial era" claim, and the link appears to have attached to the echo rather than to the institution. The Celtic Union remains linked from the page's See-also list, where it belongs.

## [1.7.0] - 2026-07-26

A cosmology release. Four structural questions about the Cascade were settled in one sitting — what a Universal Authority is made of, what a Dynarch actually is, what scale a membrane is, and which of two mechanisms "boundary zone" names — and in three of the four the answer resolved a contradiction the corpus was already carrying rather than adding new ground.

**Not yet tagged.** `v1.7.0` needs cutting from a local clone at the merge commit for this release; the automation path used here cannot publish `refs/tags/*`.

### Changed

- **A membrane is a universe, not a zone** (settled 2026-07-26) — resolving a contradiction the corpus was already carrying. `concordant-membranes.md` said "each **Concordant** occupies its own bounded cosmic membrane", while `tir-tairngire.md` describes "a **primary universe** whose membrane sits close enough to Tír na nÓg's own Concordant" — comparing a universe's membrane to a zone's in one sentence. The scale is now fixed: **a membrane is a primary universe**, a Concordant Zone is a region *inside* one, and **a single Worldwright authors many primary membranes** (consistent with "Worldwrights create primary universe *sets*", already canonical).
  - **The structure nests, and that decides which effects can happen where.** The **Interval** exists only *between* membranes. Two zones inside one universe share an ordinary internal edge with no Interval across it — so an internal zone edge produces instrument drift, timebase mismatch and lawful disagreement, but **never** Intermembrane Bleed, a Membrane Shadow, or a transient gravity tunnel, however sharply the two rule-sets differ. All Boundary-State Class grading belongs to the inter-membrane case.
  - **"Boundary zone" now covers two mechanisms** and is qualified where the difference is load-bearing: *intra-universe* (an internal edge) versus *inter-membrane* (a narrowing Interval between whole universes). Both `boundary-zones.md` and `boundary-zone.md` say so directly, since the unqualified term previously implied one phenomenon.
  - **Threshold Station is on an inter-universe boundary.** Its Dock Seven record includes a bleed signature, which under the nested model is only available between membranes — so Threshold stands at an Interval, not at an internal edge between two zones of its own universe. Stated explicitly in `concordant-membranes.md` rather than left to inference, since Season 1 and several codex entries lean on that location.
  - Swept across `concordant-membranes.md`, `membrane-shadows.md`, `intermembrane-bleed.md`, `membrane-shadow.md`, `interval.md`, `boundary-zone.md`, `boundary-zones.md` and the canonical glossary, with two migration-map rows — one for the scale correction, one for the ambiguous "boundary zone".

- **A Dynarch is a proxy Telearch** (settled 2026-07-26) — not merely *aligned* with the Telearch line, as the entries previously had it, but the Telearch line acting **inside** a universe, scoped to a single force-domain. Telearchs are native to no universe and supervise from outside; a force has to be administered from within the thing it runs through, and the Dynarch tier is how that reach is made. Recorded in [`dynarch.md`](src/glossary/dynarch.md), [`cosmic-cascade.md`](src/lore/cosmic-cascade.md), [`who-governs-a-universe.md`](src/lore/who-governs-a-universe.md) and the [canonical glossary](src/lore/glossary/canonical-glossary-and-migration-guide.md).
  - **Turns three asserted properties into consequences.** *Continuity prevails on conflict* — previously a bare arbitration rule — now has a reason: continuity is what a Dynarch substantially **is**, and a proxy cannot rule against the office it proxies for. *Co-created* stops meaning "two parents of equal kind" and becomes **substance from the Telearch line, jurisdiction from the Principal line**. And the *dual obligation* stops reading as divided loyalty: a proxy answering to the local office for local matters and to its own principal for everything else is an ordinary arrangement.
  - **Explains the legacy confusion rather than just correcting it.** Older records filed Dynarchs with the Telearchs — the ambiguity that retired "higher celestials" and "High Celestials" both. Those records had noticed something true and lacked the word for which part was true.
  - **Explicitly not an avatar.** The Cascade's other instrument for acting from inside crosses a temporal register, appears at Celestial level or below, and is a separate limited person immanent in Material time. A Dynarch stays in conceptual time above the Celestials and is a standing office, not a person sent down — two answers to one problem, at different depths.

- **A Universal Authority's composition, settled** — it is **not** a separate mind installed above a universe's zones. An Authority is a **body**: the **Council of Harmonarchs** (every Concordant Principal in the universe, sitting together) plus a presiding seat held by the universe's **founder** — its originating **seed mind**, where the universe was raised by noögenic seeding — or, where there is no founder, by a **lead Harmonarch** drawn from the Council itself. Same office either way; only the occupant's origin differs. Recorded in [`universal-authority.md`](src/glossary/universal-authority.md), [`concordant-principal.md`](src/glossary/concordant-principal.md), [`who-governs-a-universe.md`](src/lore/who-governs-a-universe.md), and the [canonical glossary](src/lore/glossary/canonical-glossary-and-migration-guide.md), with new canonical-term entries for **Council of Harmonarchs**, **Lead Harmonarch**, and **Founder**.
  - **Resolves the "singular or plural mind" ambiguity** the record has carried since the Concordant/Universal Authority split. Both phrasings describe one institution: a Consensus Field is *how the Council decides*, a founder is *who presides while it does*, and a plural formation descended from a seed mind (a Synarch Mind among them) takes the presiding seat as one member rather than as a second council.
  - **Reframes "Principals answer to the Authority"**, which now needs care — a Principal answers to the council it *sits in*, not to a superior being. The Council's writ is universe-wide where a Principal's ends at its zone boundary, and a Harmonarch outvoted in council is bound by the decision inside its own zone regardless. Every Harmonarch holds two seats. Migration-map row added, since the old phrasing reads as a fourth tier.
  - **Explains the protouniverse rule from the inside** rather than by assertion. A Noögenic Protouniverse is *proto* because it has no stabilized Concordants, hence no Harmonarchs, hence no Council: **a founder without a Council is not an Authority.** This is why a seeded universe doesn't inherit governance the day its seed mind lands, and it aligns with `noogenic-seeding-system.md`'s existing rule that jurisdiction passes only once the seed mind "matures into a Universal Authority in its own right."
- **Threnos-Ω's "Council of Archons" identified** ([`threnos-omega.md`](src/lore/universes/threnos-omega.md)) — an unregistered term that turns out to be that universe's own word for its Council of Harmonarchs, its Static Synod being that Council in a near-terminal-CEI state. Deliberately **not** a deprecation: separately-authored universes aren't required to share vocabulary, so *Archon* stays in Threnos-Ω's records and is simply mapped. The migration row says to read it as *Harmonarch* and not to carry it outward — elsewhere in the corpus the word names nothing in the Cascade.

### Fixed

- **Telearch glossary URL misspelling** — the entry's title has always read "Telearch", but its filename and `id` were `telerarch` (transposed letters), so the page shipped at `/glossary/telerarch/`. Nothing was broken — all 12 inbound links used the misspelling consistently, and `related:` terms resolve by *title* rather than slug, so they were unaffected — but the typo was visible to any reader looking at the address bar. Renamed to `src/glossary/telearch.md` with `id: telearch`, and swept every reference in `src/` and `story-bible/`. **This changes the page's URL**, which for a non-chapter page also changes its giscus discussion mapping (comments map by pathname) — **confirmed safe here: the page had no existing comments**, so no thread was orphaned. Contrast the Journal URLs, which were deliberately *not* re-parented when `/story-engine/` was introduced, because there the threads were known to exist. Same rule, opposite call, decided on whether a discussion was actually there.

## [1.6.0] - 2026-07-26

First release cut deliberately, rather than reconstructed after the fact. Versions 1.0.0–1.5.0 were written retroactively in one sitting on 2026-07-09; `package.json` went straight from 1.0.0 to 1.5.0 in a single commit, so 1.1.0–1.4.0 never existed as states of the repository. See the note under 1.5.0.

**Tagged** — `v1.6.0` at this release, plus `v1.0.0` and `v1.5.0` cut retroactively at `a0ca09a` and `45f72f3`, the only two historical versions with a real commit behind them. Tags are pushed from a local clone; the automation path used for these releases cannot publish `refs/tags/*`.

### Added

- **A fourth canon status: Chartered** (settled 2026-07-26) — for approved derivative work by another hand, above a fan work and below canon, a gap the three existing statuses left open. One rule governs it: **canon binds it; it does not bind canon.** It must be consistent with canon as it stood at approval; when later canon contradicts it, the chartered work is *superseded* rather than retconned or withdrawn; the main story may never depend on one; and it carries **no `canon_facts`**, for the same reason the Codex doesn't — it establishes nothing. What separates the four statuses is who wrote the thing and where they stand: Codex is in-universe authorship, Overlay is a lens across the same events, Chartered is new events by another hand, out-of-universe and endorsed. **None exist yet** — the policy is written in advance so the first one doesn't have to invent it. Recorded in `story-bible-summary.md`'s canon-status table, `CLAUDE.md`, and `CONTENT-LICENSE.md`.
- **Chartered works are registered, not hosted** — the repo will list an approved work and point at it; the work stays with its own author. This is a rights boundary rather than a filing preference: `CONTENT-LICENSE.md` scopes CC BY-NC-ND over `src/` as Dermot's content against an MIT engine, and a third party's work has a different rights holder, so filing it under `src/` would put content inside a licence scope he cannot grant. The register becomes a published page when a first chartered work exists, and is deliberately not created empty.
- **A referencing rule for fan images and music: "referenced, not endorsed"** — fan-made images and music may be linked from the site where appropriate. The formula exists to resolve a real collision: the Fan Works Policy requires a fan work not imply Dermot's endorsement, and an official-site link is on its face a mild endorsement. The neutral wording settles it without amending the licence — a link is a pointer, not approval, and referencing something never confers chartered status. The alternative considered and not taken, "featured with permission", is genuine endorsement and would require a carve-out in the Fan Works Policy; it remains available as a deliberate licence change rather than a wording tweak. Documented alongside the three-axis split (licence / canon force / visibility) that keeps these decisions from being conflated.
- **Lore entry: "New London Space Habitat"** (`src/lore/new-london-space-habitat.md`) — three 1.5 km Stanford torus rings (Westminster, City, Crown) at **Earth–Moon L5**, built in the 2380s UCSD as a refuge for British cultural heritage after the Crisis Centuries' coastal fragmentation events, joined to a non-rotating hub ("The Spire") and threaded by the Thames Canal. Roughly 180,000 residents under a constitutional monarchy. Three canon interactions resolved rather than glossed: **(1)** it is explicitly *not* a member of the [Orbital Habitats Compact](src/lore/orbital-habitats-compact.md), which preserves that entry's hard "five self-governing habitats" figure and is what makes its ties to Eden genuinely diplomatic rather than intra-jurisdictional — the largest inhabited body in Earth orbit no Compact officer has jurisdiction over. **(2)** [Lagrange Points and Fold-Space Transit](src/lore/lagrange-fold-points.md) makes L4/L5 of any planet–moon system a **Tier 1 designated fold-staging zone**, so the designation (post-2712 UCSD) arrived around a city that had held station there for three centuries — a sovereign polity outside the Compact sitting on Survey Corps/SSDC charter infrastructure with no shared chain to arbitrate through. **(3)** Because [the Crisis Centuries](src/lore/crisis-centuries-terran-wildlife.md) records Earth's recovery under SSDC stewardship, the habitat's founding rationale is written as *expired*: it preserves a heritage at a remove rather than against extinction, an unresolved argument in its own politics. Closes with the deliberate contrast against the [Celtic Union](src/lore/celtic-union-of-planets.md)'s Currach Fleet — two opposite answers to the same fear, both still running — and both archives still printing CE beside UCSD for the same reason. Rotation figures check out: 1.5 km diameter gives 1.09 rpm and 86 m/s rim speed for 1 g, under the vestibular-comfort threshold.
- **`scripts/check-related-terms.js`** — a local authoring check (like `check-internal-links.js`; not wired into `npm test` or CI, exits non-zero so it can be) that verifies every front-matter `related:` term matches a real page title. This covers a gap all three existing checks structurally miss: `glossaryUrl` in `.eleventy.js` resolves a related term against page *titles* and falls back to `/glossary/` on a miss rather than erroring, so a stale term still renders a perfectly valid link to the wrong place — schema validation passes (related terms are free text), the Eleventy build passes, and the link checker passes (the emitted URL is real). Retitling a single lore or glossary page silently degrades every `related:` list naming it, which is exactly what the Common Manifold rename could have done. Matching is exact — case, punctuation and leading articles included — so misses print near-miss suggestions. Also warns, without failing, on duplicated page titles where only the first is reachable; it currently reports two long-standing glossary/lore title pairs (`FTL Mechanics`, `Allocation Units of Cognition (AUC)`), left as they are since the glossary entry winning is the sensible resolution.

### Fixed

- **`npm test` restored on `main`** — `scripts/validate-content.js` declared `privateThreadForPage` twice after the private-thread-boundary merge, so schema validation crashed before checking a single file. Collapsed to one import.
- **Canon errors inherited from Copilot-era edits** — a targeted pass over the six files whose last commit was the Copilot bot found and fixed: United Space Industry Standards described as holding its independence "through the Coherence Wars" 163 years *before* those wars began (now the 2130s–40s CE climate-crisis decades, immediately preceding the USC's founding); a claim that the UCSD calendar is anchored to the USC's founding, flatly contradicted by [Universal Cosmic Stardate](src/lore/universal-cosmic-stardate.md)'s own `UCSD = CE + 200` rule; the Three-Era Framework presented as USC-era scholarship analysing the 29th century — its own future — and shaping a 2340 charter with the result (reframed as historiography maturing across eras, with the SSSA anticipating the conclusion in practice); an undefined "Phase A/B" periodization; and a fourth-wall leak ("not canon-valid") in the in-universe [FTL Mechanics](src/glossary/ftl-mechanics.md) entry. Mixed bare CE/UCSD years across the pre-USC timeline cluster are now labelled per the CE+200 rule.
- **MSC lifespan contradiction** — [Military Space Command](src/lore/military-space-command.md) and [Jehu Among the Comparanda](src/codex/jehu-among-the-comparanda.md) both put the MSC's span at "approximately two centuries", against a dated record fixing it at ~114 years (Imperium ends 2609; charter 2723) and against [the Imperium](src/lore/the-imperium.md)'s own "a century after". Both now read "a little over a century" — which strengthens the Jehu comparison, that span being almost exactly the four generations the scriptural captain's house was granted.
- **`src/images/codex/cosmic-limitation-on-evil.jpg` rebuilt** — was a stray blurry stock photo breaking the designed-cover template every other codex entry uses. Regenerated as a proper title card (a ring dissolving round its own circumference; `CONTESTED` stamp taken from the paper's own filed status) using the new cover generator, so the title renders in real type rather than generated lettering.

- **Four mismatched character portraits removed** — a portrait audit found Naomi Kestrel, Rosalind Vey, and Tamsin Reyes (all written as women) rendered with male stock portraits, two of them pixel-identical duplicates of Bertram Ashcombe's and Kai Larsen's own images, and Sethka Ru (an alien Serephine Dunekin) shown as an ordinary human. Dropped all four `image`/`image_alt` front-matter fields and deleted the wrong image files rather than leave inaccurate art in place; `character.njk` already renders cleanly with no portrait (five other characters have none).
- **`src/images/lore/trigrian.jpg` re-graded toward an alien palette** — the site's own copy of "Three Suns over the Mara" (distinct from the source photo it derives from) was an unmodified Earth sunset standing in for an alien planet's sky. Applied a global hue/saturation shift plus distinctly-toned halos on the three suns matching the lore page's own trinary description (a tight orange pair, a paler wide-orbit companion).

### Changed

- **"Etheric" split into three canonical terms** — the word had been carrying three jobs at once: the Layer 3 causal mode, the seven compactified spatial dimensions of the home universe's 3+7+1 floor, and (historically) the separation between adjacent cosmic membranes. **Etheric keeps the first only**, and the other two are now named. The seven dimensions are **compact dimensions** ([`src/glossary/compact-dimensions.md`](src/glossary/compact-dimensions.md)) — ordinary space, too tightly wound to traverse, and the geometry Etheric templates have extent *through* rather than anything the layer is made of. The membrane separation is **the Interval** ([`src/glossary/interval.md`](src/glossary/interval.md)) — a distance term rather than a place, previously unnamed and described only as "manifold distance"; a boundary zone is a narrowed Interval, and Membrane Resonance, Intermembrane Bleed, Membrane Shadows and transient gravity tunnels are all consequences of that narrowing. Same shape as the earlier Concordant zone-versus-mind split: where one term named both a place and a non-place, the place got the new name. Canonical-terms entries and five legacy→canonical migration rows added to [the canonical glossary](src/lore/glossary/canonical-glossary-and-migration-guide.md); swept across `post-eleven-dimensional-manifold.md`, `ensemble-multiverse.md`, `concordant-membranes.md`, `membrane-shadows.md`, and the `intermembrane-bleed`/`membrane-shadow`/`etheric` glossary entries. **Idiomatic "into the Etheric layer" is deliberately not migrated** — roots reaching into a mode of constraint is correct in its own register, and the ~190 uses of the layer sense (chapters, `canon_facts`, characters, story bible) are untouched. The canonical glossary and [the Etheric entry](src/glossary/etheric.md) now both carry an explicit **register rule** so a later sweep doesn't re-derive it: *Etheric* works as working jargon even where it isn't literally accurate, and which register is speaking decides whether looseness is a fault. Chapters, characters and Codex sources are **voices** — imprecise field vocabulary there is characterization, not error, and is not a migration target. Lore and glossary pages are the **Archive** — held to the definition, where asserting the Etheric *is* a place is a mistake. Same principle the setting already applies to in-world "magic," and the reason [the Overfold](src/glossary/overfold.md) isn't ranked below Etheric.
- **A latent contradiction the shared word was hiding, now resolved** — `ensemble-multiverse.md` had Etheric templates propagating through the seven local dimensions while `concordant-membranes.md` routed template coupling through the trans-concordant constraint field at Dimensions 20+. Both are right, at different scopes: a Concordant's compact dimensions carry its templates *at home*, inside its own membrane, and the constraint field carries them *across the Interval* to a neighbour. Stated explicitly in all three affected pages, since an analyst who conflates the two looks for a bleed signature in the wrong band. Two paragraphs of self-disclaiming prose ("a geometric substrate claim, not a revision of the Five Layers…") that existed only to hold the overloaded word apart are gone, the distinction now being carried by the terms themselves.
- **The post-11 manifold named: the Common Manifold** ([`src/glossary/common-manifold.md`](src/glossary/common-manifold.md)) — "post-11" is positional, and positioned relative to *our* dimensional floor, which `ensemble-multiverse.md` explicitly establishes is "a local fact rather than a cosmic constant." Analysts in a universe with a different floor would count from their own number and mean the same structure, so the old name silently assumed the arithmetic it exists to deny. **Both names stay canonical**: "Common Manifold" is the formal name and records what it is (the one structure universes with different floors demonstrably share), "post-11 manifold" remains correct Survey Corps shorthand and in-world voice, now flagged as knowingly parochial — the same naming-from-where-you-stand habit that already gave the setting three names for one boundary phenomenon (see [Overfold](src/glossary/overfold.md)). The manifold's band numbering (12–15, 16–19, 20+) is likewise labelled local bookkeeping. **The page URL is unchanged** at `/lore/post-eleven-dimensional-manifold/`, so no inbound link or comment thread moves.
- **Church Space reframed as an overlay, not a parallel storyline** — the registry and its landing page described "a parallel storyline with its own cast," which is not what is on disk: there are no church-space chapters, `seasons` is deliberately empty, and the material is lore, codex entries, characters, and an author's FAQ. It is an optional commentary layer reading the *same* reality through an explicitly Christian and evangelical lens, concentrated on the spiritual layer, opted into per domain. Both descriptions now say so. This adds a third canon status to the internal glossary — **overlay**, alongside canon and valid-for-its-author: laid *across* the record rather than filed inside it, binding nothing and never load-bearing for the main story. The awkwardness of housing it in a registry of storyline threads is recorded rather than papered over: the mismatch is vocabulary, not behaviour, since tag-based membership plus opt-in visibility is exactly what an overlay needs, and the note says what a cleaner split would look like if the overlay ever grows chapters of its own.
- **New `/story-engine/` section, parent of the Journal** — the out-of-character part of the site now has a home of its own: the Journal's entries listed in full, plus a spoiler-free orientation to how the story is put together (seasons as timeline slots rather than release order, storyline threads, scenes and points of view, and the three different promises Lore, Glossary, and Codex each make). Replaces "Journal" in the main navigation, which now highlights for both URLs. **Journal URLs are unchanged** — every entry stays at `/journal/<slug>/`, deliberately, because giscus maps non-chapter discussions by pathname and re-parenting the URLs would orphan every existing journal comment thread. The Journal index gains a breadcrumb to its new parent.
- **An internal glossary of story-engine terms**, in `story-bible/story-bible-summary.md`'s Terminology sections: thread/strand/arc, visibility and filtering, the front-matter fields whose confusions are silent (`id` vs `comment_id`, `date` vs `timestamp`, `canon_facts`, `povs`), canon status (canon vs. valid-for-its-author vs. the lore/codex boundary vs. house voice), and craft (scene, POV block, scene-POV page, convergence point, deliberate mystery, reserved season, gap). Also records the standing policy that `story-bible/` is **permanently unpublished** — it is the only place spoilers live, and `/story-engine/` is derived from it rather than a mirror of it.
- **"Thread" split into thread and strand** — the story bible had been using one word for two structurally different things: a **storyline thread** groups whole seasons and is real machinery (`lib/storyline-threads.js`, `/threads/`, `threadForSeason`, `deploy.conf`'s `THREADS`, private-thread hiding), while "Thread A / Thread B" meant two parallel storylines *inside* one season, with no id, page, or registry anywhere. The within-season sense is now a **strand** — a thread is braided from strands, so the metaphor nests instead of colliding — and **arc** is reserved for a character's trajectory, which is not a reading path at all. Terminology table, the rules that follow (a season has exactly one thread and any number of strands; deploy filtering acts only on threads), and a legacy→canonical migration map are in `story-bible/story-bible-summary.md`; swept across all three story-bible documents. No reader-facing page or template used "Thread A/B", so no URL, thread id, or `deploy.conf` key changed. Also records the scope split the sweep depended on: the canonical glossary governs *in-universe* terminology, while craft vocabulary (thread, strand, arc, scene, POV block) belongs in `story-bible/` rather than a page readers see as lore.
- **The Codex's canon status stated explicitly, and `author` made a required field** — a codex entry is not canon; it is one named in-universe source's account, held to being valid *from that source's point of view* (their era, access, institution, bias) rather than to being true. The rule is now in `CLAUDE.md` alongside the lore/codex boundary it underwrites, and `lib/content-schema.js` enforces the attribution it depends on: an entry with nobody behind it has no viewpoint to be valid from and silently reverts to Archive-voice fact. All 29 existing entries already carry an `author`, so nothing needed backfilling. `scripts/new-content.js` now prompts for any schema-required field beyond `title`, so a scaffolded codex entry can't be created in a state that fails validation.
- **All seasons ratified as canon (2026-07-25)** — nothing in `src/seasons/` is provisional any longer, the Season 6–7 arc (`s06e01c01–c03`, `s07e01c01–c03`) included. Every chapter's `canon_facts` now binds on anything written afterward, and `story-bible/tissadelle-arc-s6-7.md` becomes background reasoning rather than a specification those chapters are measured against. Two consequences recorded in `story-bible/narrative-gaps-checklist.md`: four of its five Season 6–7 boxes were already satisfied by chapters on disk and are now ticked (the note claiming otherwise was stale), and **The Last Stand itself remains genuinely unwritten** — every existing chapter reaches Dock Seven backwards, through a citation draft, a residual signal, and an unreliable interior, with no chapter or POV of its own.
- **Threshold Station's chronometer discrepancy re-aged in `s06e01c02`** — the drift is eleven years old in 2826 (Season 1) and therefore sixteen in 2831, but the chapter carried the Season 1 figure into Season 6 twice, in prose and in a canon fact. Caught by ratification: the number only became load-bearing once the arc stopped being provisional.
- **Narrative drafting permission changed (2026-07-25)** — the rule that every narrative first draft is the author's, and that unprompted narrative prose is unwelcome, is retired in favour of standing permission to draft new scenes. `CLAUDE.md`'s prose-authorship convention now carries the constraints that come with it: work from `story-bible/narrative-gaps-checklist.md`, leave the deliberately-unwritten seasons and the standing mysteries (the *Patience First* terminus, the 2732 recovery) alone, add to the Season 6–7 outline rather than resolving it, match the `scene`/`pov` container structure, and state plainly what any drafting session wrote.
- **The voice and style of all existing prose approved by the author (2026-07-25)** — the corpus as it stands is now the reference for the house voice, and the two authorship-provenance notes (`story-bible/prose-needs-your-voice.md`, `prose-needs-review.md`) are records of who wrote what rather than tone-review queues. Scope is deliberately narrow: register only, not canon — the Season 6–7 chapters (`s06e01c01–c03`, `s07e01c01–c03`) need no rewrite for voice, but whether their events are settled story remains open, to be read against `story-bible/tissadelle-arc-s6-7.md`. The go-forward convention in `CLAUDE.md` is unchanged — narrative first drafts are the author's, and unprompted narrative prose is still out of scope.
- **Heroes of their own for `/story-engine/` and the Journal** — both pages (and the About page) had been opening with the same `hero/about-writer.jpg`. [Story Engine](src/story-engine/index.md) now leads with `hero/story-engine.jpg`, a brass machine whose riveted nameplate reads *Story Engine*, and the [Journal](src/journal/index.md) index with `hero/journal-notebook.jpg`, an open journal headed *Author's Journal* above a handwritten entry; About keeps the writer-at-a-desk photograph it always had. Both were picked from eight generated candidates on the same rule the codex-cover generator exists to enforce — every legible word must be short and correctly spelled — which ruled out six of them, and both were cropped to 16:9 around the lettering so `.page-hero-image`'s 3.4:1 centre band doesn't cut it off. Selection criteria and crop recipe in `story-bible/images.md`.
- **Cascade terminology law: the three senses of "Concordant" separated** ([canonical glossary](src/lore/glossary/canonical-glossary-and-migration-guide.md), with migration mappings). The word had been carrying both a bounded *region* and a universe-level governing *mind*; the governance sense is now **Universal Authority**, the zone-level governing mind a **Concordant Principal** (commonly **Harmonarch**), and the polity [the Solar System Concordant](src/lore/solar-system-concordant.md). Legacy phrasings migrated across affected lore and glossary pages. Also retires "High Celestials" as an ambiguous term rather than a Telearch synonym — it was used for both Telearchs and the new [Dynarchs](src/glossary/dynarch.md), and [its page](src/glossary/high-celestials.md) is now the disambiguation rule.
- **The Cascade documented as *mostly* hierarchical, with time in three registers** ([Cosmic Cascade](src/lore/cosmic-cascade.md)) — Worldwrights and Telearchs are parallel branches under the Archewrights rather than a chain; Dynarchs are co-created under both the Telearchs and the Concordant Principals; descent is creative before imperative. Material-layer time holds the Celestials and below, **conceptual time** the middle strata, and outright eternity only above the Worldwrights — superseding the earlier flat "timeless above the Celestials" framing and legitimising the operational record's active verbs for those strata.
- **Twelve character/lore/hero images replaced**, each `image_alt` rewritten to describe actual content — including the four worst content mismatches (an Imperium cyber-revenant shown as a smiling US Army soldier, the protagonist Aldera as a blue-furred fantasy cat contradicting her own gallery photos, a historical MSC general as a contemporary policewoman, and the Cerebraun species as the grey-alien bust its sibling entry explicitly avoids). Prompts and per-file notes in `story-bible/images.md`.

- **About page's fan-fiction-clone links now point to on-site pages instead of GitHub repo files** — the Fan Works Policy link now goes to the homepage's [Licence section](src/index.md) (`/star-rangers/#license`), which already carries the full CC BY-NC-ND text, and the forking pointer now goes to a new `src/forking/index.md` page instead of linking directly to `CONTENT-LICENSE.md`/`FORKING.md` in the repository.

### Added

- **S01E03C03, "The Root and the Rest of It"** (`src/seasons/s01/e03/s01e03c03.md`) — the dryadic grove's Etheric root-anchor intervention, planned at the end of S01E02C02 and explicitly deferred by S01E03C02's closing log ("that work is not tonight's"), now written. Two scenes, four POVs (Elvira, Galahad, Rook-7, Aldera): Elvira severs the Court-Fae's coupling at the root-plate overlap the seven trees make together, with Galahad reading the classification aloud — the vocabulary he once withheld from her now supplied as part of the working. The grove's own Etheric rooting survives the severance untouched; leaf phase-lag settles from 0.22 s to 0.19 s and is logged rather than explained; the entity's destination is deliberately not established. The chapter's substantive canon move is a **retraction**: Threshold Station's forty-second chronometer discrepancy is unchanged four hours after a clean severance 1.3 km away, so Rook-7 withdraws the two-source boundary model he filed in S01E02C02 and the drift reverts to an active unknown. Placed after the season's naming endpoint deliberately — S01E03C02 stays the thematic close, and this is its physical follow-through.
- **Cascade governance expanded: who actually governs a universe** — new lore entry [Who Governs a Universe](src/lore/who-governs-a-universe.md) (universe vs. Concordant Zone; the three kinds of authority; the matrix exceptions; the timeless/conceptual/immanent split) with supporting glossary entries [Universal Authority](src/glossary/universal-authority.md), [Concordant Principal](src/glossary/concordant-principal.md), [Dynarch](src/glossary/dynarch.md) (the force-governance tier — Gravity, Electromagnetics, Nature — commonly **Exarchs**), and [Avatar](src/glossary/avatar.md) (the one lawful crossing between temporal registers: a higher stratum incarnated as a limited person, like its source without being the same person as it). Plus [Asteria the Sage](src/characters/asteria-the-sage.md), the retired Star Captain whose sigh — *"Where do I even begin?"* — now opens the Archive's own primer.
- **[The Solar System Concordant](src/lore/solar-system-concord.md)** — the polity referenced across a dozen pages but never defined: not a government but a standing compact of shared civil law founded 2543 UCSD with the Tycho Accords, enforced by every regime since and owned by none, and the reason "the Concordant period" names an era.
- **[The Star Rangers Frontier Corps](src/lore/star-rangers-frontier-corps.md)** — caretaker law enforcement for frontier worlds with no local government of any kind, reconciled with the charter's do-not-police clause via a self-terminating mandate that ends at a colony's first sworn sheriff. Includes the second-landing problem (failed or abandoned governments, where re-entry needs an invitation a dead government cannot issue) and the Corps' non-combatant posture — shield, evacuate, document, never fight.
- **[The Fusion Ceiling](src/lore/the-fusion-ceiling.md) and [Ascent Javelins](src/lore/ascent-javelins.md)** — fusion is the top of the lawful energy ladder (no antimatter, no exotic taps, with the refusal argued from certification practice and the Kernel's waste invariant), sufficient everywhere and immediate nowhere; and the missile-launched winged craft that carry passengers surface-to-orbit, chemical-cycle to ~1g and fusion-thermal above it. Together they yield the frontier consequence that a heavy world is easier to land on than to leave.
- **[Embodied Cognition](src/lore/embodied-cognition.md)** — why a small embodied mind with a grounded world model resolves what a vastly larger ship or habitat AI cannot (boundary-zone telemetry contradictions, schematic drift, presence as a first-invariant obligation), and why Concordant practice pairs the two classes rather than choosing.
- **The charter's terraforming prohibition** — the Star Rangers may not conduct, certify, or support the terraforming of any world bearing existing life of any kind, with no sapience threshold or significance test ([charter](src/timeline/2723-star-rangers-charter.md), [Frontier Transformation Protocols](src/lore/frontier-transformation-protocols.md)). Living worlds are settled by compatibility, not conversion.
- **Two codex entries** — [The Twelve Sultans of AI](src/codex/the-twelve-sultans-of-ai.md) (the Imperium era's AI oligarchs, their systems' informal cooperation without convergence, and why no singularity is on record) and [The Friend Who Forgot Her Cat](src/codex/the-friend-who-forgot-her-cat.md) (a Verification Desk case file on six years of relay correspondence undone by one small impossible absence, filed without verdict).
- **Local authoring tools** (`scripts/`, none wired into the build) — `make-codex-cover.ps1` regenerates a codex cover card in the designed template with real type; `import-image.ps1` converts a source image to a repo-ready JPG at site conventions; `check-internal-links.js` verifies every internal `/star-rangers/` link resolves, catching the link rot `npm test` cannot see. Documented in `CLAUDE.md`.

- **A second scene added to S05E02C01, "What the Hill Keeps"** (`src/seasons/s05/e02/s05e02c01.md`): the chapter's existing hillside content is now wrapped as Scene 1, followed by a new Scene 2 — Shepherd's escorted departure from the Union shuttle gate the next morning, POVs Galen and Tissadelle. Alongside the Highland Guard's correct, chilly farewell, she tells the Rangers' own liaison "It is good to home. I mean back home. With the Star Rangers" — a small, unrehearsed slip that names, ahead of the [Season 6–7 arc](story-bible/tissadelle-arc-s6-7.md), which home actually holds her. New minor character **`src/characters/galen.md`**, the Star Rangers' standing liaison officer at the gate. This is the chapter's first use of the `::::: scene N` wrapper (`lib/markdown-containers.js`) — every prior chapter has relied on the implicit single-scene fallback — so it's also the first chapter to produce a `scene-2/` set of per-POV pages. Deliberately left "A Fraction of a Second" at its existing `s05e02c02` slot rather than renumbering to make room, since S07E01C03 already cross-links it by that path.
- **`src/characters/reeves-eden.md`, "Reeves (Eden Space Habitat)"** — a new character page for Eden Space Habitat's own Detective Assistant Reeves, previously referenced in prose by `eden-warden.md` and `rasa-oyelaran.md` but with no page of its own; both pages' "Reeves" links (which pointed at [Threshold Station's Reeves](src/characters/reeves.md) despite the text explicitly calling Eden's Reeves "a separate deployment") now point here instead. `reeves.md`'s existing cross-reference note is now a working link too.
- **A line acknowledging "Orbital Five-O" is also a nod to the classic *Hawaii Five-O*** — added to `src/threads/orbital-five-o/index.md`'s intro, alongside the existing in-universe explanation (the task force covers all five Compact habitats).

- **`src/forking/index.md`, "Forking This Site"** — a reader-facing page adapting `FORKING.md`'s guide (the two licences, Path A vs. Path B, what's engine vs. content, step-by-step fork instructions) so the About page can link to an on-site page rather than a repository file.

- **Shared deploy machinery extracted to `scripts/deploy-lib.sh`** — the site-agnostic parts of `scripts/cpanel-deploy.sh` (log-file setup, the notification-email list, the notify-on-any-outcome mailer, per-run `deploy-logs/` persistence and pruning) now live in a new `scripts/deploy-lib.sh`, kept **byte-identical** with the same file in the `dermot-cochran-photography` repository (the same convention `scripts/ensure-node.sh` already follows), so fixes to that machinery are ported by copying one file instead of hand-merging two diverged scripts. `cpanel-deploy.sh` keeps everything site-specific (deploy.conf keys, multi-domain/ALT_DOMAINS handling, themes, giscus, the `/star-rangers/` prefix rewrite, pagefind) and behaves identically — same log/email/exit-code semantics, verified against a stubbed end-to-end deploy simulation of the success, failure, and multi-domain paths. CI's shellcheck step now covers the new file.

- **Season 0 is now presented as "Founding Era" in the UI** — a display-only relabel, leaving every URL (`/seasons/s00/…`), chapter `id` (`s00e01c01`), and the `season`/`episode`/`chapter` schema untouched, so no links or comment threads move. New `seasonLabel` Eleventy filter (`.eleventy.js`) maps season `0` → "Founding Era" and every other season → "Season N", used by the dynamic breadcrumbs (`src/_includes/chapter.njk`, `src/_includes/scene-pov.njk`) and the season-block titles on `src/seasons/index.md` and both thread pages (`src/threads/founding-era/index.md`, `src/threads/tissadelle-arc/index.md`). The hardcoded `src/seasons/s00/index.md` and its three episode pages (title, breadcrumb, `<h1>`, prose, descriptions) were relabelled to match. "Season 0" no longer appears anywhere reader-facing; the prequel reads under its existing `founding-era` thread name instead. A companion `seasonsInThread` filter lets the thread-grouped listings (`src/threads/founding-era/index.md`, `src/threads/tissadelle-arc/index.md`, and the per-thread sections of `src/seasons/index.md`) **suppress the per-season block title when a thread renders only one season** — so the Founding Era, whose single season's label is identical to its thread heading, no longer prints that heading twice; multi-season threads (Tissadelle's Season 1/3/5) keep their per-season titles.

### Added

- **`src/characters/turquoise-dove.md`, "The Turquoise Dove"** — a new Active character: a Higher Levril, distinguished among named dragons by the turquoise iridescence of her dimensional signature. Consistent with the Higher Levril subclass's Cascade-permitted role ([Levrils lore](src/lore/levrils.md)), she's associated with cross-Concordant coordination and post-instability advisory contact rather than direct intervention, and with mentoring — in constraint literacy — Champions selected by other Levrils rather than selecting them herself. No Material-layer archive holds a first-person account of an actual meeting; her presence is inferred from field-anomaly logs. Introduced ahead of an upcoming chapter appearance.
- **`src/characters/osric-fenholt.md`, "Osric Fenholt"** — a new Historical character: an Imperium-era Assistant Deputy Viceroy in the Belt Settlements Directorate's Bureau of Outer Compliance, whose nineteen years of unaltered settlement condition reports survived the Imperium precisely because the institution's own doctrine of technical rigor read his accuracy as competence rather than sedition. Filed under the Imperium/pre-MSC period, cross-linked to [The Imperium](src/lore/the-imperium.md) and [Military Space Command](src/lore/military-space-command.md).
- **Seasons 6 and 7 of Tissadelle Shepherd's Arc — the Last Stand and after** (`lib/storyline-threads.js`, `src/threads/tissadelle-arc/index.md`, six new chapters, two season and two episode index pages, one Codex working paper). The `tissadelle-arc` thread now claims seasons `[1, 3, 5, 6, 7]` (was `[1, 3, 5]`); its registry description and landing-page intro update from "Seasons 1, 3, 5, and beyond" to "Seasons 1, 3, 5, 6, and 7". No template change was needed — the thread and season listings pick up the new seasons automatically. New index pages `src/seasons/s06/index.md`, `src/seasons/s06/e01/index.md`, `src/seasons/s07/index.md`, `src/seasons/s07/e01/index.md` follow the `s02` no-hero-image pattern (no `season-06`/`season-07` hero asset exists yet, so they omit the image rather than reference a placeholder). The arc dramatizes the [Season 6–7 treatment](story-bible/tissadelle-arc-s6-7.md) with **no new cosmological system** — every mechanism cites existing canon ([Seed Mind Lifecycle](src/lore/seed-mind-lifecycle.md), [Noögenic Protouniverse](src/glossary/noogenic-protouniverse.md), [Levrils](src/lore/levrils.md), [Gilded Saints](src/glossary/gilded-saints.md)/[predatory-entities](src/lore/predatory-entities.md) counter-doctrine, [Saint Aoife](src/lore/saint-aoife.md)'s thorn-well account). Line Captain Shepherd is a stalled noöseed — a vulnerable, still-becoming protouniverse — kept from collapse by three help vectors the story keeps strictly inside canon limits: a **levril** holding her boundary open (the same Cascade-entity class the Union reads behind Aoife's vision, able to mentor constraint literacy but forbidden to complete her transference or reach in); **Saint Aoife's** inherited discipline of refusing to collapse *shown* into *healed*, carried as the Shepherd holding's own "keep the rule without inventing the reason"; and her IWD-reconstructed **dreams of friends** (Órla and Karla Wender), written to refuse to be more comforting than the originals. Cognitive-horror-into-tender-rescue, no magic and no sexualized content, per the treatment's tone note. The resolution follows the treatment's recommended option 3 (contested on the record and off it — Council citation, Codex, and what Wender privately knows never fully reconcile) with option 2's mechanics (real two-way contact) as the private truth.
  - **`src/seasons/s06/e01/s06e01c01.md`, "First Light, Off the Record"** — Shepherd (POV) and Órla-as-remembered: the interior homecoming opens, warm and total, then produces two of the same clearing, and her mother chooses, on the doorstep, to let a daughter who *is and is not* her daughter be both true at once rather than smooth the discrepancy away.
  - **`src/seasons/s06/e01/s06e01c02.md`, "What the Instruments Kept"** — Wender and Rook-7 (POVs): Wender leaves the Oversight Council's hero's citation unsigned; Rook-7's non-standard arrays log a warm, iterating signal at the Dock Seven failure point that is inconsistent with total loss and phrases the way the [Sentinel pulse](src/seasons/s03/e01/s03e01c01.md) once did. Forwarded to Sen's reconciliation desk.
  - **`src/seasons/s06/e01/s06e01c03.md`, "The Well Ran Warm Again"** — Shepherd and a self-aware reconstructed Wender (POVs): Shepherd runs her own anomaly diagnostic on herself, finds the recursion never resolves, names her condition before anyone outside can, and a levril arrives at the edge of her inner world — folding in without tearing, at every distance at once — and *holds* without entering. Season 6's confirmation-without-rescue turn.
  - **`src/seasons/s07/e01/s07e01c01.md`, "The Accurate Account"** — Wender and Syra (POVs): the external team assembles the true account, first ruling out whether the closure is being held open by a [Gilded Saint](src/glossary/gilded-saints.md), by physics, or by the Council's own martyrdom narrative (all real hazards; the counter-doctrine's precision aimed at each), and correlates the Dock Seven warmth with the eight-century-old warm-well signature in Sen's archive.
  - **`src/seasons/s07/e01/s07e01c02.md`, "Shown, Not Healed"** — Shepherd and Órla-as-remembered (POVs): the real danger is the *mercy* — the pull to let the loop resolve into a finished, unbearably kind homecoming and stop. Shepherd holds it open using Aoife's exact discipline (shown ≠ healed) and her family's, and the levril teaches her to see the wall she is inside without breaking it for her.
  - **`src/seasons/s07/e01/s07e01c03.md`, "Enough Is Enough"** — Shepherd and Wender (POVs): the accurate account becomes a rope, a detail only Shepherd could know (the unfiled Hollow from [S05E02C02](src/seasons/s05/e02/s05e02c02.md)) crosses the warm edge in both directions, and the two threads finally touch. Nobody pulls her out; nobody closes the file; she names her own state true and keeps it open on her own terms — not gone, not saved, and not alone.
  - **`src/codex/the-warm-edge-correlation.md`, "The Warm-Edge Correlation"** — a Codex working paper (a Ridgemoot chaplain of Saint Aoife's Celtic Union devotion, Bréanainn Ó Sé, with the Survey Archive reconciliation desk) reading the Dock Seven warm signature against Aoife's thorn-well account. Filed in the **Codex, not Lore**, per the lore/codex boundary rule: the *instrument signature* correlation is settled and cited, but the identification (same levril? mercy or mere observation?) is contested and left standing — with an explicit caution that the devotion has every reason to want the warm edge to mean mercy, which is exactly why it must not be the one to say it does, and that "divine" fixes no referent here (it points at Kieme, or the whole Cascade, or nothing the invariant record names). Kept to public Aoife-devotion framing rather than the private `church-space` Communion, per the one-way public→private link boundary. Cross-referenced from the existing [Dock Seven Night Watch Addendum](src/codex/dock-seven-night-watch-addendum-day-52.md).

- **`src/codex/baby-universe-ballad.md`, "Baby Universe (Circulating Ballad)" — a Cultural Record with recovered audio**: an unattributed ballad that circulates *about* Line Captain Shepherd after the Last Stand, transcribed lyrics plus the recovered recording embedded via a `<video controls>` player (`src/video/baby-universe.mp4`, served at `/star-rangers/video/`, the first real use of the existing `src/video` passthrough). The song opens naming her in the third person and slips into a first-person plea in the chorus ("St. Aoife, find the thread / Before I fade and die"), voicing the S6–7 arc's own beats — the seam into higher space, the bruised "baby universe," the levrils "with lantern hands and grace," the "dreams of friends" — from the outside. Filed in the **Codex** and, within it, under the Survey Archive's *reconciliation* binders rather than the music stock: [Sen's](src/characters/sen.md) archivist note keeps the [closure-prevention caution](src/lore/predatory-entities.md) beside it, since a beautiful, never-quite-closed sacrifice sung by people with good reasons to keep singing it is the exact shape the counter-doctrine watches. Cross-linked to [Ballad of the Stars](src/codex/ballad-of-the-stars.md) (whose audio/transcription convention it follows), [The Warm-Edge Correlation](src/codex/the-warm-edge-correlation.md), and the [S7 finale](src/seasons/s07/e01/s07e01c03.md).

- **One-way public→private thread link boundary, enforced at build time** (`scripts/validate-content.js`, plus a new `privateThreadForPage` reused from `lib/content-filter.js`): a public page may no longer hardcode a link *into* a private-thread page (currently `church-space`'s), since on the full site and every clone that hasn't opted the thread in, that target renders the "not included in this edition" placeholder rather than the real page — a dead end for the reader. `npm test` now fails, file-by-file, on any such link. The reverse direction stays allowed: a private page can link out to public pages freely (a private page is only ever seen where its thread is opted in, and the public pages it references exist there too). Removed the two pre-existing violations this surfaced — `src/lore/physics-comparison.md`'s editorial note pointing at the private `softening-the-real-cosmos-side` journal entry, and `src/lore/universes/si-gaoithe.md`'s comparison linking the private `cnoc-na-mbeach` lore page — by trimming each to stand without the private reference.
- **Explicit friendly-AI-crawler section in `robots.txt`** (`src/robots.njk`): named `User-agent` groups welcoming the major AI assistant, answer-engine, and training/search crawlers — Anthropic (`ClaudeBot`, `Claude-Web`, `Claude-User`, `Claude-SearchBot`, `anthropic-ai`), OpenAI (`GPTBot`, `ChatGPT-User`, `OAI-SearchBot`), `Google-Extended`, `Applebot-Extended`, Perplexity (`PerplexityBot`, `Perplexity-User`), and `CCBot` (Common Crawl) — each with `Allow: /`. Declarative rather than functional: the existing `User-agent: * / Allow: /` wildcard already permits every crawler, so this grants no new access — it makes the welcome explicit and gives one obvious place to adjust any single crawler later without touching the wildcard rule.
- **Character `known_codex` field**: characters can now carry an optional `known_codex` front-matter array of codex-entry filename slugs (e.g. `[star-rangers-anthem, ballad-of-the-stars]`), rendered as a "Known Codex Documents" list on `character.njk` (`.character-known-codex` in `main.css`, regenerated across every theme) via a new `codexByIds` Eleventy filter (`.eleventy.js`, matching codex entries by `fileSlug` since codex has no `id` field). `scripts/validate-content.js` cross-checks every listed slug against actual `src/codex/` files. `src/characters/tissadelle-shepherd.md` is the first entry to use it, formalizing the two Slipwave-era recordings her page already linked in prose.
- **`major-character` POV validation**: `scripts/validate-content.js` now requires every chapter to have at least 2 `povs` entries, and — when at least one POV id resolves to an actual character file — that at least one of them carry the existing `major-character` tag (a convention 6 characters already used informally; a chapter built entirely from undocumented, chapter-only POV figures isn't held to this second check, since there's no page to classify). One pre-existing chapter, `src/seasons/s01/e00/s01e00c02.md` ("What the Stones Confirmed," a deliberate single-POV scene), is grandfathered past the POV-count minimum rather than rewritten. Promoted three characters to `major-character` to satisfy the rule for their own storylines: [Kai Larsen](src/characters/kai-larsen.md) (Orbital Five-O's lead across all of Season 2 so far), [Tissadelle Shepherd](src/characters/tissadelle-shepherd.md) (the multi-season protagonist of Tissadelle's Arc, previously untagged), and [Maren Solveig Krast](src/characters/maren-solveig-krast.md) (the Military Space Command's founder-in-memory, sole resolvable POV of `s00e02c02`).
- **The Orbital Five-O storyline thread** (`lib/storyline-threads.js`, `src/threads/orbital-five-o/index.md`): a new, non-private thread registry entry for the Governor's Investigative Task Force — Commander Kai Larsen, Governor Petra Voss, and Chief Commissioner Dorian Calloway, all previously tagged `orbital-five-o` but with no registered thread or landing page to collect them. Claims Season 2 (left open by `tissadelle-arc` for exactly this — a storyline that doesn't run through Tissadelle Shepherd), now that the thread's first chapter exists (see below).
- **`src/seasons/s02/e01/s02e01c01.md`, "The Desk That Called First"**: Season 2's first chapter, opening the Orbital Five-O thread. Two POVs — Commander Kai Larsen and Governor Petra Voss — cover an Eden compliance-framework referral (a ration-manifest discrepancy Detective Inspector Wendell Albercombe couldn't trace past Eden's own jurisdiction) turning out to touch a Compact-wide routing code, the exact shape of case Five-O was chartered to close. Albercombe and his household intelligence [Jeeves](src/characters/jeeves.md) appear as minor/supporting characters in Larsen's POV, not as leads. Adds `src/seasons/s02/index.md` and `src/seasons/s02/e01/index.md` season/episode index pages, matching the existing `s01`/`s03` pattern (no hero image — none exists yet for this season, so the pages omit it rather than reference a placeholder asset).
- **`src/seasons/s02/e01/s02e01c02.md`, "The Office That Reads Everything"**: Season 2, Episode 1's second chapter. Larsen and Chief Commissioner Dorian Calloway POVs — Larsen brings the reassigned routing code to Calloway's office and gets back a name, Threnody Logistics, plus the reconciliation discrepancy Calloway's office had already noticed six weeks earlier and filed as a curiosity rather than escalated. Ends on Calloway quietly following a second thread of his own (an unnamed habitat Commissioner's countersigned freight authorization) before handing Larsen anything more than a fact that "hadn't finished arguing for itself yet" — a deliberate cliffhanger, not yet a named suspect.
- **`src/seasons/s02/e01/s02e01c03.md`, "A Very Ordinary Call"**: Season 2, Episode 1's third chapter. Calloway and Larsen POVs — Calloway places his routine liaison call to Meridian's Commissioner, Anselm Duarte, and gets back answers that are individually true and collectively too well-rehearsed for an unannounced question. Introduces **Meridian** as the Compact's second named member habitat (alongside Eden) and Duarte as a new named, chapter-level character — kept to dialogue and description here rather than a dedicated character/lore page, the same way `s02e01c02` introduced Threnody Logistics without one. Ends with Larsen deciding to visit Meridian in person, the first time Five-O has exercised its five-habitat charter beyond Eden.
- **`src/characters/wendell-albercombe.md`, "Detective Inspector Wendell Albercombe"**: a new minor/supporting character — an Eden Space Habitat detective inspector under Superintendent Oyelaran, with no standing in Five-O's own casework but occasionally the first call when an "ordinary" referral turns out bigger than it read. Cross-linked from [Superintendent Rasa Oyelaran](src/characters/rasa-oyelaran.md) (the existing bureau-roster mention is now a link) and tagged `orbital-five-o`.
- **`src/characters/jeeves.md`, "Jeeves"**: a new character, a domestic-companion AI assigned to Detective Inspector Wendell Albercombe under Eden Space Habitat's welfare program — distinct from the bureau-assigned [Reeves](src/characters/reeves.md) at Eden (and from Threshold Station's own Reeves/Ashcombe pairing), working Albercombe's caseload sideways from outside institutional process rather than from inside it. Cross-linked from [Superintendent Rasa Oyelaran](src/characters/rasa-oyelaran.md) and, now that his own page exists, [Wendell Albercombe](src/characters/wendell-albercombe.md); tagged `orbital-five-o` as a minor/supporting figure in that thread.
- **`src/codex/jehu-among-the-comparanda.md`, "Jehu Among the Comparanda"** and **`src/codex/the-captain-who-drove-furiously.md`, "The Captain Who Drove Furiously"**: two paired Codex entries reading an Old-Earth scriptural pair against Solar System founding memory. The first is a Fellowship comparative-archive working paper (Sister Ione Marrec, contemplative chapter) that files the prophet **Elijah** as an [Arilon](src/lore/arilon.md)-pattern witness — names the boundary truth the royal house won't, is opposed, is gone before the naming is vindicated — and pairs the captain **Jehu** (who ends the rotten house but "departs not from" its older idol, and whose dynasty gets a bounded span then is narrowed into its successors) with General **[Maren Solveig Krast](src/characters/maren-solveig-krast.md)** and the [Military Space Command](src/lore/military-space-command.md): the founder-in-memory (not in fact) whose word ended one failure by reproducing its deeper one, whose institution got ~two centuries then was narrowed into the SSDC, and whose own sentence became the outer-station critics' vindication after the namers were gone. The second is the plain-voice telling — a contemplative answering a cadet at the Eden commissioning who asks why the Rangers sing an Old-Earth prophet's song ([Hymn of the Thin Places](src/codex/hymn-of-the-thin-places.md)), threading the twinned story to Krast without ever naming her. Both are filed in the Codex, not Lore, per the contested/interpretive rule (the mapping is one correspondent's, non-diegetic to the political record); the Cascade's no-moral-cosmology and "misattribution as divine will" cautions are carried through both, and the mythic overstatement that gives the MSC a founder it never had is itself flagged as an Arilon-adjacent effect. Reciprocal links added from `src/lore/arilon.md` and `src/characters/maren-solveig-krast.md` (settled MSC lore left unedited).
- **Multilingual approach: English as canon, browser translation, and human translations as fan works** — no official per-locale build, by design (an unverifiable translation on the canonical site would assert canon its author can't confirm, worst of all in the Codex/narrative where precise diction is the point). `src/_includes/base.njk`'s footer gains a labeled note (`.site-lang-note` in `main.css`, regenerated across every theme) telling readers their browser can translate any page but that such translations are automatic/**unofficial** and the English text is always authoritative on canon. `CONTENT-LICENSE.md`'s Fan Works Policy and the About page's Fan Works section (now anchored `#fan-works`) explicitly welcome human translations as non-commercial, clearly-labeled fan works. New Journal entry **`src/journal/a-canon-i-cannot-verify.md`, "A Canon I Can't Verify in Another Language"** records the reasoning.
- **Named giscus comment-repo profiles (`GISCUS_PROFILE`) + a local override file for forks** (`src/_data/giscus.js`, `scripts/cpanel-deploy.sh`, `sample-deploy.conf`, `sample-giscus.local.json`, `.gitignore`, `README.md`, `FORKING.md`). The project's own comment repos are now a `GISCUS_PROFILES` registry in `giscus.js` (`default` → `sciencefiction-site-comments` for the full-site/reference domains incl. starquest.*; `church-space` → `churchspace-site-comments` for church-space.site/.online and their Fellowship of Light addon domains). A deploy selects one with a single `GISCUS_PROFILE` key instead of pasting six repo/category IDs — so `sample-deploy.conf`'s church-space example blocks collapse from ~7 giscus lines each to one, and a Fellowship of Light sample block was added alongside. An unknown profile name fails the build (typo guard) instead of silently using the default board. The six explicit `GISCUS_REPO`/`GISCUS_REPO_ID`/`GISCUS_CATEGORY_*_ID` keys remain as a per-field escape hatch (each overrides just its field of the selected profile). Separately, a **third-party fork** can now point comments at its own repo without editing engine code or `deploy.conf`: an untracked `giscus.local.json` (copy `sample-giscus.local.json`) is read at build time and becomes the fork's default board on every path — `npm start`, GitHub Pages, and any cPanel deploy that doesn't select a profile — with `GISCUS_PROFILE`/`GISCUS_*` env vars still taking precedence. Default (unset) behavior is unchanged: the same `sciencefiction-site-comments` board with the same IDs as before.
- **`src/journal/two-copies-forty-seconds-apart.md`, "Two Copies, Forty Seconds Apart"**: a new Journal entry giving an honest account of the tools the site has been written with over time — GitHub Copilot and Microsoft 365 Copilot for early scaffolding (folded invisibly into human-authored commits, since accepted suggestions land under the author's name), Sudowrite for some of the Codex's documentary prose, and Claude Code once a Sudowrite draft and the committed file drifted out of sync and the repository became the single source of truth. Frames the sync-drift problem as a small real-world echo of the story's own premise (records that disagree and stay that way). The About page's new "How this site is written" section (below) links to it.
- **"How this site is written" section on the About page** (`src/about/index.md`): a short, honestly-scoped note on the drafting/editing toolchain (GitHub Copilot + M365 Copilot early on, Sudowrite for parts of the Codex, Claude Code against the repository now that it's the single source of truth), sitting alongside the existing "How this site is built" (tech stack) and "How this site is deployed" sections, and linking to the fuller Journal entry above.
- **`src/lore/universes/tir-tairngire.md`, "Tír Tairngire: The Harmonic Membrane"** and **`src/lore/universes/si-gaoithe.md`, "Sí Gaoithe: The Discordant Membrane"**: two new Universes entries documenting a mechanical, hard-SF explanation for Celtic Union "fair folk" folklore — a lawful, mechanism-level reading rather than a magical one. Tír Tairngire's membrane cycles on a rhythm regular enough to correlate with [Tír na nÓg's own Conjunction](src/lore/planets/tir-na-nog.md); its Class II crossers (the "Good People") are documented with no feeding signature of any kind. Sí Gaoithe's membrane never settles into a stable Boundary-State Class, tied speculatively to its own high [Creative Entropy Index](src/lore/creative-entropy-framework.md); its crossers resist clean Class II/III sorting and produce only localized mischief, never a confirmed drain. Both are explicitly unrelated discoveries, not two faces of one thing, despite the shared mythic register. `src/lore/concordant-membranes.md` gains a new "Beyond Class III: Transient Gravity Tunnels" section naming the shared, rarer matter-crossing mechanism (distinct from a Membrane Shadow's gravitational-imprint-only case) that both entries document instances of. Cross-linked from `tir-na-nog.md`, `meta-dimensional-beings.md` (a "not every Class II being is predatory" clarification), `predatory-entities.md`, and `creative-entropy-framework.md`.
- **`src/lore/lagrange-fold-points.md`**: new "Quiet-Zone Tunnels: Undetected Natural Fold Conduits" section documenting a distinct, intra-Concordant natural fold phenomenon — a stable (non-collapsing) tunnel that can form wherever deep interstellar space is gravitationally flat enough, by distance rather than Lagrange balance, for an admissible fold corridor to thread through it. Unlike the cross-membrane transient gravity tunnels above, this stays within one universe; unlike engineered Higher-Dimensional Folding, it requires no scaffold and carries no Lagrange-like signature to survey by, so a vessel typically confirms one only after already drifting through it. Left deliberately unresolved whether this accounts for any of the setting's existing founding-era fold mysteries. Cross-linked from `src/lore/ftl-mechanics.md`.
- **`src/journal/sorting-doctrine-out-of-lore.md`, "Sorting Doctrine Out of Lore, and a Paragraph That Knew Too Much"**: a new Journal entry documenting the editorial reasoning behind moving `cosmic-limitation-on-evil.md` to the Codex and trimming `predatory-entities.md`'s "How to counter them" paragraphs (both below), without restating the specific mechanism the trim removed.
