- **`src/codex/cosmic-limitation-on-evil.md`** (moved from `src/lore/cosmic-limitation-on-evil.md`): "The Cosmic Limitation on Evil" refiled as a Doctrinal Division working paper — a named theorist, institution, and archive location — rather than settled lore, since its Archive-theorist-vs-devotional-tradition argument and its unresolved tension with the Cascade's own no-moral-cosmology invariant is exactly the kind of contested, POV-laden content the Codex is for, not Lore. Content and canon facts unchanged; added a closing archivist's note cautioning against reading it as predictive of any specific case. `src/images/lore/cosmic-limitation-on-evil.jpg` moved to `src/images/codex/` alongside it. Cross-links updated in `cosmic-cascade.md`, `kieme-visible-hand.md`, `communion-of-the-called.md`, and `glossary/kieme.md` (the last also trimmed to state the claim's contested status more tersely, consistent with lore/glossary now leaning harder toward settled, hard-SF-consistent fact and leaving argued positions to the Codex).
- **Trimmed `src/lore/predatory-entities.md`**: removed the "How to counter them" paragraphs for Court-Fae and Gilded Saints, which stated outright the specific tactical mechanism resolving an in-progress/planned story convergence. General lore is allowed to state settled cosmological fact ahead of the prose, per the section's own intro, but not the answer to a scene not yet told. The underlying craft/canon detail now lives in `story-bible/story-bible-summary.md`'s "Threats/entities" section (not rendered on the site) and `prompts/star-rangers-universe-engine.md`, both of which also gain a new standing editorial rule on the lore/codex boundary and spoiler discipline (see `story-bible-summary.md`'s new "Editorial note" section for the full reasoning).
- **Backlink to the page's true home on the "Not included in this edition" placeholder** (`src/_includes/excluded.njk`, `lib/storyline-threads.js`, `lib/content-filter.js`, `.eleventy.js`): a narrowed deploy (e.g. `church-space.site`, `undercover-pets.com`) already renders this placeholder in place of any page its own `CHARACTERS`/`TOPICS`/`THREADS` filtering excludes, but gave the reader no way to actually reach that content — it just said the page wasn't part of this deployment. Now links to the same path on the domain that *actually has* the page, built from `page.url` rather than hardcoded, so it resolves correctly for every excluded page regardless of content type. Ordinary excluded pages link to the full-site reference domain (`sciencefiction.site`, now the `DEFAULT_REFERENCE_DOMAIN` constant in `lib/storyline-threads.js`), which is a superset of everything ordinary narrowing hides. A **private thread**'s pages are the exception: the reference domain excludes those too (a private thread is opt-in on *every* build, including the default full-site one), so pointing there produced a **self-referential loop** — on `sciencefiction.site` itself, a church-space page's placeholder linked straight back to the same church-space URL, which just re-rendered the same placeholder. A private thread now carries an optional `homeDomain` (`church-space` → `church-space.site`), and its excluded pages link there — the one clone that actually opts the thread in — instead. Resolved per page by a new `referenceDomain` Eleventy computed field (`.eleventy.js`) backed by `privateThreadForPage` (`lib/content-filter.js`). A plain link, not a redirect — the reader chooses whether to follow it.
- **`src/glossary/cyborg.md`, "Cyborg"**: a new glossary entry defining physical cybernetic modification as a category distinct from [Smart Pet](src/glossary/smart-pet.md)'s purely cognitive AI subsystem — a distinction `smart-pet.md` had already asserted ("A Smart Pet is not, by definition, a cyborg") without the term ever being defined anywhere. Covers its history under [the Imperium](src/lore/the-imperium.md)'s military augmentation programs and its regulation since, first by the Military Space Command and tightened by every government after. Cross-linked from `smart-pet.md`'s `related` list, `the-imperium.md`, and `military-space-command.md`, both of which gain a paragraph on the same history from their own side.
- **`src/lore/star-rangers-science-corps.md`, "The Star Rangers Science Corps"**: a new Institutions entry for the specialist guild that interprets, models, and publishes on what the [Survey Corps](src/codex/survey-corps-protocol.md) collects in the field — Survey collects, Science explains what was collected — and for the **Chief Science Officer** duty title that leads it post by post. `star-rangers-command-hierarchy.md`'s specialist-corps list and Chief-rank duty-title rundown both named Survey, Safety, Provost, Medical, and Engineering but never Science, despite the site already using terms like "boundary science" loosely elsewhere; this closes that gap and gives the role its own institutional history — descended from the MSC's own Boundary Research Division, reconstituted at founding on the same independence principle that reconstituted the SSSA as the Safety Corps. Cross-linked from `star-rangers-command-hierarchy.md` (ladder entry + See Also) and `star-rangers-safety-corps.md`'s See Also.

- **`src/characters/lorien-the-wanderer.md`, "Lorien the Wanderer"**: a new character, an unaffiliated freelance captain who charts unclaimed fold corridors and sells the survey data to whoever pays first — Survey Corps included, when the price and the politics both work out. Flies the *Restless Verge*, a stripped-down long-range courier hull. Not yet featured in any chapter; her own "See also" links out to the existing `src/lore/lagrange-fold-points.md` and `src/lore/frontier-transformation-protocols.md` entries (no reciprocal link added on either, since neither is specifically about her).
- **Character gallery field**: characters can now carry an optional `gallery` front-matter array (`image`/`image_alt` pairs, rendered under a new "Gallery" section on `character.njk` via `.character-gallery`/`.character-gallery__grid` in `main.css`, propagated to every theme). `src/characters/aldera.md` is the first entry to use it — four candid field photos in `src/images/characters/aldera/`, tagged `pets` alongside her existing tags.
- **`src/glossary/metafold.md`, "Metafold"**: a new Misconception-category glossary entry for the popular misnomer that conflates the [Overfold](src/glossary/overfold.md) (a standing boundary-zone condition) with [Higher-Dimensional Folding](src/glossary/higher-dimensional-folding.md) (the FTL transit mechanism) — the shared "fold" root invites the mistake even though the two share no actual mechanism. Cross-linked from both entries' `related` lists.
- **`src/lore/eden-ring-rail.md`, "The Ring-Rail"**: a new Technology entry for Eden's circumferential commuter line — the everyday transit system running the inner rim of the spin ring, distinct from the short radial spoke-cars connecting the ring to the low-gravity hub. Scheduled and dispatched by the Eden Warden (Ward's largest routine administrative task, and by its own account an informal early-warning signal), funded and defended by Mayor Petrakis's office against Commissioner Wayland's periodic Compact-wide standardisation proposals — the same Mayor/Commissioner dual line `orbital-habitats-compact.md` already documents, applied to an ordinary utility instead of a governance question. One stretch, the hub-ward spoke terminating near the Eden Passage monitoring stations, requires Survey Corps/SSDC clearance the rest of the line doesn't — the one point where Eden's civil transit visibly touches the habitat's separate fold-route oversight chain. Cross-linked from `eden-space-habitat.md`, `orbital-habitats-compact.md`, `eden-warden.md`, `imogen-petrakis.md`, and `zara-wayland.md`.
- **`src/lore/planets/thalassa.md`, "Thalassa"**: a new virgin ocean-world Locations entry, colonised entirely on Saltmere/Venice-style platform hulls and mooring towers rather than any landmass — its two founding cities, **New Venice** and **New Atlantis**, deliberately disagree about how to be a floating settlement. New Venice, built by heritage engineers with direct professional lineage to Earth's own Venice, reproduces the historic city's campaniles, facades, and calli-width geometry from nothing rather than preserving it from something; New Atlantis, a later and less heritage-minded second wave, builds low and structurally exposed, wearing the myth's warning as an ironic civic motto ("built to bend, not to boast") instead of hiding from it. Framed as the first colony to take Saltmere's platform-hull method off-world by choice rather than necessity. Cross-linked from `src/lore/venice.md` (which gains a new closing paragraph on Venetian engineers exporting the retrofit method off-world), `src/lore/planets/saltmere.md`, and `src/lore/environmental-technology-design.md`.
- **`src/lore/venice.md`, "Venice"**: a new Locations entry for Earth's Venice, in 2826 UCSD a fully engineered floating city rather than a flood-prone one — its historic foundation replaced sestiere by sestiere with the same platform-hull-and-mooring-tower construction documented at `src/lore/planets/saltmere.md`, contrasted against Saltmere's build-from-nothing approach since Venice's retrofit had to happen underneath a city already occupied and unwilling to relocate. Ties the Crisis Centuries' coastal fragmentation events (`src/lore/crisis-centuries-terran-wildlife.md`) to a concrete Earth outcome, and reads its "old face, new foundation" preservation choice in the same old-and-new register `src/lore/environmental-technology-design.md` documents elsewhere, explicitly paralleled with Mars's own popular-vote refusal to finish terraforming (`src/lore/planets/mars.md`). Cross-linked from all four.
- **Journal** (`/journal/`), a sixth content type alongside characters/lore/codex/glossary/chapters — out-of-character author's notes, kept next to About as the site's only two non-diegetic sections. New `journal` entry in `lib/content-schema.js` (`title`/`date` required, `tags`/`description` optional), `src/_includes/journal-entry.njk` layout, `src/journal/index.md` listing page (newest-first, via a new `journalEntries` collection and `previousJournalEntryIn`/`nextJournalEntryIn` filters in `.eleventy.js` for prev/next nav), a "Journal" nav link in `base.njk` next to About, and `npm run new -- journal` scaffolding (auto-sets `date` to today, same convention as a chapter). Comments map by plain `pathname` (safe — journal entries are flat and never get repositioned the way chapters do), via a new fourth page-mapped giscus category, **Journal** (`src/_data/giscus.js`'s `GISCUS_CATEGORY_JOURNAL_ID`, threaded through `scripts/cpanel-deploy.sh`'s per-clone override mechanism and documented in `README.md`/`sample-deploy.conf` alongside the existing three). Seeded with a first entry, ["A Photo, a Homophone, and How Membrane Shadows Got Their Name"](src/journal/a-photo-a-homophone-and-membrane-shadows.md), covering the naming decision in the entry right above this one.
- **`src/lore/membrane-shadows.md`, "Membrane Shadows: Gravitational Imprints from Adjacent Membranes"**: names the Physical-layer counterpart to the Etheric-layer Intermembrane Bleed already documented in `src/lore/concordant-membranes.md` — at Class III boundary-zone proximity, a coherent mass on the far side of a narrowed membrane gap (usually a living being) leaks enough gravitational field structure across it to bend and dim ambient light, producing a full silhouette with nothing physically present on this side to cast it. Explicitly disambiguated from the Class III non-sapient shadow beings in `src/lore/meta-dimensional-beings.md`, which have actually entered material space — a Membrane Shadow hasn't, and falls outside the meta-dimensional-being classification entirely rather than at the bottom of it. Also explicitly not an alternate-timeline double when it happens to resemble someone familiar: primary universes are independently authored, not branches of a shared history, so there is nothing for a far-side being to have diverged from. Paired with a new `src/glossary/membrane-shadow.md` entry. Cross-linked from `concordant-membranes.md`, `meta-dimensional-beings.md`, and `intermembrane-bleed.md`, each updated to note the Physical channel this entry covers.
- **Renamed "brane" to "cosmic membrane" (short form "membrane") across the boundary-zone cosmology**: the word "brane" — Survey Corps' existing shorthand for a Concordant's bounded region in the post-11 manifold, itself already short for "membrane" in real brane-world physics — reads too easily as "brain" when spoken over a comm channel or read aloud, which the newly-added Membrane Shadows entry made a live problem rather than a hypothetical one. `src/lore/concordant-branes.md` → `src/lore/concordant-membranes.md` ("Concordant Branes and Interbrane Bleed" → "Concordant Membranes and Intermembrane Bleed"), `src/glossary/interbrane-bleed.md` → `src/glossary/intermembrane-bleed.md`, `src/glossary/brane-shadow.md` → `src/glossary/membrane-shadow.md`, plus every "Brane Resonance"/"brane-proximity"/"cross-brane" mention across `ensemble-multiverse.md`, `meta-dimensional-beings.md`, `fellowship-of-light.md`, and `overfold.md`. Purely a rename — no mechanism, class, or hierarchy changed.
- **S00E02C01, "Unauthorised, Therefore"** (`src/seasons/s00/e02/s00e02c01.md`): a year after *Patience First* disappeared, Adaeze Okafor — sister of the ship's boundary analyst — travels to Mars in person after eleven months of form-letter correspondence gets her nowhere. Dramatizes the family pressure `src/lore/formation-of-star-rangers.md` credits as part of what eventually forces the 2719 Hearing, previously only asserted, never shown. Told from Adaeze and from Lieutenant Rutger Voss, staffing the MSC's Casualty Correspondence desk — the same Voss who returns, years later and several ranks up, in "What They Were Forbidden to Become" (S00E03C01), planting the seed of the disillusionment that later lets him accept the charter's accountability limits without calling it a concession. Cross-linked from `src/lore/formation-of-star-rangers.md` and `src/lore/eden-space-habitat.md`.
- **Renumbered "The Volunteered Word" from S00E02C01 to S00E02C02** (`src/seasons/s00/e02/s00e02c02.md`) to keep Episode 2 in chronological order (2715 UCSD before 2719 UCSD) after adding "Unauthorised, Therefore" above as the new E02C01. All cross-links updated: `src/timeline/2719-outer-stations-consolidation-hearing.md`, `src/lore/formation-of-star-rangers.md`, `src/lore/military-space-command.md`. `story-bible/narrative-gaps-checklist.md` updated for both chapters.
- **`church-space` theme**: a new domain re-skin (`src/css/theme-church-space.css`, generated via `scripts/generate-themes.js`) for the private `church-space` thread's own domains — a candlelit stone background with wine-red accents and stained-glass jewel tones for the five `.pov-block--<character>` colors, alongside the existing `fellowship`/`pets`/`starquest` re-skins. `sample-deploy.conf`'s church-space.site/.online example block now sets `THEME=church-space` for both. Documented in `README.md`'s theme table.
- **`DEPLOY_PRIMARY`** `deploy.conf`/`scripts/cpanel-deploy.sh` key (default `true`): set `false` to skip deploying to `/home/<CPANEL_USER>/public_html/` entirely, for a cPanel account whose `public_html` is reserved for something else (or deliberately left parked) and should only serve one or more `ALT_DOMAINS`. `DEPLOY_PRIMARY=false` with `ALT_DOMAINS` also unset/empty fails the run loudly rather than silently deploying nothing — same "fail loud, not silent" philosophy the script already applies to a misconfigured `ALT_<id>_*` entry. Documented in `README.md` and `sample-deploy.conf`.
- **S00E03C02, "No Longer Supplementary"** (`src/seasons/s00/e03/s00e03c02.md`): a closing beat for Season 0's two returning POVs, same signing day as "What They Were Forbidden to Become." Dr. Pitch reads her once-buried "supplementary material" cited by name as a founding asset in the ratified charter — the payoff of "Supplementary Material" (S00E01C01)'s title. Captain Kilbride, recruited into the new Survey Corps on the strength of the *Constant Margin* transit, carries what the charter's carefully-worded *Patience First* recovery mandate actually means to the person who trained alongside Okafor before she left. Resolves nothing about the terminus or the eventual 2732 recovery — deliberately — but gives the season's founding generation a human close rather than ending on the charter's text alone. Cross-linked from `src/lore/formation-of-star-rangers.md`'s "What the Star Rangers Inherited" section.
- **S00E03C01, "What They Were Forbidden to Become"** (`src/seasons/s00/e03/s00e03c01.md`): the Star Rangers Charter's ratification, 2723 UCSD, dramatized from the inside — the season's founding moment the Charter timeline entry has always documented only from the outside. Four years on from the Hearing, Delegate Petra Solano is now doing the patient, unglamorous negotiation her viral quote only bought time for; Commodore Rutger Voss of the newly formed SSDC argues the charter's jurisdiction limits sincerely (citing a real prior incident, Kessler Anchorage) and comes around to Solano's position anyway, without ever framing it to himself as a concession. Resolves the last open item on Season 0's checklist: the season is now fully dramatized from the *Constant Margin*'s 2712 departure through the 2723 signing. New Season 0, Episode 3 directory and index page. Cross-linked from `src/timeline/2723-star-rangers-charter.md` and both `src/lore/formation-of-star-rangers.md` and `src/lore/military-space-command.md`, which previously only described the negotiation and the SSDC's objection from the outside. `story-bible/narrative-gaps-checklist.md` updated — Season 0's checklist is now fully checked.
- **S00E02C01, "The Volunteered Word"** (`src/seasons/s00/e02/s00e02c01.md`): the Outer Stations Consolidation Hearing of 2719 UCSD, eleven weeks into a session scheduled for three. Dramatizes General Krast's honestly-meant defense of technocratic command — already quoted secondhand in `src/lore/military-space-command.md` and `src/lore/formation-of-star-rangers.md` — and the moment three uncoordinated civilian recordings turn one volunteered sentence into the quote that outruns six years of unresolved MSC findings. Told from Krast (who means every word, and goes on believing she was right to say it) and Delegate Petra Solano of Halyard Station, the first of the three to release her recording. New Season 0, Episode 2 directory and index page, and `src/timeline/2719-outer-stations-consolidation-hearing.md` mirroring the existing 2712/2714 entries. Cross-linked from both lore pages that previously only quoted the line secondhand. `story-bible/narrative-gaps-checklist.md` updated.
- **S00E01C02, "Beyond MSC Liability"** (`src/seasons/s00/e01/s00e01c02.md`): two years after "Supplementary Material," a six-person crew takes *Patience First* past the transit point *Constant Margin* only touched and returned from, aiming to investigate the fold terminus itself — ground Dr. Pitch's model has never been tested against. Dramatizes only the departure, told from Pitch (watching her buried model get treated as settled fact rather than a checked one) and the ship's own boundary analyst, Dr. Wren Okafor, who states the same caveat Pitch does and goes anyway. Stops at the moment of transit, well short of the ship's disappearance, its eighteen-year absence, or its 2732 recovery — all of which stay untouched per the site's existing deliberate mystery around what *Patience First*'s crew found. New `src/timeline/2714-patience-first-departs.md`, mirroring `2712-eden-fold-route.md`'s existing structure and cross-linked from `src/lore/eden-space-habitat.md`. `story-bible/narrative-gaps-checklist.md` updated.
- **`src/lore/arilon.md`**: a generic, cross-cultural "prophet archetype" — the Fellowship of Light's own comparative-archive shorthand for a recurring narrative pattern (a teacher or witness who names a boundary truth no local authority will name first) found independently across unconnected cultures, mechanically grounded in the existing `cosmic-cascade.md`'s Champions/Heroes tier and its documented "persistent misattribution as divine will by low-context observers" rather than tied to any one real-world religion. Cross-linked from `cosmic-cascade.md`'s Champions/Heroes section and `fellowship-of-light.md`. Paired with **`src/codex/hymn-of-the-thin-places.md`**, an ecumenical hymn of disputed origin sung at Ranger memorials and commissionings — deliberately uncredited to any single tradition, consistent with the charter's Neutrality clause. Written so future religious/mythic content across any culture can reference "an Arilon-pattern figure" instead of modeling a new one on a specific real-world faith.
- **Retconned `src/lore/saint-aoife.md`, `src/codex/life-of-saint-aoife.md`, `src/characters/saint-aoife.md`, and `src/characters/brother-daire.md`** to remove direct references to a specific real-world religion and a real historical/legendary figure: "the Church," "God," "Roman process," "confessor," and "IN THIS YEAR OF OUR LORD" are now generic devotional-authority language, and the vision's named figure is now an invented local patroness (**Saint Muirenn**) rather than the real Saint Brigid. The vision itself, its ambiguity, and both existing readings (hagiography vs. Levril encounter) are unchanged.

- **S00E01C01, "Supplementary Material"** (`src/seasons/s00/e01/s00e01c01.md`): Season 0's first published chapter, dramatizing the 2712 UCSD departure documented from the outside in `src/timeline/2712-eden-fold-route.md` — Dr. Ysolde Maren Pitch's fold-mechanics navigation model, buried in the Military Space Command's review process as a footnoted "supplementary" submission, handed to the *Constant Margin*'s three-person crew before any committee finishes deciding whether it's authorised. Ends at the moment of transit, deliberately stopping short of the *Patience First*'s 2714 disappearance and 2732 recovery, which stay untouched per the site's own established mystery. New `src/seasons/s00/e01/` episode directory and index page (Season 0 had none before). Cross-linked from `src/timeline/2712-eden-fold-route.md`, `src/lore/eden-space-habitat.md`, and `src/lore/formation-of-star-rangers.md`; `story-bible/narrative-gaps-checklist.md` updated. Also fixes a pre-existing continuity error caught while researching the chapter's institutional backdrop: `src/lore/military-space-command.md` dated the Krast "We tried democracy..." quote to "2689 UCSD," contradicting `formation-of-star-rangers.md`'s unambiguous "2719 UCSD" for the same Outer Stations Consolidation Hearing (and Season 0's own stated 2712-2723 range); corrected to 2719.

- **S05E02C02, "A Fraction of a Second"** (`src/seasons/s05/e02/s05e02c02.md`): ten days after "What the Hill Keeps," back on duty, a fleet-wide anomaly bulletin — Sen's unsigned cross-referencing work — matches her family's hillside against the Marsh Causeway grove's dryadic-anchor marker, filed only as an unattributed coordinate. Shepherd flags it for formal survey on documented grounds without disclosing the personal connection; High Captain Wender notices the tell and lets it go, consistent with her own established command philosophy. Advances both threads `story-bible/tissadelle-arc-s6-7.md` credits Season 5 with planting — the Threshold-drift/dryadic-anchor connection and what she chose not to file — without resolving either, since that payoff is reserved for the Last Stand (see `story-bible/narrative-gaps-checklist.md`, updated here). Cross-links added to `src/characters/tissadelle-shepherd.md`, `karla-wender.md`, `sen.md`, and `src/lore/dryadic-trees.md`'s "Known Locations" section.

- **S03E01C02, "Independent Verification"** (`src/seasons/s03/e01/s03e01c02.md`): the Sentinel reclassification survives Survey Corps review six days after the catch — reproduced independently under supervision, not taken on Shepherd's word — while Sohrel absorbs the Prime Ganglion's office noting, not approving, the authorisation that made it possible. Dramatizes "what it costs to be believed about it" from `src/seasons/s03/index.md`'s own framing, per `story-bible/narrative-gaps-checklist.md` (updated here). Introduces Sohrel's fourth declined internal request to consult Meridian's reef-cities about the Sentinel's structure — updates `src/characters/sohrel.md` and `src/lore/planets/sentinel.md`'s existing "three" to "four" and cross-links both to the new chapter, since the connection remains a deliberately open thread rather than something this chapter resolves.

- **S01E03C02, "The Right Question"** (`src/seasons/s01/e03/s01e03c02.md`): Season 1's long-missing convergence chapter. Galahad finally discloses the full survey archive to Elvira — now including the station-drift/grove-residue harmonic coupling confirmed in "Harmonic Debrief" (S01E02C03) — and Elvira, for the first time in three years, directly asks Aldera what she's found rather than simply co-existing with her. Aldera answers, per her own established protocol of only sharing requested findings, and the Court-Fae feeding loop breaks: the season's stated endpoint per `story-bible/story-bible-summary.md`'s "Season 1 endpoint (per site synopsis)," previously undramatized (see `story-bible/narrative-gaps-checklist.md`). Deliberately leaves the dryadic grove's separate Etheric root-anchor intervention (planned at the end of S01E02C02) unresolved — naming the feeding pattern and severing its physical anchor are two different problems, and this chapter closes only the first. Does not resolve what Elvira herself is; that stays an open thread per her own character page.

- **`story-bible/narrative-gaps-checklist.md`**: a season-by-season checklist of what's actually published in `src/seasons/` versus what the story bible and site copy have already committed to — Season 0 and Seasons 6-7 fully described/outlined but entirely unwritten, Season 1's own established convergence endpoint still missing, Seasons 3 and 5 each a single chapter standing in for a whole rank-era, plus the standing undramatized waypoints (Wender's rank progression, the Tissadelle/Wender relationship, founding-era open questions) from the story bible summary. Not rendered on the site - a personal tracking doc, re-derive rather than trust once stale.
- **Atom feed** (`src/feed.njk`, at `/feed/feed.xml`, autodiscoverable via a `<link rel="alternate">` in `base.njk`) listing the 20 most recently published chapters newest-first, via a new `recentChapters` collection sorted by a chapter's real-world `date` rather than story order. `date` (`YYYY-MM-DD`, distinct from a chapter's in-universe `timestamp` string) is now a required chapter field in `lib/content-schema.js`; `scripts/new-content.js` sets it to today automatically when scaffolding a new chapter, and the 13 pre-existing chapters were backfilled from each file's own first git commit date so the feed's initial publish order is accurate rather than uniformly "now." Considered `@11ty/eleventy-plugin-rss` first but skipped it: it registers its own `absoluteUrl` Nunjucks filter that would have silently overridden this project's existing one (different, deliberately-correct behavior for the `/star-rangers/` subpath — see `sitemap.njk`), and the package is ESM-only, which doesn't `require()` into this CommonJS config. Hand-rolled the one filter actually needed (`dateToRfc3339`, via the already-installed `luxon`) instead.
- **Open Graph / Twitter Card meta tags** on every page (`base.njk`'s `<head>`): title, description, url, and an image, so links shared on Discord/Reddit/etc. get a proper preview instead of a bare URL. The image is computed per page type in `.eleventy.js`'s new `eleventyComputed.ogImage` from the same `image` front-matter field each layout's own `<img>` tag already uses (character/lore/codex/glossary), falling back to the homepage's hero image for chapters and listing pages. Caught and fixed one bug while verifying: the fallback was originally written as a Nunjucks-side `ogImage | default(...)`, but Nunjucks' `default` filter only substitutes for `undefined`, not `null` — since the computed value was `null`, it silently passed through to the `absoluteUrl` filter, which has its own `!path` fallback to the bare site root. Moved the fallback into the computed function itself so `ogImage` is never null in the first place.
- **Full-text search**, powered by [Pagefind](https://pagefind.app/): `npm run build` now runs `eleventy && pagefind --site _site`, indexing the built output. A hand-rolled header search box (`src/js/search.js`, styled in `main.css`'s new `/* --- Search --- */` section) uses Pagefind's JS API directly rather than its prebuilt `pagefind-ui` widget, so it matches the site's own dark theme instead of overriding another package's bundled CSS. `<main data-pagefind-body>` scopes indexing to actual page content; breadcrumbs, "back to X" footers, chapter pagination, the chapter-scenes list, and the comments widget all carry `data-pagefind-ignore` so search results aren't full of repeated nav boilerplate. The search widget's `data-pagefind-bundle` path carries the same `/star-rangers/` prefix as every other internal link, so `SITE_PATH_PREFIX` rewrites it automatically too. Verified end-to-end with a headless-browser test against a real built+indexed site: query → results with correct titles/excerpts/highlighting → click-through to the right page, at desktop and mobile viewport widths, with zero console/network errors.
- **`npm run new`** (`scripts/new-content.js`): scaffolds a new character, lore entry, codex entry, glossary entry, or chapter, prompting for each type's fields instead of requiring a contributor to memorize a layout's exact front-matter shape by copying an existing file. Chapter numbers auto-derive the `id`, directory, and filename, removing a whole class of copy-paste drift. Timeline entries aren't covered (see the script's own header comment for why).
- **Content validation** (`scripts/validate-content.js`, run by `npm test` before the Eleventy dry run): checks every content file's front matter against a shared schema (`lib/content-schema.js`, the same one `npm run new` scaffolds from) and fails with a clear per-file message — a missing required field, a non-numeric `season`/`episode`/`chapter`/`sort_order`, or a chapter whose `id` or filename disagrees with its own front matter — instead of a blank page or a cryptic Nunjucks error surfacing later. Verified against all 223 existing content files (passes clean) and against several deliberately-broken test files (each catches correctly), including through `npm test`'s actual short-circuit behavior on failure.
- **giscus-powered discussion comments** on every character, lore, glossary, codex, episode, and chapter/scene page, backed by GitHub Discussions on a separate, dedicated `Star-Rangers/sciencefiction-site-comments` repo (kept apart from this repo's own dev-facing Discussions). Config lives in `src/_data/giscus.js`; the embed is in `src/_includes/base.njk`, gated on new `comments`/`commentsCategory` front matter set by the six relevant layouts. Three page-mapped categories (**Characters**, **Lore & Worldbuilding**, **Episode Discussion**) get one auto-created discussion per page path; five more (**Announcements**, **General**, **Q&A**, **Theories & Predictions**, **Fan Creations**) are for open community discussion unrelated to any specific page. See the README's new "Discussion forum (giscus)" section for the full category list and the one-time GitHub/giscus.app setup steps needed before the repo/category IDs can be filled in.
- **`COMMENTS_ENABLED`** `deploy.conf`/`ALT_<id>_COMMENTS_ENABLED` key (default `true`) to build a clone with the giscus widget above turned off entirely — read as a plain `.eleventy.js` global-data toggle (`process.env.COMMENTS_ENABLED`), the same pattern `THEME` already uses. The GitHub Pages workflow sets it `false`, since Pages' `/star-rangers/`-prefixed URLs would otherwise create a second, disconnected set of pathname-mapped discussions alongside the root-served cPanel domains'. In `scripts/cpanel-deploy.sh`, `build_and_deploy()`'s existing 11 fixed positional settings weren't given a 12th: this and any future simple on/off setting is instead passed as a trailing `NAME=value` string, parsed by a small `case` inside the function (unrecognized names fail the deploy loudly) — keeps deploy.conf's growing option list from making that function's call sites harder to read or reorder correctly.
- **`scripts/fetch-giscus-ids.js`** (`npm run fetch-giscus-ids`): fetches the giscus repo ID and every configured category's ID from GitHub's GraphQL API in one call, using the repo/category names already declared in `src/_data/giscus.js`, and can patch them straight into that file with `--write` — an alternative to re-running the giscus.app wizard once per category.
- **"Fan fiction" section on the About page**, pointing readers who want to write their own Star Rangers stories to AO3 or Wattpad rather than this site or its comments repo, with a suggested tag so their work stays findable. The comments repo's **Fan Creations** category (see the giscus category table above) is for linking/discussing those works, not hosting them — no in-repo fic-hosting or forum was built for this, by design, per the tradeoffs discussed when the category list was drafted.

### Removed

- **Root-level `lore/` directory** (`lore/codex/exploration-budget.md`, `lore/codex/protocols/redline-protocol.md`, `lore/codex/dialogues/codex-debate-entropy.md`) — early drafts of the Exploration Budget/Redline Protocol doctrine, sitting outside Eleventy's `src/` input dir and never built or published. Deleted as superseded: all three are fully covered, in more developed form, by the published `src/codex/exploration-budget-doctrine.md`, `src/codex/redline-protocol.md`, and `src/codex/hall-of-quiet-instruments-dialogue.md`.

### Changed

- **Tagged `src/codex/bramble-and-the-backwards-key.md`** (the Bramble Storybooks excerpt, the Concordant's best-known Smart Pet children's franchise) with `undercover-pets.com`, the tag `TOPICS`/`CHARACTERS`/`THREADS` narrowing matches to pull a page into that domain's deploy — the same convention already used by `bubochka.md`, `agent-barsik.md`, `smart-pet.md`, and over a dozen other pets-relevant pages. It was the one Cultural Record codex entry about a Smart Pet missing the tag.
- **Disambiguated the three legendary figures in `src/codex/flight-of-aldera-chronicle-of-dun-ri.md`** from their same-named modern counterparts: the legend's Princess Elvira, her cat Aldera, and Brother Daire were referred to by bare first name/title throughout, identical to the canonical `elvira.md`/`aldera.md` (Season 1 boundary practitioner and detective-agency cat) and `brother-daire.md` (the historical 1216 AD Cill Aoife scribe) character pages, even though the codex entry's own closing note already treats all three as distinct, unconfirmed namesakes rather than the same individuals. Added "of Dún Rí"/"of Dún Rí Abbey" at each figure's first named mention in the story text, and extended the closing note to explain this as a citation habit for clarity, not a claim about descent one way or the other — the underlying in-universe mystery stays exactly as open as it was.
- **Reassigned Rook-7 from the detective agency to a police department**: `rook-7.md`, `rook-7-first-week-log.md`, `aldera.md`, and `smart-pet.md` all described Rook-7 (an ordinary robot, not a Smart Pet or cyber-enhanced animal) as part of the Undercover Pets Detective Agency's own field-unit network — conflating "shares the same asymmetry-detecting cognitive architecture" with "belongs to the same institution." Rook-7 now belongs to the Threshold Station Police Department instead — technical support, investigation, and forensics, with no formal power of arrest — a separate institution from the detective agency that happens to prefer the same kind of non-rationalising cognition in robots that the agency prefers in Smart Pets and cyber-enhanced animals. `rook-7-first-week-log.md`'s institution/tags updated to match; `aldera.md`'s note that she's "aware of Rook-7 through the detective agency network" corrected to inter-agency channels rather than a shared chain of command. Ordinary robots accordingly stay out of `undercover-pets.com`'s narrowing — they were never tagged for it to begin with, but the prose no longer implies they should be.
- **Expanded `src/lore/the-imperium.md`'s Origins section**: the Inner System Defence Fleet's unified command at the Tycho Accords is now explicitly grounded in a small number of wealthy and powerful families who had already gained control of the Inner System's major technology and space industries before the Coherence Wars ended — the same "legacy economic power" `united-space-consortium.md`'s Character section already credits with skewing the USC's own assembly, continuing past the USC's collapse rather than disappearing with it. Also adds a "Militarily augmented" bullet to the Imperium's Character section, on its use of military cyborg technology, cross-linked to the new `cyborg.md` glossary entry. `military-space-command.md` gains a matching paragraph on the MSC winding down those programs and starting the certification regime later governments kept tightening.

### Fixed

- **Home-page hero slideshow dipped to the background between portraits instead of cross-fading** (`main.css`, propagated to every `theme-*.css`). Each slide's `home-hero-crossfade-{5,6}` keyframe faded it back to `opacity: 0` exactly at its slot boundary, and the next slide only began fading in from that same instant, so every transition passed through the empty `--color-surface` background — a fade-out-then-in flash, not a crossfade. The fade-out window now overlaps the incoming slide's fade-in window (each slide fades out over `[slot, slot+fade]` while the next fades in over the same interval, including across the loop seam), producing a true crossfade. Timing, slide counts (5 for `pets`, 6 elsewhere), and the `prefers-reduced-motion` fallback are unchanged; re-ran `npm run generate-themes` to propagate it.
- **Rebuilt CSS/JS could be served stale from browser/CDN cache** (`src/_includes/base.njk`, `src/_data/build.js`). `css/main.css`, `js/pov.js`, and `js/search.js` were linked with no version token, so a returning visitor could keep an old `main.css` after a redeploy — and because `scripts/cpanel-deploy.sh` rewrites `_site/css/main.css` (theme swap + optional `CUSTOM_CSS_FILE`) *after* Eleventy runs, a build-time content hash of the source wouldn't reflect what's actually served. Added `build.assetVersion` (a per-build token, computed once at build) and appended it as `?v=…` to all three same-origin asset URLs, so every rebuild/redeploy busts the cache uniformly regardless of which theme a clone deploys.
- **`sample-deploy.conf`'s `THREADS` comment listed only two of the three registered storyline threads**, omitting `church-space` — even though the same file's own church-space example block sets `THREADS=church-space`, which then read as coming from nowhere. Updated the comment to list all three (matching `README.md`) and to note that `church-space` is a `private: true` thread (hidden on every build unless explicitly named, the inverse of how the other two narrow an otherwise-full site).
- **Character portrait/text overlap on mobile** (`.character-header__inner` in `main.css`): the character header's portrait image and name/badge text column were laid out side-by-side with `flex-shrink: 0` on the image and no responsive override, so below the existing 640px breakpoint the text column collapsed to zero width and the portrait overflowed past the viewport's right edge instead of shrinking to fit — visible on every character page (e.g. `/characters/bubochka/`) on a phone-width screen, propagated to every theme including `theme-pets.css` (undercover-pets.com). Added `flex-direction: column` for `.character-header__inner`, full-width `.character-header__text`, and `max-width: 100%` for `.character-portrait` inside the same `@media (max-width: 640px)` block, and re-ran `npm run generate-themes` to propagate the fix to every theme file.
- **Chapter prev/next pagination**, dead on every single chapter since `chapter.njk` referenced `previousChapter`/`nextChapter` template variables that nothing ever actually set. Two new Nunjucks filters, `previousChapterIn`/`nextChapterIn` (`.eleventy.js`), find a chapter's immediate neighbor in the already-sorted `chapters` collection — one continuous publication order across episode and season boundaries, the same order a season/episode index's own chapter list already reads in. Naturally skips anything `CHARACTERS`/`TOPICS`/`THREADS` filtering has excluded, since the collection itself omits those chapters, so a narrowed deploy never links to hidden content. Verified against the first chapter (no previous), the last chapter (no next), the new S01E03C02 convergence chapter's neighbors on both sides, and a `CHARACTERS`-narrowed build.
- **Chapter/scene comment threads losing their original context on renumber.** Chapters and per-POV scene pages mapped their giscus discussion by `pathname` (like every other page type), but a chapter's URL isn't permanent — episodes get renumbered in place to keep story chronology in order (see this file's own "renumbered" entries), reassigning a URL like `/seasons/s00/e02/s00e02c01/` to entirely different content. Any comments already attached to that pathname would silently reattach to whatever content next occupied the slot. Chapters now require a permanent `comment_id` front-matter field (`lib/content-schema.js`), independent of the position-derived `id`/URL, and `base.njk` maps them via `data-mapping="specific"`/`data-term` on it instead; scene pages derive their own term from the parent chapter's `comment_id` (`src/scene-pov.njk`). `comment_id` is set once — `npm run new -- chapter` generates it from the title — and must be carried forward by hand if a chapter is later renumbered, rather than regenerated, so its thread stays with its content; `scripts/validate-content.js` now fails the build if two chapters ever collide on the same `comment_id`. Backfilled onto all 22 existing chapters, including S00E02C01/C02 — "The Volunteered Word" keeps the identity it had before this year's renumbering, and "Unauthorised, Therefore" (the new chapter that took over its old slot) gets its own. Other page types (characters/lore/glossary/codex) are unaffected: their URLs are never reassigned to different content, so pathname mapping stays safe for them. Also flips `data-strict` from `0` to `1`: giscus's discussion search is a title match, and without strict mode it's a loose one — a chapter's own `comment_id` (e.g. `unauthorised-therefore`) could loosely match one of its scenes' (`unauthorised-therefore-scene-1-adaeze`, which contains it as a prefix), pulling in the wrong discussion. Strict mode also makes a stale `comment_id` (e.g. a deleted chapter's) fail gracefully — no exact-title discussion to find means an empty thread, not a guessed near match.

### Added

- **`FORKING.md`**: a step-by-step guide to forking this repo either as an original interactive fiction site (replace the content, keep the engine) or as a Star Rangers fan fiction clone (keep some/all content too, per the new Fan Works Policy). Covers rebranding, the `/star-rangers/` path prefix, standing up a separate comments repo, and deployment for both GitHub Pages and cPanel.
- **`SITE_PATH_PREFIX`** env var (`.eleventy.js`): rewrites every hardcoded `/star-rangers/` absolute link across layouts *and* content (~200 files) to a different base path at build time, via an Eleventy transform. Exists for forkers serving from a different subpath or domain root, without hand-editing every file it appears in; unset by default, which leaves this project's own output byte-for-byte unchanged. The GitHub Pages workflow now passes it through from an optional `vars.SITE_PATH_PREFIX` repository variable. cPanel deploys don't need it — `scripts/cpanel-deploy.sh` already strips the same prefix with its own post-build sed step, independently of this.
- **Fan Works Policy** in `CONTENT-LICENSE.md`: an explicit, standing exception to the story content's No-Derivatives term for non-commercial fan fiction, fan art, and fan fiction clones of this site (forking the engine and some or all of the existing content) — conditioned on staying non-commercial, clearly labeled as unofficial, and attributed back to the original. The About page's "Fan fiction" section and the site's own on-page licence section both now point to it.

### Changed

- **Split the repository's licence in two**, so the site engine can be forked without implying any rights over the story itself. `LICENSE` is now plain **MIT**, covering `.eleventy.js`, `lib/`, `src/_includes/`, `src/css/`, `src/js/`, and `scripts/`; the story content (`src/seasons/`, `src/threads/`, `src/characters/`, `src/timeline/`, `src/lore/`, `src/glossary/`, `src/codex/`, `story-bible/`, `prompts/`) keeps the original **CC BY-NC-ND 4.0** terms, now in a new `CONTENT-LICENSE.md`. Previously the repo-root `LICENSE` file applied CC BY-NC-ND's NoDerivatives term to the whole repository, code included, which technically forbade forking the engine at all — a mismatch with `src/index.md`'s own licence section, which already scoped its wording to "text and world-building content" only. `package.json`'s stale `"license": "ISC"` (never matched either license) is now `"MIT"` to match, and `src/index.md`'s licence section gains a short pointer to the code's separate MIT licence.
- **Storyline Threads** as a top-level site category (`/threads/`), grouping seasons under the independent narratives established in `story-bible/story-bible-summary.md`'s "Narrative Structure" section: **Founding Era** (Season 0) and **Tissadelle Shepherd's Arc** (Seasons 1, 3, 5). The canonical thread→season registry lives in the new `lib/storyline-threads.js` (re-exported as global template data via `src/_data/storylineThreads.js`, and as the new `threadForSeason` Nunjucks filter), so it's the single source of truth for both the site's grouping and `deploy.conf`'s new filter below. `/seasons/` now groups its season blocks under a thread heading instead of listing seasons flat, each season's own index page carries a "Part of: `<thread>`" link, and each thread gets its own page at `/threads/<id>/` listing the seasons it covers. A season not yet assigned to a thread falls back to an "Unsorted" grouping rather than silently disappearing.
- **`THREADS` `deploy.conf` key**, alongside the existing `CHARACTERS`/`TOPICS`: a comma-separated list of storyline thread ids that narrows a deployed clone to the seasons those threads cover (every chapter whose `season` falls under a listed thread, plus any lore/timeline/glossary/codex entry explicitly tagged with the thread id). Combines with `CHARACTERS`/`TOPICS` rather than replacing them — matching any one of the three includes a page. Wired through `lib/content-filter.js` (`getContentFilter`, `isChapterIncluded`'s new `isSeasonInIncludedThread` check), `scripts/cpanel-deploy.sh` (including its own `ALT_<id>_THREADS` per-alt-domain variant), and documented in `sample-deploy.conf`, `.cpanel.yml`, and the README.
- **"Narrative Structure — Multiple Independent Storylines"** section in `story-bible/story-bible-summary.md`: formalizes the series' two-level storyline pattern already implicit in the published content — a macro-level season spine (Tissadelle Shepherd's career across S1/S3/S5/S6-7, with Seasons 2 and 4 deliberately left open as slots for storylines that don't involve her) and a micro-level pattern of independent, non-overlapping POV threads within a season that converge at a planned point (Season 1's Threshold Station/Marsh Causeway threads; the Season 6-7 treatment's institutional/interior threads). Documents the five criteria that make two threads "independent" rather than just alternating scenes, and flags Seasons 3 and 5 as the current exception to the pattern rather than a second template.
- **The Knarr Line** (`src/lore/knarr-line.md`), a five-century-old Belt shipping and ice-mining cooperative with Norwegian, Swedish, Danish, and Icelandic/Faroese founding roots, present at the 2337 Navigation and Trade Accords that grew into the United Space Consortium — and, having never left Sol System and never dissolved, the closest thing its own scattered habitats have to a government today, run through a delegate assembly it still calls **the Thing**. Two of its settlements get their own location entries: [Knarrheim](src/lore/knarrheim.md), its oldest habitat (a converted ice-hauler mothership and the Thing's usual meeting ground), and [Saltvik](src/lore/saltvik.md), its largest ore-refinery cluster. Cross-linked into `united-space-consortium.md`'s Origins section and contrasted, in `knarr-line.md` itself, against the Celtic Union of Planets' very different relationship to Solar System sovereignty.
- Corrected the existing `aethelrock-tir-na-nog.md` codex entry's framing: the real Aethelrock song it links is about the *mythical* Irish Otherworld, not literally the Celtic Union's Tír na nÓg planet (which merely borrows the same name) — retitled to "The Fires of Tír na nÓg" and reworded throughout to make that distinction explicit, while explaining why Union listeners (Tír na nÓg's own colonists especially) treat the difference as academic. Also added the reciprocal link from `tir-na-nog.md`'s own "See also" line, which never pointed back to this entry.
- **Clan Avalon** (`src/lore/planets/aethelrock.md`'s new "Clan Avalon: A Fellowship Without Ground" section) — a cross-clan bardic fellowship on Aethelrock, distinct from (and holding no Ridgemoot seat alongside) the world's five landholding clans, organised around keeping alive the Arthurian Avalon myth-cycle that already gave neighbouring [Ynys Wydrin](/star-rangers/lore/planets/ynys-wydrin/)'s home system, Avallach, its name — cross-linked reciprocally into that page's "See also" line. Its anthem is filed as a new codex entry, [Clan Avalon's Anthem](src/codex/clan-avalons-anthem.md), an externally hosted YouTube recording ("Echoes of Avalon" by the band Aethelrock) linked rather than archived, following the same pattern the existing `aethelrock-tir-na-nog.md` entry set.
- `ALT_DOMAINS` support in `deploy.conf`, letting one cPanel Git Version Control clone deploy additional domains from the same checkout — each to its own sibling folder under `$HOME`, at the same level as `public_html/` (typically an addon domain's document root) — instead of requiring a separate clone per domain. Each `ALT_DOMAINS` entry gets its own `ALT_<id>_DIR`/`ALT_<id>_DOMAIN` (required) plus optional `THEME`/`CHARACTERS`/`TOPICS`/`SITE_NAME`/`SITE_TITLE`/`ADMIN_EMAIL`/`CUSTOM_LORE_FILE`/`CUSTOM_CSS_FILE`, defaulting the same way their unprefixed primary-domain counterparts already do. `scripts/cpanel-deploy.sh`'s new `build_and_deploy()` runs one independent build+deploy per domain (clearing `_site/` between them so one domain's build never leaks into another's), aggregating every domain's result into one overall pass/fail rather than stopping at the first failure, and adding every configured `ADMIN_EMAIL` to the one run's notification list. See `sample-deploy.conf` and the README's new "`ALT_DOMAINS`" section for the full key reference.
- `SITE_NAME` and `SITE_TITLE` `deploy.conf` keys, letting a cPanel clone customize the brand name shown in the header/footer and the browser `<title>` tag independently of the shared repo default (`Star Rangers` for both). Wired through `scripts/cpanel-deploy.sh` into `src/_data/site.js`, consumed by `src/_includes/base.njk`.
- **Mnemari** (`src/lore/mnemari.md`), a sapient Federation species native to Ilenne with no natural upper bound on lifespan and no natural decay of episodic memory — balanced by an actuarial profile driven entirely by accident and violence rather than age, a deliberately low birthrate, and **the Setting-Down**, the voluntary retirement custom that gives a species with no natural mortality curve a working substitute for institutional turnover. Mnemari mediators and treaty-witnesses are noted as disproportionately valued in Federation assembly sessions revisiting old, contested compacts, for the same reason the Star Rangers themselves keep running into elsewhere in the setting: what happens to the truth of an event once everyone who could contradict a convenient retelling is gone. Cross-linked into `federation-of-sentient-beings.md`'s member-world roster and reciprocally into `krenyi.md`, `chthonari.md`, and `prismeri.md`.
- **Virtual Reality** (`src/glossary/virtual-reality.md`): mass-market VR entertainment declined well before 2826 UCSD because it reads as low-novelty recombination to the same Creative Entropy Index culture that audits pop-culture artifacts like "Paper Galaxies" — while fold-scaffold visualization remains a valued, unremarkable exception, since it renders a real, otherwise-imperceptible higher-dimensional structure rather than manufacturing one. Cross-linked into `creative-entropy-index-cei.md`'s example and related-terms list.
- **"AI: Present, Never Intrusive"** section added to `src/lore/environmental-technology-design.md`: names 2826 UCSD's ambient AI texture explicitly — Kernel-compliant systems running everywhere, announcing almost none of it — as the lived, day-to-day expression of the AI Safety Kernel's "obedience narrow, protection wide" doctrine.
- **"Bramble and the Backwards Key"** (`src/codex/bramble-and-the-backwards-key.md`): a codex excerpt from the Bramble Storybooks, the Concordant's best-loved Smart Pet children's-book franchise, plus a "Public Reputation" section added to `src/glossary/smart-pet.md` covering the cute/cool/clever cultural image the series cemented — dramatic irony fully intact, since the author has no idea any of it resembles real agency work.
- **Chthonari** (`src/lore/chthonari.md`) and their home, **the Undersong Belt** (`src/lore/undersong-belt.md`): a low-gravity, asteroid-burrowing insectoid Federation species whose vibration-based senses unify their engineering aptitude, abstract mathematics, and music into one structural trait, and who are disproportionately represented in the Star Rangers' Engineering Corps fold-scaffold specialization. Adds "Engineering" to the named specialist corps in `star-rangers-command-hierarchy.md` and cross-links the Undersong Belt into `federation-of-sentient-beings.md`'s member-world roster alongside Aspenar and Prismere.
- `CHARACTERS`-filtered deploys now automatically include any lore, timeline, or glossary entry that an included character's own bio links to directly, on top of the existing tag/category matching (`lib/content-filter.js`'s new `getRelatedContentUrls`). A character's bio is already the record of what background matters for understanding them, so that background no longer needs separate hand-tagging to survive a narrowed deploy.

- **Saltmere** (`src/lore/planets/saltmere.md`), a newly first-contacted planet in the Annwyn System with no landmass at all — a single global ocean settled entirely on engineered floating city-platforms tethered to the seafloor by mooring towers, built to give under storm load rather than hold rigid. Its **aquabots** — Kernel-compliant autonomous underwater maintenance vehicles — are noted as a convergent, not descended, echo of Earth's classified Subsea Cable Warden Programme, with a reciprocal cross-link added to that page.
- **Prismere** (`src/lore/planets/prismere.md`) and its native people, the **Prismeri** (`src/lore/prismeri.md`): a new Federation of Sentient Beings charter world with a bioluminescent silicate-carbon biosphere and a naked-eye fold-corridor phenomenon, the Lattice, tying into existing Lagrange Fold Points and Quantum Space Harmonics canon.
- **Bubochka**, a trainee rabbit in the Undercover Pets Detective Agency, mentored by Agent Barsik at Eden Space Habitat (`src/characters/bubochka.md`).
- **The Orbital Habitats Compact** (`src/lore/orbital-habitats-compact.md`): the civil governance chain for Eden and the other four self-governing orbital habitats around Earth, running parallel to — and never overlapping — the Star Rangers' charter-limited authority. Introduces Superintendent Rasa Oyelaran, Space Commissioner Zara Wayland, Mayor Imogen Petrakis, and Chief Commissioner Dorian Calloway, and gives Governor Petra Voss (previously only referenced from Commander Kai Larsen's page) her own character profile.
- **The Eden Warden** (`src/characters/eden-warden.md`): a per-habitat AI collective, plural in the same sense the [Plural Minds](/star-rangers/glossary/plural-minds/) glossary entry already describes for organic minds — two Kernel-compliant personas, Ward and Custos, sharing one system, reporting jointly to the Mayor and Commissioner, and holding standards authority over mobile AI humanoids (Reeves, Lucene-9000) and welfare responsibility for cyber-enhanced animals, alongside — not through — the Detective Superintendent's operational chain.
- **Smart Pet** (`src/glossary/smart-pet.md`): the formal classification for an animal carrying a certified AI cognitive subsystem — distinct from, and broader than, "cyber-enhanced" — with its own independent, heavily regulated animal-welfare certification track separate from Kernel compliance. Retroactively clarifies that Barsik and Bubochka hold Smart Pet status without being cyber-enhanced, unlike Aldera, who holds both.
- **"Obedience Is Narrow. Protection Is Not."** section added to `src/lore/ai-safety-kernel.md`: names the Kernel's core asymmetry between invariant 3 (obedience limited to lawful, legitimate authority) and invariant 1 (protection owed universally, without the protected party needing standing to claim it) — the doctrinal basis for the Habitat AI Collectives' welfare authority over parties, human or not, with no seat at the table that assigns their own protection.
- **Frontier Transformation Protocols** (`src/lore/frontier-transformation-protocols.md`): the safety doctrine governing when a frontier world may be terraformed at all — guarding against undetected native sapience, boundary-proximate instability (the Eden precedent), and irreversibility — plus the AI Safety Kernel's own structural backstop against a Kernel-compliant system being ordered past it. Documents each major polity's own version (SSDC centralised review, Federation per-world autonomy, Celtic Union's never-yet-met unanimous-consent bar, Cerebraun Hegemony central authorisation), explaining why Kernowek Reach's reclamation, Mars's incomplete terraforming, and Aspenar's domes-over-conversion choice all read the way they already did.
- **"First Breath: A Founding Thanksgiving"** and **"Survey Note: On the Origins of Tír na nÓg's Compatibility"** (`src/codex/`): two codex documents on Tír na nÓg's mysterious origins — the founding cooperative's own devotional thanksgiving text crediting Manannán mac Lir, and a Survey Corps xenobiology review of six competing theories (convergent evolution, precursor engineering, an undetected Concordant mechanism, Levrilic influence/divine providence, a wild fringe theory of an ancient lost inter-planetary fold gate predating Lagrange-point staging, and a more physically grounded theory involving transient natural fold apertures during rare conjunctions of Tír na nÓg's two moons, Donn and Cliona). Levrilic influence/divine providence is the most popular opinion among the public, but explicitly *not* the least credible of the six — that distinction belongs to the fold-gate theory, since it contradicts confirmed fold-shear physics, while the lunar-conjunction theory is consistent with it (per Eden's own confirmed natural fold route) and is the survey note's recommended candidate for future funding. Cross-linked into `tir-na-nog.md`'s anomaly section, `lagrange-fold-points.md`, and `eden-space-habitat.md`.

### Changed

- **Tír na nÓg** (`src/lore/planets/tir-na-nog.md`) is reframed as a standing, unexplained scientific anomaly rather than a comfortable "convergent evolution" story, to establish as firm setting canon that no world or species is ever naturally compatible with Earthlike gravity/atmosphere without engineering — Tír na nÓg remains the sole confirmed exception, now explicitly flagged as one nobody has closed the file on. Cross-linked update in `celtic-union-of-planets.md`. `kingdom-of-the-four-islands.md` gets a small clarifying addition (centuries-old, since-forgotten atmospheric engineering by the lost colony's founders) so it doesn't read as a second, unflagged exception to the same rule.
- `ADMIN_EMAIL` deploy.conf key now defaults to `admin@<DOMAIN>` instead of staying unset, so every cPanel clone gets deploy-log notifications out of the box without needing its own `deploy.conf` entry for it.

## [1.5.0] - 2026-07-09

> **Note on 1.0.0–1.5.0.** These six entries were written in one sitting, in the commit that introduced this changelog (`45f72f3`, "Add theme generator, 4 standard themes, and a real changelog/semver"). They reconstruct development phases rather than record releases that were cut at the time: `package.json` held 1.0.0 from the first content commit (`a0ca09a`, 2026-05-27) until that commit set it directly to 1.5.0, so **1.1.0, 1.2.0, 1.3.0 and 1.4.0 never existed as states of this repository**. Only 1.0.0 and 1.5.0 correspond to a real commit (`a0ca09a` and `45f72f3`); the other four are not taggable and should not be given tags pointing at stand-in commits. The history below is still accurate about *what changed*; it is not a record of *when it shipped*.

### Added

- `scripts/generate-themes.js` (`npm run generate-themes`): generates every `src/css/theme-<name>.css` from `main.css` plus a small per-theme palette registry, so a theme can only ever differ from `main.css` in its `:root` custom properties, its five `.pov-block--<character>` colors, and `.character-badge--status-active` — everything else is guaranteed structurally identical to `main.css`.
- Four new standard, non-domain-specific themes: `light` (day mode), `high-contrast` (low-vision accessibility), `sepia` (e-reader tone), `solarized` (Solarized Dark).
- Theme catalog documented in `sample-deploy.conf` and `README.md`.

### Fixed

- The `pets` theme (undercover-pets.com) had drifted significantly out of sync with `main.css`: it was missing link-color styling across nearly every content body (`.chapter-body a`, `.codex-entry__body a`, `.character-body a`, `.glossary-entry__body a`, `.lore-entry__body a`, and `.character-portrait`), meaning most internal links on that production domain rendered in the browser's default blue instead of the theme's own accent color. The `fellowship` and `starquest` themes had smaller drift (missing the 1.2.0 link-color fallback and two newer component rules). All three are now regenerated in sync with `main.css` by `scripts/generate-themes.js`; their palettes are unchanged.

## [1.4.0] - 2026-07-09

### Added

- `CUSTOM_LORE_FILE` deploy.conf key: a clone-local, untracked markdown file with valid lore-entry front matter, copied into `src/lore/custom/` before the build (builds at `/lore/custom/<name>/`) and removed again afterward, so one cPanel clone can carry a domain-exclusive lore page without touching the shared repo.
- `CUSTOM_CSS_FILE` deploy.conf key: a clone-local, untracked CSS file appended after the theme stylesheet, so one clone can override a handful of rules without a whole new `theme-<name>.css`.
- Both fail the deploy loudly if set to a path that doesn't exist.

## [1.3.0] - 2026-07-09

### Added

- `DOMAIN` deploy.conf key, exported as `SITE_DOMAIN` for the Eleventy build.
- `src/_data/site.js`, `src/robots.njk`, `src/sitemap.njk`: `robots.txt` and a real `sitemap.xml` are now rendered at build time from the clone's own domain, instead of `robots.txt` being a static file hardcoded to one production domain.

### Fixed

- `robots.txt`'s `Sitemap:` line pointed at `https://sciencefiction.site/sitemap.xml` on every deploy target, including the other four production domains this repo serves — and no `sitemap.xml` was ever actually generated by any build, so the directive 404'd everywhere, including on sciencefiction.site itself.

## [1.2.0] - 2026-07-09

### Changed

- cPanel deploy (`scripts/cpanel-deploy.sh`) now fails the deployment — and triggers the existing `ADMIN_EMAIL` failure notification — if `.htaccess` or `.well-known/security.txt` are missing from the deployed destination, instead of only checking for `index.html`. cPanel is the only deploy target that reads `.htaccess` at all (GitHub Pages ignores it), so a silent regression there would previously have shipped with none of its security headers and still reported success.

### Notes

- Audited both deploy targets for security posture: cPanel's `.htaccess` already set CSP, `X-Content-Type-Options`, `X-Frame-Options`, `Referrer-Policy`, and `Permissions-Policy`; `.well-known/security.txt` was present and current. GitHub Pages has no supported mechanism for custom response headers at all, so it ships with none of these — a platform limitation, not a config gap.

## [1.1.0] - 2026-07-09

### Added

- Lore entry: "The Grand Ensemble Multiverse" (`src/lore/ensemble-multiverse.md`) — names the infinite collection of Worldwright-authored universes, documents our home universe's 3 visible-physical + 7 invisible-Etheric + 1 time = 11-dimensional structure, and explains why other universes in the Cascade can use a different dimensional split with different fundamental particles and forces. Cross-linked from `post-eleven-dimensional-manifold.md`.
- Default-theme homepage hero paragraph rewritten to link into the new lore entry instead of just the Concordant glossary term.

### Fixed

- Several inline links (the homepage hero paragraph, the Atlas page intro) sat outside any styled component class and had no color rule, so they rendered in the browser's default blue instead of the site's accent color. Added a sitewide fallback `a` rule in `main.css`.

Baseline release, consolidating prior undated project history (this is the first version this changelog covers retroactively).

- Expanded fold-space material around Lagrange fold-points, linked across related FTL articles.
- Canon for the Subsea Cable Warden Programme.
- Lore for the Star Rangers Safety Corps and its historical lineage.
- Timeline events from before the United Stellar Concord.

### Changed

- Revised timeline event titles and updated charter references for the Safety Corps and the SSSA.
- Renamed references to "UL Standards International" as "United Space Industry Standards" across lore and timeline content.
